Moreover, in all world-systems, this is the second deva-world, as stated in the Janavasabha Sutta, and it is the established abode for thirty-three deva-kings in Sakka's position, such as Pajāpati, Varuṇa, and Īsāna. A thousand (devas) belong to the Cātumahārājika realm, and a thousand to the Tāvatiṃsa—as mentioned in the Aṅguttara Nikāya. However, the men of Māgha's company are reborn in those assembled deva-king positions. And since they are still existing at present, this meaning of the word should be understood in reference to them. Others, however, say that just as in the Vidhura Jātaka, where it is said that 'the Indagopaka insects appear thirty at a time,' the word 'tāva' is merely an accessory to the word 'thirty.' Similarly here, it would be fitting to say that they are named Tāvatiṃsa because it is the abode of approximately thirty deva-royal families who are in Sakka's position. However, in the commentaries, having adopted the aforementioned etymological method, they also say that in the stories of Māgha and in those various places, the number thirty-three is stated only for the Sakkas. This is incorrect, for in the Pāli itself, it is said that Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra created thirty-three forms and sat on the couches of the Tāvatiṃsa devas. 'Yāma' is the name of the ruling deva-family in that deva-world, and likewise 'Suyāma.' However, due to their association, that deva-world and the devas born there are also called Yāma. They are called 'Tusita' because they are endowed with abundant glorious wealth and are always delighted, their faces very joyous and happy. They are called 'Nimmānaratī' because they themselves create pleasures as they wish and delight in them. They are called 'Paranimmitavasavattī' because, knowing their own desire, they wield power over pleasures created by others. They are called 'Brahmās' because they grow, increase, and attain vastness through exceedingly excellent qualities such as jhāna. Though it should be said 'Mahābrahmās' (Great Brahmās), the word 'mahā' is dropped.

Parisati bhavāti pārisajjā. Parisāsu jātātivā pārisajjā. Paricārikāti attho. Mahābrahmānaṃ pārisajjāti brahma pārisajjā. Pure ucce ṭhāne odahanti tiṭṭhantīti purohitā. Mahābrahmānaṃ purohitāti brahmapurohitā. Mahantā brahmāno mahābrahmāno. Sahassobrahmā dvisahassobrahmā. Tisahassobrahmātiādinā saṅkhārupapattisutte āgatā adhipatibrahmānoti attho. Tattha sahassobrahmāti cakkavāḷasahassamhi issaro brahmā. Dvisahassoti dvīsu cakkavāḷa sahassesu issaroti attho. Tayopete ekatala vāsino honti. Tattha loke mahājanā visuṃ visuṃ kuladevatāyonāma upaṭṭhahanti. Keci mahādevaṃnāma upaṭṭhahanti. Keci vāsudevaṃnāma. Keci mahesaraṃnāma. Keci paramesvāraṃ nāmāti. Gharadevatā gāmadevatā rukkhadevatādayopi tesaṃ mahādevarājānaṃ upaṭṭhakāeva sampajjanti. Tattha mahādevarā jānoviya mahābrahmāno daṭṭhabbā. Gharadevatādayoviya brahma purohitādaṭṭhabbā, [M 0.0199] manussāviya brahmapārisajjādaṭṭhabbā. Tatthaca ghara devatādayo mahādevarā jāno adisvāva upaṭṭhahanti. Manussā ca teubhopi adisvāva upaṭṭhahanti. Evamevaṃ brahmapurohitā mahābrahmānopi napassanti. Mahābrahmānaṃ nivāsaṭṭhānaṃpi najānanti. Brahmapārisajjāubhopi napassanti. Ubhinnaṃnivāsaṭṭhānaṃpi najānanti. Yadā pana oḷārikaṃ rūpaṃ māpetvā attānaṃ dassenti. Tadā eva passanti. Esanayo uparibhūmīsupi. Yaṃ pana brahmanimantana suttaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ brahmānaṃ pakatirūpaṃ kassaci āpātaṃ na gacchatīti. Taṃ brahmapuro hitā dīnaṃ uparimānaṃ brahmānaṃ pakatirūpaṃ kassaci brahmapārisajjādinovā devassavā manussassavāāpātaṃ nagacchatīti katvā vuttaṃ. Heṭṭhimānaṃ pana pakatirūpaṃ uparimassa āpātaṃ āgacchissatiyeva. Teneva hi janavasabhasuttaṭṭhakathāyaṃ heṭṭhimaheṭṭhimāhi devā uparimadevānaṃ oḷārikaṃ katvā māpitameva attabhāvaṃ passituṃ sakkontīti vuttaṃ. Tatthadutīyatale parittābhāti brahmapārisajjāeva. Appamāṇābhāti brahmapurohitā eva. Ābhassarāti mahābrahmānoeva. Tasmiṃ tale adhipati brahmānoevāti attho. Heṭṭhimatalato pana visesa karaṇatthaṃ ābhāvasena nāmagahaṇaṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Being in an assembly, they are 'retinue' (pārisajjā). Or, born in assemblies, they are 'retinue.' The meaning is 'attendants.' The retinue of the Great Brahmās is the Brahma retinue. Those who are placed in a high position in front are 'chaplains' (purohitā). The chaplains of the Great Brahmās are the Brahma chaplains. The great Brahmās are the Great Brahmās. The thousandfold Brahmās, the twofold thousand Brahmās, the threefold thousand Brahmās—these, as mentioned in the Saṅkhārupapatti Sutta, signify the overlord Brahmās. Among them, the thousandfold Brahmā is the lord in a thousand world-systems. The twofold thousand signifies the lord in two thousand world-systems. These three dwell together on one plane. In the world, many people attend upon various family deities. Some attend upon Mahādeva, some Vāsudeva, some Maheśvara, some Parameśvara. Household deities, village deities, tree deities, and others also become attendants of these great divine kings. Among them, the Great Brahmās should be regarded as the great divine kings; household deities and others as the Brahma chaplains; and humans as the Brahma retinue. And just as household deities and others attend upon the great divine kings without seeing them, and humans also attend upon both without seeing them, similarly, the Brahma chaplains do not see the Great Brahmās, nor do they know their dwelling place. The Brahma retinue does not see both, nor do they know the dwelling place of both. Only when they manifest a gross form and show themselves, then they see them. This principle applies to the higher realms as well. However, what was stated in the commentary to the Brahmanimantanika Sutta, 'the natural form of a Brahmā does not come into the range of vision for anyone,' was stated on the grounds that the natural form of the higher Brahmās does not come into the range of vision for the Brahma chaplains and others below them, nor for any god or human. But the natural form of the lower ones will indeed come into the range of vision for the higher ones. Thus, indeed, in the commentary to the Janavasabha Sutta, it is said that the lower gods are able to see only the manifested individual existence that the higher gods have made gross. There, in the second plane, 'of Limited Radiance' refers to the Brahma retinue. 'Of Immeasurable Radiance' refers to the Brahma chaplains. 'The Radiant' refers to the Great Brahmās. The meaning is that in that plane, they are the overlord Brahmās. It should be understood that the naming is based on radiance for the purpose of distinguishing it from the lower plane.

Tattha parittā ābhā etesanti parittābhā. Appamāṇā ābhā etesanti appamāṇābhā. Ābhāsaranti niccharanti etesūti ābhassarāti. Tatīyatale parittasubhāti brahmapārisajjāeva. Appamāṇasutāti brahmapurohitāeva. Sutakiṇṇāti mahābrahmanoeva. Tasmiṃ tale adhipatibrahmāno evāti attho. Tattha subhāti ekagghanā acalasaṇṭhitā ābhāeva vuccanti. Parittā subhā etesanti parittasubhā. Appamāṇā subhā etesanti appamāṇasubhā. Sutehi ākiṇṇāti subhākiṇṇā. Subhakiṇhātipi paṭhanti. Tesaṃ ākārassa rasso antimaṇakārassa ca hakāro daṭṭhabbo. Imesu pana dvīsu talesu pakatikāyappabhā adhimattā honti. Tasmā tāsaṃ vasena parittābhātiādikaṃ nāmaṃ siddhaṃ. Na brahmapāri sajjātiādikaṃ. [M 0.0200] Evañca katvā verañjasutte pathamatalavāsino brahmakāyikā devāti āgatā. Dutīyatalavāsino ābhādevāti. Tatīyatalavāsino subhādevāti catutthatale vipulaṃ phalaṃ etesanti vehapphalā. Athavā iñjanajātikehi somanassajjhānehi nibbattānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ heṭṭhimatalānaṃ tejosaṃ vaṭṭādikena antarāyena bhūmitalena saha āyukappanivattivasena iñjitaṃ puññaphalaṃ atthi. Tesu hi yaṃ subhākiṇṇānaṃ devānaṃ catusaṭṭhikappānīti vuttaṃ. Taṃ tasmiṃ tale ādikappikānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Pacchimikānaṃ pana tesaṭṭhikappa dvāsaṭṭhikappa ekasaṭṭhi kappādi vasena iñjitaṃ paṭilīnaṃ puññaphalaṃ hotīti. Āneñjajātikena upekkhājhānena nibbattānaṃ pana kenaci antarāyena tādisaṃ iñjitaṃ puññaphalaṃ nāma natthi. Tasmā jhāna sāmatthiyānurūpaṃ visesena īhitaṃ abhivaḍḍhitaṃ puññaphalaṃ ettha atthīti vehapphalā.

Here, 'of Limited Radiance' (parittābhā) means 'limited radiance belongs to them.' 'Of Immeasurable Radiance' (appamāṇābhā) means 'immeasurable radiance belongs to them.' Radiance issues forth from them, thus they are 'the Radiant' (ābhassarā). In the third plane, 'of Limited Lustre' (parittasubhā) refers just to the Brahma retinue. 'Of Immeasurable Lustre' (appamāṇasubhā) refers just to the Brahma chaplains. 'Replete with Lustre' (subhakiṇṇā) refers just to the Great Brahmās. The meaning is that in that plane, they are the overlord Brahmās. There, 'lustre' (subhā) refers to a radiance that is unified, unwavering, and firmly established. 'Limited lustre belongs to them,' thus they are 'of Limited Lustre' (parittasubhā). 'Immeasurable lustre belongs to them,' thus they are 'of Immeasurable Lustre' (appamāṇasubhā). 'They are replete with lustre,' thus they are 'Replete with Lustre' (subhakiṇṇā). Some also read 'subhakiṇhā.' The shortening of the vowel 'ā' and the change of the final 'ṇ' to 'h' should be noted. In these two planes, the natural radiance of the body is exceedingly great. Therefore, the names 'of Limited Radiance' and so on are established based on that, not 'Brahma retinue' and so on. And so, in the Verañja Sutta, the dwellers of the first plane are called 'Brahmakāyika deities,' the dwellers of the second plane are called 'Ābhā deities,' and the dwellers of the third plane are called 'Subhā deities.' In the fourth plane, 'their fruit is abundant (vipulaṃ phalaṃ),' thus they are 'of Abundant Fruit' (vehapphalā). Alternatively, for those born from the jhānas associated with gladness, which are of a moving nature, the meritorious fruit of the three lower planes is 'moved' because of the turning back of the life-eon, along with the ground-plane, due to an obstacle such as the world-destruction by fire. For among them, what is stated as the sixty-four eons of the 'Replete with Lustre' deities is stated with reference to those at the beginning of the aeon in that plane. But for later ones, the meritorious fruit is moved and withdrawn, becoming sixty-three eons, sixty-two eons, sixty-one eons, and so on. But for those born from the jhānas of equanimity, which are of an imperturbable nature, there is no such 'moved' meritorious fruit due to any obstacle. Therefore, because here there is a meritorious fruit that is specially striven for and augmented in accordance with the power of the jhānas, they are 'of Abundant Fruit' (vehapphalā).

Natthi saññāmukhena gahitā cattāro arūpakkhandhā etesanti asaññā. Asaññāca te sattācāti asaññasattā. Cittace tasikānaṃ pana natthitāya tesaṃ asattapasaṅgatā sambhavatīti sattagahaṇaṃ katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ete dvepi ekatalavāsino eva honti. Etthapi nibbattakajjhānassa hīnamajjhimapaṇītatā visesassa atthitāya tadanurūpaṃ brahmānaṃpi pārisajja purohita mahābrahmatta viseso sambhavatiyeva. Āyuvemattatāya pana aññamañña adassanādīnañca natthitāya pārisajjādivasena bhūmivibhāgo natthīti veditabbo. Evaṃ avihādīsupi. Oḷārikānaṃ kāmarāgapaṭighānusayānaṃ natthitāya suddhānaṃ anāgāmiarahantānameva āvāsāti suddhāvāsā. Tattha pathamabhūmivāsino appakena kālena attano ṭhānaṃ navijahantīti avihā. Athavā, oḷārikānaṃ pañcannaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahīnattā natthi cittassa vihaññanaṃ samathavipassa nādhammesu avipphārikatāpatti etesanti avihā. Dutīyabhūmi vāsino na kenaci cittapariḷāhena tappantīti atappā. Tatīya talavāsino parisuddhehi pasādacakkhu dibbacakkhu dhammacakkhu paññā cakkhūhi sampannattā suṭṭhu passantīti sudassā. Catutthabhūmivāsino pana [M 0.0201] tato atisayena suṭṭhu dassanabhāvena samannāgatāti sudassino. Atisayatthe hi ayaṃ īkāroti. Pañcamabhūmi vāsino upari aññassa bhūmantaragatassa rūpibrahmuno natthitāya natthi rūpīnaṃ sattānaṃ majjhe kenaci guṇena kaniṭṭhabhāvo etesanti akaniṭṭhā.

'For them, the four immaterial aggregates grasped by way of perception do not exist,' thus they are 'non-percipient' (asaññā). And those beings are non-percipient, thus they are 'non-percipient beings' (asaññasattā). It should be understood that since consciousness and mental factors are absent for them, the implication of their not being 'beings' might arise; therefore, the term 'being' (satta) is included. These two also dwell on the same plane. Here too, due to the inferior, middling, and superior distinctions of the jhānas that produce them, corresponding distinctions among the Brahmās—as retinue, chaplains, or Great Brahmās—can arise. However, because there is no difference in their lifespans nor do they see one another, and so on, it should be understood that there is no division of planes in terms of retinue and so forth. The same applies to the Avihā and so forth. Because the underlying tendencies of gross sensual desire and ill will are absent, they are the dwellings of the pure ones, the non-returners and arahants; thus they are the 'Pure Abodes' (suddhāvāsā). There, the dwellers of the first plane do not abandon their place in a short time; hence, they are 'the Non-Falling' (avihā). Alternatively, because the five lower fetters are abandoned, there is no affliction of mind for them, no lapse from steadfastness in the qualities of serenity and insight; hence, they are 'the Non-Falling' (avihā). The dwellers of the second plane are not tormented by any mental fever; hence, they are 'the Untormented' (atappā). The dwellers of the third plane see well, being endowed with purified eyes; hence, they are 'the Clearly-Seeing' (sudassā). The dwellers of the fourth plane, however, are endowed with a state of seeing that is exceedingly good, surpassing the former; hence, they are 'the Very Clearly-Seeing' (sudassino). The suffix 'ī' here is in the sense of 'exceeding.' The dwellers of the fifth plane: because there is no other form-brahmā existing in a plane above them, there is for them no state of being junior in any quality among beings with form; hence, they are 'the Not Junior' (akaniṭṭhā).

Ākāsānañcāyatanabhūmīti ettha yattakaṃ ākāsapadesaṃ pharitvā ākāsānañcāyatana saññitā catukkhandhā pavattanti. So khandhasahito ākāsapadeso ākāsānañcāyayanabhūmi. Evaṃ sesāsu. Puthujjanā sotāpannā sakadāgāminocāpi puggalā suddhāvāsesu sabbathā sabbapakārenapi nalabbhantīti yojanā. Etthaca sakadāgāmīnaṃ paṭikkhepena anāgāmi maggaṭṭhassapi tattha paṭikkhepo siddho hotīti uparimānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ ariyānameva tattha paṭilābho imāya gāthāya vuttoti veditabbo. Sesaṭṭhānesūti pañcasuddhāvāsato asaññāpāyatoca avasesesu ekavīsatiyā ṭhānesu, anariyāti puthujjanā. [Bhūmicatukkaṃ]

The plane of the sphere of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatanabhūmi)—here, whatever portion of space is pervaded, therein arise the four aggregates designated as 'the sphere of infinite space'. That portion of space, together with the aggregates, is the plane of the sphere of infinite space. The same applies to the remaining spheres. Ordinary persons (puthujjanā), stream-enterers (sotāpannā), and once-returners (sakadāgāmino) are not found in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsā) in any way or manner—this is the connection. Here, by the exclusion of once-returners, the exclusion of one on the path to non-returning is also established. It should be understood that the attainment therein of only the three higher noble ones is stated by this verse. In the remaining places—apart from the five Pure Abodes and the realm of non-percipient beings (asaññāpāyato), in the remaining twenty-one places, the non-noble ones (anariyā) are ordinary persons (puthujjanā). [The Fourfold Division of Planes]

144. Okkantikkhaṇeti paṭisandhikkhaṇe. Paṭisandhihi bhavantare okkamanaṃ anupavisananthi atthena okkantīti vuccati. Tato paraṃ bhavaṅgaṃ hutvāti yojanā. Keci pana bhavaṅgapariyosāneti paṭhanti. Taṃ na yujjati. Jātiyā andho jaccandho. Ādisaddena jāti badhira jaccaghānaka jātimūga jacceḷa jaccummattaka paṇḍaka ubhato byañjanaka napuṃsaka mammādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Tattha yassa cakkhuṃ uppādetuṃ asamatthena kammena paṭisandhi laddhā. So jaccandho nāma. Esanayo sesesupi. Tattha pasādasota rahito jātibadhiro nāma. Pasāda ghānarahito jacca ghānako nāma. Pasādajivhārahito nāma natthi. Vacanarahito jātimūgonāma. Disāvidisāmattaṃpi saññāpetuṃ asakkuṇeyyo jātieḷo nāma. Sabbakālaṃpi vipallaṭṭhacitto jaccummattakonāma. Kāmahetu āsittakādibhāvena vippakārapatto paṇḍakonāma. Dvīhi byañjanehi samannāgato ubhato byañjanakonāma. Bhāvadvaya rahito napuṃsakonāma. Pakativacanepi ekamekaṃ akkharaṃ mahussāhena [M 0.0202] uppādento vibacchavacano mammonāma. Etthaca cakkhuṃ uppādetuṃ samatthena kammena laddhapaṭisandhikassa pavattikāle taṃvā aññaṃvā kammaṃ cakkhuṃ uppādeti. Asamatthenakammena laddhapaṭisandhi kassa pana vatthuvipannassa pavattikāle aññaṃpi kammaṃ cakkhuṃ uppādetīti natthi. Tasmā gabbhaseyyakānaṃpi jaccandhabhāvo paṭisandhikkhaṇeyeva siddhoti veditabbo. Esanayo sesesu jāti badhirādīsu. Āyatanānaṃ paṭilābho jātīti vuttattā cakkhussa uppajjanārahakālo cakkhussa jātikālonāma. Tadā anuppanna cakkhuko jaccandhonāmāti evaṃ attano attano uppajjanāraha kālavasena tassa tassa āyatanassa jātikālo veditabbo. Evañhisati jātimūgādayopi upapanno hontītica vadanti. Vibhāvani yaṃpi ayamattho vibhāvitoti.

144. The moment of 'descent' (okkanti) is the moment of rebirth-linking (paṭisandhi). For 'rebirth-linking' is called 'descent' in the sense of entering into another existence. The connection is that 'after that, it becomes the life-continuum (bhavaṅga).' Some, however, read 'at the end of the life-continuum.' That is not appropriate. One blind from birth is 'jaccandha.' By the term 'etc.' are included those born deaf (jātibadhira), congenitally anosmic (jaccaghānaka), mute from birth (jātimūga), congenitally idiotic (jacceḷa), congenitally insane (jaccummattaka), eunuchs (paṇḍaka), hermaphrodites (ubhatobyañjanaka), neuters (napuṃsaka), and stammerers (mammādayo). Here, one whose rebirth-linking was obtained through kamma incapable of producing the eye is called 'jaccandha.' The same method applies to the others. Here, one lacking the sensitive auditory faculty is called 'jātibadhira.' One lacking the sensitive olfactory faculty is called 'jaccaghānaka.' There is no one lacking the sensitive gustatory faculty. One incapable of speech is called 'jātimūga.' One unable to communicate even the cardinal and intermediate directions is called 'jāti-eḷa.' One whose mind is always deranged is called 'jaccummattaka.' One whose nature is impaired due to sensual craving, such as being effeminate, is called 'paṇḍaka.' One endowed with both sexual characteristics is called 'ubhatobyañjanaka.' One devoid of both sexual characteristics is called 'napuṃsaka.' One who produces each single syllable with great effort, speaking indistinctly, is called 'mamma.' In this case, for one whose rebirth-linking was obtained through kamma capable of producing the eye, during the course of existence, either that same kamma or another kamma may produce the eye. But for one whose rebirth-linking was obtained through kamma incapable of producing the eye, whose physical base is impaired, even if another kamma arises during the course of existence, it cannot produce the eye. Therefore, it should be understood that even for those lying in the womb, congenital blindness is established at the very moment of rebirth-linking. The same method applies to the other congenital conditions like deafness, etc. Since it is said, 'Birth is the acquisition of the sense bases,' the time when the eye is fit to arise is called the moment of the eye's birth. At that time, one whose eye has not arisen is called 'jaccandha.' Thus, the moment of birth for each sense base should be understood according to its own time when it is fit to arise. This being so, some say that even the mute and others are thus reborn. This meaning has indeed been clarified in the Vibhāvanī.

[142] Yaṃ pana vibhāvaniyaṃ

But what is stated in the Vibhāvanī:

“Apare pana jaccandhoti pasutiyaṃyeva andho. Mātu kucchiyaṃ andho hutvā nikkhantoti attho. Tena duhetukatihetukānaṃ mātukucchiyaṃ cakkhussa avipajjanaṃ siddhanti vadantīti” vuttaṃ. Taṃ na yuttaṃ.

“Others, however, say that 'jaccandha' means blind right from birth, that is, having emerged from the mother's womb blind. By this, they claim that the non-impairment of the eye in the mother's womb is established for those with two or three roots.” This is said, but it is not appropriate.

Loke mātukucchiyaṃyeva andho hutvā nikkhantassapi ekaccassa taṃ taṃ sippavijjāṭhānesu paññāveyyattiyabhāvassa diṭṭhattā. Thapetvā hi mahābodhisatte aññeca pacchimabhavike satte avasesānaṃ dvihetuka tihetukānaṃpi mātukucchimhi parūpakkamenavā mātuyā visamapayogenavā nānābādhenavā uppannānaṃpi cakkhusotānaṃ vipattināma natthīti na sakkā niyametunti. Bhummassitānañca vinipātikāsurānanti ettha bhūmiyaṃ jātāti bhummā. Bhūmisambandhesu rukkhaṭṭhaka pabbataṭṭhaka vimānesu nibbattā āḷavaka sātāgira hemavatādayo mahiddhikā bhummādevā. Ye loke baliharaṇa vasena pūjanīyaṭṭhena yakkhātipi vuccanti. Ye pana bhummadevajātikāpi samānā attano puññanibbattassa kassaci bhogasukhassa abhāvā kicchajīvi kappattā [M 0.0203] vicaranti. Te tesaṃ mahiddhikānaṃ bhummadevānaṃ paraṃpara pārisajjesu pariyāpannattā bhumme deve sitā nissitāti atthena bhummassitānāma honti. Bhummissitātipi pāṭho. Puññanibbattassa nivāsaṭṭhānassa abhāvā rukkhagumbaleṇaguhāsusānā dīsu vivittesu bhūmipadesesu nissāya vasantīti attho. Teyeva virūpā hutvā bhavantare nipatantīti vinipātikā. Vinipātikāca te heṭṭhāvuttaṭṭhena asurācāti vinipātikā surā. Te pana gāmasamīpevā antogāmevā vivittaṭṭhānesu vasitvā gāmavāsīhi chaḍḍitāni bhattasitthapūvakhajjamacchamaṃsādīni pariyesitvāvā tāni alabhitvā dārakevā gilānevā pīḷetvāvā sakkontā pana aññepi manusse tāsetvā pīḷetvāvā jīvitaṃ kappentīti. Tesaṃ vinipātikāsurānaṃ. Ekaccānanti adhippāyo. Na hi sabbe vinipātikā surānāma ahetu kāevāti sakkā vattuṃ. Dvihetukatihetukānaṃpi sabbhāvato. Evañca katvā tesaṃ ekaccānaṃ piyaṅkaramātā uttaramātā dhammaguttā phussamittādīnaṃ dhammābhisamayopi aṭṭhakathāsu vuttoti. Ekacce yakkhajātikāpi rakkhasajātikāpi vemānikapetāpi paradattupajīvi petāpi ettha saṅgahitāti daṭṭhabbā.

In the world, even some who have emerged from the mother's womb blind are seen to possess wisdom and intelligence in various arts and sciences. For, apart from the Great Bodhisattas and other beings in their final existence, for the rest—even those with two or three roots—it cannot be definitively stated that there is no such thing as impairment of the eyes and ears which have arisen in the mother’s womb, an impairment due to external interference, the mother’s improper regimen, or various illnesses. As for 'earth-bound beings and fallen asuras' (bhummassitānañca vinipātikāsurānaṃ), here 'earth-bound' (bhummā) means born on the earth. Those connected to the earth—such as the powerful earth deities like Āḷavaka, Sātāgira, and Hemavata, who are reborn in tree-dwelling, mountain-dwelling, or mansion-dwelling abodes—are earth deities. In the world, they are also called yakkhas due to their being worthy of offerings by virtue of their power. However, some, though of the earth-deity class, wander in hardship, their lives afflicted due to the lack of any enjoyment of wealth produced by their own merit. Because they are included among the retinues of those powerful earth deities, they are called 'earth-bound' (bhummassitā), in the sense of being supported by the earth deities. 'Bhummissitā' is also a reading. Due to the absence of a dwelling place produced by merit, the meaning is that they reside dependent on secluded spots like tree clumps, caves, and cemeteries. These same beings, having become deformed, fall into another existence—hence they are 'fallen ones' (vinipātikā). And those fallen ones are also asuras according to the meaning stated above—hence 'fallen asuras' (vinipātikāsurā). They dwell near villages or even within villages, in secluded places, and search for food discarded by villagers—such as lumps of rice, cakes, sweets, fish, or meat. If they cannot obtain these, they torment children or the sick, or if they are able, they frighten and harass other people to sustain their lives. This refers to 'some' of those fallen asuras. For it cannot be said that all fallen asuras are without roots, as even those with two or three roots exist among them. And thus, it is stated in the commentaries that some of them—like Piyaṅkaramātā, Uttaramātā, Dhammagutta, and Phussamitta—also attained the Dhamma. It should be understood that some yakkha-born beings, rakkhasa-born beings, celestial-mansion petas, and petas who subsist on offerings given by others are also included here.

Tesūti yathāvuttapaṭisandhi yuttesu puggalesu. Yasmā āyuparicchedonāma ekabhūmipariyāpannānaṃ sabbasattānaṃ asesasā dhāraṇaniyamaparimāṇavasena pavatto. Apāyānaṃ manussānaṃ bhumma devānañca tādiso niyamaparimāṇonāma natthi. Na hi sakalacakka vāḷapariyāpannā ekabhūmakā sabbanirayā ekaāyuparicchedā honti. Tiracchānādīsupi esevanayo. Tasmā vuttaṃ catunnaṃ apāyānantiādi. Catunnaṃ apāyānaṃ āpāyikapuggalānaṃ āyuppamāṇa gaṇanāya niyamo natthi, tattha yebhuyyena kammapamāṇattā. Tattha nirayesu abbudādīnaṃ dasannaṃ nirayānaṃ bhagavatā vutto āyuparicchedopi tattha tattha nibbattakena kammenevasiddhoti veditabbo. Manussānanti idaṃ jambudīpagāsīnaṃ vasena vuttanti vadanti. Te saññeva [M 0.0204] hi āyukappassa ārohaṇaṃ orohaṇañca atthi. Na itaradīpavāsīnaṃ. Tesu hi uttarakuruvāsīnaṃ niyamato vassa sahassaṃ hoti. Itaresaṃ dvinnaṃ pañcavassa satānītica vadanti. Evaṃ sante tesu dīpesu ādikappikānaṃpi soeva paricchedoti āpajjati. Jambudīpavāsīnaṃ pana samavisamācāranisandabhūtā candasūriyanakkhattādīnaṃ visamasamagatimūlikāutuāhārānaṃ sampatti vipattiyo tesaṃpi sādhāraṇāeva honti. Tasmā tesupi āyuparicchedānaṃ ārohaṇaṃ orohaṇañca natthīti navattabbaṃ. Nisandamattattā jambudīpagatiyā ekagatikā nahontīti pana vattabbaṃ. Tathā hi pāḷiyaṃ uttarakurukā manussā amamā apariggahā. Niyatāyukā avasesāyunāti vuttaṃ. Tattha avasesāyunāti asaṅkhyeyyato orohitvā niccalaṃ ṭhitena vassasahassenāti atthoti.

Herein, 'among them' (tesu) refers to beings endowed with rebirth as described. Because the determination of lifespan is established for all beings included in a single plane of existence by way of a fixed measure common to all without exception. For those in the states of deprivation, humans, and terrestrial deities, there is no such fixed measure. Indeed, not all hells belonging to a single plane, encompassed by the entire world-system, have a single, determined lifespan. The same principle applies to animals and others. Therefore, it is said, 'For the four states of deprivation,' and so on. For the beings in the four states of deprivation, there is no fixed rule for calculating the lifespan, as it is generally determined by the measure of their kamma. Among them, the fixed lifespans for the ten hells, beginning with Abbuda, stated by the Blessed One, are to be understood as established solely by the kamma that caused rebirth in each respective hell. Regarding humans, they say this is spoken with reference to those dwelling in Jambudīpa. For them alone, there is an increase and decrease in the lifespan over an aeon. This does not apply to inhabitants of other continents. For those dwelling in Uttarakuru, the lifespan is fixed at a thousand years. For the other two, it is said to be five hundred years. If this is so, it would follow that even for those at the beginning of the aeon in those continents, the same determination applies. However, for inhabitants of Jambudīpa, the successes and failures relating to climate and food—which are rooted in the irregular and regular movements of the moon, sun, and constellations, and which are the result of their righteous and unrighteous conduct—are common to them as well. Therefore, it should not be said that for them, too, there is no increase or decrease in their lifespans. However, it should be said that because it is merely a consequence of the course of Jambudīpa, they do not have a single destiny. As stated in the Pāli, the humans of Uttarakuru are without 'mine-making' and without possessions, with a fixed lifespan and a 'remaining lifespan.' Here, 'remaining lifespan' means that after descending from an incalculable duration, it remains fixed at a thousand years.

Vinipātikāsurānanti idaṃ nidassanamattaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sabbesaṃpi mahesakkhānaṃ appesakkhānañca bhummadevānaṃ vemānikapetādīnañca idha adhippetattā. Tesañhi sabbesaṃpi kammameva pamāṇanti. Cātumahārājikānaṃpanadevānanti idaṃ uparime cātumahārājike sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dibbānīti tasmiṃ devaloke siddhāni. Pañca vassasatānīti idañca yebhuyyavasena vuttanti gahetabbaṃ. Yasmā pana kassapabuddhassa sāvakabhūtā sotāpannadeva puttā ākāsaṭṭhaka vimānesu nibbattā yāva nimirājakālāpi tiṭṭhantīti jātakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttā. Tasmā kesañci ākāsaṭṭhakadevānaṃpi kammapamāṇatā siddhā hotīti veditabbaṃ. Na cettha punappunaṃ nibbatti cintetabbā. Na hi sotā pannānaṃ sattakkhattuto paraṃ kāmabhave paṭisandhināma atthi. Na ca tasmiṃ devaloke sahassakkhattuṃ nibbattamānāpi tattakaṃ kālaṃ saṃpāpuṇituṃ sakkontīti. Manussagaṇanāyāti manussānaṃ vassagaṇanāya. Manussaloke hi paññāsavassāni cātumahārājike eko dibbarattidivo hoti. Tiṃsarattidivā eko dibbamāso. Dvādasamāsā ekaṃ dibbavassaṃ. Tena dibbavassena tesaṃ pañcavassasatāni [M 0.0205] manussagaṇanāya navutivassasatasahassaṃ hotīti. Tatoti cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇato. Catuguṇanti āyupamāṇassa diguṇavuddhiyāceva dibbassa rattidivassa diguṇavuddhiyāca vasena catūhi bhāgehi guṇitaṃ vaḍḍhitanti attho. Esanayo sesesupi. Tattha āyupamāṇassa diguṇavuddhināma heṭṭhimānaṃ devānaṃ āyupamāṇato uparimānaṃ devānaṃ āyupamāṇassa diguṇavuddhi. Etena tāvatiṃsānaṃ dibbaṃ ekaṃ vassasahassaṃ. Yāmānaṃ dvevassasahassāni. Tusitānaṃ cattāri, nimmānaratīnaṃ aṭṭha. Vasavattīnaṃ dibbāni soḷasavassa sahassāni āyuppamāṇaṃ hotīti siddhaṃ hoti.

'Of the Vinipātika asuras': this should be seen as a mere illustration, for it is intended to refer here to all powerful and powerless terrestrial deities, Vemanika petas, and so on. For all of them, kamma alone is the measure. 'But of the Cātumahārājika deities': this is said with reference to the Cātumahārājika deities above. 'Divine' means accomplished in that deva-world. 'Five hundred years': this should be taken as a general statement. Since it is said in the Jātaka commentary that disciples of the Buddha Kassapa who were stream-enterers were reborn as devaputtas in mansions established in space and remained there until the time of King Nimi, it should be understood that for some of these space-dwelling deities too, their lifespan is determined by kamma. Here, one should not consider repeated rebirth, for there is no rebirth-linking in the sense-desire realm for stream-enterers beyond a seventh time. Nor could they, even by being reborn a thousand times in that deva-world, attain such a long duration. 'By human reckoning' means by the count of human years. For in the human world, fifty years is one divine day and night for the Cātumahārājikas. Thirty such days and nights are one divine month. Twelve such months are one divine year. By that divine year count, their five hundred years become nine million years by human reckoning. 'From that' means from the lifespan of the Cātumahārājika deities. 'Fourfold' means multiplied or increased by four parts, by way of the doubling of the lifespan and the doubling of the divine day and night. This is the principle in the remaining cases as well. Here, the doubling of the lifespan means that the lifespan of the deities above is double the lifespan of the deities below. By this, it is established that the lifespan of the Tāvatiṃsa deities is one thousand divine years; of the Yāma deities, two thousand divine years; of the Tusita deities, four thousand; of the Nimmānaratī deities, eight thousand; and of the Paranimmitavasavattī deities, sixteen thousand divine years.

Dibbassa rattidivassa diguṇavuddhināma heṭṭhimānaṃ devānaṃ rattidivato uparimānaṃ rattidivassa diguṇavuddhi. Etena manussaloke ekaṃ vassasataṃ tāvatiṃse eko dibbarattidivo. Dvevassasatāni yāme. Cattāri tusite. Aṭṭha nimmānaratiyaṃ. Sahassaṃ cha cavassasatāni vasavattiyaṃ eko dibbarattidivoti siddhaṃ hoti. Rattidivānañca diguṇavuddhiyā siddhāya māsasaṃvaccharānaṃpi diguṇavuddhi siddhāva hotīti. Evañcasati yathāvuttāni tāvatiṃsādīnaṃ dibbavassasahassādinipi attano attano rattidivamāsasaṃvaccharetieva veditabbānīti siddhaṃ hoti. Tathāca sati uparimānaṃ āyuparimāṇāni heṭṭhimānaṃ āyuparimāṇato catuguṇānīti siddhaṃ hoti. Tena vuttaṃ. Tato catuguṇaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ. Tato catuguṇaṃ yāmānantiādi. Dibbagaṇanāya ca tathā siddhāya sati manussagaṇanāyapi catuguṇabhāvo siddhoyeva hoti. Tasmā manussagaṇanāyapi heṭṭhimānaṃ navutivassasatasahassādīni catūhi uparūpariguṇitāni uparimānaṃ tikoṭisaṭṭhivassasata sahassādini bhavantīti katvā tāni sabbānipi ādiantadassana vasena niddisanto navasatanti gāthamāha. Vassānaṃ navasataṃ koṭiyo ca ekavīsa koṭiyo ca tathāsaṭṭhivassa satasahassāni ca vasavattīsu devesu āyuppamāṇaṃ hotīti yojanā.

The doubling of the divine day and night means that the divine day and night of the deities in a higher realm is double that of the deities in the realm below. By this, it is established that in the human world, one hundred years are one divine day and night in the Tāvatiṃsa realm; two hundred years in the Yāma realm; four hundred in the Tusita realm; eight hundred in the Nimmānaratī realm; and one thousand six hundred years in the Paranimmitavasavattī realm is one divine day and night. With the doubling of days and nights established, the doubling of months and years is also established. This being so, it is established that the aforementioned divine years—thousands and so on—of the Tāvatiṃsa and other realms should be understood according to their own respective days, months, and years. And that being so, it is established that the lifespans of the higher realms are four times those of the lower realms. Hence it is said: 'Four times that for the Tāvatiṃsa, four times that for the Yāma,' and so on. With the divine reckoning thus established, the fourfold nature is also established in human reckoning. Therefore, in human reckoning, the lifespans of the lower realms—nine million years and so on—when multiplied by four for each successively higher realm, become the lifespans of the upper realms—thirty-six million years, and so on. Indicating all of them by showing the first and the last, he states the verse: 'Nine hundred and twenty-one koṭis and sixty hundred-thousands of years is the measure of the lifespan among the Vasavattī devas.' This is the construction.

Yasmā [M 0.0206] avitakkavicāramattaṃ jhānaṃ oḷārikassa vitakkassa samatikkamā pathamajjhānato suṭṭhubalavaṃ hoti. Tatoyeva tatīyajjhānatopi nātidubbalañca hoti. Tasmā taṃ tatīyajjhānena ekato hutvā samatale bhūmantare vipākaṃ detīti vuttaṃ dutīyajjhānavipākaṃ tatiyajjhānavipākañca dutīyajjhānabhūmiyanti. Tenevaca bhūmīnaṃ ṭhitikkamopi catutthajjhāna vaseneva siddho. Therena pana heṭṭhā pañcakanayavaseneva jhānāni vuttāni. Tasmā idhapi teneva nayena vipākāni gahetvā catutthajjhānavipākaṃ tatīyajjhānabhūmiyantiādi vuttaṃ. Tesūti tāhi chahi paṭisandhīti gahitapaṭisandhikesu. Kappassāti idaṃ asaṅkhyeyyakappaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Catubbidhā hi kappāmahākappo asaṅkhyeyyakappo antarakappo āyukappoti, tattha āyukapponāma tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ taṃtaṃ āyuparicchedo vuccati. Antarakapponāma ekassavivaṭṭaṭṭhāyiasaṅkhyeyyassa abbhantare manussānaṃ āyukappassa hāyanavaḍḍhanavasena dissamānantarā catusaṭṭhipabhedā cūḷakappā vuccanti. Pīsatibhedāti keci. Asītibhedāti apare. Cuddasappa bhedāti vedavidu. Ye loke manvantarakappāti vuccanti. Ekamekena manunāmakena mahāsammatarājena upalakkhitā antarakappāti vuttaṃ hoti. Keci pana ekasmiṃ vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyimhi mahāsammatarā jānaṃ ekameva icchanti. Catusaṭṭhiantarakappā pana eko asaṅkhye kapponāma. So catubbidho saṃvaṭṭo saṃvaṭṭaṭṭhāyī vivaṭṭo vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyīti. Tattha vinassamāno kappo saṃvaṭṭo. Yathā vinaṭṭhaṃ tiṭṭhamāno kappo saṃvaṭṭaṭṭhāyī. Vaḍḍhamāno kappo vivaṭṭo. Yathā vivaṭṭaṃ tiṭṭhamāno kappo vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyīti veditabbo. Te pana cattāro asaṅkhyeyyakappā eko mahākapponāma. Etthaca yo janāyāmavitthāre setasāsaparāsimhi vassasata vassasataccayena ekekabījaharaṇena parikkhīṇepi eko mahākappo parikkhayaṃ nagacchati. Evaṃ digho mahākappoti veditabbo.

Because the jhāna that is only without initial thought and sustained thought is much stronger than the first jhāna due to the overcoming of the coarser initial thought. For that very reason, it is not too weak compared to the third jhāna. Therefore, it is said that it, together with the third jhāna, gives a result on the same plane; thus, the result of the second jhāna and the result of the third jhāna are on the plane of the second jhāna. And indeed, the order of the duration of the planes is established only by means of the fourth jhāna. However, the Elder has previously explained the jhānas according to the fivefold method. Therefore, here too, having taken the results in the same way, it is said that the result of the fourth jhāna is on the plane of the third jhāna, and so on. 'Among these' refers to those who have taken rebirth through these six kinds of rebirth-linking. 'Of an eon' refers here to an incalculable eon. There are four kinds of eons: the great eon, the incalculable eon, the intermediate eon, and the lifespan eon. Among these, the lifespan eon is called the limit of the life of those particular beings. The intermediate eon is the name for the sixty-four kinds of minor eons that appear as fluctuations in the lifespan of humans within one incalculable eon of expansion-duration, due to decrease and increase. Some say thirty divisions. Others say eighty divisions. Those who know the Vedas say fourteen divisions. These are called Manvantara eons in the world. It is said that the intermediate eons are marked by a great king named Manu. Some, however, hold that there is only one Mahāsammata king in one eon of expansion-duration. Sixty-four intermediate eons are called one incalculable eon. That is of four kinds: contraction, the duration of contraction, expansion, and the duration of expansion. Therein, the eon that is being destroyed is contraction. The eon that is standing as destroyed is the duration of contraction. The eon that is expanding is expansion. The eon that is standing as expanded is the duration of expansion. These four incalculable eons are called one great eon. Herein, even if a heap of white mustard seeds, spread over a length and width of one yojana, were exhausted by removing one seed every hundred years, a great eon would not come to an end. Thus, a great eon is to be understood as exceedingly long.

Tattha yadā kappo tejena saṃvaṭṭati. Ābhassarato heṭṭhā agginā dayhati. Yadā āpena saṃvaṭṭati. Subhākiṇṇato heṭṭhā udakena [M 0.0207] vilīyati. Yadā vāyunā saṃvaṭṭati. Vehapphalato heṭṭhā vātena viddhaṃsatīti evaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā ayaṃ loko nirantaraṃ sattasu vāresu agginā vinassati. Aṭṭhame vāre udakena vinassati. Puna sattasu agginā. Aṭṭhame udakenāti evaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ aṭṭhakānaṃ vasena catusaṭṭhivāresu antime udakavāre udakaṃ pahāya vātavāro hotīti ayamattho siddho hoti. Kathaṃ. Yaṃ vuttaṃ ābhassarānaṃ aṭṭhakappānīti. Etena aṭṭhame vāre āposaṃvaṭṭo hoti. Antarā sattasu sattasu vāresu tejosaṃvaṭṭā hontīti siddhaṃ. Yañca vuttaṃ subhākiṇṇānaṃ catusaṭṭhikappānīti. Etena catusaṭṭhime catusaṭṭhime vāre vātasaṃvaṭṭohoti. Antarā tesaṭṭhiyā vāresu tejosaṃvaṭṭā āposaṃvaṭṭāca hontīti siddhaṃ hotīti. Tenāhu porāṇā –

Therein, when the eon contracts by fire, what is below the Ābhassara realm is burnt by fire. When it contracts by water, what is below the Subhakiṇṇa realm dissolves in water. When it contracts by wind, what is below the Vehapphala realm is scattered by the wind. Thus, as stated in the commentary, this world is continuously destroyed seven times by fire. On the eighth occasion, it is destroyed by water. Again, seven times by fire, and on the eighth by water. In this way, by means of eight sets of eight, on the sixty-fourth turn, the final water-turn is omitted and a turn of wind occurs—this meaning is established. How so? It was said that the lifespan of the Ābhassara beings is eight eons. By this, it is established that on the eighth occasion there is a contraction by water, and that in between, on seven occasions each, there are contractions by fire. And it was said that the lifespan of the Subhakiṇṇa beings is sixty-four eons. By this, it is established that on the sixty-fourth occasion there is a contraction by wind, and that in between, on the sixty-three occasions, there are contractions by fire and water. Therefore, the ancients have said:

Agginā bhassarā heṭṭhā, āpena subhākiṇṇato;

Vehapphalato vātena, evaṃ loko vinassati.

By fire, what is below the Ābhassaras; by water, from the Subhakiṇṇas; by wind, from the Vehapphalas; thus the world is destroyed.

Sattasattagginā vārā, aṭṭhame aṭṭhame dakā;

Catusaṭṭhi yadā puṇṇā, eko vāyuvāro siyāti.

Seven turns are by fire; on each eighth turn, by water; when sixty-four are complete, there will be one turn of wind.

Evañca vinaṭṭhe loke ekasmiṃ kappepi pathamajjhānabhūmi avinaṭṭhānāma natthi. Tasmā brahmapārisajjānaṃdevānaṃ kappassatatīyo bhāgo āyuppamāṇaṃ, brahmapurohitānaṃupaḍḍhakappo, mahā brahmānaṃekokappoti ettha asaṅkhyeyya kappova sambhavati. Namahākappo. Tena vuttaṃ kappassāti idaṃ asaṅkhyeyyakappaṃ sandhāya vuttanti. Āyukappaṃ sandhāya vuttantipi yujjatiyeva. Tejosaṃvaṭṭakappesu hi pathamajjhānatalaṃ vivaṭṭamānaṃ sabbapathamaṃ vivaṭṭati. Saṃvaṭṭamānaṃ sabbapacchā saṃvaṭṭati. Tasmā vivaṭṭassa pacchimaḍḍhena saṃvaṭṭassaca pubbaḍḍhena saha ekaṃ vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyikappaṃ gahetvā dve asaṅkhyeyyāni tasmiṃ tale eko āyukappoti sakkā vattunti. Dutīya talato paṭṭhāya pana mahākappova gahetabbo. Appakaṃ ūnakaṃvā adhikaṃvā gaṇanūpagaṃ na hotīti katvā upaḍḍhehi [M 0.0208] saha sattakappāni sandhāya ābhassarānaṃ aṭṭhakappānīti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ catusaṭṭhikappānīti etthapīti. Ākāsānañcāyatanabhavaṃ upagacchantīti ākāsānañcāyatanupagā, tesaṃ. Ekova visayo ārammaṇaṃ yassa taṃ ekavisayaṃ. Ekajātiyanti ekasmiṃ bhave. [Paṭisandhicatukkaṃ.]

And thus, when the world is destroyed, in any given eon, there is no such thing as a first jhāna plane that remains undestroyed. Therefore, for the devas of Brahmā's Retinue, a third of an eon is their lifespan; for Brahmā's Ministers, half an eon; and for the Great Brahmās, a full eon. Here, only an incalculable eon is possible, not a great eon. Hence, it is said, 'of an eon'—this refers to an incalculable eon. It is also appropriate to say it refers to a lifespan eon. For in the eons of contraction by fire, the plane of the first jhāna is the very first to re-evolve and the very last to devolve. Therefore, by taking one eon of expansion-duration along with the latter half of the expansion eon and the first half of the contraction eon, it can be said that in that plane two incalculable eons constitute one lifespan eon. From the second plane onward, however, a great eon should be taken. Since a small amount, whether less or more, is not suitable for calculation, it is said that the Ābhassara gods have 'eight eons,' referring to seven eons together with halves. Similarly, this applies to 'sixty-four eons.' 'Those who attain the existence of the base of infinite space' are the 'ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā'; of them. That which has a single sphere as its object is 'ekavisayaṃ'. 'In one birth' means in one existence. [The Quaternary of Rebirth-linking.]

145. Janetīti janakaṃ upatthambhetīti upatthambhakaṃ. Upapīḷetīti upapīḷakaṃ. Upaghātetīti upaghātakaṃ. Tattha janakaṃ nāma paṭisandhipavattīsu vipākakkhandha kaṭattārūpānaṃ nibbattikā kusalākusalacetanā. Tattha paṭisandhinibbattikā kammapathapattāva daṭṭhabbā. Pavattinibbattikā pana kammapathaṃ pattāpi apattāpi antamaso pañcadvārikajavanacetanāpi supinante kusalākusalacetanāpīti. Upatthambhakaṃnāma vipaccituṃ aladdhokāsāvā vipakkavipākā vā sabbāpi kusalākusalacetanā. Sā hi janakabhūtāpi samānā attanovipākavārato purevā pacchāvā sabhāṅgaṃ kammanta raṃvākammanibbattakkhandhasantānaṃvāupatthambhamānā pavattati. Yathā ganthārabbhe ratanattayapaṇāmacetanāti. Yaṃ pana visuddhimagge upatthambhakaṃ pana vipākaṃ janetuṃ nasakkotīti vuttaṃ. Taṃ aladdhavipākavāraṃ sandhāya vuttanti gahetabbaṃ. Na hi paccayasāmaggiyaṃ sati kiñcikammaṃ pavattivipākamattassapi ajanakaṃnāma atthīti. Tattha kammantarassa upatthambhanaṃnāma aladdhokāsassa aññassa janakakammassa okāsakaraṇaṃ. Taṃ pana maraṇāsannakāle pākaṭaṃ. Tadā hi kusale javite aññaṃ paṭisandhijanakaṃ kusalakammaṃ okāsaṃ labhati. Akusale javite aññaṃ akusalakammanti. Vuttañhetaṃ iti vuttake –

145. 'It generates,' thus it is 'generative.' 'It supports,' thus it is 'supportive.' 'It oppresses,' thus it is 'oppressive.' 'It destroys,' thus it is 'destructive.' Herein, 'generative' refers to the wholesome and unwholesome volitions that produce the resultant aggregates and kamma-born materiality during rebirth-linking and in the course of existence. Among these, the volition that produces rebirth-linking should be understood as having reached a course of action. However, the volition that produces results in the course of existence may or may not have reached a course of action; even the wholesome or unwholesome volition in a five-door cognitive process or in a dream is included. 'Supportive' refers to any wholesome or unwholesome volition that has not had an opportunity to ripen or whose result has already ripened. For even while being generative, it functions by supporting another kamma of its own kind or the continuity of aggregates produced by kamma, either before or after its own result is due. An example is the volition of paying homage to the Triple Gem at the beginning of a book. As for what is said in the Visuddhimagga, 'supportive kamma cannot produce a result,' that should be understood as referring to a kamma whose turn to give a result has not come. For when the necessary conditions are present, there is no kamma whatsoever that does not produce at least a result in the course of existence. Here, the 'supporting' of another kamma means creating an opportunity for another generative kamma that has not yet had its chance. This becomes evident at the time near death. For then, if a wholesome javana arises, another wholesome kamma capable of producing rebirth-linking obtains the opportunity. If an unwholesome javana arises, another unwholesome kamma does so. This is stated in the Itivuttaka:

Imasmiṃ cāyaṃ samaye, kālaṅkariyātha puggalo;

Saggamhi upapajjeyya, cittañhissa pasāditaṃ.

And should a person pass away at this time, he would be reborn in heaven, for his mind was serene.

Imasmiṃ cāyaṃ samaye, kālaṅkariyātha puggalo;

Niraye upapajjeyya, cittañhissa padūsitanti.

And should a person pass away at this time, he would be reborn in hell, for his mind was corrupted.

Pavattikālepi etaṃ bahulaṃ labbhatiyeva. Kammanibbattakhandhasantānassa upatthambhanaṃnāma aññena laddhokāsena kusalakammenavā akusalakammenavā [M 0.0209] nibbattassa khandhasantānassa jīvitantarāye apanetvā jīvitaparikkhāre samudānetvā ciratara pavattikaraṇaṃ. Yathāha –

Even during the course of existence, this is often obtained. Supporting the kamma-produced stream of aggregates means to prolong the existence of a stream of aggregates—which was produced by some other wholesome or unwholesome kamma that has obtained an opportunity—by removing dangers to its life and providing the requisites for life. As it is said:

Abhivādanasīlissa, niccaṃ vuddhāpacāyino;

Cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti, āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṃ balanti.

For one of respectful nature, who constantly honors the aged,

Four things increase: life, beauty, happiness, and strength.

Ettha pana kusalaṃpi akusalakammanibbattassa khandhasantānassa akusalaṃpi kusalakammanibbattassa upatthambhakaṃnāma natthīti navattabbaṃ. Akusala kamma nibbattassapi hi mahiddhikānaṃ nāgasupaṇṇādīnaṃ khandhasantānassa pavattikāle pubbakataṃ kusalaṃ vuttanayena upabrūhanaṃ karotiyeva. Tathākusalakammanibbattassapi kesañci vinipātikāsurādīnaṃ khandhasantānassa pavattikāle pubbakataṃ akusalaṃ ciratarappavattiṃ karotiyevāti. Upapīḷakaupaghātakānipi vuttappakārā kusalākusala cetanāyoeva. Tāpi hi janakabhūtāpi samānā attano vipākavārato purevā pacchā vā vipākavāra gahaṇa kālepi vā kammantaraṃvā kammanibbatta khandhasantānaṃvā dubbalataraṃ katvāvā vibādhayamānā sabbasovā upacchindamānā pavattantīti. Tattha upapīḷake tāva kammantarassa vibādhanaṃnāma aññassa janakakammassa dubbalabhāvakaraṇaṃ. Kammañhi nāma āyūhanakāle balavantaṃpi pacchā katena ujupaṭipakkhena kammantarena vibādhiyamānaṃ puna vihatasāmatthiyaṃ hoti. Uparibhūmi nibbattakaṃpi samānaṃ heṭṭhābhūmiyaṃ nibbatteti. Mahesakkhesu mahiddhikesu nibbattakaṃpi samānaṃ appesakkhesu nibbatteti. Tathā uccakulesu nibbattakaṃpi nīcakulesu. Dīghāyukesu nibbattakaṃpi appāyukesu. Mahābhogesu nibbattakaṃpi appabhogesu. Purisatta bhāvanibbattakaṃpi samānaṃ itthattabhāvaṃvā napuṃsakabhāvaṃ vā nibbatteti. Vaṇṇasampattinibbattakaṃpi dubbaṇṇabhāvaṃ. Indriyasampattinibbattakaṃpi andhaṃvā badhiraṃvā yaṃkiñci indriyavekallaṃ. Aṅgapaccaṅga sampattijanakaṃpi hatthapādādi aṅgavekallaṃ janeti. Tathā āyūhanakāle mahānirayesu nibbattakaṃpi akusalaṃ pacchākatena balavakusalena vibādhiyamānaṃ [M 0.0210] ussadesuvā petesuvā nibbatteti. Ajātasattu rājā cettha nidassanaṃ. Ussadesu nibbattakaṃpi petesuvā tiracchā nesuvāti ādisabbaṃ vattabbaṃ.

Here, it should not be said that there is no such thing as wholesome kamma supporting the stream of aggregates produced by unwholesome kamma, or unwholesome kamma supporting the stream of aggregates produced by wholesome kamma. For even in the stream of aggregates produced by unwholesome kamma of powerful nāgas, supaṇṇas, etc., previously performed wholesome kamma does strengthen them in the way described during their existence. Similarly, even in the stream of aggregates produced by wholesome kamma of certain beings in the woeful states, such as asuras, previously performed unwholesome kamma prolongs their existence. 'Oppressive' and 'destructive' kamma are just wholesome and unwholesome volitions of the types previously described. Although these are generative, they function by weakening other kamma or the stream of aggregates produced by kamma, making them feebler either before, after, or even at the time of the ripening of their results, thereby obstructing, suppressing, or even completely cutting them off. In that context, with regard to oppressive kamma, hindering another kamma means causing the weakening of another generative kamma. For even a strong kamma at the time of accumulation, if countered by a directly opposing subsequent kamma, becomes weakened, and its efficacy is destroyed. A kamma that would produce rebirth in a higher plane may instead produce rebirth in a lower plane. A kamma that would produce rebirth among very powerful beings may instead produce rebirth among those of little power. Similarly, a kamma that would produce rebirth in a high family may instead produce rebirth in a low family. A kamma that would produce long life may instead produce short life. A kamma that would produce great wealth may instead produce little wealth. A kamma that would produce the state of masculinity may instead produce the state of femininity or the state of being neuter. A kamma that would produce beauty may instead produce ugliness. A kamma that would produce healthy faculties may instead produce blindness, deafness, or any other deficiency of the faculties. A kamma that generates perfection of limbs and features may instead generate deficiency of limbs, such as hands, feet, etc. Similarly, an unwholesome kamma that would produce rebirth in the great hells, if countered by a subsequent strong wholesome kamma, may instead produce rebirth in the borderlands or among the ghosts. King Ajātasattu is an example here. A kamma that would produce rebirth in the borderlands may instead produce rebirth among the ghosts or animals, and so on for all other cases.

Upatthambhakaṃpi tabbipariyāyena veditabbameva. Tathā hi kammaṃ nāma katakāledubbalaṃpisamānaṃ pacchāsabhāgenabalavatākusalenavā akusalenavā upatthambhīyamānaṃ suṭṭhu balavaṃ hotīti. Kammanibbatta khandhasantānassa vibādhanaṃnāma aññena kammena nibbattassa sattassa gahitapaṭisandhito paṭṭhāya yadākadāci sarīre nānāantarāye uppādetvāvā ṭhānantarakhettavatthu gomahiṃsa dhana dhaññabhoga sampattīnaṃ puttadārañāti mittānañca vipattiṃ katvāvā dukkhuppatti karaṇaṃ. Duvidhañhi kammaphalaṃnāma vipākaphalaṃ nisandaphalanti. Tattha vipākaphalaṃnāma kammakārakasseva hoti. Na aññassa. Nisanda phalaṃ pana aññesaṃpi sādhāraṇameva. Dhammapade ānandaseṭṭhivatthu ettha vattabbaṃ. Cakkhādīsu pana kammajasantathisīsesu yena kammena yaṃkiñci ekaṃvā dvevā tīṇivā sabbaso bhijjanti. Cakkhupālatthe rādīnaṃ viya. Taṃ kammaṃ upaghātake saṅgahitanti yuttaṃ. Upaghā takanti pana upacchedakantica atthato ekaṃ. Tathā hi majjhimaṭṭha kathāyaṃ pathamaṃ upacchedakanāmena vatvā upaghātakantipi etasseva nāmanti vuttaṃ. Aṅguttaraṭṭhakathāyaṃ pathamaṃ upaghātakanāmena vatvā upacchedakantipi tassevetaṃ nāmanti vuttaṃ. Visuddhi maggepi maraṇassatiniddese tadeva kammupacchedakakammanti vuttaṃ. Idhaca parato upacchedakakammunāti vakkhati.

The supportive kamma should also be understood in the opposite way. For an action, even if weak when performed, becomes very strong when later supported by a strong wholesome or unwholesome kamma of a similar nature. The hindering of the kamma-produced stream of aggregates is the causing of suffering for a being produced by some other kamma; this occurs from the moment of rebirth-linking onwards by occasionally producing various dangers in the body, or by causing the loss of position, field, property, cattle, buffaloes, wealth, grain, possessions, wife, children, relatives, and friends. There are two kinds of kamma-results: the resultant fruit and the outflow fruit. Among these, the resultant fruit belongs solely to the doer of the kamma, not to others. The outflow fruit, however, is common to others as well. The story of Ānanda the merchant in the Dhammapada should be cited here. Regarding the eye and other sense faculties produced by kamma, if any one, two, three, or all of them are destroyed due to a particular kamma—as in the case of the Elder Cakkhupāla and others—that kamma is rightly called 'destructive kamma'. 'Destructive' and 'cutting off' are the same in meaning. For instance, in the Majjhima Commentary, it is first called 'cutting off' and then stated that 'destructive' is another name for the same. In the Aṅguttara Commentary, it is first called 'destructive' and then stated that 'cutting off' is another name for it. In the Visuddhimagga, in the section on mindfulness of death, that same kamma is called 'kamma that cuts off kamma'. And here, later, it will be spoken of as 'cutting-off kamma'.

Imassapi kammantarupacchedanaṃ maraṇāsannakāle pākaṭaṃ. Tadāhi pathamaṃ pāpakammabalena duggatinimitte upaṭṭhahante puna kalyāṇa kammaṃ taṃ paṭibāhitvā sugatinimittaṃ dassetvā sagge nibbatteti. Kalyāṇakammabalena sugatinimitte upaṭṭhahante puna pāpakammaṃ taṃ paṭibāhitvā duggatinimittaṃ dassetvā apāye nibbatteti. Duṭṭha gāmaṇirañño soṇattherapituca vatthūni kathetabbāni. Aṅguttaraṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana kusalākusalakammakkhaya karassa maggakammassapi kammantarupacchedakahā [M 0.0211] vuttā. Aṅgulimālattherādīnaṃ viyāti. Imasmiṃ bhave laddhāni mahaggatakammāni yena akusalena parihāyanti. Tassapi kammantarupacchedake saṅgaho yutto. Devadattassa viyāti. Kammanibbattakhandhasantānupacchedanaṃ pana tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhave āyu kammesu vijjamānesu laddhokāsassa kassaci aparādhakammassa balena kalalakālato paṭṭhāya antarāva kenacirogenavā bhayenavā upakkamenavā marantānaṃ vasena veditabbaṃ.

The cutting off of another kamma by this one becomes evident at the time of death. For then, first, when signs of a bad destination appear due to the power of unwholesome kamma, a wholesome kamma, having obstructed that, shows signs of a good destination and brings about rebirth in heaven. Conversely, when signs of a good destination appear due to the power of wholesome kamma, an unwholesome kamma, having obstructed that, shows signs of a bad destination and brings about rebirth in the lower realms. Here, the stories of King Duṭṭhagāmaṇī and the father of Elder Soṇa should be recounted. In the Aṅguttara Commentary, it is said that even the path-kamma, which destroys wholesome and unwholesome kammas, has the quality of cutting off other kamma, as in the cases of Elder Aṅgulimāla and others. The decline of great attainments obtained in this existence due to some unwholesome act is also appropriately included under 'cutting off other kamma', as in the case of Devadatta. The cutting off of the kamma-produced continuum of aggregates, however, should be understood as occurring in the case of those who die prematurely—whether due to some illness, fear, or violence—even when the life-sustaining kamma is still present in a given existence, from the moment of the kalala stage onward, due to the power of some other kamma that has obtained an opportunity.

Etthaca kammantarassavā kammanibbattakhandhasantānassavā upatthambhanā dīni sandhāya imesaṃ catunnaṃpi kammānaṃ kusalākusalabhāvo visuddhimagge aṅguttaraṭṭhakathāyañca vutto. Majjhimaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana saṃvaṇṇetabbasuttānurūpaṃ kammanibbattakhandhasantānasseva upatthambhanādīni sandhāya upatthambhakassa kusalabhāvo upapīḷakaupaghātakānaṃ akusalabhāvo vutto. So pana majjhimaṭīkāyaṃ aṅguttaraṭīkāyañca aruccamāno viya vutto. Mahāṭīkāyaṃ pana so keci vādopi kato. Tatthapana saṃvaṇṇetabbasuttānurūpaṃ vuttattā visuṃ pāḷinayoti daṭṭhabbo. Na ca kecivādo kattabbo. Suttasmiṃhi appāyukasaṃvattanikāesā māṇavapaṭipadā, yadidaṃ pāṇātipātī hotītiādinā upaghātakaṃ pāṇātipātavaseneva vuttaṃ. Upapīḷakañca batvābādhasaṃvattanikā esā māṇava paṭipadā, yadidaṃ sattānaṃ viheṭhakajātiko hotītiādinā vihiṃsādīnaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Upatthambhakañca dīghāyukasaṃvattanikā esā māṇava paṭipadā. Yadidaṃ pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hotītiādinā pāṇātipātaviratiādīnaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Sabbañcetaṃ manussattaṃ āgatasseva sattassa vasenāti evaṃ visuṃ pāḷinayo veditabboti. Mahāṭīkāyaṃ pana aṅguttaraṭīkāyañca kammantarupatthambhanādīni anicchantehi janakādibhāvonāma vipākaṃ paṭiicchitabbo. Nakammanti vipākasseva upaghātakatā yuttā viya dissatīti vuttaṃ.

Here, referring to supporting and so on, the wholesome and unwholesome nature of these four kinds of kamma—whether of another kamma or of the kamma-produced continuum of aggregates—is stated in the Visuddhimagga and the Aṅguttara Commentary. In the Majjhima Commentary, however, in accordance with the Cūḷakammavibhaṅga Sutta, referring to supporting and so on only in relation to the kamma-produced continuum of aggregates, it is stated that supporting kamma is wholesome, while oppressive and destructive kammas are unwholesome. Yet, this explanation appears as if not approved of in the Majjhima Subcommentary and the Aṅguttara Subcommentary. In the Great Subcommentary, however, this has been put forward as a 'view of some.' But there, since it is stated in accordance with the Cūḷakammavibhaṅga Sutta, it should be regarded as a distinct Pāli method. And it should not be made into a 'view of some.' For in the Sutta, the destructive (upaghātaka) aspect, which leads to a short life, is explained through the act of killing, as in 'this practice of a person, young man, leads to a short life, namely, that one is a killer of living beings.' The oppressive (upapīḷaka) aspect, which leads to much sickness, is explained through the nature of harming beings, as in 'this practice of a person, young man, leads to much sickness, namely, that one is of a nature to harm beings,' referring to violence and similar acts. The supporting (upatthambaka) aspect, which leads to a long life, is explained through abstaining from killing, as in 'this practice of a person, young man, leads to a long life, namely, having abandoned the killing of living beings, one refrains from killing,' referring to abstention from killing and similar virtues. All this pertains to a being who has attained human existence. Thus, the distinct Pāli method should be understood in this way. However, in the Great Subcommentary and the Aṅguttara Subcommentary, it is stated that those who do not accept the supporting and so on of another kamma must accept that the nature of being generative and so on pertains to the result. It is said that it is not kamma, but the destructiveness of the result itself that seems appropriate.

Kiccavasenāti jananaṃ upatthambhanaṃ upapīḷanaṃ upacchindananti catunnaṃ kiccānaṃ vasena. Tattha ekā pāṇātipātacetanā cattāri kiccāni [M 0.0212] sādheti. Sā hi yāva vipaccituṃ okāsaṃ nalabhati. Tāva upatthambhanādīsu tīsu kiccesu yaṃkiñci laddhapaccayaṃ kiccaṃ karoti. Yadā vipaccituṃ okāsaṃ labhati. Tadā ekāya cetanāya ekāeva paṭisandhi hotīti evaṃ sāketapañhe vuttanayena ekaṃ apāyabhavaṃ janeti. Tato paraṃ pana paṭisandhijananakiccaṃ natthi. Pavatti vipākajananena saha itarāni tīṇi kiccāni bhavasatasahassepi kappasatasahassepi sādhetiyeva. Dhammadinnāyanāma uggasena rañño deviyā vatthu ettha vattabbaṃ. Sā pana yadā attano vipākavārato pure ariyabhūtassavā puthujjanabhūtassapi kalyāṇa cittasamaṅginovā upacchedanaṃ karoti. Tadā upacchinditvā kammanta rasseva okāsaṃ karoti. Sayaṃ vipākaṃ najaneti. Yadā pana pāpacittasamaṅgino khandhasantānaṃ upacchindati. Tadāeva upacchinditvā attano vipākaṃ janeti. Sakiṃ laddhapaṭisandhivārato pana paṭṭhāya anekesu attabhāva satasahassesupi upacchedanādīniyeva karoti. Ettha mahāmoggalāna tthera vatthu sāmāvati vatthu vaggumudātīriyabhikkhu vatthu dussimāra kalāburājavatthūni kathetabbāni. Yasmā pana idaṃ upacchedakakammaṃ nāma tiracchānagatānaṃ bahulaṃ labbhati. Tasmā suṭṭhu balavaṃ akusalakammaṃ dubbalassa akusalakammassavā akusalakammanibbattakhandhasantānassavā upacchedakaṃnāma na hotīti na vattabbaṃ. Teneva hi majjhimaṭṭhakathāyaṃ bahukasmiñhi akusalakamme āyūhite balavakammaṃ dubbala kammassa vipākaṃ paṭibāhitvā attano vipākassa okāsaṃ karotīti vuttaṃ.

By way of function means by way of the four functions: generating, supporting, oppressing, and cutting off. Therein, a single volition of killing accomplishes four functions. For as long as it does not get an opportunity to ripen, it performs whatever function among the three—supporting and so on—has found a condition. When it gets an opportunity to ripen, then, in accordance with the method stated in the Sāketa-pañha, 'by one volition, there is only one rebirth-linking,' it generates one existence in a plane of misery. Thereafter, however, there is no function of generating rebirth-linking. But, along with generating results in the course of life, it still accomplishes the other three functions even in a hundred thousand existences, a hundred thousand eons. Here, the story of Dhammadinnā, the queen of King Uggasena, should be told. When that [volition], before its own turn for a result, performs the cutting off of one who is a noble one or an ordinary person endowed with a wholesome mind, then, having cut off, it creates an opportunity for another kamma only; it does not itself generate a result. But when it cuts off the continuum of aggregates of one with an unwholesome mind, then, having cut off, it generates its own result. And from the time it has once had its turn for rebirth-linking, it performs only cutting off and so on in many hundreds of thousands of individual existences. Here, the stories of the Elder Mahāmoggallāna, Sāmāvatī, the monks of the Vaggumudā river, and King Kalābu of Dussīla should be related. However, since this cutting-off kamma is found frequently among those born as animals, it should not be said that a very strong unwholesome kamma is not a cutting-off kamma for a weak unwholesome kamma or for the kamma-produced continuum of aggregates. For this very reason, it is said in the Majjhima Commentary: 'When much unwholesome kamma has been accumulated, a strong kamma, having obstructed the result of a weak kamma, creates an opportunity for its own result.'

Apica pavattiyaṃpi kammantarajanitaṃ bhavaṅgasantānaṃ anupacchinditvā pañcasu cakkhu sota ghāna jivhā bhāva dasaka saṅkhātesu santati sīsesu aññatarassa santatisīsassa sabbaso upacchindanaṃpi imasseva kiccanti yuttaṃ. Yaṃ pana mahāṭīkāyaṃ aṅguttaraṭīkāyañca upapīḷikaṃ aññassa vipākaṃ chindati. Na sayaṃ attano vipākaṃ janetīti vuttaṃ. Taṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ sukhadukkhaṃ pīḷeti, addhānaṃ pavattituṃ na detīti idaṃ disvā vuttaṃ siyā. Addhānaṃ pavattituṃ nadetīti ettha pana [M 0.0213] sukhasantānaṃvā dukkhasantānaṃvā cirakālaṃ pavattituṃ nadeti iccevattho. Na pana upaghātakaṃ viya bhavaṅgasantānena saha aññassa kammassa vipākaṃ chindatīti.

Moreover, even during the course of existence, without cutting off the life-continuum generated by another kamma, the complete cutting off of any one of the series-heads among the five reckoned as the eye-decade, ear-decade, nose-decade, tongue-decade, and sex-decade—is also fittingly the function of this same kamma. However, in the Great Subcommentary and the Aṅguttara Subcommentary, it is stated: 'Oppressive kamma cuts off the result of another; it does not itself generate its own result.' That statement may have been made after seeing this in the commentary: 'It oppresses pleasure and pain, not allowing it to continue for long.' But, 'not allowing it to continue for long' here simply means not allowing the continuity of pleasure or the continuity of pain to persist for a long time. It does not, however, mean that it cuts off the result of another kamma together with the life-continuum, like destructive kamma.

[143] Yaṃpana vibhāvaniyaṃ

Now, as for what is stated in the Vibhāvanī,

“Janakaṃ kammantarassa vipākaṃ anupacchinditvāva vipākaṃ janeti. Upaghātakaṃ upacchedanapubbakanti idaṃ tāva aṭṭhakathāsu sanniṭṭhānanti vuttaṃ”. Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

'Generative kamma produces a result without cutting off the result of another kamma. Destructive kamma is preceded by cutting off'—this much is stated as established in the commentaries. This is not well-stated.

Idha pubbakatena upacchedanakakammena maritvā sagge nibbattānaṃ vatthūnaṃ aṭṭhakathāsuyeva āgatattāti.

Here, because the accounts of those who died due to a previously performed cutting-off kamma and were reborn in heaven are found in the commentaries themselves.

[144] Yañca tattha

And as for what is further stated therein,

Apare pana ācariyā vadantītiādinā upaghātakassa sayaṃ vipākanibbattakattā bhāvavacanaṃ vuttaṃ. Taṃpi na sundaraṃ.

The statement, beginning with 'But other teachers say,' that an abstract noun is used because the destructive kamma itself produces a result—that too is not well-stated.

Teneva kammena apāye nibbattānaṃ dussimāra kalāburājā dīnaṃ tassa kammassa upacchedakakammabhāvena aṭṭhakathāsu āgatattāti. [Janakacatukkaṃ]

Because it is found in the commentaries that for King Kalābu of Dussīla and others, who were reborn in the lower realms by that very kamma, that kamma was a cutting-off kamma. [The Generative Fourfold]

146. Garukanti aññena kammena paṭibāhituṃ asakkuṇeyyaṃ kusalapakkhe mahaggatakammaṃ akusalapakkhe niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā saha pañcānantariyakammaṃ. Ettha siyā. Mahaggatakammanti kasmā vuttaṃ. Tañhi pamādavasenavā nīvaraṇadhammapavattiyāvā parihāyiyamānaṃ nikantibalenavā paṭibāhiyamānaṃ vipākaṃ na detīti. Tathā ekassa bahūsu ānantariyakammesu katesu ekasmiṃ vipaccante sesāni na vipaccantīti. Vuccate, mahaggatakammaṃ tāvathapetvā pamādadhammanīvaraṇadhammanikantidhamme attano balavatarañca mahaggatakammantaraṃ aññena puññakammena appaṭibāhaniyaṭṭhena garukaṃ nāma hoti. Ānantariyakammāni pana thapetvā attano balavataraṃ ānantariyakammaṃ aññena kenaci dhammena appaṭibāhaniyaṭṭhenāti evaṃ yathārahaṃ tesaṃ garukatā veditabbāti. Āsannanti maraṇakāle [M 0.0214] anussaritaṃ tadā katañca. Tattha tadākatanti antima javanavīthito pubbabhāge āsanne kataṃ yaṃkiñci kusalākusalakammaṃ. Micchādiṭṭhikammaṃ pana vipassanādivasena pavattaṃ sammādiṭṭhikammañca antimajavanavīsiyaṃpi katanti gahetabbaṃ. Yathāha-maraṇakāle vāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhi samattā samādinnāti. Etena tato micchādiṭṭhikammato aññaṃ antimajavanavīthiyaṃ pavattaṃ kammaṃ paṭisandhiṃ janetuṃ na sakkotīti siddhaṃ hotīti. Āciṇṇanti dīgharattaṃ abhiṇhaso kataṃ. Sakiṃ karitvāpivā pacchā punappunaṃ somanassajanakaṃ santāpajanakañca. Kaṭattākammanti kāriyitthāti kammanti evaṃ katakāraṇāeva kammanti vattabbaṃ kammaṃ. Garukādibhāvena vattabbaṃ kammaṃ na hotīti attho. Tattha purimāni tīṇi imasmiṃ bhave katāni upapajjavedanīyakammānieva. Kaṭattākammaṃ pana atītabhavesu katehi aparapariyāyavedanīyehi saha imasmiṃ bhave kataṃ garukā sannāciṇṇabhāvarahitaṃ kammapathapattaṃ yaṃkiñci upapajjavedanīyakammaṃ. Mahāṭīkāyaṃ pana kaṭattākammaṃ purima jātīsu kataṃeva gahitaṃ. Taṃ aṭṭhakathāya na sameti. Etehi pana tīhi muttaṃ punappunaṃ laddhāsevanaṃ kaṭattāvā pana kammaṃnāma hotīti hi vuttaṃ. Na ca atītabhavesu katāni mātughātakādīnipi aparapariyāya kammāni etehi tīhi muttānītivā amuttānītivā punappunaṃ laddhāsevanānītivā aladdhāsevanānītivā sakkā visesetuṃ. Tadā hi tāni garuka kammasantāne pavattānipi honti. Āsannavaciṇṇakammasantāne pavattānipīti.

146. Weighty kamma is that which cannot be obstructed by any other kamma, whether it be a sublime wholesome kamma on the wholesome side, or one of the five deeds of immediate retribution together with fixed wrong view on the unwholesome side. Here, it might be asked: Why is sublime kamma mentioned? Because when it is declining through negligence or the arising of hindrances, or when it is obstructed by the power of attachment, it does not yield its result. Similarly, when one has committed many deeds of immediate retribution, if one ripens, the others do not ripen. It is said: Sublime kamma—setting aside negligence, hindrances, attachment, and another sublime kamma more powerful than itself—is called 'weighty' in the sense that it cannot be obstructed by any other meritorious kamma. As for deeds of immediate retribution, setting aside a deed of immediate retribution more powerful than itself, they cannot be obstructed by any other factor. Thus, their weightiness should be understood accordingly. Near-death kamma refers to that which is recollected at the time of death and that which is done at that time. Here, 'that which is done at that time' means any wholesome or unwholesome kamma performed in the proximate period before the final cognitive process. However, kamma of wrong view and kamma of right view arising by way of insight and so forth should be understood as performed even in the final cognitive process. As it is said: 'At the time of death, one may hold wrong view or right view, fully adopted.' By this, it is established that any other kamma arising in the final cognitive process, apart from the kamma of wrong view, cannot generate rebirth-linking. Habitual kamma refers to what is done repeatedly over a long time, or, even if done only once, what later repeatedly generates joy or remorse. 'Kamma-because-it-was-done' means kamma that should be called 'kamma' simply because it was done, as in 'it was done, therefore it is kamma.' The meaning is that it is not kamma that should be spoken of in terms of being weighty and so forth. Here, the first three are kammas performed in this existence that are to be experienced in the next existence. 'Kamma-because-it-was-done,' however, is any kamma to be experienced in the next existence that is performed in this life, is devoid of the nature of being weighty, near-death, or habitual, and has reached the path of action, together with kammas from past existences that are to be experienced in a subsequent life. In the Great Subcommentary, however, 'kamma-because-it-was-done' is taken as only that which was done in previous births. This does not accord with the Commentary. For it is said: 'Kamma that is free from these three, has been repeatedly practiced, or is simply kamma because it was done, is called kamma.' And it is not possible to distinguish whether deeds such as matricide done in past existences, which are kammas to be experienced in a subsequent life, are free from these three or not free, or whether they were repeatedly practiced or not repeatedly practiced. For at times, they may have occurred in the continuum of weighty kamma, or in the continuum of near-death or habitual kamma.

Aṅguttaraṭṭhakathāyañca etehi pana tīhi muttaṃ aññāṇavasenakataṃ kaṭattāvā pana kammaṃnāmāti vuttaṃ. Na tāni aññāṇavasena kabhānīti sakkā visesetuṃ. Tāni hi purimabhavesu aññāṇa vasena katānipi honti. Ñāṇavasena katānipīti. Tāni pana visesanāni imasmiṃ bhave katānaṃ garukādīhi tīhi muttānaṃ sattamajavana kammānaṃ vasena vuttānīti tehi saha purimajātīsu katāni aparapariyāya kammāni kaṭattā kammaṃnāmāti veditabbāni. Evañca katvā yattha taṃpubbakataṃ kammanti āgataṃ. Tatthapi imasmiṃ bhavevā [M 0.0215] atītabhavesuvā pubbakāle katanti attho veditabboti. Imesu pana catūsu kammesu vijjamānesu garukameva anantare bhave paṭisandhiṃ deti. Garuke asati āsannaṃ. Āsanne asati āciṇṇaṃ. Āciṇṇe asati kaṭattākammaṃ. Tenāha pākadānapariyāyenāti. Pākadānavārenāti attho. Ettha siyā. Kasmā idha āsannaṃ āciṇṇato pathamaṃ vuttaṃ. Nanu pāḷiyaṃ āsannato āciṇṇameva pathamaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathāha-yaṃ garukaṃ yaṃ bahulaṃ. Yadāsannaṃ. Kaṭattāvā pana kammanti. Aṭṭhakathāsuca teneva kamena pākadānavāro vihitoti. Vuccate, sabhāvato balavadubbalakkamena pāḷiyaṃ āciṇṇaṃ pathamaṃ vuttaṃ. So pana kamo kadāci pākadānapariyāyopi sambhavatīti katvā aṭṭhakathāsu teneva kamena pākadānavāro vihito. Āsannaṃpi hisamānaṃ cittaṃ tosetuṃvā santāpetuṃvā asakkontaṃ hutvā dubbalaṃ balavato āciṇṇassa nivattakaṃ na hotīti. Yasmā pana mahākammavibhaṅgasutte pubbevāssataṃ kataṃ hoti kalyāṇakammaṃ sukhavedanīyaṃ. Pacchāvāssataṃ kataṃ hoti kalyāṇakammaṃ sukhavedanīyaṃ. Maraṇakālevāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi samattā samādinnāti evaṃ āciṇṇaduccaritassapi ekaccassa āsannena kalyāṇa kammena saggagamanaṃ vuttaṃ. Tathā pubbevāssataṃ kataṃ hoti pāpakammaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ.La. Micchādiṭṭhi samattā samādinnāti evaṃ āciṇṇa sucaritassapi ekaccassa āsannena pāpakammena apāyagamanaṃ vuttaṃ. Yasmāca ubhinnaṃpi balavabhāve sati āsannameva pariyattaṃ bhavituṃ arahati. Tasmā idha therena āsannameva pathamaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etthaca pubbevāssakataṃ hotīti idaṃ āsannānussaritakammavasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tambadāṭhikanāmassa coraghātakassa mahāvātakālanāmassaca upāsakassa vatthu ettha kathetabbanti.

And in the Commentary to the Aṅguttara Nikāya, it is said: 'Kamma that is free from these three, or kamma done through ignorance, is called kamma-because-it-was-done.' It is not possible to distinguish that those deeds are done through ignorance, for in past existences, some of them were done through ignorance, and some were done with knowledge. However, those distinctions are stated with reference to the seventh moment of the cognitive process of kamma performed in this existence, which is free from the three, weighty and so forth. Therefore, along with these, kammas performed in previous births that are to be experienced in a subsequent life should be understood as 'kamma-because-it-was-done.' And so, wherever the phrase 'that previously done kamma' occurs, the meaning should be understood as 'done at an earlier time, either in this existence or in past existences.' Among these four kammas, if they are present, only weighty kamma produces rebirth in the immediately following existence. In the absence of weighty kamma, near-death kamma does. In the absence of near-death kamma, habitual kamma does. In the absence of habitual kamma, kamma-because-it-was-done does. Therefore, it is said, 'by way of the order of giving fruit.' The meaning is 'in the turn of yielding results.' Here, it might be asked: Why is near-death kamma mentioned here before habitual kamma? Is it not so that in the Pāli canon, habitual kamma is mentioned before near-death kamma? As it is said: 'That which is weighty, that which is frequent, that which is near, or kamma because it was done.' And in the Commentaries, the turn of yielding results is set forth in that very order. It is said: In the Pāli canon, habitual kamma is mentioned first according to the order of natural strength and weakness. But since that order can sometimes also be the order of giving fruit, the turn of yielding results is set forth in the Commentaries in that very order. For near-death kamma, if it is weak and unable to gladden or distress the mind, does not become an obstructor of strong habitual kamma. However, since in the Mahākammavibhaṅga Sutta it is said: 'Previously, he has done wholesome kamma to be experienced as pleasant; or later, he has done wholesome kamma to be experienced as pleasant; or at the time of death, he holds right view, fully adopted'—thus, for someone who habitually engaged in misconduct, attaining a heavenly realm is spoken of due to a near-death wholesome kamma. Similarly: 'Previously, he has done unwholesome kamma to be experienced as painful... or at the time of death, he holds wrong view, fully adopted'—thus, for someone who habitually engaged in good conduct, going to a lower realm is spoken of due to a near-death unwholesome kamma. And since, when both are strong, the near-death kamma alone is fit to be decisive, it should therefore be seen that the Elder here mentioned the near-death kamma first. And here, 'previously was done by him' should be understood as spoken with reference to kamma recollected at the time of death. The stories of the executioner named Tambadāṭhika and the lay devotee named Mahāvātakāla should be recounted here.

[145] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[145] However, a clarification:

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgataṃ jaraggavopamaṃ dassetvā āsannameva pathamaṃ vipākaṃ detīti ekaṃsena vuttaṃ. Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

Having presented the simile of the old ox found in the Commentary, it is stated categorically that the near-death kamma alone gives the first result. That is not correct.

Na [M 0.0216] hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ evaṃ ekaṃsena vuttaṃ. Naca uṭṭhātuṃpi asakkonto so jaraggavo pajadvārassa āsanne ṭhitopi pathamataraṃ nikkhamissatīti. [Garukacatukkaṃ]

For it is not stated so categorically in the Commentary. Nor can it be asserted that the old ox, unable even to rise, will emerge first even if it is standing near the pen's gate. [The Quaternad on Weighty Kamma]

147. Diṭṭhadhammo vuccati paccakkhabhūto paccuppanno attabhāvo. Veditabbaṃ anu bhavitabbanti vedanīyaṃ. Phalaṃ. Diṭṭhadhamme vedanīyaṃ phalaṃ etassāti diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ.

147. The 'presently visible phenomena' is said to be the present existence, which is directly perceived. 'To be experienced' means to be felt. It is the fruit. 'To be experienced in the presently visible phenomena' is that which has a fruit to be experienced in this very life.

[146] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[146] However, a clarification:

“Diṭṭhadhamme veditabbaṃ vipākānubhavana vasenāti diṭṭhadhammavedanīya”nti vuttaṃ. Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

It is said: '"To be experienced in the presently visible phenomena" means to be experienced in this very life by way of experiencing the result.' That is not correct.

Diṭṭheva dhamme vipākaṃ paṭisaṃvedetīti hi pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Ettha hi vipākaṃ paṭisaṃvedetīti etena idha vedanīyasaddo kammasādhano vipākātidheyyoca hotīti dasseti. Evañca sati idha aññapadatthasamāso eva labbhati. Na uttarapadatthasamāsoti. Diṭṭhadhammaṃ upecca tassa anantare pajjitvā pāpuṇitvā veditabbaṃ phalaṃ etassāti upapajjavedanīyaṃ. Teneva hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ upapajja saddassa atthaṃ vadantena upapajjitvāti vuttaṃ. Suttapadesu pana upapajjevāti pāṭho diṭṭho. Tasmā diṭṭhadhammassa samīpe anantare pajjitabbo gantabboti upapajjo. Dutīyo attabhāvo upapajjeveditabbaṃ phalaṃ etassāti upapajjavedanīyanti evamattho pāṭhassa vasena veditabbo. Upapajjātivā anantare bhave pavatto eko nipāto. Yathā paccāti.

For in the Pāli it is said: 'One experiences the result in this very life.' Here, by 'experiences the result', it is shown that the word 'vedanīya' is derived in the objective sense and also designates the result.
