Vibhāvaniyaṃ

Clarification

“Idaṃ pana nerayikānaṃ uttarakuruvāsinaṃ kesañci devānañca nahotīti” vuttaṃ.

But it is said: 'This, however, does not occur for beings in hell, for the inhabitants of Uttarakuru, or for certain devas.'

Yathā [M 0.0254] pana mahāṭīkāyaṃ kesañci petānaṃ ito ñātake hi dinnaṃ puññapatti anumoditvā taṅkhaṇeyeva cavitvā sugatiyaṃ nibbattānaṃ kusalabhūtaṃ upacchedakaṃ vuttaṃ. Tathā kesañci nerayi kānaṃpi yamarañño samanuyuñjanakālādīsu attanā katapuññaṃ anussaritvā taṅkhaṇeyeva cavitvā sugatiyaṃ nibbattānaṃ upacche dakamaraṇaṃnāma na na sakkā vattuṃ. Kesañci tāvatiṃsādīnaṃ devānañca taṃ upacchedakamaraṇaṃ hotiyeva. Tathā hi subrahmadeva putta saṃyuttaṭṭhakathāyaṃ atha rukkhaṃ abhiruḷhā upacchedakakammādi vasenaekappahāreneva kālaṅkatvā avīcimhi nibbattāti vuttaṃ. Tattha rukkhanti tāvatiṃse pāricchattakarukkhaṃ. Abhiruḷhāti āruḷhā pañca satadevaccharāyo. Manopadosika khiṭṭāpadosika devānaṃ maraṇaṃ mahābodhisattānaṃ dighāyuke devalokevā brahmalokevā nibbattānaṃ adhimutti kālaṅkiriyā channattheragodhikattherādīnaṃviya sayameva satthaṃ āharitvā parinibbāyantānaṃ maraṇañca ettheva saṅgayhatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tathācāti tehi pakārehica. Marantānaṃ channaṃ dvārānaṃ aññatarasmiṃ paccupaṭṭhātīti sambandho. Maraṇakāleti maraṇāsannakāle. Yathārahanti sugatiduggatigāmīnaṃ arahānurūpaṃ. Yepana khīṇāsavā katthaci nuppajjanti. Tesu sukkhavipassakānaṃ pakatiyā yatho paṭṭhitaṃ nāmarūpa meva antima javanānaṃ ārammaṇaṃhoti. Samāpattilābhīnaṃ pana jhānasamanantare parinibbāyantānaṃ kasiṇanimittādikaṃ. Paccavekkhanasamanantare parinibbāyantānaṃ jhānaṅgāni abhiññāsamanantare parinibbāyantānaṃ attano karajarūpaṃ. Jīvita samasīsīnaṃ pana aggamaggassa paccavekkhanasamanantare parinibbāyantānaṃ maggaṅgādini antimajavanānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hotīti. Parinibbānacuticittassa pana sabbesaṃpi ādito attano attano paṭisandhiyāyathāgahitaṃ kammādīsu aññatarameva ārammaṇaṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yepana anejosanti mārabbhayaṃ kālamakarīmunīti imaṃ suttapadaṃ disvā nibbānameva bhagavato parinibbānacutiyā ārammaṇanti vadanti. Te tena sayameva abhidhamme ārammaṇattikesu attano akovidataṃ dassenti. Yathāha –

Just as in the Great Subcommentary it is said that for some petas, having rejoiced in the transference of merit given by relatives from here, they pass away at that very moment and are reborn in a happy destination; for them, a wholesome cutting-off kamma is mentioned. Similarly, for some beings in hell, too, when they are being interrogated by King Yama, upon recollecting merit they themselves have done, they pass away at that very moment and are reborn in a happy destination; for them, it is indeed possible to speak of a 'cutting-off death.' For some devas of Tāvatiṃsa and so on, that cutting-off death does indeed occur. Thus it is said in the commentary to the Subrahmadevaputta Saṃyutta that some, having climbed a tree, died in a single instant by way of a cutting-off kamma, etc., and were reborn in the Avīci hell. Here, 'tree' means the Pāricchattaka tree in Tāvatiṃsa. 'Having climbed' refers to the five hundred celestial nymphs who had ascended it. The death of the Manopadosika and Khiḍḍāpadosika devas; the death by resolution of great bodhisattas reborn in the long-lived deva or brahma worlds; and the death of those like the Venerable Channa and the Venerable Godhika, who took up a weapon against themselves and attained parinibbāna—all these should be understood as included here. And thus, by these means, for those who are dying, an object presents itself at one of the six doors—this is the connection. 'At the time of death' means when death is near. 'According to what is fitting' means in a way that is appropriate for those heading to a good or a bad destination. But for those destroyers of the taints who are not reborn anywhere—among them, for the dry-insight meditators—mind-and-matter as it is naturally attended to is the object of the final impulsions. For those who are attainers of meditative absorptions, if they attain parinibbāna immediately after a jhāna, their object is the kasiṇa sign, etc. If they attain parinibbāna immediately after reviewing, their object is the jhāna factors. If they attain parinibbāna immediately after a direct knowledge, their object is their own physical body. For those whose life ends simultaneously with the path, if they attain parinibbāna immediately after reviewing the highest path, their object for the final impulsions is the path factors, etc. It should be understood that for the parinibbāna-demise-consciousness of all of them, the object is one of kamma, kamma-sign, or destination-sign, just as it was grasped at their respective rebirth-linkings from the beginning. As for those who, seeing the scriptural passage, 'The sage, unstirred, serene, has made an end to time, beyond Māra's fear,' say that Nibbāna itself was the object of the Blessed One's parinibbāna-demise-consciousness, they thereby reveal their own lack of expertise in the triads on objects in the Abhidhamma. As it is said:

Katame [M 0.0255] dhammā parittārammaṇā, sabbo kāmāvacaravipāko kriyamanodhātu kriyāhetuka manoviññāṇa dhātu somanassasahagatā. Ime dhammā parittārammaṇāti.

Which states have limited objects? All sense-sphere resultant consciousness; the functional mind-element; the functional, rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy. These states have limited objects.

Yasmā pana parinibbānaṃnāma santi atthāyeva hoti. Ajjhāsayo cassa ekantena santininnoyeva hoti. Tasmā anejosanti mārabbhāti suttapadaṃ vuttaṃ. Tathā hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ santimārabbhāti anupādisesaṃ nibbānaṃ ārabbha paṭicca sandhāyāti vuttaṃ. Na pana vuttaṃ ārabbha ālambitvā ārammaṇaṃ katvāti. Theragāthaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana santimārabbhāti santiṃ anupādisesaṃ nibbānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvāti vuttaṃ. Taṃ mahāparinibbānapāḷiyā tadaṭṭhakathāyaca nasameti. Tāsu hi bhagavato parinibbānaṃ jhānaṅga paccavekkhanasamanantaranti vuttaṃ. Etthaca purimāni dve samanantarāni parinibbānasuttaṭṭhakathāsu vuttāni. Abhiññāsamanantaraṃ udānaṭṭhakathādisu āgataṃ. Yathāha-vuṭṭhahitvā parinibbāyīti iddhicittato vuṭṭhahitvā bhavaṅgacittena parinibbāyīti. Aggamaggassa paccavekkhanasamanantaraṃ puggalapaññattiṭṭhakathādīsu āgataṃ. Yathāha-ekūnavīsati me paccavekkhanaññāṇe patiṭṭhāya bhavaṅgaṃ otaritvā parinibbāyatīti. Saṃyuttaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana arahattamaggānantaraṃ phalaṃ. Phalānantaraṃ bhavaṅgato vuṭṭhāya paccavekkhanaṃ. Taṃ pana paripuṇṇaṃvā hoti aparipuṇṇaṃvā. Tikhiṇena asinā sīse chijjamānepi ekaṃvā dvevā paccavekkhanāni uppajjantiyevāti vuttaṃ.

However, because parinibbāna is indeed for the sake of peace, and his inclination is solely toward peace, the sutta phrase `anejosantimārabbha` was spoken. Thus, in the commentary, `santimārabbha` is explained as 'with reference to, in connection with, concerning Nibbāna without residue.' But it was not said as `ārabbha` in the sense of 'having taken as a cognitive object' (`ālambitvā`) or 'having made it an object' (`ārammaṇaṃ katvā`). In the Theragāthā commentary, however, `santimārabbha` is explained as 'having made peace, Nibbāna without residue, an object.' This, however, does not accord with the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta and its commentary. For in those, the Blessed One's parinibbāna is said to have occurred 'immediately after reviewing the jhāna factors.' And here, the former two 'immediately after' cases are mentioned in the commentaries on the Parinibbāna Sutta. The 'immediately after a direct knowledge' case is found in the Udāna commentary and others. As it says: 'Having arisen, he attained parinibbāna' means 'having arisen from the mind of psychic power, he attained parinibbāna with the life-continuum consciousness.' The 'immediately after reviewing the supreme path' case is found in the Puggalapaññatti commentary and others. As it says: 'Having established in the nineteen reviewing knowledges, descending into the life-continuum, he attains parinibbāna.' In the Saṃyutta commentary, however, it is said that immediately after the Arahant path comes the fruition; after the fruition, one arises from the life-continuum for review. This review may be complete or incomplete. Even if one's head is being cut off with a sharp sword, one or two reviewing moments still arise.

[164] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

In the Vibhāvanī, however,

Evaṃ vavatthānaṃ akatvā yaṃ vuttaṃ. “Katthaci pana anuppajjamānassa khīṇāsavassa yathopaṭṭhitaṃ nāmarūpadhammādikameva cutipariyosānānaṃ gocarabhāvaṃ gacchati. Na kamma kammani mittādayoti.” Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

Without making such a determination, what was said is: ‘But for a taint-destroyed one who is not reborn anywhere, merely the mind-and-matter phenomena, etc., that are present become the object up to the final demise, not kamma, kamma-sign, etc.’ That is not well stated.

Na hi tassa cuticittaṃ kammakammanimittādayo ārammaṇaṃ nakaroti. Naca cutiyā gahitāni kammādīnināma sabbasattānaṃpi bhavantarassa atthāya bhavantīti. Abhimukhībhūtanti kammantarassa okāsaṃ adatvā attano okāsaṃ katvā paccupaṭṭhitaṃ. Kammaṃvā paccupaṭṭhātīti [M 0.0256] sambandho. Upaladdhapubbanti tassa kammassa ārammaṇa bhūtāni deyyadhamma vatthādīni parapāṇādīnica sandhāya vuttaṃ. Upakaraṇabhūtanti kammasiddhiyā upakaraṇabhūtāni parivārabhūtānica paṭiggāhakādīni āvudhabhaṇḍādinica sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yasmāca lakkhaṇa saṃyutte gavādīni vadhitvā rāsikatāni aṭṭhipuñjādīni kammanimittāni hutvā upaṭṭhahantīti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā kammasambandhāni yāni kānici vatthūni vā ārammaṇānivā idha upakaraṇe saṅgahi tānīti daṭṭhabbāni. Upalabhitabbanti duggatinimittaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Upabhogabhūtanti sugatinimittaṃ. Ubhayaṃpi vā yaṃ kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ hutvā labhitabbaṃ hoti. Taṃ upalabhitabbaṃnāma. Apaṭibaddhaṃ hutvā kevalaṃ sukhadukkhānubhavanatthāya labhitabbaṃ upabhoga bhūtaṃnāma. Etthaca aggijāla lohakumbhi nirayapāla nirayasunakhādīni nirayanimittaṃ. Taṃ pana kesañci janānaṃ attano vasanaṭṭhāneviya upaṭṭhāti. Kesañci tato tato āgantvā attānaṃ saṃparivārentaṃ viya upaṭṭhāti. Yathāha-tassa gilānaseyyāya nippannassa nirayo upaṭṭhāti. Soṇagiripādato mahantā mahantā sunakhā āgantvā khāditukāmāviya saṃparivāresunti. Tathā deva nimittepi. Yathāha-nandavana cittalatāvana missakavana phārusakavana vimānāniceva devanāṭakānica parivāretvā ṭhitāniviya ahesunti. Kesañci pana sayaṃ tattha tattha patvā diṭṭhaṃviya upaṭṭhāti. Kambalayānasadiso mātukucchivaṇṇo manussanimittaṃ. Pabbatapāda vanasaṇḍa narakapapātādīni tiracchānagatānaṃ nimittānīti. Kammabalenāti idāni paṭisandhiṃ janetuṃ paccupaṭṭhitassa kammassa ānubhāvena. Idañca yebhuyyavasena vuttaṃ. Pakatiyā pana āciṇṇa bhūtaṃvā taṅkhaṇakataṃvā parena sarāpitaṃvā sayameva anussaritaṃvā pakatiyāva kukkuccaṃvā somanassaṃvā janetvā ṭhitaṃvā kammaṃvā tassanimittaṃvā aññenapi kāraṇabalena paccupaṭṭhātiye vāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tameva tatopaṭṭhitaṃ ārammaṇaṃ ārabbhāti idañca yebhuyyavasena vuttaṃ. Tato hi kesañci pathamaṃ kammabalenavā kāraṇantarenavā pāpapakkhiyesu upaṭṭhahantesu puna duṭṭha gāmaṇi rañño [M 0.0257] viya pubbakataṃ balavantaṃ puññaṃ anussarantānaṃvā soṇatthera vitu viya taṅkhaṇeyeva pasādajanakaṃ puññaṃ karontānaṃvā pacchā kalyāṇapakkhiyāni upaṭṭhahanti. Tathā kesañci pathamaṃ kalyāṇa pakkhiyesu upaṭṭhahantesu dhammāsokarañño viya pacchā kenaci kāraṇena domanassaṃ uppādetvā pāpakammassa okāsaṃ karontānaṃ pāpapakkhiyāni upaṭṭhahantīti. Vipaccamānaka kammānurūpanti yassa vipaccamānakaṃ kammaṃ kusalaṃ hoti. Tassa parisuddhaṃ kusalacittasantānaṃ abhiṇhaṃ pavattati. Yassa taṃ akusalaṃ hoti. Tassa upakiliṭṭhaṃ akusala cittasantānaṃ abhiṇhaṃ pavattatīti attho. Tathā hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃpi sugatigāmīnaṃ kusaluppatti hetubhūtaṃ paṇītaṃ ārammaṇaṃ āpātamāgacchatītica duggatigāmīnaṃ akusaluppatti hetubhūtaṃ hīnārammaṇaṃ āpāta māgacchatī tica vuttaṃ. Mūlaṭīkāyaṃ mahāṭīkāyañca āsanne akusalaṃ duggatiyaṃ kusalañca sugatiyaṃ paṭisandhiyā upanissayo hotīti vuttaṃ. Ettha siyā, yadā devaccharādīni sagganimittāni upaṭṭhahanti. Tadā tāni taṇhāya assādentasseva sato cavantassa kathanti. Vuccate. Upakiliṭṭhaṃyeva tassa cittaṃ. Tasmā duggatieva tassa pāṭikaṅkhitabbāti vadanti. Yasmā pana paṭisambhidā magge tādisiyā taṇhāya kusalakammassa sahakāri kāraṇa bhāvo vutto. Yathāha-nikantikkhaṇe dve hetū akusalāti. Tasmā sugatibhavanibbattanepi ayaṃ taṇhā ekantena kusala kammassa niyāmakasahakāripaccayabhūtāti katvā tassa tānivā devaccharādīni kusalakamma kammanimittānivā assādentasseva sato cavantassa sātaṇhā tadupatthambhikāeva bhavituṃ arahati. Na taṃ paṭibāhikāti sakkā viññātuṃ. Yañca nimittassādagadhitaṃvā bhikkhave viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭhati, anubyañjanassādagadhitaṃ vā. Tasmiṃ ce bhikkhave samaye kālaṅkareyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Yaṃ dvinnaṃgatīnaṃ aññataragatiṃ gaccheyya, nirayaṃvā tiracchāna yoniṃvātiādittapariyāye vuttaṃ. Taṃpi attano paresaṃ vā hatthapādādīsu gadhitaṃ taṇhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Nakammādīsūti sakkā vattunti. [M 0.0258] Upalabhitabba bhavānurūpanti upalabhitabbo bhavo yadi sugatibhavo hoti, taṃ assādanākārena. Yadi duggatibhavo hoti, taṃ anassādanākārenāti evaṃ upalabhi tabbassa bhavassa anurūpaṃ. Tatthoṇataṃvāti tasmiṃ yatho paṭṭhite ārammaṇe oṇamantaṃeva. Tathā hi bālapaṇḍitasutte tānissa tasmiṃ samaye olambanti ajjholambanti abhippalambantīti vuttaṃ. Tattha tānissāti assa puggalassa tāni puññāpuñña kammāni. Kammasīsena vuttāni kammanimitta gatinimittānica. Olambantīti tassa cittasantānaṃ attanieva oṇamantaṃ ajjhoṇamantaṃ abhimukhībhūtaṃ katvā lambanti palambanti. Bandhitvā ākaḍḍhantāni viya upaṭṭhahantīti attho. Evaṃ pana tesu tathā olambantesu taṃcittasantānaṃ tesu ninnapoṇapabbhārameva hotīti vuttaṃ tatthoṇataṃvāti. Tathā hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ kilesabalavināmitaṃ sutvā tadevaṃ pavattamānaṃ taṇhāavijjānaṃ appahīnattā avijjāya paṭicchā ditādīnave tasmiṃ visaye taṇhā nāmeti sahajāta saṅkhārā khipantīti vuttaṃ. Tattha tanti viññāṇaṃ. Cittasantānaṃ icceva attho. Tasmiṃvisayeti kammādiārammaṇe. Taṇhānāmetīti vaṭṭamūlaka taṇhā taṃ tasmiṃ oṇamantaṃ katvā niyojetīti attho.

For the dying consciousness of that one does not make kamma, kamma-sign, or other such things its object. Nor do the kamma and other signs grasped at death exist for the sake of the next existence for all beings. ‘Having come face-to-face’ (abhimukhībhūta) means that it has presented itself by making its own opportunity, not giving an opportunity to other kamma. The connection is with the phrase ‘or kamma presents itself’. ‘Previously experienced’ (upaladdhapubba) is said in reference to things that have been the object of that kamma, such as items for donation, material goods, and other living beings. ‘Having become an instrument’ (upakaraṇabhūta) is said in reference to things that have become instruments for the accomplishment of kamma and its accessories, such as recipients, weapons, and other goods. And because it is said in the commentary on the Lakkhaṇa Saṃyutta that the piled-up bones of slaughtered cattle and so on appear as kamma-signs, therefore it should be understood that whatever things or objects are connected with kamma are included here under ‘instrument’. ‘To be obtained’ (upalabhitabba) is said in reference to a sign of a woeful destination. ‘To be enjoyed’ (upabhogabhūta) is said in reference to a sign of a happy destination. Or, both may be distinguished thus: that which is to be obtained connected to the body is called ‘obtainable’ (upalabhitabba); that which is to be obtained unconnected to the body, merely for the experience of pleasure and pain, is called ‘to be enjoyed’ (upabhogabhūta). Here, the sign of hell includes a mass of flames, iron cauldrons, hell-guardians, hell-dogs, and so on. For some people, this appears as if in their own dwelling place. For others, it appears as if coming from here and there to surround them. As it is said: ‘For one lying on a sickbed, hell appears. From the foot of Mount Soṇa, huge dogs come as if wanting to devour him, and they surround him.’ Likewise for a divine sign. As it is said: ‘The Nandana Grove, Cittalatā Grove, Missaka Grove, and Phārusaka Grove, as well as celestial mansions and divine performances, appeared as if they were standing surrounding him.’ For some, however, it appears as if seen by having gone to those various places oneself. A sign of a human rebirth is something like a vehicle of woolen cloth or the color of a mother’s womb. Signs for those going to the animal realm are the foot of a mountain, a forest thicket, a precipice, and so on. ‘By the power of kamma’ means by the influence of the kamma that has now presented itself to generate rebirth-linking. And this is said for the general case. But it should be understood that, as a rule, kamma or its sign also presents itself due to some other causal power—whether it be kamma that has become habitual, or was done at that moment, or was brought to mind by another, or was recollected by oneself, or that which stands having generated remorse or gladness by its very nature. And the statement that one takes as object that very object which has presented itself there, this too is said for the general case. For, in the case of some, when things on the side of evil first appear by the power of kamma or by another cause, later things on the side of good appear—as for the wicked village headman or the king who recollected powerful merit done previously, or as for the father of Elder Soṇa who at that very moment performed a meritorious act that inspired faith. Likewise, in the case of some, when things on the side of good first appear, as for King Dhammāsoka, later things on the side of evil appear for some reason, for those who, having generated grief, make an opportunity for evil kamma. ‘In accordance with the ripening kamma’ means: for one whose ripening kamma is wholesome, a pure stream of wholesome consciousness proceeds frequently; for one whose ripening kamma is unwholesome, a defiled stream of unwholesome consciousness proceeds frequently. For thus it is also said in the commentary: ‘For those going to a happy destination, a sublime object that is a cause for the arising of the wholesome comes into range; and for those going to a woeful destination, an inferior object that is a cause for the arising of the unwholesome comes into range.’ And in the Mūlaṭīkā and the Mahāṭīkā it is said: ‘When death is near, the unwholesome is a decisive support condition for rebirth-linking in a woeful destination, and the wholesome is a decisive support condition for rebirth-linking in a happy destination.’ Here, it might be asked: When celestial nymphs and other heavenly signs appear, what is the outcome for one who is dying while delighting in them with craving? It is said: His mind is indeed defiled; therefore, they say that only a woeful destination is to be expected for him. But since in the Paṭisambhidāmagga it is said that such craving has the nature of an assisting cause for wholesome kamma—as it is stated: ‘At the moment of longing, the two roots are unwholesome’—therefore, it can be understood that even in producing a happy existence, this craving, being entirely a directing and assisting condition for wholesome kamma, is able to be a support for one who is dying while delighting in those celestial nymphs or in the wholesome kamma or kamma-signs, and is not an obstruction to it. And as for what was said in the Ādittapariyāya Sutta: ‘Bhikkhus, when consciousness, being established, is established greedy for the taste of the sign or greedy for the taste of the details, if, bhikkhus, he should die at that time, this is possible: that he would go to one of two destinations, either hell or the animal womb’—this too, it can be said, is stated in reference to craving that is greedy for one's own or others' hands, feet, etc., not in reference to kamma and so on. ‘In accordance with the existence to be obtained’ means: if the existence to be obtained is a happy existence, it is in the mode of savoring; if it is a woeful existence, it is in the mode of not savoring—thus, it is in accordance with the existence to be obtained. ‘Or bent towards that’ means just inclining towards that object as it has appeared. For thus it is said in the Bālapaṇḍita Sutta: ‘At that time, those things hang on him, hang down on him, hang all over him.’ There, ‘those things of his’ refers to that person's meritorious and demeritorious kammas, spoken of under the heading of kamma, and also kamma-signs and destination-signs. ‘They hang on’ means they hang on and hang down, having made his stream of consciousness bend towards them, incline towards them, and face them. The meaning is that they appear as if binding and dragging him. But thus, when they hang on in such a way, that stream of consciousness becomes inclined, sloping, and bent towards them; this is what is meant by ‘or bent towards that’. For thus it is said in the commentary: Because craving and ignorance are not abandoned, in that object whose dangers are concealed by ignorance, craving bends that consciousness—which is proceeding in this way, having been bent down by the power of the defilements—and the co-nascent formations hurl it. There, ‘that’ means consciousness; the meaning is simply the stream of consciousness. ‘In that object’ means in the object of kamma, etc. ‘Craving bends’ means that craving, which is the root of the round of rebirth, engages it, having made it bend towards that.

[165] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

id

“Tatthoṇataṃvāti tasmiṃ upapajjitabbabhave oṇataṃ viya oṇataṃeva vā”ti vuttaṃ. Taṃ aṭṭhakathāya na sameti.

id

Abhiṇhanti nirantaraṃ. Tathāpavatti pana saṇikaṃ marantānaṃ eva labbhati. Lahuka maraṇena marantānaṃ pana na labbhatīti vuttaṃ. Bāhullenāti

id

[166] Yaṃ pana vibhāvaniyaṃ

id

“Bāhullenātiettha adhippāyo yebhuyyena bhavantareti ettha vuttanayena daṭṭhabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Taṃ na yujjati.

id

Na hi tasmiṃ vuttānaṃ asaññisattānaṃ cittasantānassa abhiṇhappagattipasaṅgonāma atthi. Cittasantānasseva tesaṃ abhāvatoti. Idāni [M 0.0259] aparena pakārena kammu paṭṭhānaṃ dassetuṃ tamevavā pana.La. Dvārapattaṃ hotīti vuttaṃ. Tattha abhinavakaraṇavasena dvārappattaṃ hotīti pubbe katasaññaṃ ajanetvā taṅkhaṇe eva karaṇākāraṃ janetvā attānaṃ abhinavaṃ viya katvā manodvāre taṃsadisajavanappavattivasena pattaṃ pātubhūtaṃ hotīti attho. Yathā hi imasmiṃbhavepavattaṃ kiñci pākaṭaṃ kammaṃ asukasmiṃ kāle idaṃnāmamayākatanti evaṃ pubbekatasaññaṃ janetvāpi upaṭṭhāti. Na tathā bhavantare pavattaṃ bhavapaṭicchannaṃñca imasmiṃ bhave pavattaṃ apākaṭañcāti. Apica, idhekacce buddhādīsu tīsu vatthusu dānapūjādivasena āciṇṇabahulā honti. Te maraṇanti kābādhabalena visīdappattā kiñci dukkhaṃajānitvā visīdantare pubbe viya bhikkhusaṅghassa dānaṃ dentācetiyaṃ vandantā pūjaṃ karontā vippasannacittā pamodacittā eva honti. Tabbiparītena pāpakammabahulāpi vattabbāti. Idaṃpi dvārapattamevāti. Sabbañcetaṃ lakkhaṇa saṃyuttaṭṭhakathāya dīpetabbaṃ. Tattha asilomapetādi patthūsu tassa ukkhittāsikabhāvova nimittaṃ ahosīti ca. Tassa sattiyā vijjhanaka bhāvova nimittaṃ ahosītica. Tassa usunā vijjhanakabhāvova nimittaṃ ahosītica. Tassa patodasūciyā vijjhanakabhāvova nimittaṃ ahosītica. Tassa sūcīhi patodanadukkhaṃ paccanubhavituṃ kammameva nimittaṃ katvā sūcilomapeto jātotica evaṃ bahuṃdvāra pattavasena kammupaṭṭhānaṃ vuttanti. Tattha hi tassa ukkhittāsika bhāvova nimittaṃ ahosīti tassa niraye pacitvā puna āsanna maraṇassa taṃkammaṃ tadā tassa ukkhittāsikasaññaṃ janetvā dvāra pattavasena nimittaṃ ahosīti attho. Esanayo sesesupīti. Soca dvārappattākāro kammakoṭṭhāsiko eva hoti. Tassa sattassaca apākaṭonāma natthīti tassa paṭisandhiyā gahaṇayogyatā jātāti. Paccāsanna maraṇassāti antima javanapavattivasena puna āsannamaraṇassa. Vīthicittā vasānevāti kāmabhavato cavitvā kāmabhaveyeva uppajjamānānaṃ javana pariyosānānaṃvā tadārammaṇa pariyosānānaṃvā vīthicittānaṃ avasāne. [M 0.0260] Itaresaṃ pana javanapariyosānānaṃeva vīthicittānaṃ avasāneti attho. Ayamattho aṭṭhakathāyaṃpi vuttoyeva. Yathāha-taṃ ārabbha uppannāya tadārammaṇapariyosānāya suddhāyavā javanavīthiyā anantaraṃ cuticittaṃ uppajjatīti.

id

[167] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

id

“Tattha kāmabhavato cavitvā tattheva uppajjamānānaṃ tadārammaṇapariyosānāni sesānaṃ javanapariyosānānīti dhammānusāraṇiyaṃ vutta”nti vuttaṃ. Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

id

Aṭṭhakathāyañhi paripuṇṇaṃ katvā vutte kiṃaparipuṇṇāya dhammā nusāraṇiyāti. Bhavaṅgakkhayevāti bhavaṅgāvasānevā iccevattho. Yadi duvidhapīthicittato paraṃ pañcavokāre vatthurūpaṃ catuvokāre cittasantānaṃ dvicittakkhaṇāyusesaṃ hoti. Tadā ekassa bhavaṅgassa avasāneti vuttaṃ hoti. Etthaca somanassa paṭisandhikassa domanassacittena cavantassa āgantukabhavaṅga sambhavo. Taṃ sambhaveca sati aññabhavaṅgasambhavopi avāri toti suvuttametaṃ bhavaṅgakkhayevāti. Tasmiṃniruddhāvasāneti tasmiṃ niruddhe tassa niruddhassa avasāne. Ye pana loke cuti paṭisandhīnaṃ antare eko antarābhavonāma atthi. Yattha uppanno satto dibbacakkhuko viya iddhimā viya ca khaṇena icchitaṃ ṭhānaṃ gantuṃ samattho. Ito cutā keci tattha uppajjitvā mātāpitu samāgamādīni āgamentā sattāhaṃvā atireka sattāhaṃvā tiṭṭhantīti laddhiṃ gaṇhanti. Tesaṃ taṃnisedhetuṃ tassānantaramevāti vuttaṃ. Savatthukaṃ pañcavokāre avatthukamevavā catuvokāre. Yathārahanti kusalabhūtassavā akusalabhūtassa vā saṅkhārassa arahānurūpaṃ. Avijjātaṇhānusayā kusalabhūtassa appahīnaṭṭhena akusalabhūtassa pana sahajātabhāvenāpi parivārabhūtā mūlabhūtāca hontīti attho. Pariyuṭṭhānāvatthaṃ apatvā kusalābyākatacittasantānenapi aviruddhabhāvena anurūpaṃ. Anubandhamānovā seti, anuanuvānirantaraṃ setīti anusayo. Anusayabhūtāya [M 0.0261] avijjāya parikkhittoti avijjānusayaparikkhitto. Taṇhānusayo mūlaṃ etassāti taṇhānusaya mūlako. Avijjānusaya mūlakena taṇhānusaya parikkhittenāti pana vutte suṭṭhutaraṃ yujjati. Avijjā hi taṇhāyapi mūlabhūtā hoti. Tāya paṭicchāditādīnave eva ārammaṇe taṇhāpavattisambhavato. Taṇhā ca pana sahakāri kāraṇa bhāvena taṃ taṃ saṅkhāraṃ niyojentī pavattatīti saṅkhārassa parivārabhūtā balavaāsanna sahāyabhūtā hotīti.

id

Etthaca akusalakamma sahajātānaṃvā kammanikanti nimittanikanti sahajātānaṃvā vippaṭisāra saha jātānaṃvā maraṇāsanna javana sahajātānaṃvā avijjātaṇhānaṃpi dhammato anusayasadisatāya anusaya vohārasambhavo veditabbo. Apica, anusayānāma paṭisandhijanane kusalasaṅkhārassapi balavasahāyabhūtā honti. Tasmā idha ekantānusayabhūtāeva pariyattāti kiṃsahajātānaṃ gahaṇenāti. Teneva aṭṭhakathāyaṃpi taṇhā avijjānaṃ appahīnattāti evaṃ appahīnasaddena ekantānusayāeva gahitāti. Saṅkhārenāti paṭisandhijanakakammasaṅkhātena cetanāsaṅkhārena. Taṃ sahajātaphassādidhammasamūhenapivā. Sopi hi upanissayabhāve na paṭisandhiṃ janetiyevāti. Athavā, saṅkhārenāti maraṇasanna javanaviññāṇa sahajātena cetanāsaṅkhārena. Taṃ sahajāta phassādidhammasamūhenapivā. Tadubhayaṃpi hi kammādivisaye khipanaka saṅkhārabhāvena paṭisandhiṃ janetīti. Tathā hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ taṇhā avijjānaṃ appahīnattā avijjāya paṭicchāditādīnave tasmiṃ visaye taṇhā nāmeti. Sahajātasaṅkhārā khipantīti vuttaṃ. Mūlaṭīkāyañca sahajātasaṅkhārāti cutiāsannajavanaviññāṇasahajātā cetanā. Sabbepivā phassādayoti vuttaṃ. Sakalena pana vacanena aggamaggena appahīnā avijjākammādivisayevā bhavantarevā ādīnavaṃ paṭicchādeti, tathā rūpāyeva taṇhā tadubhayasmiṃ cittasantānaṃ nāmeti. Yathāvuttasaṅkhārā taṃ tattha khipanti. Tasmiṃ abhinava viññāṇapātubhāvaṃ sādhentīti dassetīti.

And here, it should be understood that even ignorance and craving, which co-arise with unwholesome kamma, or with a kamma-sign or destiny-sign, or with remorse, or with death-proximate javana, can be conventionally termed 'latent tendencies' due to their resemblance to latent tendencies in nature. Moreover, latent tendencies are powerful allies even for wholesome formations in generating rebirth-linking. Therefore, here, only those that are exclusively latent tendencies are sufficient—why mention co-arising states? For this reason, the commentary also states: 'Because craving and ignorance are not abandoned,' and thus by the word 'unabandoned,' only those that are exclusively latent tendencies are taken. 'Formations' here refer to volitional formations, specifically the kamma-formation that generates rebirth-linking. This may also refer to the group of its co-arisen mental factors, such as contact. However, even that group, by way of being a strong supporting condition, does not itself generate rebirth-linking. Alternatively, 'formations' can mean the volitional formations co-arising with death-proximate javana consciousness. This may also refer to the group of its co-arisen mental factors, such as contact. Both of these, in the sphere of kamma and so on, generate rebirth-linking by being projecting formations. For so it is said in the commentary: 'Because craving and ignorance are unabandoned, and because ignorance conceals the dangers in that sphere, craving inclines the mind toward it. Co-arising formations project it.' And in the Mūlaṭīkā it is said: '“Co-arising formations” means the volition co-arisen with the consciousness of the death-proximate javana, or all the factors such as contact.' But by the entire statement, it is shown that ignorance, unabandoned by the highest path, conceals the danger in the sphere of kamma and so on, or in another existence; likewise, craving of that nature inclines the mental continuum in both respects; and the aforementioned formations project it there, bringing about the manifestation of a new consciousness in that state.

Sampayuttehi [M 0.0262] pariggayhamānanti phassādīhi sampayuttadhammehi parivāretvā gayhamānaṃ. Sahajātānanti nāmarūpadhammānaṃ. Adhiṭṭhāna bhāvenāti nissayabhāvena. Pubbaṅgamabhūtanti padhānabhūtaṃ. Pada dvayena vijānanadhātuyā ativiya mahānubhāvabhāvaṃ dasseti. Yathā hi loke ekasmiṃ mahānubhāve purisavisese jāyamāne parivārabhūtā sahajātajanāca tassa upabhoga paribhogabhūtā pāsādakapparukkhādayova tena saha jāyanti. Evaṃ sampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Bhavantarapaṭisandhānavasenāti ekasmiṃbhave niruddhe tena saha nirantaraṃ katvā bhavantarassa paṭisandahana vasena. Uppajjamānameva patiṭṭhāti na purimabhave uppajjitvā anirujjhitvā ṭhitibhāvena gantvā bhavantare patiṭṭhātīti adhippāyo. Na hi uppannuppannā dhammā pakatikālepi desantaraṃvā khaṇantaraṃvāsaṅkantā nāma atthi. Kuto maraṇakāle bhavantaraṃ. Yañca anamataggo yaṃ bhikkhave saṃsāro. Pubbakoṭi napaññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsaratanti vuttaṃ, taṃpi pariyāyena vuttaṃ. Yesañhi avijjā taṇhāsaṅkhārānaṃ vasena bhavantare paṭisandhi pātubhavati. Teca pubbe yassa santāne pavattanti, so tesaṃ hetuphalasambandhena bhavantaraṃ sandhāvati saṃsaratīti vuccatīti. Tatoyevaca tassā paṭisandhiyā purimabhavapari yāpannehi hetūhi vinā anuppajjanaṃpi siddhaṃ hotīti. Paṭighosa padīpamuddhādīni cettha nidassanānīti.

“Being grasped by associated factors” means being surrounded and grasped by associated phenomena such as contact. “Of co-nascent things” refers to the phenomena of mentality-materiality. “By way of being a support” means by way of being a foundation. “Being the forerunner” means being principal. This pair of terms demonstrates the exceedingly great power of the consciousness element. For just as in the world, when a special person of great power is born, his co-nascent retinue and the palaces, wish-fulfilling trees, and so on, for his use and enjoyment are born together with him, so should this success be understood. “By means of rebirth-linking in another existence” means by way of linking to another existence immediately after one existence has ceased. The meaning is that it is established just as it arises; it does not arise in the previous existence and, without ceasing, go and become established in the next existence. For arisen phenomena do not, even in the normal course, transmigrate to another place or another moment. How much less so to another existence at the time of death? And as to what was said: “Monks, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving”—this too is stated figuratively. For it is said of those for whom rebirth-linking in another existence arises on account of ignorance, craving, and formations, that they wander and transmigrate to another existence through the cause-and-effect connection with those factors that were previously active in their continuum. And from that very reason, it is also established that the arising of that rebirth-linking is not without the causes pertaining to the previous existence. Here, an echo, a lamp, a seal, and so on, are the illustrations.

Etthāti maraṇuppattiṭṭhāne. Mandappavattānīti kammadubbalabhāvena vatthudubbalabhāvenaca mandaṃ hutvā pavattāni. Tasmā paccuppannā lambaṇakā labbhatīti sambandho. Dharantesvevāti tiṭṭhantesu eva. Paṭisandhi bhavaṅgānaṃpīti paṭisandhiyāpi katipayabhavaṅgānaṃpi. Iti katvāti iminā kāraṇena. Kāmañcettha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ gatinimittaṃnāma nibbattanakaokāse eko vaṇṇo upaṭṭhātīti vatvā sabbesu gatinimittavāresu gabhinimittaṃ vaṇṇāyatanameva manodvāra gahitameva paccuppannamevaca dassitaṃ. Tathāpi chadevalokato attano santikaṃ āgate dibbaratheyeva gatinimittaṃ katvā cavantānaṃ [M 0.0263] dhammikaupāsaka duṭṭhagāmaṇi abhayarājādīnaṃ vasena taṃpi kammanimittaṃviya chabbidhaṃpi chadvāragahitaṃpi paccuppannamatītaṃpi sambhavatīti adhippāyena taṃkammanimittena nibbisesaṃ katvā kāmāvacarapaṭisandhiyā.La. Upalabbhatīti vuttaṃ. Tathā cavantā hi dibbavaṇṇopi devatānaṃ ānubhāvena cakkhunā diṭṭhoyeva hoti. Dibbo rathasaddovā tūriyasaddovā vacanasaddovā sotena sutoyeva. Dibbagandhopi ghānena ghāyitoyeva. Nirayato uggatena aggijālena dayhamānakāyena cavantānaṃ devadatta nandayakkha nandamāṇa vakādīnaṃ khuracakke āsajjamānānaṃ mittavindakādīnañca vasena phoṭṭhabbaṃpi sambhavatiyeva. Rasadhammāpi yathā sambhavaṃ yojetabbāti. Vuttañca saccasaṅkhepe –

“Here” means at the place of death and birth. “Occurring weakly” means occurring weakly on account of the weakness of the kamma and the weakness of the physical base. Therefore, the connection is that a present object is obtained. “While they are still present” means while they are still existing. “Of rebirth-linking and life-continuum” means of the rebirth-linking and of some life-continuum moments. “Thus” means for this reason. Although in the Commentary it is said, “The sign of destiny is a single visible form that appears in the place of rebirth,” and in all the sections on the sign of destiny, the sign of the womb is shown as only a visible-form-object, apprehended by the mind door, and as present, nevertheless, in the case of the devout lay follower Dhammika, King Duṭṭhagāmaṇī Abhaya, and others who pass away having taken as the sign of destiny a divine chariot that has come near them from the six deva worlds, that sign, like the kamma-sign, can also be sixfold, apprehended by the six doors, and either present or past. With this intention it is said that for sense-sphere rebirth-linking it is obtained without distinction from the kamma-sign. For those passing away thus, a divine visible form is indeed seen by the eye through the power of the devas. A divine sound of a chariot, or of music, or of speech is heard by the ear. A divine odor is smelled by the nose. In the case of Devadatta, the yakkha Nanda, the youth Nandamāṇava, and others who pass away with their bodies burning with flames issuing from hell, and of Mittavindaka and others who are being assailed by the razor-wheel, a tangible object can also arise. Taste-objects too should be connected as is possible. And it is said in the Saccasaṅkhepa—

Pañcadvāre siyā sandhi, vinā kammaṃ dvigocareti.

Rebirth-linking may occur at the five doors; apart from kamma, its object is twofold.

Mahāṭīkāyaṃpi ayamattho vuttoyeva. Yadā pana antima javanavīthito pubbabhāge yathopaṭṭhitaṃ gatinimittaṃ antimajavanassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Tadā taṃ atītaṃpi hotiyevāti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana santativasena tassa paccuppannatāva vuttā. Tathā vaṇṇārammaṇabhāvo manodvārena gahitabhāvoca yebhuyyena vuttoti veditabbo. Itarathā kammanimittaṃpi paccuppannabhūtaṃ pañcadvāreeva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ dassitanti taṃpi manodvāragahitaṃ paccuppannabhūtaṃ pañcārammaṇaṃvā dhammārammaṇaṃvā nasambhavatīti vattabbaṃ siyā. Naca sakkā tathā vattuṃ. Kasmā, cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassantītiādinā paṭṭhāne vuttassa chaḷārammaṇa bhūtassa purejātapaccayassa manodvārika maraṇāsanna javanānampi icchitabbattā. Tatoyevaca tadanubandhāya paṭisandhiyāpi sambhava toti.

This meaning is also stated in the Great Subcommentary. But when the sign of destiny that has presented itself in the period prior to the final javana process becomes the object of the final javana, then it is indeed past. In the Commentary, however, its presentness is stated by way of continuity. Similarly, it should be understood that its being a visible-form object and its being apprehended by the mind door are stated for the most part. Otherwise, it would have to be said that the kamma-sign—which is present and shown in the Commentary as being only at the five doors—is impossible as a present five-sense object or a mental object when apprehended by the mind door. And it is not possible to say so. Why? Because the sixfold object of the pre-nascence condition mentioned in the Paṭṭhāna with the words, “contemplating the eye as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self,” etc., must also be admitted for the mind-door death-proximate javanas. And for that very reason, the rebirth-linking that follows upon them is also possible.

[168] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[168] But in the Vibhāvanī:

Tathā avicāretvā yaṃvuttaṃ “paccuppannārammaṇesu āpātamāgatesu manodvāre gatinimittavasena pañcadvāre kammanimittavasenā”ti. Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

What was said without due consideration, namely: “With present objects that have come into range, by way of the sign of destiny at the mind door, and by way of the kamma-sign at the five doors”—that is not well-stated.

[169] Yañca tattha

[169] And what was said there:

“Chadvāragahitanti kammanimittaṃ chadvāragahitaṃ gatinimittaṃ chaṭṭhadvāragahitanti yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabba”nti vuttaṃ. Taṃpi na yujjati.

The statement: “'Grasped by the six doors' should be applied as is possible, thus: the kamma-sign is grasped by the six doors, the sign of destiny is grasped by the sixth door”—that too is not tenable.

Evañhi sati kammaṃ viya gatinimittaṃpi therena bhinditvā vuttaṃ siyā. Naca taṃ vuttanayena pañcadvāragahitaṃ na sambhavatīti.

For if this were so, the Elder would have spoken distinguishing the sign of destiny just as he did the kamma-sign. And it is not that, according to the method stated, it is impossible for it to be grasped by the five doors.

[170] Yañca tattha

[170] And what was said there:

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ mūla ṭīkādīsuca yebhuyyavasena vuttaṃ sāvasesapāṭhaṃ avicāretvā “aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana gatinimittaṃ manodvāre āpātamāgacchatīti vuttattā tadārammaṇāyaca pañcadvārikapaṭisandhiyā adassitattā mūlaṭīkādīsuca kamma balena upaṭṭhāpitaṃ vaṇṇāyatanaṃ supinaṃ passantassaviya dibba cakkhussa viyaca manodvāreyeva gocarabhāvaṃ gacchatīti niyametvā vuttattā tesaṃ vacanaṃ nasampaṭicchanti ācariyā”ti vuttaṃ. Tatthapi asampaṭicchantānaṃ aññaṃ kāraṇaṃ natthi aññatra avicāraṇāyāti.

And what was said there without considering the qualified statement made for the most part in the Commentary, the Root Subcommentary, etc., namely: "The masters do not accept their statement, because it is said in the Commentary, 'However, the sign of destiny comes into range at the mind door,' and because a five-door rebirth-linking with that as object is not shown, and because it is stated definitively in the Root Subcommentary, etc., that 'the visible-form base, presented by the power of kamma, enters the cognitive field only of the mind door, like one seeing a dream or like the divine eye.'" Therein, too, for those who do not accept it, there is no other reason than lack of consideration.

Paccuppannamatītanti ettha yassa javanāvasānāya pañcadvārikavīthiyā cavanaṃ hoti. Tassa paṭisandhiyā dvinnañca bhavaṅgānaṃ paccuppannā rammaṇatā upalabbhati. Yassa tadārammaṇāvasānāya, tassa paṭisandhiyā eva. Yassa pana javanāvasānāya paccuppannārammaṇāya manodvārikavīthiyā cavanaṃ hoti, tassa paṭisandhiyā channañca bhavaṅgānaṃ. Yassa pana tadāraṇāvasānāya, tassa paṭisandhiyā catunnañca bhavaṅgānanti. Etthaca ārammaṇe bahutarāyuke balavantepi vatthudubbalabhāve sati kāmasattānaṃpi javanāvasānā vīthi hotiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana tadārammaṇāvasānāya eva yojitattā manodvāre paṭisandhito paraṃ catunnaṃ bhavaṅgānaṃ pañcadvāre paṭisandhiyāeva paccuppannārammaṇatā vuttā. Tadārammaṇa pariyosānāyavā suddhāyavā javanavīthiyāti vuttattā pana idha javanāvasānāpi yojitāti veditabbā.

Regarding "present and past": Here, for one whose passing away occurs at the end of the javanas in a five-door process, a present object is found for the rebirth-linking and for two life-continuum moments. For one whose passing away occurs at the end of registration, it is found only for the rebirth-linking. But for one whose passing away occurs at the end of the javanas in a mind-door process with a present object, it is found for the rebirth-linking and for six life-continuum moments. For one whose passing away occurs at the end of registration, it is found for the rebirth-linking and for four life-continuum moments. And here it should be seen that even for sense-sphere beings, when the object has a very long duration and is strong, if the physical basis is weak, a process ending with javana does indeed occur. In the Commentary, however, since the explanation is given only for a process ending with registration, it is said that at the mind door, a present object is had by the four life-continuum moments after rebirth-linking, and at the five doors, by the rebirth-linking only. However, since it is said "a javana process that is either concluded by registration or is a pure one," it should be understood that here the case of a process ending with javana is also included.

[171] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[171] But in the Vibhāvanī:

Evaṃ [M 0.0265] avicāretvā yaṃ vuttaṃ “manodvāre tāva paṭisandhiyā catunnaṃ bhavaṅgānañca pañcadvāre paṭisandhiyāeva paccuppannārammaṇatā labbhatī”tiādi. Taṃ anupapannaṃ.

What was said without considering this, namely: "At the mind door, a present object is obtained by the rebirth-linking and four life-continuum moments, and at the five doors, by the rebirth-linking only," and so on—that is untenable.

Etthaca yasmā paṭisandhijanakasseva kammassa ārammaṇaṃvā upakaraṇaṃvā kammanimittanti adhippetaṃ. Pañcadvārikakammañca paṭisandhijanakameva na hoti. Tasmā tadā paṭisandhijanakaṃ kammaṃ purimabhāgeeva manodvāravasena siddhaṃ hoti. Tassaca ārammaṇabhūtameva upakaraṇabhūtamevavā ekantena kammanimittaṃnāma hoti. Yaṃ pana pañcadvārikassa antimajavanassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Taṃ purimena niruddhena ārammaṇena vatthuto abhinnattāvā tassadisattāvā kammanimittanteva vuccatīti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ mūlaṭīkāyaṃ pañcadvāre āpātaṃ āgacchantaṃ paccuppannaṃ kammanimittaṃ āsannakatakammārammaṇa santatiyaṃ uppannaṃ taṃsadisañca daṭṭhabbanti. Tattha yesu deyyadhammavatthūsu cetiyādīsuvā yehi satthādīhivā pubbe kammaṃ siddhaṃ. Tesaṃ paccakkhe dharamānataṃ sandhāya santatiyaṃ uppannanti vuttaṃ. Tehi sadi savatthūnaṃ dharamānataṃ sandhāya taṃsadisañcāti vuttaṃ. Sadisavatthūnipi hi kammassa laddhokāsakāraṇāni hontiyeva. Yathā taṃ ito parittakena pāpakammena niraye ussadasāmante nibbattānaṃ pubbe puññakaraṇakāle laddhanimittasadisaṃ nirayaggijālānaṃ saddaṃ sutvāvā vaṇṇaṃ disvāvā puññaṃ saritvā cavitvā sagge nibbattānaṃ aggijālāni viyāti.

Because here the object or instrument of the very kamma that generates rebirth-linking is intended as the kamma-sign. And kamma at the five doors is not itself rebirth-generating. Therefore, at that time, the rebirth-generating kamma has already been accomplished through the mind-door in a previous phase. And its object alone or instrument alone is exclusively called the kamma-sign. But what is the object of the last impulsion in a five-door process—that, because it is not different in substance from the previous object that has ceased or because it is similar to it, is also called the kamma-sign. Thus it is said in the Mūlaṭīkā: 'The present kamma-sign that comes into the range of the five doors, what has arisen in the continuity of the object of a recently performed kamma, and what is similar to that—these should be understood.' Therein, with reference to those gift-objects such as cetiyas or those persons such as the Teacher by which kamma was previously accomplished, their being directly present is meant by 'arisen in the continuity.' And with reference to the presence of objects similar to them, it is said 'and what is similar to that.' For similar objects also become causes for kamma to find its opportunity. For example, some beings, on account of a minor evil kamma done here, are reborn in the vicinity of a subsidiary hell. Upon hearing the sound or seeing the color of the flames of hellfire, which is similar to a sign obtained previously at the time of performing a meritorious deed, they recollect that merit and, passing away from there, are reborn in heaven, as if from the flames of fire.

[172] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[172] But in the Vibhāvanī:

Mūlaṭīkāpāṭhaṃ avicāretvā taṃsadisañcātiettha naṭṭhacakāraṃ pāṭhaṃ disvā “manodvārika javanānaṃ ārammaṇabhūtena saha samānattā tadekasantatipatitaṃ cutiāsannajavanagahi taṃpi paccuppannaṃ vaṇṇādikaṃ kammanimitta bhāvena vutta”nti vuttaṃ. Taṃ anupapannameva.

Without having investigated the text of the Mūlaṭīkā, and having seen a reading where the particle 'ca' in 'taṃsadisañca' is lost, it is said: 'Because of its similarity to the object of the mind-door impulsions, and because it falls within the same continuity, the present visible form, etc., which is grasped by the death-proximate impulsions, is also spoken of as a kamma-sign.' That is indeed untenable.

Apica, [M 0.0266] aṭṭhakathāyaṃ aparassa maraṇasamaye ñātakā ayaṃ tāta tavatthāya buddhapūjā karīyati. Cittaṃ pasādehīti vatvā pupphadāmadhajapaṭākādivasena rūpārammaṇaṃvā dhammasavanatūriyapūjādi vasena saddārammaṇaṃvā dhūmavāsagandhādivasena gandhārammaṇaṃvā idaṃ tāva sāyassu, tavatthāya dātabbaṃ deyyadhammanti vatvā madhuphāṇi tādivasena rasārammaṇaṃvā idaṃ tāva phusassu, tavatthāya dātabbaṃ deyyadhammanti vatvā cīnapaṭa somārapaṭādivasena phoṭṭhabbā rammaṇaṃvā pañcadvāre upasaṃharantīti vuttaṃ. Tattha rūpasaddagandhārammaṇāni sandhāya ṭīkāyaṃ santatiyaṃ uppannanti vuttaṃ. Rasaphoṭṭhabbā rammaṇāni sandhāya taṃsadisañcāti vuttaṃ. Tāni hi pathamaṃ sāyita phusitāni aññāni honti. Pacchā dinnāni aññānīti etthaca evaṃ upasaṃhaṭāni rūpārammaṇādīni pathamaṃ pañcadvārena gahetvā acavitvā pacchā puna atthi dāni evarūpānīti suddhena manodvārena gahetvā cavantānaṃ tāni manodvāragahitāni paccuppannabhūtāni kammanimittāni hontīti veditabbānīti. Pathamatatīyāruppa paṭisandhīnaṃ paññatti bhūtaṃ dutīyacatutthāruppapaṭisandhīnaṃ mahaggatabhūtanti vuttaṃ yathārahanti. Āruppesu uparibhūminibbattānaṃ arūpīnaṃ heṭṭhimajjhānāni paṭipassambhanti. Na ca te tāni puna āyūhantīti vuttaṃ heṭṭhimāruppa vajjitāti. Pamādapakkhe patitvā vissaṭṭhajjhānānaṃ tatoyevaca appahīnehi orambhāviya saṃyojanehi heṭṭhabhāgaṃ ākaḍḍhita mānasānaṃ kāmabhave uppajjamānānaṃ tesaṃ thapetvā tihetu kukkaṭṭhabhūtaṃ upacārajjhānacetanaṃ aññaṃ dubbalakammaṃ okāsaṃ nalabhatīti vuttaṃ tathā kāmatihetukāti. Tathā hi aṅguttaraṭṭha kathāyaṃ-na hi tassa upacārajjhānato balavataraṃnāma kammaṃ atthīti vuttaṃ. Ṭīkāyañca na hi tassa.La. Atthīti iminā tato cavantānaṃ upacārajjhānameva paṭisandhijanakaṃ kammanti dīpetīti vuttanti. Rūpāvacarapaṭisandhi pana tesaṃ natthiyeva. Evañca katvā yamakearūpadhātuyā cutassa arūpadhātuṃ upapajjantassātivā arūpa dhātuyā cutassa kāmadhātuṃ upapajjantassātivā vuttaṃ. Na pana vuttaṃ arūpadhātuyā cutassa rūpadhātuṃ upapajjantassāti. Rūpa lokato [M 0.0267] cavantānaṃ pana aññaṃ dubbalakammaṃ okāsaṃ nalabhatīti navattabbaṃ. Evaṃsantepi suṭṭhu vikkhambhitanīvaraṇānaṃ tesaṃ appanā pattajjhānavisesena suparibhāvitacittasantānattā jaccandhādivipatti janakaṃ dvihetukomakakammaṃpi okāsaṃ na labhati. Kuto apāyagāmikammanti vuttaṃ ahetuka rahitā siyunti.

Furthermore, it is said in the commentary that at the time of another's death, relatives, saying, 'Dear one, this offering to the Buddha is being made for your sake. Clarify your mind,' present a visible object by way of flower garlands, banners, flags, and the like; or an audible object by way of hearing the Dhamma, music for an offering, and so on; or an odorous object by way of incense, perfumes, and so on. Or saying, 'Taste this now, this gift-object is to be given for your sake,' they present a gustatory object by way of honey, molasses, and so on. Or saying, 'Touch this now, this gift-object is to be given for your sake,' they present a tactile object by way of Chinese silk, Somāra cloth, and so on, through the five doors. Therein, with reference to visible, audible, and odorous objects, it is said in the sub-commentary 'arisen in the continuity.' With reference to gustatory and tactile objects, it is said 'and what is similar to that.' For what is first tasted and touched are one thing, and what is given afterwards are another. And here, for those who, having first grasped through the five doors the visible objects, etc., thus presented, without passing away, then afterwards grasp them by the pure mind-door with the thought 'Now there are such things,' and then pass away—for them, those objects grasped by the mind-door become present kamma-signs. This should be understood. It is said that, as is appropriate, for the rebirth-linkings of the first and third formless attainments the object is a concept, and for the rebirth-linkings of the second and fourth formless attainments the object is a sublime state. It is said that for formless beings reborn in a higher plane within the formless sphere, the lower jhānas subside, and they do not strive for them again; thus it is said, 'excluding the lower formless attainments.' It is said that for those who have fallen into the party of the heedless, who have lost their jhānas, and whose minds are dragged down to the lower part by the lower fetters that have not been abandoned, when they are being reborn in the sense-sphere existence, apart from the volition of access concentration which is three-rooted and excellent, no other weak kamma finds an opportunity; thus it is said, 'three-rooted in the sense-sphere.' For so it is said in the Aṅguttara Commentary: 'For him, there is indeed no kamma stronger than the access jhāna.' And in the sub-commentary it is said that by the passage 'For him, there is indeed no... etc. ...kamma,' it is shown that for those passing away from that state, the access jhāna itself is the kamma that generates rebirth-linking. But for them there is no rebirth-linking in the fine-material sphere. And so, in the Yamaka, it is spoken of 'one passing away from the formless element and being reborn in the formless element' or 'one passing away from the formless element and being reborn in the sense-sphere element.' But it is not spoken of 'one passing away from the formless element and being reborn in the fine-material element.' But for those passing away from the fine-material world, it should not be said that other weak kamma does not find an opportunity. Even so, for them, because their hindrances are well suppressed and because their mental continuums are thoroughly cultivated by the distinction of having attained absorption jhāna, even a two-rooted inferior kamma that would generate a defective birth such as congenital blindness does not find an opportunity. How much less so a kamma that leads to the plane of misery? Thus it is said, 'they would be devoid of a rootless rebirth-linking.'

[173] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

But what is to be made clear:

“Upacārajjhānā nubhāveneva duhetuka tihetuka paṭisandhiyo siyu”nti vuttaṃ. Taṃ vicāretabbaṃ.

It is said: 'By the power of access concentration alone, two-rooted and three-rooted rebirth-linkings could occur.' That should be investigated.

Yadi hi taṃ paṭisandhidānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ siyā. Duhetukapaṭi sandhi na yujjati. Na hi suṭṭhu vikkhambhitanīvaraṇānaṃ appanāvīthiyaṃ pavattaṃ upacārajjhānaṃ tihetukomakaṃnāma sambhavatīti. Atha kammantarassa upatthambhanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ siyā. Sayaṃ balavatarassapi sato paṭisandhiṃ adatvā dubbalassa kammantarassa upatthambhane kāraṇaṃ natthīti. Yasmā pana rūpabrahmānaṃ upacārajjhānato aññānipi kāyavacīmanokammakusalāni uppajjantiyeva tāniyevaca kānici tihetukomakānipi kānici dvihetukukkaṭṭhānipi bhavanti. Oḷārikānaṃ pana nīvaraṇānaṃ suṭṭhu vikkhambhitattā savipattikapaṭi sandhijanakāni dvihetukomakāni tesaṃ nuppajjanti. Aparapariyāya bhūtānica tādisāni tesaṃ okāsaṃ nalabbhanti. Nānārammaṇesuca nesaṃ chandovā nikantivā pavattatiyeva. Yena nānākammānipi vipaccituṃ okāsaṃ labhanti. Yenaca te cakkhu sotadvārehipi tato cavanti. Tasmā ettha upacārajjhānena kāraṇaṃ avatvā vuttanayeneva taṃkāraṇaṃ vattuṃ yuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kāmatihetumhā cutiyā paraṃ sabbā vīsati paṭisandhiyo siyuṃ. Itarā duhetukāhetukacutito paraṃ kāmesveva bhavesu dasapaṭisandhiyo siyunti yojanā. Evaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe visayappavattiyā saha vīthimuttacittānaṃ pavattākāraṃ dassetvā idāni pavattikāle paraṃparabhavesuca dassetuṃ iccevantiādimāha. Paṭisandhinirodhānantaratoti paṭisandhiyā nirodhassa bhaṅgassa anantarakālato. [M 0.0268] Tamevacittanti tassadise tabbohāro daṭṭhabbo. Yathā tāniyeva osadhānīti. Yāva cuticittuppādāti ettha cutiggahaṇena tadāsanna vīthicittānampi gahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Asati vīthicittuppādeti antarantarā vīthicittānaṃ uppattiyā asati. Bhavassaaṅgabhāvenāti upapattibhavassa aviccheda kāraṇabhāvena. Tasmiṃti avattamāne pacchājātapaccayarahitānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ vassodaka rahitānaṃ taruṇasassānaṃ viya milāta bhāvapattiyā upapattibhavo occhijjatīti. Cuticittaṃ hutvā nirujjhati tameva cittanti sambandho. Yathākkamaṃ eva parivattantā pavattantīti yāva parinibbānacutiyā yathākkamaṃ parivattantā pavattantieva. Na pana parasamaye viya kadāci katthaci nivattiṃ pāpuṇantīti attho.

For if that were said with reference to the giving of rebirth-linking, a two-rooted rebirth-linking would not be appropriate. For it is not possible that access concentration, which occurs in the absorption process of one whose hindrances are well suppressed, could be anything inferior to three-rooted. But if it were said with reference to supporting another kamma, there would be no reason for it to support a weaker other kamma without giving rebirth itself, even though it is stronger. However, since for the fine-material brahmās other wholesome kammas of body, speech, and mind do arise, and some of these are inferior to three-rooted while some are two-rooted and excellent; and since for them, because their gross hindrances are well suppressed, two-rooted inferior kammas that generate a defective rebirth-linking do not arise, and such kammas belonging to a subsequent time also do not find an opportunity; and since, moreover, their desire or longing does operate in regard to various objects, whereby various kammas find an opportunity to ripen, and whereby they pass away from there even through the eye- and ear-doors—therefore, it should be understood that here it is proper to state the reason in the way already explained, without stating access concentration as the reason. The connection is: After a three-rooted death in the sense sphere, all twenty rebirth-linkings may occur. After other two-rooted or rootless deaths, only ten rebirth-linkings may occur, and only in sense-sphere existences. Having thus shown the mode of occurrence of process-freed consciousnesses together with the occurrence of their object at the rebirth-linking moment, now, to explain the subsequent continuity in this and future existences, he begins with 'Thus…' and so on. 'Immediately after the cessation of rebirth-linking' means from the time immediately after the dissolution, i.e., the breaking up, of the rebirth-linking. 'That very consciousness': this usage should be understood as referring to something of the same kind, as in 'those very medicinal herbs.' 'Until the arising of the death-consciousness': here, the taking up of 'death' should be understood to include also the process-consciousness near to it. 'In the absence of the arising of process-consciousness' means in the absence of the intermittent arising of process-consciousness. 'As a factor of existence' means by being the cause for the uninterrupted continuation of rebirth-existence. 'When that is not occurring': the rebirth-existence is cut off, like young crops withering without rainwater because the material phenomena are devoid of the postnascent condition. 'Having become the death-consciousness, it ceases; that very consciousness…': this is the connection. 'They proceed changing in sequence': they continue to change and occur in sequence until the final parinibbāna of the aggregates. The meaning is that they do not, as at other times, come to a halt anywhere at any time.

[174] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

But what is to be made clear:

“Yāva vaṭṭa mūla samucchedā”ti vuttaṃ, vaṭṭamūlasamucchedo vuccati arahattamaggo. Tato paraṃpi yāvakhandhaparinibbānā pavattantiyeva.

It is said: 'Until the utter extirpation of the root of the round.' The utter extirpation of the root of the round is called the path of arahantship. Even after that, they continue right up to the final parinibbāna of the aggregates.

Ihāti imasmiṃ bhave. Iccayanti iti ayaṃ. Itisaddo ādiattho. Yathā iha paṭisandhica bhavaṅgañca āvajjanādi vīthiyoca cuticāti ayaṃ cittasantati pavattati. Tathā puna bhavantarepi sandhibhavaṅgādikā ayaṃcittasantati parivattati parivattamānā pavattatīti attho. Idāni yassa vipassanā maggaphalanibbānassa atthāya cittacetasikānaṃ pabhedapavattisaṅgahā paṭṭhapiyanti. Tadatthaṃ dassento gāthamāha. Tattha paṭisaṅkhāyāti paṭisaṅkhāna saṅkhātena vipassanā ñāṇena punappunaṃ ñatvā. Etanti yathāvuttaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ pabhedapavattividhānaṃ. Adhuvanti aniccaṃ. Adhigantvāti adhigamasaṅkhātena catumaggaññāṇena patilabhitvā sacchikatvā. Padanti saupādisesaṃ nibbānaṃ. Budhāti paṇḍitā. Suṭṭhu anusaya mattaṃpi asesetvā sesakilesehi saddhiṃ ucchinnaṃ yathā vuttesu cittacetasikesu adhisayitaṃ taṇhāsineha saṅkhātaṃ [M 0.0269] bandhanaṃ etehīti susamucchinna sineha bandhanā. Samanti vūpasamanti vaṭṭadukkhasantāpā etasminti samo. Anupādisesanibbānaṃ. Essantīti gamissanti. Cirāyāti cirakālaṃ. Sundaraṃ adhigamāvahaṃ sīla dhutaṅgasaṅkhātaṃ vataṃ etesanti subbatā. Suparisuddhasīlasallekha vuttinoti attho. Cirāya subbatā budhā etaṃ adhuvaṃ paṭisaṅkhāya accutaṃ padaṃ adhigantvā susamucchinnasinehabandhanā samaṃ essantīti yojanā.

Iha means 'in this existence'. Iccayanti means 'thus, this'. The word 'iti' has the sense of 'and so on'. Just as in this existence this continuity of mind proceeds through rebirth-linking, the life-continuum, adverting, and other cognitive processes up to death, so too in another existence this continuity of mind, beginning with rebirth-linking and the life-continuum, revolves, and in revolving, proceeds—this is the meaning. Now, for the sake of insight, path, fruition, and Nibbāna, for which the compendia on the classification and occurrence of mind and mental factors are established, he speaks a verse to show this purpose. Herein, 'paṭisaṅkhāya' means having repeatedly known through the insight knowledge called 'thorough reflection'. 'Etaṃ' refers to the classification and modes of occurrence of mind and mental factors as described. 'Adhuvaṃ' means impermanent. 'Adhigantvā' means having attained and realized through the knowledge of the four paths, which is called 'attainment'. 'Padaṃ' means Nibbāna with residue remaining. 'Budhā' means the wise. 'Susamucchinna sinehabandhanā' means those by whom the bond of craving, called 'sineha' (affection), which lies latent in the mind and mental factors as described, has been completely severed, having thoroughly eradicated even the slightest trace of latent tendencies along with the remaining defilements. 'Samaṃ' means that wherein the suffering and torment of the cycle of existence cease—thus, 'samo' (peace). It refers to Nibbāna without residue remaining. 'Essanti' means they will go. 'Cirāya' means for a long time. 'Subbatā' refers to those whose vows, consisting of virtue and ascetic practices, bring about beautiful attainments; the meaning is 'those of supremely purified virtue and austere practice'. The construction is as follows: The wise, who are of excellent vows, having for a long time thoroughly reflected on this impermanence, having attained the deathless state, and having completely severed the bonds of craving, will go to peace.

Iti paramatthadīpaniyānāma abhidhammatthasaṅgahassa

Thus, in the Paramatthadīpanī, the commentary on the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha,

Catutthavaṇṇanāya vīthimutta saṅgahassa

The Fourth Explanation of the Compendium on the Process-Freed.

Paramatthadīpanā niṭṭhitā.

The Paramatthadīpanā is completed.

Rūpa saṅgaha paramatthadīpanī

The Paramatthadīpanī on the Compendium of Materiality

156. Evaṃ [M 0.0270] cittacetasike dvīhi pabhedappavattīhi dassetvā idāni yathānuppattaṃ rūpaṃ dassento ādigātha māha. Tattha etaṃ parimāṇaṃ assāti ettāvaṃ. Tena ettavatā. Nipātapadaṃvā etaṃ. Hi saddo padapūraṇe. Pabhedoca pavattica pabhedappavattiyo. Tāhi saha ye vattanti te sappabhedappavattikā. Ettāvatā sappabhedappavattikā cittacetasikā dhammā mayā vibhattā. Idāni rūpaṃ pavuccatīti yojanā. Saṅkhepato uddisanaṃ kathanaṃ samuddeso. Samuddiṭṭhassa rūpassa puna vibhajanaṃ vibhāgo. Samuṭṭhāti rūpaṃ etenāti samuṭṭhānaṃ. Kammādi. Kalā vuccanti avayavā. Tā appenti pavisanti etthāti kalāpo. Piṇḍīti attho. Pavattikkamatoti uppattikkamato. Salakkhaṇato sasambhāratoca mahantāni hutvā bhavanti pātubhavantīti mahābhūtāni. Tāni hi attano sabhāvatopi mahantānieva hutvā pātubhavanti upādārūpāni upādāyāti.

156. Having thus shown mind and mental factors by their two aspects of classification and occurrence, now, to present material form in due order, the initial verse is spoken. Herein, 'ettāvaṃ' means 'so much', from 'etaṃ parimāṇaṃ assa' (let this be the measure). By that much, 'ettāvatā'. Or this is a particle. The word 'hi' is a mere expletive. Classification and occurrence are 'pabhedappavattiyo'. Those that occur together with these are 'sappabhedappavattikā'. The construction is as follows: 'By this much, the mind and mental factors with their classifications and occurrences have been analyzed by me. Now material form is spoken of'. The brief statement is the enumeration (samuddeso). The further analysis of the material form that has been enumerated is the division (vibhāgo). 'That by which material form arises' is the origin (samuṭṭhānaṃ), such as kamma. Parts are called 'kalā'. They enter and come together herein—thus 'kalāpa'. The meaning is 'group' or 'mass'. 'Pavattikkamato' means 'according to the sequence of occurrence', i.e., according to the sequence of arising. Because they become great and manifest by their own characteristics and by their constituents, they are called 'mahābhūtāni' (great elements). For they become great and manifest by their own nature, and derived material forms are so called because they are dependent upon them.

[175] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana mahāṭīkāyañca

[175] However, in the Vibhāvanī and the Great Commentary,

“Sasambhāradhātuvasenāti” vuttaṃ. Taṃ anupapannaṃ.

It is said: 'by way of the element of their own constituents.' That is untenable.

Na hi sasambhāravatthuvaseneva tesaṃ ayaṃ vohāro pavattoti sakkā vattuṃ. Naca salakkhaṇato mahattena vinā tesaṃ sasambhārato mahattaṃnāma sambhavatīti. Tasmā yaṃ tesaṃ indriyānindriyabaddhasantānesu pathavipabbatādivasena samudde macchakacchapādivasena sasambhārato mahattaṃ. Taṃpi salakkhaṇamahattamūlakamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Mahābhūtātivā loke visaṃvāda kaṭṭhena māyākārāvā āvisanagahaṇesu acinteyyaṭṭhānaṭṭhena yakkhādayovā vañcakaṭṭhena yakkhiniyovā vuccanti. Tenevaṭṭhena tehi sadisattā imānipi mahābhūtāviyāti mahābhūtāni. Ubhayatthapica [M 0.0271] mahantāni abhūtāni abbhutānivā etesūti nibbacanaṃ yujjatiyeva.

For it cannot be said that this designation of theirs arises merely by way of their constituent basis. Nor does greatness by way of their constituents occur in them without greatness by way of their own characteristics. Therefore, whatever greatness they possess by way of their constituents—such as mountains and the like in the continuity bound to faculties and not bound to faculties, or fish and turtles in the ocean—that too should be understood as rooted in the greatness of their own characteristics. Alternatively, in the world, magicians who deceive with wooden devices, or yakshas and the like who are inconceivable in their entering and seizing, or yakkhinīs who are deceptive, are called 'mahābhūtā' (great beings). For this very reason, because these elements resemble them, they too are called 'mahābhūtāni'. And in both cases, the derivation 'mahantāni abhūtāni abbhutāni vā etesu' (great and non-existent or wonderful things are in them) is indeed appropriate.

[176] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[176] However, in the Vibhāvanī,

Yakkhiniṃ visuṃ upamāmattaṃ katvā “manāpavaṇṇasaṇṭhānā dīhivā sattānaṃ vañcikā yakkhinīādayo viya manāpa itthipurisarūpadassanādinā sattānaṃ vañcakattā mahantāni abhūtāni etesūti mahābhūtāti” vuttaṃ. Taṃ aṭṭhakathā ya na sameti.

Having made the yakkhiṇī a separate, mere comparison, it is said: 'Because they are deceivers of beings by showing pleasing forms of men and women, like yakkhiṇīs and the like who deceive beings with pleasing appearance and form, therefore they are 'mahābhūtā' (great elements) because there are great non-existent things in them'. This does not accord with the commentary.

Aṭṭhakathāyañhi mahābhūtasāmaññatoti padassa vitthāre eva māyākāro yakkho yakkhinīti tayo mahābhūtā vuttāti. Catunnañcamahābhūtānanti upayogatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Upādāyāti daḷhaṃ nissāya. Pavattanti pāṭhaseso. Upādāya rūpantivā samāsapadaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

For in the commentary, in the detailed explanation of the word 'mahābhūtasāmaññato', it is stated that the magician, the yaksha, and the yakkhinī are three 'mahābhūtā' (great beings). The genitive case in 'catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ' (of the four great elements) is in the sense of dependence. 'Upādāya' means 'firmly relying on'. 'Pavattanti' is a remainder of the text. Or 'upādāya rūpaṃ' should be understood as a compound word.

[177] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[177] However, in the Vibhāvanī,

“Upādāya pavattaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpanti” vuttaṃ. Taṃ idha na yujjati.

It is said: 'Material form that occurs dependently is derived material form (upādārūpa).' That is not appropriate here.

Na hi imasmiṃ pāṭhe katthaci yakāraviraho diṭṭho. Tathā hi mūlaṭīkāyaṃ upādāyati nissayatīti upādāyaṃ. Tameva rūpantipi vuttaṃ. Pathayatīti pathavī. Sahajātarūpānaṃ patiṭṭhāna bhāvena pakkhāyati upaṭṭhātīti attho. Puthu mahantī hutvā jāyatītipi pathavī. Pakārena thavīyati sabbesaṃ rūpasambhārānaṃ adhiṭṭhānattā. Ayaṃ tesaṃ adhiṭṭhānā patiṭṭhānā vatthubhūtā bhūmi bhūtātiādinā nānāppakārena guṇapadena abhitthavīyatīti pathavī. Sāeva nisattanijīvaṭṭhena dhātūti pathavīdhātu. Āpeti sahajātarūpāni byāpetvā tiṭṭhati, appāyati vā tāni suṭṭhu brūheti vaḍḍhetīti āpo. Tānivā avippakiṇṇāni katvā bhuso pāti rakkhati, pivativā vivanto viya tāni saṅgaṇhati sampiṇḍetīti āpo. Soyeva dhātūti āpodhātu. Te jati tikkhabhāvena samujjalanto viya sahajātadhammānaṃ majjhe pakāsati, [M 0.0272] tejetivā niseti sahajātadhamme tikkhathāma bale karoti, paripācetivā usmāpetīti tejo, so eva dhātūti tejodhātu. Vāyati samīreti desantaruppatti hetubhāvena bhūtasaṅghāṭaṃ desantaraṃ gametīti vāyo. Vāyati vā sahajātadhamme apatamāne katvā vahatīti vāyo. Soeva dhātūti vāyodhātu. Tattha kakkhaḷalakkhaṇā pathavī. Ābandhanalakkhaṇo āpo. Uṇhattalakkhaṇo tejo. Vitthambhanalakkhaṇo vāyo. Ettha siyā, kasmā pathavī kakkhaḷalakkhaṇāti vuttā. Nanu sā mudubhūtāpi hotīti. Saccaṃ, mudubhūtāpi pana sā sesabhūtattayaṃ upādāya kakkhaḷā tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Aññamaññaṃ upādāyeva pana ayaṃmudu ayaṃ kakkhaḷāti bhavati. Teneva mudukakkhaḷānaṃ dīgharassānaṃ viya anavaṭṭhānatā hoti. Mudubhūtāpi hi tato mudutaraṃ patvā kakkhaḷānāma jātā. Kakkhaḷāpi kakkhaḷataraṃ patvā mudubhūtānāma jātāti. Ābandhanalakkhaṇo āpoti vutto. Soca pakatiudake adhimattoti pakatiudakaṃ baddhaṃ ghanībhūtameva siyāti ce. Na. Ābandhitabbāya pathaviyā tattha paridubbalattāti, yattha pana pathavī balavatī hoti tattheva so baddhataraṃ ābandhatīti. Uṇhatta lakkhaṇo tejoti vutto. Evañcasati sītabhāvo tejoyeva na siyāti ce. Na. Usati dahati paripāceti pariṇa tabhāvaṃ gametīti uṇhonāma. Sītabhāvoca dahati paripāceti tabbhāvaṃ gametiyevāti. Vuttañca mūlaṭīkāyaṃ tejoeva hi sītaṃ. Himapātasamayādīsu sītassa paripācakatādassana toti. Vitthambhana lakkhaṇo vāyoti vutto. So pana ghana thaddhesu silāthambhādīsu nalabbhatīti ce. Na. Tattha hi pathavī attanā sahajātavāyuvitthambhanaṃ labhitvā thāmappattā thiratarappattāca hutvā vahatīti. Cakkhatīti cakkhu. Samavisamaṃ ācikkhati samavisamajānanassa tammūlakattā. Rūpaṃvā assādeti āpātaṃ āgatāgatassa rūpassa anirākaraṇato. Taṃvā vibhāvetīti attho. Suṇātīti sotaṃ. Suṇanti suyyantivā ete nāti [M 0.0273] sotaṃ. Ghāyatīti ghānaṃ. Ghāyanti ghāyiyantivā etenāti ghānaṃ. Jīvitanimittaṃ raso jīvitanti vuccati. Tasmiṃ ninnatāya taṃ avhāyatīti jivhā. Athavā. Jīvitaṃ vahati etāyavā taṃ vahanti pavattenti jīvitavuttisampādanattāti jivhā. Jītivā jayo parājayovā vuccati. Tadubhayaṃ vahati vahantivā etāyāti jivhā. Sasambhārajivhā. Yathāha –

For in this text, the absence of the letter 'y' is nowhere seen. Thus, in the Subcommentary it is said: 'It depends on, it relies on' (upādāyati nissayati), hence upādāyaṃ. That very form is also stated. 'It extends' (pathayati), hence 'earth' (pathavī). The meaning is that it is manifest (pakkhāyati) as a foundation (patiṭṭhāna) for co-nascent material phenomena, that is, it serves as their support. Or, 'it comes to be (jāyati) as something extensive (puthu), great (mahantī),' hence pathavī. 'It is praised (thavīyati) in various ways (pakārena) because it is the basis (adhiṭṭhāna) for all collections of material phenomena.' 'It is extolled (abhitthavīyati) with various qualitative terms such as: "This is their basis, their foundation, their ground, their footing,"' hence pathavī. That very thing, in the sense of being non-sentient and lifeless, is an element (dhātu), hence the 'earth element' (pathavīdhātu). 'It pervades' (āpeti) co-nascent material phenomena and subsists by pervading them; or 'it makes them grow' (appāyati), that is, it nourishes (brūheti) and increases (vaḍḍheti) them, hence 'water' (āpo). 'Or, having made them unscattered, it protects (pāti) them well; or, as if drinking, it gathers (saṅgaṇhati) and binds them together (sampiṇḍeti),' hence āpo. That very thing is an element, hence the 'water element' (āpodhātu). 'It shines' (tejati), that is, with its sharpness it appears as if blazing and is manifest (pakāsati) among co-nascent phenomena; 'or it sharpens' (tejeti), that is, it makes co-nascent phenomena keen, strong, and powerful; 'or it matures' (paripāceti), that is, it heats them, hence 'fire' (tejo). That very thing is an element, hence the 'fire element' (tejodhātu). 'It moves' (vāyati), that is, it impels (samīreti); by being the cause for arising in another place, it makes the material composite move (gameti) to another place, hence 'air' (vāyo). 'Or it blows' (vāyati), that is, it carries (vahati) co-nascent phenomena, preventing them from falling, hence vāyo. That very thing is an element, hence the 'air element' (vāyodhātu). Therein, the earth element has the characteristic of hardness. The water element has the characteristic of cohesion. The fire element has the characteristic of heat. The air element has the characteristic of distension. Here it might be asked: Why is it said that the earth element has the characteristic of hardness? Is it not also soft? True, but even when it is soft, in relation to the other three elements it is reckoned only as hard. For it is only in relation to one another that something is 'soft' and something is 'hard.' Thus, like long and short, there is no fixed state. For what is soft, on encountering what is softer, becomes designated 'hard'; and what is hard, on encountering what is harder, becomes designated 'soft.' It is said that the water element has the characteristic of cohesion. If so, since this is abundant in natural water, natural water should be bound and solidified. This is not so, because there the earth element to be bound is very weak. But where the earth element is strong, there it binds more firmly. It is said that the fire element has the characteristic of heat. If this is so, then coldness would not be fire at all. This is not so. Because it burns (usati), consumes (dahati), matures (paripāceti), and brings to a state of change (pariṇatabhāvaṃ gameti), it is called 'heat' (uṇha). And the state of coldness also consumes, matures, and brings to that same state. And it is said in the Subcommentary: 'For cold itself is fire, because in times of snowfall and so on, cold is seen to have a maturing effect.' It is said that the air element has the characteristic of distension. But this is not found in dense, rigid things like stone pillars. This is not so. For there the earth element, having obtained the distension of the co-nascent air element, becomes strong and very firm, and thus it endures. 'It indicates' (cakkhati), hence 'eye' (cakkhu). It points out what is even and uneven, because the knowledge of even and uneven is rooted in it. Or, it 'savors' form, in the sense of not rejecting a form that has come into its range. Or, the meaning is, 'it clarifies it.' 'One hears' (suṇāti) with it, hence 'ear' (sota). Or, 'sounds are heard' (suyyanti) by this, hence sota. 'One smells' (ghāyati) with it, hence 'nose' (ghāna). Or, 'odors are smelled' (ghāyiyanti) by this, hence ghāna. The taste that is a condition for life (jīvita) is called 'life.' Because it is inclined towards that and 'calls for' (avhāyati) it, it is called 'tongue' (jivhā). Alternatively, 'it carries (vahati) life (jīvita)' or 'they carry or maintain it by means of this,' because it helps to accomplish the process of life, hence jivhā. Or, jīti means victory or defeat. 'It carries (vahati) both of these' or 'they carry them by means of this,' hence jivhā. The tongue with its supporting matter. As it is said:

Purisassa hi jātassa, kudārī jāyate mukhe;

Yāya chindati attānaṃ, naro dubbhāsitaṃ bhaṇanti.

For when a person is born, an axe is born in his mouth, with which the fool, speaking ill-spoken words, cuts himself.

Idha pana taṃ sahacaritattā jivhāti pasādarūpamo vuccati. Kucchitānaṃ kesādīnaṃ pāpadhammānañca āyo uppattiṭṭhānanti kāyo. Sasambhārakāyo. Idha pana taṃ sahacarito pasāda kāyoeva adhippeto. Pasīdantīti pasādā. Pasīdanti vā ettha candamaṇḍalādīni ārammaṇanimittāni tattha saṃsīdamānāni viya sarūpato sandissantīti pasādā, suparisuddhaādāsamaṇḍasadisā kammajamaṇḍā. Ime pana pañca daṭṭhukāmatādi nidāna kammasamuṭṭhāna bhūtapasāda lakkhaṇā rūpādi abhighātāraha bhūtapasādalakkhaṇā vā cakkhupasādādayo daṭṭhabbā. Tattha cakkhu tāva setamaṇḍala parikkhittassa kaṇhamaṇḍalassa majjhe ūkāsirapamāṇe atimukhe ṭhitānaṃ sarīrasaṇṭhānuppatti padesabhūte diṭṭhamaṇḍale telamiva sattapicupaṭalāni sattaakkhipaṭalāni byāpetvā tiṭṭhati. Sotaṃ sotabilabbhantare aṅguliveṭhanākāraṃ upacitatanutambalomaṃ padesaṃ byāpetvā tiṭṭhati. Ghānaṃ nāsikabbhantare ajapadasaṇṭhānaṃ padesaṃ byāpetvā tiṭṭhati. Jivhā sasambhāra jivhāmajjhe uppala dalagga saṇṭhānaṃ padesaṃ byāpetvā tiṭṭhati. Kāyo pana mahanti yā kappāsa paṭalavaṭṭiyaṃ āsittatelaṃviya thapetvā pācaka tejassa patiṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ kesagga lomagga nakhagga sukkhacammānica avasesaṃ sakalasarīraṃ byāpetvā tiṭṭhatīti. Te pana pañca yathārahaṃ pañcadvārikacittānaṃ vatthudvārabhāvaṃ sādhenti. Tesuca ekekassa catasso catasso dhātuyo sandhāraṇaābandhana paripācana samudīraṇa kiccehi upakāraṃ karonti. Yathākhatti yakumārassa [M 0.0274] catasso dhātiyo dhāraṇa nahāpana maṇḍana bījana kiccehīti. Utucittāhārāca naṃ upatthambhenti. Yathā taṃ khattiyakumāraṃ pitu jeṭṭhabhātu jeṭṭhabhaginiyoviya. Āyuca naṃ suṭṭhu anupāleti. Yathā taṃ khattiyakumāraṃ disāpāmokkho rājasammato mahābhisakkoviya. Vaṇṇādayoca naṃ parivārenti. Yathā taṃ khattiyakumāraṃ sahajātā amaccaputtā viyāti. Yasmā pana sattānaṃ cittaṃ nāma vicittaṃ hoti. Cittavicittatāya saññāvicittā. Saññāvicittatāya taṇhāvicittā. Taṇhāvicitta tāya kammāni vicittāni. Kammavicittatāya kammasamuṭṭhānāni bhūtāni vicittāni. Bhūtavicittatāya ime pasādā vicittā. Aññamaññaṃ asadisā honti. Tehi pasādamaṇḍabhūtāpi samānā keci rūpasseva abhighātārahā honti, na saddādīnaṃ. Keci saddādīnaṃ eva, na rūpassāti. Tasmā tesaṃ aññamaññañca aññarūpehica lakkhaṇato asaṃmissatā veditabbāti.

Here, however, on account of its association with the physical tongue, the sensitive matter is also called 'tongue.' The body (kāyo) is so called because it is the source (āyo) and place of origin of repulsive things such as hair, etc., and of bad things. The body with its components. Here, however, what is intended is the sensitive body associated with it. They are called 'sensitivities' (pasādā) because they make clear (pasīdanti). Or, because objects and signs like the moon's disk become clear in them, appearing in their own nature as if settling down in them, they are called 'sensitivities.' They are kamma-born spheres similar to a perfectly clear mirror. These five—the eye-sensitivity and so on—should be understood as having the characteristic of being sensitivities that have arisen from kamma conditioned by the desire to see, etc., or as having the characteristic of being sensitivities fit to be impinged upon by form, etc. Therein, the eye-sensitivity is situated in the middle of the black disk surrounded by the white disk, in the pupil which is the size of a louse's head and is the region where the body's formation originates. It pervades the seven layers of the eye like oil in seven cotton wicks. The ear-sensitivity is situated inside the ear-hole, in the place shaped like a finger-ring, which is covered with fine, copper-colored hairs, and it pervades that region. The nose-sensitivity is situated inside the nostril, in the place shaped like a goat's hoof, and it pervades that region. The tongue-sensitivity is situated in the middle of the physical tongue, in the place shaped like the tip of a blue lotus petal, and it pervades that region. The body-sensitivity, however, is vast. Like oil poured on a roll of cotton cloth, it pervades the entire body, except for the place that is the basis for the digestive fire, and the tips of the head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, and dry skin. These five, as appropriate, serve as the basis and door for the five-door consciousnesses. And for each of them, the four great elements provide support through their respective functions of supporting, binding, maturing, and impelling, just as four nurses serve a khattiya prince with the duties of carrying, bathing, adorning, and fanning. Temperature, consciousness, and nutriment sustain them, just as a khattiya prince is supported by his father, elder brother, and elder sister. The life faculty protects them well, just as a great physician honored by the king protects a khattiya prince. Color and the other derived material phenomena surround them, just as the sons of ministers born at the same time surround a khattiya prince. Because the minds of beings are diverse, their perceptions are diverse. Because their perceptions are diverse, their craving is diverse. Because their craving is diverse, their kammas are diverse. Because their kammas are diverse, the primary elements born of kamma are diverse. Because the primary elements are diverse, these sensitivities are diverse and dissimilar to one another. For this reason, though they are all sensitive spheres, some are receptive only to the impact of form, not of sound, etc.; others are receptive only to sound, etc., not to form. Therefore, their unmixedness with one another and with other kinds of matter should be understood in terms of their characteristics.
