Tasmā idha atītabhave avijjāya siddhāya tassāadhiṭṭhānabhūto attabhāvopi tasmiṃ bhave sijjhatiyeva. Sijjhanto ca imassaṃ dasanoyaṃ vutta nayena aññāya avijjāya eva sijjhati, na aññathā. Evañca sabhi puna tassapi adhiṭṭhānabhūto attabhāvo sijjhatiyevāti avijjā attabhāvocāti ubhayaṃ petaṃ anavaṭṭhitaṃ anādikameva hotīti. Vaṭṭassa pana tividhassapi padhānapaccayabhūtattā sā vaṭṭakathāya sīsabhūtā hoti. Yadi sā vaṭṭassa ādibhūtā na hoti. Atha tassāpi paccayo vattabboti. Saccaṃ. Tassā pana [M 0.0387] paccaye vuttepi tassa paccayassapi paccayo vattabboti āgacchatiyeva. Evañca sati tassa tassāti niṭṭhānameva napaññā yeyyāti. Aññattha pana vuttoyeva. Yathāha-āsavasamudayā avijjāsamudayoti. Yathācāha-avijjaṃ pāhaṃ bhikkhave sāhāraṃ sanidānaṃ vadāmi. Kocassā āhāro. Pañcanīvaraṇā tissa vacanīyanti. Yathācāha-avijjā paccayo, saṅkhārā paccayuppannā. Ubhayametaṃ paṭicca samuppannanti. Paṭhapesīti paññāpesi desesīti attho. [Paṭiccasamuppādanayo.]

Here, in this way, they are bound again and again, by the method stated beginning with 'aging and death, infatuation, and so on'. Why is it said to be without beginning? Is not ignorance mentioned as the beginning? It is said: it is not mentioned as the beginning in the sense of being the actual origin of the round. It is mentioned as the beginning because it is the head of the discourse on the round. Yet, even when stated thus, the beginningless nature of the round is also shown by it. For ignorance is not found externally; it is found only in the continuum of beings—this is directly evident. Therefore, here, when ignorance is established in a past existence, the individual existence that is its basis also arises in that existence. And arising thus, this individual existence, by the method stated in this exposition, arises dependent on another ignorance and not otherwise. And when this is the case, again, the individual existence that is its basis also arises. Thus, both ignorance and individual existence are unestablished and without beginning. Moreover, because it is the chief condition for the threefold round, it is the head of the discourse on the round. If it were not the origin of the round, then its condition would have to be stated. True. But even if its condition is stated, the condition of that condition would also have to be stated, and so on indefinitely. In this way, there would be no end, and no wisdom would arise. Elsewhere, it is indeed stated: 'With the arising of the taints, there is the arising of ignorance.' And as it is said: 'Monks, I say that ignorance has nutriment, has a source.' What is its nutriment? The five hindrances should be mentioned. And as it is said: 'Ignorance is a condition, formations are conditionally arisen. Both are dependently arisen.' 'Paṭhapesī' means 'he made known, he taught'—this is the meaning. [The method of dependent origination.]

167. Idāni paṭṭhānanayaṃ dassetuṃ hetupaccayotiādi āraddhaṃ. Tatthahetuca so paccayocāti hetupaccayo, hetu hutvā paccayo hetubhāvena paccayoti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha kenaṭṭhena hetūti mūlaṭṭhena, koca mūlaṭṭhoti. Rukkhānaṃ rukkhamūlassa viya bhūmiyaṃ sahajātadhammānaṃ ārammaṇesu suppatiṭṭhi tabhāvasādhanaṭṭho mūlaṭṭhonāma. Sahajātadhammānaṃ kusalādi bhāvasādhanaṭṭho mūlaṭṭhonāmātipi vadanti. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Saddatthato pana hinonti vuddhiviruḷhivepullapattivasena suṭṭhu patiṭṭhahanti sahajātadhammā ettha etenavā ārammaṇe daḷhanipātinā thāmabalasampannenāti hetu. Paccaya saddo pana upakārakaṭṭho. Upakārakotica sayaṃ yādisena sabhāvena upalabbhamāne anuppannāvā dhammā uppajjanti. Uppannāvā tiṭṭhanti ṭhitāvā uparuparivuddhiviruḷhiyā paccayattaṃ upagacchanti. Tādi senasabhāvena upaladdhiyeva. Nahi sabhāvadhammesu īhāvā byāpārovā upalabbhati. Yena kattāvā kāretāvā upalabbheyyāti. Tathā upaladdhiyaṃ pana sati anurūpānaṃ paccayuppannadhammānaṃ anuppannānaṃvā uppajjanato uppannānaṃvā ṭhitibhāvapattito ṭhitānaṃ vā uparuparivuddhiviruḷhiyā paccayattupagamanato suṭṭhu karānto viya sādhento viya hotīti katvā upakārako tveva vuccatīti. Iti ārammaṇe thirabhāvavuddhi viruḷhibhāvasādhana saṅkhātena mūlabhāvena upakārakā chahetudhammā hetupaccayo nāma.

167. Now, to explain the method of the Paṭṭhāna, the section beginning with 'root condition' (hetupaccayo) is commenced. Herein, 'hetu' and also 'paccaya'—thus, 'hetupaccaya'. It is said that it is a condition by being a root, by the nature of a root. Herein, in what sense is it a root? In the sense of being a foundation. And what is the sense of being a foundation? Just as the root of a tree is to the earth, so too, for co-arisen phenomena (sahajātadhammā), the sense of being a foundation is the accomplishment of their firm establishment in their objects (ārammaṇa). Some also say that the sense of being a foundation is the accomplishment of the state of wholesome and other co-arisen phenomena. What should be said here has already been stated below. From the perspective of the meaning of the word, however, 'hetu' (root) is that by which co-arisen phenomena are firmly established here, in this object, either by it or in it, because they grow, increase, and reach abundance, by that which is strong, firmly planted, and endowed with powerful strength. The term 'condition' (paccaya), however, signifies the sense of being supportive. And 'supportive' means that when it is found with its own nature, unarisen phenomena arise, arisen phenomena persist, and those that persist attain the state of being a condition for further growth and development. Such is the nature of its being found. For in intrinsic phenomena (sabhāvadhammesu), no exertion or effort is found—by which a doer or instigator could be found. Yet, when such a finding exists, since suitable unarisen conditioned phenomena arise, arisen ones attain stability, and stable ones become a condition for further growth and development, it is as if it were thoroughly acting or accomplishing. Therefore, it is simply called 'supportive'. Thus, the six root phenomena (chahetudhammā) are called the root condition (hetupaccayo) because they are supportive, with the nature of a foundation, designated as accomplishing firm establishment, increase, and flourishing in their object.

Āramanti [M 0.0388] cittacetasikā dhammā suṭṭhu ratiṃ anubhavantā viya ajjholambamānā pavattanti etthāti ārammaṇaṃ. Ārammaṇabhāneva upakārakā chaḷārammaṇadhammā ārammaṇapaccayo. Adhipati saddattho heṭṭhā vuttoyeva. Adhipati bhāvena upakārako dhammo adhipatipaccayo. So duvidho ārammaṇādhipati sahājātādhipativasena. Ārammaṇadhammāpi hi keci garukatā attano ārammaṇikadhamme sāmino viya dāse attano vasevattayamānā attani niccaṃ ninnapoṇapabbhāreeva karontīti. Natthi antaraṃ etassāti anantaro, anantarabhāvena upakārako dhammo anantarapaccayo. Suṭṭhu anantarabhāvena upakārako dhammo samanantarapaccayo. Imesaṃ dvinnaṃ paccayānaṃ dhammato viseso natthi. Atthato pana purimacitte niruddhepi pacchā santānaṃ ucchijjituṃ adatvā santānānubandhavasena sārammaṇadhamma bhāvena attasadisassa dhammantarassa uppādanaṃ anantarapaccayatā. Dhammantare uppādiyamānepi yaṃkiñci dhammaṃ anuppādetvā paṭisandhādīnaṃ kiccaṭṭhānānaṃ paṭipāṭiyā cittaniyāmaṃ nāma sādhetvā anurūpasseva dhammantarassa uppādanaṃ samanantarapaccayatāti. Evañhi sati nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa asaññasattā cavantassaca purimapacchimabhāgapavattānaṃ cittuppādānaṃpi anantaratā samanantaratāca upapannā hotīti. Nahi abhāva bhūto antare kālo tesaṃ antaraṃ karotināma. Naca aññasantānabhūto antare rūpadhammo. Aññañhi rūpasantānaṃ, aññaṃ arūpasantānaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana kālānantaratā samanantarapaccayoti vādaṃ paṭikkhipitvā saṇṭhānābhāvato suṭṭhu anantarāti samanantarāti vuttaṃ. Etena yathāsaṇṭhānavantānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ anantaratānāma majjhe paricchedasahitāyeva hoti. Na tathā saṇṭhānarahitānaṃ arūpadhammānaṃ. Tasmā purimapacchimānaṃ tesaṃ ekībhūtānaṃ viya pavattisamanantaratānāma. Tathā pavattana samatthatā samanantarapaccayatāti dasseti.

Consciousness and mental factors delight in it, they proceed clinging to it as if experiencing great enjoyment—thus, it is called an object (ārammaṇa). The six object-phenomena that are helpful by way of being objects are the object condition. The meaning of the term 'adhipati' has already been stated below. A phenomenon that is helpful by way of being dominant is the dominance condition. It is twofold: by way of object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Indeed, some object-phenomena, by their weightiness, make their object-related phenomena constantly incline and lean towards themselves, as if a master were making slaves subject to his will. There is no interval for it, hence 'immediate' (anantaro). A phenomenon that is helpful by way of being immediate is the immediate condition. A phenomenon that is helpful by way of being thoroughly immediate is the contiguity condition. There is no difference in terms of nature between these two conditions. However, in terms of meaning, the immediacy condition is the production of another phenomenon similar to itself, by way of being a phenomenon with an object, through the continuity of the stream, without allowing the subsequent continuum to be cut off, even when the preceding consciousness has ceased. Even when another phenomenon is being produced, without producing just any phenomenon, but having established the natural order of consciousness according to the sequence of functional occasions such as rebirth-linking, etc., the production of a suitable other phenomenon is the contiguity condition. This being so, the immediacy and contiguity of the consciousness-arisings occurring in the preceding and succeeding parts are established even for one emerging from cessation and for one passing away from the non-percipient realm. For no non-existent time in between creates an interval for them, nor does any material phenomenon belonging to a different continuum in between. Indeed, the material continuum is one thing, and the immaterial continuum is another. However, in the commentary, rejecting the view that temporal immediacy is the contiguity condition, it is stated that 'samanantara' means 'thoroughly immediate' (suṭṭhu anantaro) due to the absence of form. By this it is shown that for material phenomena which possess form, immediacy necessarily involves a separation in between. But it is not so for formless phenomena which lack form. Therefore, for them, the preceding and succeeding, their contiguity of occurrence is as if they were unified. Thus it is shown that the capacity to occur in such a way is the contiguity condition.

Ye pana dhammā attani jāte eva jāyanti, no ajāte. Attanā sahevaca jāyanti, no pure pacchāca, tesaṃ jātatthāya viya [M 0.0389] sayaṃ tehi saha jātabhāvena upakārako dhammo sahajātapaccayo. Pakāsassa padīpo viya. Padīpajālañhi uppajjamānaṃ pakāsasaṅkhātena ālokena saheva uppajjatīti. Aññamaññaṃ upatthambhantaṃ tidaṇḍaṃ viya aññamaññaṃ upatthambhanavasena upakārako dhammo aññamaññapaccayo. Evañca sati imassa paccayassa purimena saha viseso pākaṭo hoti. Nahi saha jātasaddo evarūpaṃ aññamaññopatthambhanaṃ bodhetīti. Nissayanti etthāti nissayo. Nissayabhāvena upakārako dhammo nissayapaccayo. So pana sahajātanissayo vatthupurejāta nissayoti duvidho hoti. Tattha sahajātova samāno paṭakoṭṭhako viya cittakammānaṃ patiṭṭhābhāvena upakārako dhammo sahajātanissayo. Pathavī viya tiṇarukkhādīnaṃ pure jāto hutvā adhiṭṭhānabhāvena upakārako vatthupurejāta nissayo. Balavataro pana nissayo upanissayo. Yathā hi sālibhattassa uppattiyā sūdovā ukkhalivākaṭṭhaṃvā aggivānissayo eva hoti, na upanissayo. Sālikhettavuṭṭhidhārā eva pana upanissayo, na hi tāsuasati bhattuppattiyā sūdādīnaṃpi thāmonāma atthīti. Tathā yahiṃ paccaye asati nissayadhammāpi natthi. Kuto nissitadhammā. So paccayo nissayatopi balavataraṭṭhena upanissayoti vuccatīti.

Now, those phenomena that arise only when they themselves have arisen, not when they have not arisen; and arise together with themselves, not before or after—a phenomenon that is helpful by way of arising together with them, as if for their arising, is the co-nascence condition. Like a lamp for light. For when a lamp flame arises, it arises together with the light called illumination. Like three sticks supporting one another, a phenomenon that is helpful by way of mutual support is the mutuality condition. And this being so, the distinction of this condition from the former becomes clear. For the term 'co-nascence' does not signify such mutual support. One depends on it, thus it is a dependence (nissaya). A phenomenon that is helpful by way of being a dependence is the dependence condition. It is twofold: co-nascence dependence and pre-nascence base dependence. Among these, a phenomenon that, being co-nascent, is helpful by way of being a foundation for mental activities, like a wall for paintings, is the co-nascence dependence. A phenomenon that, having arisen before, is helpful by way of being a foundation for grass, trees, and so forth, like the earth, is the pre-nascence base dependence. But a stronger dependence is decisive support. Just as for the production of cooked rice, a cook, a pot, firewood, or fire is merely a dependence, not a decisive support. But a rain shower on the rice field is indeed the decisive support, for in its absence, even the cook and the like have no power for the production of rice. Similarly, when that condition is absent, the dependence phenomena themselves do not exist. How then could the dependent phenomena exist? That condition, by reason of being stronger than dependence, is called 'decisive support'.

So pana ārammaṇūpanissayo anantarūpanissayo pakatūpanissayoti tividho hoti. Tattha garukatā ārammaṇa dhammā garukatattāeva adhipatibhūtā balava nissayabhūtāca honti. Anantarapaccayadhammāca tehi vinā cittasantānapavattiyā eva abhāvato balavanissayāeva honti. Pakatūpanissayoti ettha pana pakato upanissayoti pakatūpanissayo. Pakatotica yathā kate sati anurūpe kāle tasmiṃsantāne ekantena paccayuppannadhammā pātubhavanti, tathā suṭṭhu katoti attho. Karaṇañcettha saddhā sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgo paññātica rāgo doso moho māno diṭṭhi patthanātica vuttānaṃ dhammānaṃ attano [M 0.0390] santāne pubbabhāge vuttappakārena suṭṭhu uppādanaṃ. Kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ puggalo utu bhojanaṃ senāsananti evaṃ vuttānaṃ dhammānaṃ suṭṭhu upasevanañca veditabbaṃ.

This decisive support is threefold: object decisive support, immediate decisive support, and natural decisive support. Among these, weighty object-phenomena become dominant and strong supports precisely by reason of their weightiness. And immediate condition phenomena, because without them there is no continuity of the stream of consciousness at all, are indeed strong supports. Here, 'natural decisive support' (pakatūpanissayo) means 'a natural support' (pakato upanissayo). And 'natural' (pakato) means 'well done' (suṭṭhu kato), in the sense that when it is done, conditionally arisen phenomena invariably appear in that continuum at a suitable time. And here, 'doing' (karaṇaṃ) should be understood as the proper production, in the earlier part of one's own continuum, in the manner stated, of the stated phenomena such as faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, and also lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, views, and aspirations; and also the proper cultivation of the stated phenomena such as bodily pleasure, bodily pain, individuals, climate, food, and lodgings.

Puretaraṃ uppajjitvā vattamānabhāvena upakārako dhammo purejātapaccayo. So duvidho ārammaṇapurejāta nissaya purejāta vasena. Nissayārammaṇadhammā eva hi keci purejāta tāmattavisiṭṭhā purejātapaccayoti vuttāti. Ācariyānandattherena pana nissayārammaṇākārādīhi visiṭṭhā purejātākārena upakārakatā purejātapaccayatāti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ santepi pure jātatāvisiṭṭhehi nissayārammaṇasattivisesehi añño visuṃ purejātasattivisesonāma nadissatiyeva. Pure ropetvā jātānaṃ rukkhapotakānaṃ viya pacchā āsiñciyamānaṃ udakaṃ pure jātānaṃ catusamuṭṭhānikarūpadhammānaṃ vuddhaviruḷhabhāvañca pacchāpi attanā sadisassa rūpasantānassa pavattiyā paccayabhāvañca pāpetvā upatthambhanavasena upakārako pacchājāto arūpadhammo pacchā jātapaccayo. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana gijjhapotakasarīrānaṃ āhārāsā cetanāviyāti vuttaṃ. Mūlaṭīkāyañca etena manosañce tanāhāravasena pavattamānehi arūpadhammehi rūpakāyassa upatthambhita bhāvaṃ dasseti, teneva āhārāsā viyāti avatvā cetanāgahaṇaṃ karotīti vuttaṃ. Sā pana pacchājātā sasampayuttā āhārāsā cetanā purejātānaṃ tesaṃ gijjhasarīrarūpānaṃ cirakālaṃ kabaḷīkārāhārena vināpi amilāta bhāvaṃ uparūparica vuddhaviruḷharūpasantānuppattiyā paccayabhāvaṃ pāpetvā upatthambhatiyeva. Yasmā supākaṭena pacchājātapaccayeka desena sakalassa pacchājātapaccayassa sādhanatthāya ayaṃ upamā idha vuttā viya dissati. Cetanā gahaṇañca pacchājāta paccayaṃ patvāpi cetanāeva padhānā jātāti dassanatthaṃ gahitanti na na sakkā vattuṃ. Evañhi sati pacchājātassa atthassa pacchā jātāya eva upamāya sādhanaṃ upapannaṃ hotīti. Yathāvutta ṭīkāpāṭhepi ayamattho labbhatiyeva.

A phenomenon that is helpful by way of having arisen earlier and being present is the pre-nascence condition. It is twofold: object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Indeed, some phenomena that are base and object are called pre-nascence conditions, being distinguished merely by the state of having arisen earlier. However, the venerable teacher Ānanda stated that helpfulness by way of having arisen earlier, being distinguished by modes such as base and object, is called the pre-nascence condition. Even so, no other distinct specific potency of pre-nascence is seen apart from the specific potencies of base and object, which are distinguished by having arisen earlier. Just as water poured later supports tree saplings that have arisen from being planted earlier, so too the later-arisen immaterial phenomenon, by way of supporting, becomes a post-nascence condition, by causing the growth and development of the earlier-arisen four-originated material phenomena and by bringing about the conditionality for the continuation of a similar material continuum even afterwards. However, in the commentary, it is said to be like the intention (cetanā) that is the craving for food (āhārāsā) for the bodies of vulture chicks. And in the Mūlaṭīkā, it is stated that by this, it shows how the material body is supported by immaterial phenomena functioning by way of mental intention as food, and therefore, without saying 'like craving for food', it takes 'intention'. That later-arisen intention, which is craving for food and associated with consciousness, supports those earlier-arisen material bodies of the vultures by bringing about their unwithering state for a long time even without solid food, and by bringing about the conditionality for the arising of continuously growing and developing material continua. Because this simile seems to have been stated here for the purpose of establishing the entire post-nascence condition by means of a very clear part of the post-nascence condition. And the taking of 'intention' is to show that intention itself is primary even when it comes to the post-nascence condition; it cannot be said that it is not so. Thus, when this is the case, the proof of the meaning of the post-nascence condition is appropriately established by the simile of the later-arisen. This meaning is indeed found in the sub-commentary passage as stated.

Āsevanti [M 0.0391] taṃ suṭṭhu bhajanti aparāparaṃ uppajjamānā dhammā suṭṭhu sevamānā viya bhajamānā viya tassa purimassa sabbapāripūraṃ ākāraṃ gahetvā eva punappunaṃ pavattantīti āsevanaṃ. Āsevetivā te dhamme attano parivāsaṃ suṭṭhu gāhāpeti. Vaḍḍhetītivā āsevanaṃ. Apica kusalādibhāvena attanā sadisassa payogena karaṇīyassa anantaradhammassa punappunaṃ karaṇaṃ pavattanaṃ attasadisassavā attasadisabhāvāpādanaṃ vāsanaṃ āsevanaṭṭhoti mūlaṭīkāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha payogena karaṇīyassāti etena āvajjanadvayañca sabbavipākadhammeca nivatteti. Nahi āvajjana dvayassa dvattikkhattuṃ pavattamānassapi vaḍḍhetuṃvā hāpetuṃvā payogena karaṇīyatānāma atthi paridubbalattā. Vipākesuca ariyaphalāni parikammapayogena karaṇīyānipi maggacetanānubhāvena vinā kevalena tena payogeneva sādhetabbāni na honti. Kevalaṃ kammavegena santāne pātitesu lokiyavipākesu vattabbameva natthīti. Punappunaṃ karaṇaṃ pavattananti uparupari paguṇa balavabhāvāpādanena saha pavattanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Evañhi sati pariyattidhamma vijjāsippuggahaṇesu purimābhiyogo viya āsevanaṭṭhena anantare pavattānaṃ sajātiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ paguṇabalavabhāvāya upakārako dhammo āsevanapaccayo nāmāti siddhaṃ hotīti.

Phenomena that arise one after another, by, as it were, associating well with and cultivating it, and by taking on the complete character of the preceding one, occur again and again—this is called 'āsevana' (repetition). Or, by associating, one causes those phenomena to firmly take root in oneself. Or, it is āsevana because it increases. Furthermore, in the Mūlaṭīkā, it is said: 'The repeated performance and occurrence of a subsequent phenomenon that should be done by effort, whether wholesome or unwholesome, making it similar to oneself, or instilling a similar nature, is the meaning of āsevana.' Here, by 'that which should be done by effort,' both types of attention (āvajjana) and all resultant phenomena (vipāka-dhamma) are excluded. For even if the two types of attention occur two or three times, there is no possibility of increasing or decreasing them through effort, due to their extreme weakness. And as for results, even the noble fruits, though they should be achieved through preparatory effort, cannot be accomplished by that effort alone without the power of path-volition. As for mundane results, which arise in the continuum solely by the force of kamma, there is nothing to be said. 'Repeated performance and occurrence' is said with reference to occurrence together with the production of increasing proficiency and strength. Thus, when this is the case, just as in the case of prior effort in learning scriptures, arts, or crafts, the phenomenon that aids in the proficiency and strength of subsequently arising phenomena of the same kind, by way of repetition, is established as the āsevana-paccaya (repetition condition).

Kāyaṅgavācaṅgacittaṅgābhisaṅkharaṇabhūtena cittappayogasaṅkhāte na kiriyābhāvena upakārako dhammo kammapaccayo. So duvidho sahajātanānākkhaṇikavasena. Tattha jeṭṭhasissa mahā vaḍḍhakiādayo viya sakiccaparakiccasādhanavasena pavattā sabbāpi sahajātacetanā sahajātapaccayo. Yathā pana itthipurisānaṃ sakiṃ sannipātappayogo kāmasukhānubhavanakiccañca kālantare puttapātubhāvatthāyavatthumhi bījanidhāna kiccañca sampādeti. Evamevaṃ yathāvuttābhisaṅkharaṇakiccañca tadabhisaṅkharaṇavegajanitaṃ kālantare vipākakaṭattārūpānaṃ pātubhāvatthāya santāne kiriyā visesanidhāna kiccañca sampādetvā niruddhā kusalākusala cetanā nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayonāma. [M 0.0392] Vipaccanamattabhāvena upakārako dhammo vipākapaccayo. Vipaccana bhāvoca nāma loke sabbesaṃ pupphaphalādīnaṃ suṭṭhu vipakkabhāvaṃ pattakāle sabbākārena mandabhāvo hoti. Evaṃ nirussāhasanta bhāvasaṅkhākena mandamandākārena santāne pātubhāvo. Tatoyevaca vipākānaṃ pavatti avibhūtā hoti. Sabbarattiṃ niddāyantassa purimabhavasiddhe kammādi ārammaṇe pavattānipi tāni vuṭṭhitakāle kiñcijānanacitta pavattiyā paccayā nahontīti. Pañcaviññāṇādīni pana pacchājānanacitta pavattiyā paccayā hontānipi vatthārammaṇa ghaṭṭanānubhāva balena saheva honti. Na tesaṃ ussāhabyāpāramatta vasenāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

The phenomenon that assists by way of the activity of mind, which is designated as the application of mind, and which is the conditioning of the bodily, verbal, and mental constituents, is the kamma condition. It is twofold, by way of co-nascence and difference of moment. Herein, all co-nascent volitions, like those of a chief disciple or a great carpenter, which occur by way of accomplishing their own tasks and the tasks of others, are the co-nascent condition. Just as the single act of union of a man and a woman accomplishes the function of experiencing sensual pleasure and, after some time, the function of depositing a seed in the womb for the manifestation of offspring, even so, wholesome and unwholesome volitions, having accomplished the aforementioned function of conditioning and the function of depositing a special activity in the continuum for the manifestation of resultant kamma-born material phenomena at a later time, generated by the force of that conditioning, and then ceased, are called the kamma condition occurring at different moments. The phenomenon that assists by the mere fact of ripening is the resultant condition. And the state of ripening means that in the world, when all things like flowers and fruits have reached a state of complete ripeness, they become weak in every way. Similarly, the manifestation in the continuum occurs gradually and weakly, characterized by a state of being without vigor and tranquil. And for that very reason, the occurrence of results is indistinct. For one who sleeps all night, even if objects such as kamma, established in a previous existence, are present, they do not serve as conditions for the occurrence of any knowing consciousness upon waking. However, the five sense consciousnesses and others, though they are conditions for the occurrence of subsequent knowing consciousness, arise only through the power of contact with the base and the object. They do not arise by way of mere effort or exertion. This should be understood.

Arūpino tayo āhārā sahajātadhammānaṃ jananaṭṭhena upatthambhanaṭṭhenaca, kabaḷīkārāhāro pana imassa catusamuṭṭhāni kassa kāyassa upatthambhanaṭṭheneva upakārakatā āhārapaccayo. Apica, āhāraṭṭhonāma upatthambhanappadhāno hoti. Teneva hi pāḷiyaṃ kabaḷīkāro āhāro āhārasamuṭṭhānassa rūpassa āhārapaccayena paccayoti avatvā imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayotveva vuttaṃ. Tasmā arūpāhārānaṃpi āhāraṭṭho upatthambhanavaseneva veditabbo. Janayantāpi hi āhārā attanā janitānañca tadaññesañcasantānaṭṭhitiyā paccayabhāvatthāya upatthambhanena saheva janentīti.

The three immaterial nutriments assist co-nascent phenomena by way of generation and support, whereas edible food nutriment assists this body of fourfold origination solely by way of support; thus, it is the nutriment condition. Furthermore, the characteristic of nutriment is primarily support. For this very reason, in the Pāli Canon, it is not said that edible food is a condition for materiality arisen from nutriment by way of the nutriment condition, but rather it is said to be a condition for this body by way of the nutriment condition. Therefore, the characteristic of the immaterial nutriments should also be understood by way of support. For even though nutriments generate, they generate together with support, for the sake of being a condition for the continuity and existence of what is born from them and of other states.

Issariyaṭṭhena upakārako dhammo indriyapaccayo. So tividho sahajātādivasena. Tattha sahajātadhammānaṃ attano attano kiccesu issarabhūtā arūpindriyadhammā sahajātindriyapaccayo. Pacchā jātānaṃ pañcaviññāṇa dhammānaṃ dassanādi kiccesu issarabhūtā pure jātā pañcapasādindriyadhammā pure jātindriyapaccayo. Sahajātānaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ ciratarapavattiyaṃ issarabhūtaṃ rūpajīvitaṃ rūpajīvitindriyapaccayo. Kasmā panettha bhāvindriyadvayaṃ idha na gahitanti. Vuccate, yassa janakattaṃvā upatthambhakattaṃvā anupālakattaṃvā atthi. So paccayadhammonāma. Bhāvadvayassa [M 0.0393] pana sahajāta dhammānaṃ atthāya etaṃ tayaṃpi natthi. Kevalaṃ pana taṃsahite santāne kammādīhi attano attano paccayehi pavattamānānaṃ catusamuṭṭhānikadhammānaṃ itthākārādivaseneva yo pavattiniyamo atthi, so bhāvarūpā nubhāvena siddho. Tasmā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ tādise niyāmakicce issarattāyeva dvayaṃ indriyaṃnāma hoti. Na indriyapaccayatte nāti taṃ idha nagahitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ārammaṇaṃ upagantvā tasmiṃ bhusaṃ daḷhaṃ nipatitvā viya jhāyanaṭṭhena olokanaṭṭhena upakārako dhammo jhānapaccayo. Duggati sugati nibbāna sampāpakaṭṭhena upakārako dhammo maggapaccayo. Etthaca yenayena sammādassanādinā lakkhaṇavisesena sampannattā kusalabhūtā sammādiṭṭhādayo sugati nibbāna sampāpakaṭṭhena maggapaccayānāma honti. Abyākatabhūtānaṃpi tesaṃ so so lakkhaṇaviseso atthiyevāti tesampi tenevaṭṭhena maggapaccayatā vuttāti daṭṭhabbā. Satipi maggaṅgānaṃ taṃtaṃ sampāpakaṭṭhenaca upakārakatte taṃsamuṭṭhitānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ so attho na pāpuṇāti. Tesaṃ pana maggapaccayadhammehi samuṭṭhitattāyeva maggapaccayuppannatā paccetabbā. Esanayo hetukammindriyajhāna paccayesupīti.

The phenomenon that assists by way of sovereignty is the faculty condition. It is threefold, by way of co-nascence, etc. Herein, the immaterial faculty phenomena, being sovereign in their respective functions among co-nascent phenomena, are the co-nascent faculty condition. The five physical sense faculties, having arisen previously, being sovereign in the functions of seeing, etc., for the subsequently arising five consciousness phenomena, are the pre-nascent faculty condition. For co-nascent kamma-born material phenomena, the material life faculty, being sovereign in their prolonged continuation, is the material life faculty condition. Why are the two sex faculties not included here? It is said: Whatever has the nature of generating, supporting, or maintaining is called a conditioning phenomenon. However, for the two sex faculties, these three functions do not exist for the sake of co-nascent phenomena. Rather, the regulation of the occurrence of the four-originated phenomena—arising in the continuum together with them by their respective conditions such as kamma—by way of being female, etc., is accomplished by the influence of the sex faculties. Therefore, these two are called faculties solely because of their sovereignty in such a regulatory function for those phenomena, but not by way of being faculty conditions. Hence, they are not included here, it should be understood. The phenomenon that assists by way of contemplating or observing, as if having thoroughly approached an object and fallen very firmly upon it, is the jhāna condition. The phenomenon that assists by way of leading to a bad destination, a good destination, or Nibbāna, is the path condition. And here, wholesome right view and other factors, being endowed with their specific characteristics such as right seeing, are called path conditions by way of leading to a good destination or Nibbāna. Even for those that are indeterminate, their specific characteristics still exist; therefore, their path conditionality is also stated in the same sense, it should be understood. Even though the path factors assist by way of leading to their respective destinations, that meaning does not apply to the material phenomena arisen from them. However, because those material phenomena have arisen from path-condition phenomena, their being path-condition-produced should be understood. This method applies similarly to the conditions of root, kamma, faculty, and jhāna.

Ekuppādatādīhi pakārehi samaṃ ekībhūto viya hutvā aññamaññayuttabhāvena upakārako dhammo sampayuttapaccayo. Samānepi sahajātabhāvena nissaya nissita bhāvenaca yuttabhāve ekuppādatādikassa sampayogalakkhaṇassa virahato vippayuttabhāvena upakārako dhammo vippayuttapaccayo. Yattha sampayuttā saṅkā sambhavati, tattheva tadāsaṅkā vigamanatthaṃ ayaṃ vippayuttapaccayonāma vuttoti tadāsaṅkhā rahitesu ārammaṇānantarādīsu vippayuttapaccayapasaṅgo natthīti veditabbo. Heṭṭhāvuttappakāresu eva paccayadhammesu yo yo atthitā saṅkhātena khaṇapaccuppanna samaṅgibhāvena tādisasseva khaṇapaccuppanna samaṅgino dhammassa sahajātādivasena upakārako so so atthipaccayo. Yasmiṃ vijjāmāne sati añño uppajjituṃ okāsaṃ [M 0.0394] nalabhati. So tassa aññassa okāsadāna saṅkhātena sayaṃ antarahitabhāvena upakārako dhammo natthipaccayo. Ayaṃpi visuṃ sattiviseso na hoti. Teneva cittena gacchati nisīdati tiṭṭhatītiādinā pacchimacitte ṭhitānaṃpi purimacittaṃ vattatiyevāti lokassa abhimāno hoti. Tasmā yattha atthitāsaṅkā sambhavati. Tattha tadāsaṅkā nivattanatthaṃ ayaṃ paccayo vuttoti veditabbo.

The phenomenon that assists by way of mutual connection, having become as if united as one by means of simultaneous arising and other such modes, is the associated condition. Even though there is connection by way of co-nascence and the relationship of support and supported, due to the absence of the characteristic of association, such as simultaneous arising, the phenomenon that assists by way of dissociation is the dissociated condition. Where doubt about association arises, there, for the sake of dispelling that doubt, this is called the dissociated condition. Therefore, in cases like object and contiguity conditions, where there is no such doubt, the application of the dissociated condition is not relevant, it should be understood. Among the previously mentioned modes of conditional phenomena, whatever assists a phenomenon that is likewise present at the moment, by way of co-nascence, etc., by being present at the moment, is the presence condition. That phenomenon which, while it is present another does not get an opportunity to arise, assists that other by its own state of having disappeared, designated as 'giving opportunity', is the absence condition. This too is not a separate special power. For this very reason, people assume that 'one goes, sits, stands, etc., with that mind,' meaning that even when the later mind has arisen, the earlier mind continues to function. Therefore, wherever doubt about existence arises, there, for the sake of removing that doubt, this condition is stated, it should be understood.

Vināsaṃ gato vigato. Yasmiṃ avigate añño uppajjituṃ okāsaṃ nalabhati, so tassa okāsadānasaṅkhātena sayaṃ vigatabhāvena upakārako dhammo vigatapaccayo. Vattamānatā saṅkhātena avigatabhāvena tādisasseva dhammassa upakārako dhammo avigatapaccayo. Purimapaccaya dukameva cettha nānattha pasaṅganivattanatthaṃ ñāṇavisadatthañca pariyāyantarena vigatadukaṃnāma katvā desitanti veditabbaṃ. Tathā hi atthīti kho kaccāna ayameko anto. Natthīti ayaṃ dutīyo antotiādinā nānāatthadīpakā atthi natthi saddā sāsane lokeca dissanti. Pubbe vuttasseva ca atthassa puna pariyāyantarena vacanaṃ sotūnaṃ ñāṇavisadatthāya hotīti. Ṭīkākārā pana bahuṃ tesaṃ paccaya dukānaṃ nānatthasambhavaṃ vaṇṇentiyevāti. [Paccayuddeso]

Having gone to destruction, it is 'vanished'. That phenomenon which, while it has not vanished another does not obtain an opportunity to arise, assists that other by its own state of having vanished, by way of granting opportunity, is the vanished condition. A phenomenon that assists a similar phenomenon by its state of not vanishing, designated as presence, is the unvanished condition. It should be understood that this very pair of preceding conditions is taught here, having been made into the 'duality of vanishing' by way of an alternative explanation, for the sake of averting the contingency of different meanings and for the sake of clarity of knowledge. For indeed, 'It exists,' Kaccāna, is one extreme; 'It does not exist' is the second extreme—thus, in the Dispensation and in the world, the words 'exists' and 'does not exist' are seen, illuminating various meanings. And the repetition of the previously stated meaning by way of an alternative explanation is for the sake of the listeners' clarity of knowledge. However, the commentators extensively elaborate on the possibility of diverse meanings for those dual conditions. [Exposition of Conditions]

168. Idāni yathā uddiṭṭhe catuvīsatipaccaye pathamaṃ chahi rāsīhi saṅgahetvā puna rāsīnaṃ anukkamena tesaṃ paccayānaṃ niddesaṃ dassento chadhānāmantunāmassāti gāthādvaya māha. Nāmaṃ nāmassa chadhā chabbidhehi paccayehi paccayo hoti. Nāmaṃ nāmarūpīnaṃ pañcadhā. Puna nāmaṃ rūpassa ekadhā, rūpaṃ nāmassa ekadhāeva. Paññattināmarūpāni nāmassa duvidhā, dvayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ dvayasseva nāmarūpassa navadhāti evaṃ chakkapañcakādivasena paccayā chabbidhā honti. Kathaṃ hontīti yojanā.

168. Now, having first grouped the twenty-four conditions as enumerated into six aggregates, and then demonstrating the specification of those conditions in the order of the aggregates, he speaks two verses beginning with 'Chadhānāmantunāmassāti'. Name is a condition for name in six ways, by six kinds of conditions. Name is a condition for name-and-form in five ways. Again, name is a condition for form in one way, and form is a condition for name in one way only. Designation and name-and-form are conditions for name in two ways; the pair, name-and-form, is a condition for the pair, name-and-form, in nine ways. Thus, the conditions are sixfold, fivefold, etc. How are they so? This is the connection.

[229] Yaṃpana vibhāvaniyaṃ

[229] But what is to be explained:

“Paññattināmarūpāni nāmassa dvidhā dvipakārā paccayā hontīti vuttaṃ”. Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

It is said that 'Designation and name-and-form are conditions for name in two ways, of two kinds.' That is not well-stated.

Paccayakathā [M 0.0395] hi nāma paccayato paccayuppannato paccayasattitoti tīhi pakārehi vuttāyeva suvuttā hotīti. Yasmā pana anantarādipaccayānāma cittasantānassa avicchedāya kiccaṭṭhānānukkamapaṭipādanāya eva ca honti. Tasmā kusalādīsu arūpadhammesu yokoci dhammo yassa kassaci aviruddhassa dhammassa paccayo na na hotīti vuttaṃ anantaraniruddhācittacetasikādhammātiādi. Tattha aviruddhassātietena aññamaññaviruddhānaṃ kusalākusalānaṃ somanassadomanassānañca aññamaññaṃ anantara paccayapaṭikkhepo veditabbo. Paṭuppannānanti punuppannānaṃ paṭipāṭiyā uppannānaṃvā. Punappunaṃ santānaparibhāvanāvasena pavatto āsevanapaccayonāma, kevalaṃ payogasādhanīyesu javavega sahitesu cittuppādesu eva labbhatīti vuttaṃ purimāni javanānītiādi. Tattha javanānīti maggaphalajavanavajjāni lokiya kusalā kusalakriyajavanāni pacchimānaṃjavanānanti phalajavanavajjānaṃ kusalākusalakriyajavanānaṃ. Bhinnajātikā hi dhammā aññamaññaṃ sabbākārapāripūraṃ parivāsaṃnāma gahetuṃvā gāhāpetuṃpā na sakkonti. Yadi sakkuṇeyyuṃ, jātimattenapi dhammā pubbāparaṃ abhinnāeva siyunti. Tasmā bhinnajātikaṃ phalajavanaṃ maggato parivāsaṃ gahetuṃ na sakkoti. Maggopi attano parivāsaṃ phalassa dātuṃ na sakkoti. Phalacittānica parikammapayogabalena javana kiccāni honti, na aññamaññaṃ parivāsadāna gahaṇa balenāti. Yasmā kāmāvacarabhāvato mahaggatā nuttara bhāvappattināma āsevanabalena hoti, tasmā gotrabhu jhāna maggānaṃ bhūmi bhedo idha appamāṇanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Indeed, the discussion of conditions is well explained when it is stated in three ways: by way of the condition, by way of the conditioned, and by way of the entity of the condition. Since conditions such as contiguity and so forth serve to prevent the interruption of the mental continuum and to facilitate the orderly succession of functions, it is therefore said that in wholesome and other immaterial states, any phenomenon can indeed be a condition for any other non-opposing phenomenon, as in 'immediately ceased mind and mental states,' and so forth. Here, by 'non-opposing,' the rejection of the contiguity condition between mutually opposing wholesome and unwholesome states, and between joy and displeasure, should be understood. 'Of those that have arisen' refers either to those that have arisen repeatedly or to those that have arisen in succession. The repetition condition operates through the repeated cultivation of the mental continuum. It is obtained only in instances of consciousness that are accomplishable by effort and endowed with swift momentum, as stated in phrases like 'the preceding impulsions,' and so forth. Here, 'impulsions' refers to mundane wholesome, unwholesome, and functional impulsions, excluding path and fruition impulsions; 'of subsequent impulsions' refers to wholesome, unwholesome, and functional impulsions, excluding fruition impulsions. For phenomena of different natures cannot fully take up or cause to be taken up the mutual imparting of influence in every way. If they could, phenomena would remain undifferentiated as preceding and succeeding even by their mere nature. Therefore, fruition impulsion, being of a different nature, cannot take up the imparting of influence from the path, nor can the path give its imparting of influence to fruition. Moreover, fruition consciousnesses perform the function of impulsion through the power of preliminary effort, not through the power of mutually giving and taking influence. Since the attainment of the exalted and supramundane states from the sense-sphere state arises from the power of repetition, it should be understood here that the difference of plane—such as that of the change-of-lineage, jhāna, and path—is of great significance.

Hetu.La. Nāmarūpānanti ettha hetumaggaṅgāni ahetukavajjitānaṃ, jhānaṅgāni pañcaviññāṇavajjitānaṃ sahajātānaṃ nāmarūpānaṃ. Sahajātarūpalakkhaṇaṃ pana sayameva vakkhati. Cetanānāma pavattamānā dve kiccāni sādheti sahajātānaṃ saṃvidhānañca āyatiṃ vipākapātu bhāvatthāya tasmiṃ santāne attano pavattā kārasaṅkhāta bījanidhānañcāti. Tattha saṃvidhānakiccaṃ sabbacetanā sādhāraṇaṃ [M 0.0396] hoti. Bījanidhānakiccaṃ pana kusalākusalabhāvappattāyaeva cetanāya hotīti vuttaṃ sahajātācetanātiādi. Tattha sahajātācetanāti antamaso pañcaviññāṇa sahajātāpi cetanā. Sāpi hi sahajātānaṃ saṃvidahanasaṅkhātena kammabhāvena pavattattā kammaṃevanāma hotīti. Yasmā attano pavattākārasaṅkhātassa vipākabījassa nidahanaṃnāma, na tāvadeva bījakiccaṃ sampādeti. Ambabījādīni viya pariṇatabhāvaṃ patvā khaṇantareeva sampādetīti vuttaṃ nānākkhaṇikā cetanātiādi. Tattha nānākkhaṇikācetanāti attano paccayuppannadhamma pavattikkhaṇato visuṃ bhūte atītakāle siddhā kusalā kusalacetanā. Kusalākusalacetanātivā pāṭho siyā.

Cause. Here, the root factors and path factors are conditions for co-arisen name-and-form, excluding those without roots; the jhāna factors are conditions for co-arisen name-and-form, excluding the five sense-consciousnesses. The characteristic of co-arisen form, however, he himself will explain. Volition, while occurring, accomplishes two functions: the arrangement of co-arisen phenomena, and the depositing of a seed in that continuum for the future manifestation of a result, a seed which is designated as the mode of its own occurrence. Among these, the function of arrangement is common to all volitions. The function of depositing the seed, however, belongs only to volition that has attained the state of being wholesome or unwholesome—thus it is said, 'co-arisen volition,' and so forth. Here, 'co-arisen volition' means even the volition co-arisen with the five sense-consciousnesses. For that too, by occurring as kamma through the function of arranging co-arisen phenomena, is indeed called kamma. Because the depositing of the result-seed, which is called its own mode of occurrence, does not accomplish the seed-function immediately—just like mango seeds and so forth, which only accomplish it in a subsequent moment after attaining a matured state—it is said, 'volition of different moments,' and so forth. Here, 'volition of different moments' refers to wholesome or unwholesome volition established in a past time, distinct from the moment of occurrence of the phenomena produced by its condition. Or there may also be a reading as 'wholesome and unwholesome volition'.

Vipākakkhandhāaññamaññaṃsahajātānaṃrūpānanti ettha aññamaññassaca sahajātarūpānañcāti attho. Yathānāma pure jātā sālarukkhapotakā pacchā anuvassaṃ vassantānaṃ vuṭṭhidhārānaṃ vasena vuddhiṃ viruḷhiṃ vepullaṃ patvā tasmiṃ ṭhāne yāvakappāvasānāpi mahantassa sālavanasaṇḍassa pavattiyā paccayā honti. Evaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇato paṭṭhāya purimacittakkhaṇesu uppannā sakalasarīre kammajakāyo cittajakāyo utujakāyo āhāraja kāyoti sabbe sakalasarīraṭṭhakā catusamuṭṭhānika rūpadhammā pacchājātānaṃ pathamabhavaṅgādīnaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ vasena vuddhiṃ viruḷhiṃ vepullaṃ patvā uparupari catusamuṭṭhānika rūpaparaṃparāpavattiyā paccayattaṃ upagacchantīti vuttaṃ pacchājātā cittacetasikā dhammātiādi. Tattha purejātassāti ātītānantaracitte jātassāti vadanti. Yāva aṭṭhamacittāvā purejātassa. Ettako hi kālo rūpadhammānaṃ vaḍḍhanakālonāma. Tatoparaṃ hāyanakāle pacchājātena payojanaṃ natthīti. Yāva soḷasamacittā eva vā purejātassa. Yadaggena hi maraṇāsannakāle vatthurūpaṃ cuticittassa purejātapaccayataṃ upagacchati. Tadaggena cuticittaṃpi tassa vatthurūpassa pacchājātapaccayo na hotīti navattabbo. Tathā sesarūpānañca. Yathā hi upatthambhanto āhāro [M 0.0397] vaḍḍhanapakkhe ṭhitameva upatthambhati. Hāyanapakkhe ṭhitaṃ nupatthambhatīti natthi. Tadāpi tadanurūpassa upatthambhanassa icchitabbattā. Evamayaṃpīti.

In the phrase 'the resultant aggregates for one another and for co-arisen material phenomena,' the meaning is that they are a condition for one another and for co-arisen material phenomena. Just as, for example, young sal saplings born earlier, when later nourished year after year by pouring rain showers, attain growth, development, and expansion, and thus become a condition for the continued existence of a great sal forest stand in that place until the end of the eon; similarly, from the moment of rebirth-linking onward, the kamma-born body, mind-born body, temperature-born body, and nutriment-born body—all the fourfold-originated material phenomena that pervade the entire body, having arisen in the preceding moments of consciousness—attain growth, development, and expansion through the influence of the subsequently arisen first life-continuum and other mental states. Thus, they become a condition for the continuous succession of fourfold-originated material phenomena, one after another. This is what is meant by 'subsequently arisen mind and mental factors,' and so forth. Here, by 'pre-arisen,' they mean what has arisen in the immediately preceding moment of consciousness. Or, it is pre-arisen up to the eighth consciousness, for that long is the growth period of material phenomena. Beyond that, in the decay period, there is no benefit from what is subsequently arisen. Alternatively, it is pre-arisen up to the sixteenth consciousness. For near death, the physical base becomes a pre-arisen condition for the death consciousness. At that point, it should not be said that the death consciousness is not also a subsequently arisen condition for that physical base. The same applies to the remaining material phenomena. Just as it is not the case that supporting nutriment sustains only what is in the growth phase and does not sustain what is in the decay phase, because even then, corresponding support is desirable; so too is it in this case.

Arūpadhammānaṃ ānubhāvonāma mahāvipphāro hoti. Tasmā te kāyekadese vatthumhi uppannāpi sakalaṃ imaṃ catujakāyaṃ upatthambhetuṃ sakkontiyevāti vuttaṃ imassakāyassāti. Cakkhādīni pasādavatthūni rūpādīhi sahaladdhaghaṭṭanānieva viññāṇassa ādhārabhāvaṃ gacchanti. Ghaṭṭanañca ṭhitipattakāleevāti tesaṃ niccakālaṃpi attano viññāṇassa purejātapaccayatā siddhi hoti. Viññāṇañcanāma pañcavokārabhave vatthunissayena vinā uppajjituṃ nasakkotīti, yadā purejātaṃvā vaḍḍhanapakkhe ṭhitaṃvā vatthuṃ na labhati, tadā paṭisandhikālevā maraṇāsannakālevā yaṃ yaṃ labhati, taṃ taṃ nissāya uppajjatiyeva. Yadā pana pure jātaṃ suṭṭhu balavantañca vatthuṃ labhati, tadā tadeva nissāya pavattati. Tañca niyamato pavattikāleeva labbhati, no paṭisandhikāle. Nahi tadā viññāṇapaccayena uppannaṃ vatthupurejātaṃ bhavituṃ sakkotīti vuttaṃ chavatthūni pavattiyanti.

The influence of formless phenomena is indeed a great pervasive power. Therefore, even when they arise in a part of the body, in a physical base, they are indeed capable of supporting this entire body, as stated in 'of this body.' The sensitive organs such as the eye and so forth only become the support for consciousness when they are struck by forms and so forth. And since this striking occurs only at the static phase of their existence, their being a pre-arisen condition for their own consciousness is always established. Consciousness, indeed, cannot arise in the five-aggregate existence without relying on a physical base. When it does not obtain a base that is pre-arisen or one that is in its growth phase, then at the moment of rebirth-linking or near death, it arises relying on whatever base it obtains. But when it obtains a pre-arisen base that is very strong, it continues to occur relying on that alone. And that, as a rule, is obtained only during the course of existence, not at the moment of rebirth-linking. For at that time, a base arisen with that consciousness as its condition cannot be pre-arisen. Thus, it is said, 'the six bases, during the course of existence.'

Pañcālambaṇānica pañcaviññāṇavīthiyāti idaṃ niyamasiddhigahaṇa vasena vuttaṃ. Sabbāni pana paccuppannabhūtāni nipphannarūpāni manoviññāṇa vīthiyā purejātapaccayā hontiyeva. Evañca katvā paṭṭhāne paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati. Sotaṃ, ghānaṃ, jivhaṃ, kāyaṃ, rūpe, sadde, gandhe, rase, phoṭṭhabbe, vatthuṃ, paccuppanne khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, paccuppannaṃ cakkhuṃ assādeti abhinandatītiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyañca uppādakkhaṇaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitipattaṃ aṭṭhārasavidhaṃ rūpameva purejātapaccayoti vuttanti. Etthaca kiñcāpi paṭṭhāne paccuppannārammaṇaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ paccuppannārammaṇassa bhavaṅgassaanantarapaccayena paccayoti evaṃ paṭisandhibhavaṅgānaṃpi paccuppannārammaṇatāya vuttattā [M 0.0398] paccuppannabhūtāni kammanimitta gatinimittāni ārabbha pavatti kāle paṭisandhicittānaṃpi ārammaṇapurejātaṃ labbhamānaṃ viya dissati. Evaṃsantepi purejātapaccayassa paccaniye paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākā byākato eko khandhotiādinā pāḷiyaṃeva taṃ paṭikkhittanti. Etthaca āruppe viya paṭisandhikkhaṇepi vatthupure jātassa abhāvā aparibyattattāvā tassa ārammaṇassa ārammaṇamattabhāveeva ṭhitattā paṭikkhittanti kāraṇaṃ vadanti. Ārammaṇamevagarukatanti paccavekkhanavasena assādanādivasenaca garukataṃ iṭṭhārammaṇa māha. Tañca kho tassatassa puggalassa icchāvasena veditabbaṃ. Gūthakuṇapādīnipi hi tadabhinandantānaṃ kimimakkhika sunakha gijjha kākādīnaṃ garukatānieva ārammaṇāni hontīti.

The five sense objects are mentioned in connection with the five sense-door cognitive processes by way of establishing a rule. However, all present, produced material forms are indeed pre-nascence conditions for the mind-door cognitive process. Thus, in the Paṭṭhāna, a present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition. One contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self through the pre-nascence object condition. Similarly, one contemplates the ear, nose, tongue, body, visible forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, the physical base, and the present aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. It is also said that one delights in and enjoys the present eye, etc. And in the commentary, it is stated that only the eighteen kinds of material form that have passed the moment of arising and reached the moment of staticity are pre-nascence conditions. Here, although in the Paṭṭhāna it is stated that the rebirth-linking consciousness with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum with a present object by way of contiguity condition, and thus rebirth-linking and life-continuum states are also said to have present objects, it appears that even rebirth-linking consciousness can have a pre-nascence object condition when arising based on present kamma-signs or destiny-signs. Yet, even so, in the negative section on the pre-nascence condition, this is rejected in the Pāli itself for the moment of rebirth-linking with the words, 'one resultant, indeterminate aggregate,' etc. Here, just as in the formless realms, at the moment of rebirth-linking, due to the absence or non-manifestation of a pre-nascent physical base, they say the object remains merely an object and is therefore rejected. It is said that 'only the object is considered significant' refers to a desirable object made significant through reflection, delight, etc. And this should be understood according to the desire of each individual. For example, excrement and corpses are indeed significant objects for those who delight in them, such as worms, flies, dogs, vultures, and crows.

[230] Yaṃ pana vibhāvaniyaṃ

[230] But what is to be explained:

“Garukatanti garuṃ katvā paccavekkhita”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Taṃ anupapannaṃ.

It is said, 'significant' means 'reflected upon after having made it significant,' etc. That is untenable.

Cakkhuṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandatītiādinā assā danādivasenapi assa niddesassa pavattattāti. Rāgādayo pana dhammāti etena rāgo doso moho māno diṭṭhi patthanāti evaṃ vuttehi dhammehi saha dasa akusalakammapathā pañcaanantariya kammānica gahitāni honti. Tattha anantariyavajjāni tāni samatikkamamukhena yathārahaṃ ajjhattaṃ sabbesaṃ catubhūmaka kusalānaṃ anantariyakammāni pana kāmāvacarakusalānameva uppattiyā balavanissayā honti. Tāniyevaca sabbāni yathārahaṃ ajjhattañca bahiddhāca rāgādīnaṃ pāṇātipātādīnañca sabbesaṃ akusalānaṃ kāyikasukhadukkhādīnañca abyākatadhammānaṃ uppattiyā balava nissayā honti. Saddhādayoti etena saddhā sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgo paññāti evaṃ vuttehi dhammehi saha sabbe dānasīlādayo catubhūmakaku salānaṃ rāgādi akusalānaṃ sukhadukkhādicatubhūmaka abyākatā nañca uppattiyā balavanissayā hontīti. Sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ puggalo bhojanaṃ utusenāsananti etena nibbānavajjā sabbe catubhūmakā byākatā [M 0.0399] gahitā, tepi hi yathārahaṃ ajjhattañca bahiddhāca kusalākusalā byākatadhammānaṃ uppattiyā balavanissayā hontīti. Kammaṃvipākānanti ettha suṭṭhu balavaṃ kammaṃ adhippetaṃ, na dubbalanti. Kasmā panettha rūpadhammā paccayuppannesu na gahitā. Nanu tesaṃpi bahiddhā rukkhatiṇādīnaṃ vuddhiviruḷhi vepullatthāya ajjhattañca ārogyādiatthāya pathavirasa āporasa vassodaka bijamūlabhesajjādayo balavanissayā hontīti. Ayaṃ panattho mūlaṭīkāyaṃ kathitoyeva. Vuttañhi tattha –

For this explanation proceeds also by way of delight and so on, as in 'one delights in and enjoys the eye, having made it significant,' etc. As for 'states such as lust,' by this are included, along with the states thus stated—lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and longing—the ten unwholesome courses of action and the five heinous deeds. Among these, those excluding the heinous deeds are, by way of overcoming, strong supports for the arising of all four-plane wholesome states internally, as appropriate. However, the heinous deeds are strong supports for the arising of only sense-sphere wholesome states. And all of them, as appropriate, both internally and externally, are strong supports for the arising of lust and other unwholesome states, killing and the like, and all unwholesome states, as well as indeterminate states such as bodily pleasure and pain. By 'faith and the rest' are included, along with the states thus stated—faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom—all acts of giving, virtue, and other four-plane wholesome states, which are strong supports for the arising of lust and other unwholesome states, and pleasure, pain, and other four-plane indeterminate states. By 'pleasure, pain, the individual, food, climate, and lodging' are included all four-plane indeterminate states except Nibbāna. These too, both internally and externally, are strong supports for the arising of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states, as appropriate. As for 'kamma and its results,' here very strong kamma is intended, not weak kamma. Why, then, are material phenomena not included among the conditionally arisen states here? Are not the earth element, the water element, rainwater, seeds, roots, and medicines also strong supports externally for the growth, development, and abundance of trees and grass, and internally for health and the like? This meaning, however, has already been explained in the Mūlaṭīkā. For it is said there—

Nahi rūpābyākataṃ pakatūpanissayaṃ labhati. Acetanena rūpasantānena pakatasseva abhāvato. Yathā hi arūpasantānena kattubhūtena saddhādayo nipphāditā utubhojanādayoca upasevitā. Na evaṃ rūpasantānena. Yasmiñca utubījādike kammādikeca sati rūpaṃ pavattati. Na taṃ tena rūpena pakataṃ hoti. Sacetanasseva hi uppādanupasevanapayogavasena cetanaṃ pakappanaṃ pakaraṇaṃ. Rūpañca acetananti.

Indeed, indeterminate material form does not obtain a natural decisive support, because there is no making by an unconscious material continuum. For just as faith and other qualities are produced, and climate, food, and so on are utilized, by an immaterial continuum acting as an agent, it is not so with a material continuum. And when form continues to exist in the presence of climate, seeds, kamma, and so on, it is not something made by that form itself. For making, which is arranging and intending, belongs only to a conscious being, by way of production, utilization, and application. But form is unconscious.

Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, duvidhaṃ santānaṃ rūpasantānaṃ arūpasantānanti. Tattha yena santānena pubbe kiñci suṭṭhuuppāditaṃvā hoti upasevitaṃvā, tasseva pubbe attanā uppāditupasevitā dhammā kālantare attano upanissayapaccayā honti. Pakaraṇasaṅkhātañca tathā uppādanupasevanaṃnāma sacetane arūpasantāneeva labbhati, na acetane rūpasantāneti. Tasmā rūpadhammā upanissayaṃnāma nalabbhantīti. Imasmiṃ sati idaṃ hoti, asati na hotīti evaṃ vuttena suttantikapariyāyena pana upanissayo nāma rūpadhammānaṃ majjhepi vattabboyevāti.

This is what is meant: there are two kinds of continuities—material continuity and immaterial continuity. Therein, by whatever continuity something was previously well-produced or cultivated, those very things previously produced or cultivated by oneself become, after a time, decisive support conditions for oneself. And such production and cultivation, called 'making,' is found only in the conscious immaterial continuum, not in the unconscious material continuum. Therefore, material phenomena do not obtain decisive support. However, according to the Suttanta method, which states, 'When this exists, this comes to be; when this does not exist, this does not come to be,' the term 'decisive support' should indeed be spoken of even among material phenomena.

[231] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[231] But what is to be explained:

“Yathārahaṃ ajjhattañca bahiddhāca rāgādayo.La. Senāsanañcāti” viyojetvā “rāgādayo hi ajjhattaṃ nipphādikā. Puggalādayo bahiddhā sevitāti” vuttaṃ. Taṃ nasundaraṃ.

It is said, 'lust and so on, internally and externally, as appropriate... and lodging,' separating them, and then 'for lust and so on are internally produced; persons and so on are externally utilized.' That is not well-stated.

Na [M 0.0400] hi attano parassaca uppannā rāgādayo parassa attano ca santāne rāgādīnaṃ balavanissayā na honti. Samānacchandānaṃ itthi purisādīnaṃ manopadosika devādīnañcettha rāgādayo nidassanaṃ.

For it is not the case that lust and so on, arisen in oneself or in others, do not become strong decisive supports for lust and so on in the continuities of others and oneself. Here, the lust and so on of men and women with similar desires, and of malevolent deities, etc., serve as examples.

[232] Yāca tattha

[232] And that which is there,

“Yathāṭhitavasena yojanaṃ” katvā “attanohi rāgādayo”tiādinā atthavibhāvanā katā. Sāpi anupapannāyeva.

having made a connection 'according to the existing state,' an explanation of meaning is given beginning with 'for one's own lust and so on,' etc. That too is inappropriate.

Tāya hi attano rāgādayo saddhādayoca ajjhattaṃ kusalādīnaṃ attano saddhāyo pana bahiddhā kusalassāti evaṃ aparipuṇṇassa atthassa vibhāvitattāti.

For by that, an incomplete meaning was clarified, as in 'one's own lust and so on, and faith and so on, are internal for wholesome states and the like; but one's own faith is external for wholesome states,' etc.

[233] Yañca

[233] And what

‘Tatthā’tiādinā attanorāgādayonissāyaajjhattaṃ kusalākusalānameva uppattividhānaṃ vuttaṃ. Taṃpi anupapannameva.

by 'therein,' etc., the arrangement for the arising of only wholesome and unwholesome states internally, based on one's own lust and so on, is stated. That too is inappropriate.

Nayadassanamattabhūtaṃpi hi saṃvaṇṇanāvākyaṃnāma nayamukhaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ katvā vattabbaṃ hotīti. Garukataṃārammaṇanti ettha sabbaṃ lokiyakusalaṃ heṭṭhimamaggaphalanibbānāni ca kāmāvacara kusalassa arahattamaggaphalanibbānāni catunnaṃ ñāṇasampayutta mahākriyajavanānaṃ. Nibbānaṃ aṭṭhavidhalokuttarassa thapetvā paṭighadvaya momūha dvaya dukkhasahagata kāyaviññāṇāni avasesaṃ sabbaṃ lokiya kusalākusalābyākatadhammajātaṃ lobhasahagatacittassāti evaṃ paccaya paccayuppanna vibhāgo veditabbo.

For even a mere illustrative statement of the method should be made by fully completing the approach. As for 'significant object,' here, the division of conditions and conditionally arisen states should be understood thus: for sense-sphere wholesome consciousness, the objects are all mundane wholesome states, the lower paths and fruits, and Nibbāna; for the four great functional impulsions associated with knowledge, the Arahantship path and fruit, and Nibbāna; for the eight kinds of supramundane consciousness, Nibbāna; and for consciousness accompanied by greed, all remaining mundane wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena are the objects, except for the two types of consciousness rooted in aversion, the two rooted in delusion, and body-consciousness accompanied by pain.

[234] Yaṃ pana vibhāvaniyaṃ

[234] But whatever is to be explained:

“Garuka taṃālambaṇanti paccavekkhanaassādādinā garukataṃ ārammaṇa”nti vatvā taṃ vibhāventena “tañhi jhānamagga phalavipassanā nibbānādibhedaṃ paccavekkhana assādādimaggaphalādidhamme attādhīne karotīti ārammaṇādhipatināmā”ti vuttaṃ. Taṃ na sundaraṃ.

Having said, 'a significant object means an object made significant through reflection, delight, etc.,' and explaining that, it is said, 'for that makes phenomena such as jhāna, path, fruition, insight, Nibbāna, etc., dependent on oneself by way of reflection, delight, etc., with respect to path, fruition, etc., and thus it is called 'object-predominance.' That is not well-stated.

Dāna [M 0.0401] sīla uposathakamma pubbe suciṇṇagotrabhu vodāna maggaphala nibbānāniceva rāgadiṭṭhicakkhusotādīnicāti pana vattabbaṃ. Vipassanātica idaṃ gotrabhuvodānāniyeva sandhāya vuttaṃ siyā. Naca tāni nibbānārammaṇāni vipassanānāma hontīti. Sahajātānaṃnāmarūpānanti dvihetuka tihetuka javanasaha jātānanti adhippāyo. Aññamaññaṃ sahajāta rūpānañcāti aññamaññassaca paṭisandhikkhaṇe kammasamuṭṭhānarūpānaṃ pavattiyaṃ citta samuṭṭhānarūpānañca. Esa nayo paratthapi. Pañcavokārabhave paṭisandhikkhaṇe viññāṇaṃ vatthunā vinā patiṭṭhaṃ nalabhati. Vatthucatena vinā patiṭṭhaṃ nalabhatīti vuttaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuvipākā aññamaññanti. Aññamaññapaccaye yo attano upatthambhakaṃ paccupatthambhati. Soeva paccayuppannabhāvaṃ gacchati. Cittasamuṭṭhāna rūpānica cittaṃ kiñci upatthambhetuṃ nasakkonti. Tathā upādārūpānica mahābhūteti vuttaṃ cittacetasikādhammāaññamaññantiādi.

Rather, it should be said: generosity, virtue, observance of the Uposatha, and previously well-practiced [kamma]; change-of-lineage, purification, path, fruit, and Nibbāna; and also lust, wrong view, eye, ear, etc. And as for insight, this may be said with reference to change-of-lineage and purification themselves. Nor are those, having Nibbāna as their object, called insight. The meaning of 'of simultaneously arisen name-and-form' is 'arisen simultaneously with two-rooted or three-rooted impulsions.' And 'of mutually co-arisen forms' refers to the mutual [conditionality] of kamma-originated forms at the moment of rebirth-linking, and of mind-originated forms in the course of existence. The same principle applies elsewhere. In five-aggregate existence, at the moment of rebirth-linking, consciousness cannot be established without a base, and the base cannot be established without it. This is said in reference to the rebirth-linking moment, where the base and resultant consciousness are mutual conditions. In the mutuality condition, that which supports its own supporter itself attains the state of being conditionally arisen. Mind-originated forms, too, cannot support the mind in any way. Similarly, derived forms [cannot support] the great elements, and it is said, 'mind and mental factors are mutual conditions,' and so on.

[235] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

[235] But what is to be elucidated:

“Yasmā pana aññamaññuvatthambhanavaseneva aññamaññapaccayatā. Na sahajātamattatoti pavattiyaṃ rūpaṃ nāmānaṃ aññamaññapaccayo na hoti. Tasmā vuttaṃ cittacetasikā dhammā aññamaññanti” vuttaṃ. Tattha na sahajātamattatoti etena yadi sahajātamattato aññamaññapaccayatāsiyā. Evaṃsati pavattiyaṃ rūpaṃ nāmānaṃ aññamaññapaccayo siyāti anuññātaṃ hoti. Sahajātapaccayepi pana pavattiyaṃ rūpaṃ nāmānaṃ paccayo nahotiyeva. Tasmā na sundarametanti.

“Because mutual conditionality exists only by way of mutual support, and not merely by being co-arisen, in the course of existence, materiality is not a mutual condition for mentality. Therefore, it is said, ‘mind and mental factors are mutual conditions.’” Here, by ‘not merely by being co-arisen,’ it is conceded that if mutual conditionality were merely by way of co-arisen states, then in the course of existence, materiality would be a mutual condition for mentality. But even by way of the co-arisen condition, materiality is still not a condition for mentality in the course of existence. Therefore, this is not well-stated.

Chavatthūni sattannaṃ viññāṇadhātūnanti ettha vatthusahajāta nissayo vatthupurejātanissayo vatthārammaṇapurejātanissayoti tividho vatthunissayo. Tattha paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ vatthusahajātanissayo. Yaṃ pana pavattiyaṃ purejātaṃ, vatthuṃ nissāya cittaṃ uppajjati, taṃ tassa cittassa vatthupurejātanissayonāma. Yaṃ pana purejātaṃ vatthu yassa cittassa [M 0.0402] nissayoceva hoti ārammaṇañca, taṃ tassa vatthārammaṇa purejātanissayonāma. Vuttañhetaṃ paṭṭhāne ārammaṇa nissaya purejātavippayutta atthiavigatanti tīṇīti. Kathañca taṃ cittassa nissayoca ārammaṇañca hotīti. Paccuppannaṃ vatthuṃ ārabbha sammasanavasenavā assādanādivasenavā iddhividhakiccādhiṭṭhānavasenavā cittaṃ uppajjati, evaṃ taṃ cittassa nissayoca ārammaṇañca hotīti. Vuttañhetaṃ paṭṭhāne-ajjhattaṃ vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato vipassati, assādeti. Abhinandati. Taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati. Domanassaṃ uppajjatīti.

Regarding 'the six bases for the seven consciousness-elements': here, base-dependence is threefold: co-arisen base-dependence, pre-arisen base-dependence, and pre-arisen base-object-dependence. Therein, at the moment of rebirth-linking, the base is the co-arisen base-dependence for the resultant aggregates. But during the course of existence, when consciousness arises dependent on a pre-arisen base, that is called pre-arisen base-dependence for that consciousness. And when a pre-arisen base is both the dependence and the object for a certain consciousness, that is called pre-arisen base-object-dependence. As it is said in the Paṭṭhāna: 'object, dependence, prenascence, dissociation, presence, non-disappearance'—these three. And how is it both dependence and object for that consciousness? Consciousness arises by taking a present base as object, either through contemplation, through delighting, or through establishing the tasks of psychic powers, etc. Thus, it is both dependence and object for that consciousness. As it is said in the Paṭṭhāna: 'One contemplates the internal base as impermanent, as suffering. One delights in it, rejoices in it. Based on that, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and sorrow arises.'

Ettha pana ācariyā imaṃ vatthārammaṇapurejātanissayaṃnāma maraṇāsannakāleeva vācanāmaggaṃ āropayiṃsu. Ayaṃpanettha tesaṃ adhippāyo. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ tāva aniṭṭhe ṭhāne āvajjanena vinā vīthicittānaṃ pavatti paṭisiddhā hoti. Tathā ekāvajjanavīthi yañca cittānaṃ ārammaṇaṃnāma dhammatoca kālatoca abhinnameva icchanti aṭṭhakathācariyā. Pakatikāleca cittānināma pacceka vatthunissayāni honti. Tasmā yadā paccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vatthuṃ ārabbhaaniccādivasena sammasanti, etaṃ mamātivā assādenti, tadāyaṃ vatthu āvajjitaṃ hoti. Javanānipi tadeva gaṇhanti. Na attano attano nissayavatthūni. Yadi hi tānivā aññaṃvā ārammaṇaṃ gaṇheyyuṃ. Nirāvajjanānināma javanāni honti. Kasmā, āvajjanena āvajjitaṃ agahetvā aññaṃ gahetvā pavattanatoti. Bhinnā rammaṇānicanāma honti. Pacchā uppannāni paccekavatthūnivā aññaṃvā gahetvā pavattanatoti. Naca tathā sakkā bhavituṃ aṭṭhakathā virodhato. Tasmā so vatthārammaṇa purejātapaccayo pakati kāle na sakkā laddhunti. Maraṇāsannakāle pana sabbāni āvajjanādīni cittāni ekameva vatthuṃ nissāya pavattantīti taṃ ārabbha pavattānaṃ āvajjanādīnaṃ tesaṃ tadeva vatthuca ārammaṇañca hoti. Evañhi sati tesaṃ nirāvajjanatāvā bhinnārammaṇatāvā natthīti ayaṃ tesaṃ adhippāyoti.

Here, however, the teachers applied this so-called pre-arisen base-object-dependence to the path of exposition only at the moment near death. This is their intention here. In the commentaries, for one, the occurrence of a cognitive process of consciousnesses without adverting is prohibited in an undesirable situation. And likewise, the commentary teachers desire that the object of consciousnesses in a single-adverting cognitive process should be undivided both in nature and in time. Moreover, in the normal course of events, consciousnesses have individual material supports. Therefore, when one reflects on a currently arisen internal base by contemplating impermanence and so forth, or enjoys it thinking “This is mine,” then this base has been adverted to. The impulsions also grasp that same object, not their own separate material supports. For if they were to grasp their own supports, or even a different object, the impulsions would be without adverting. Why? Because that would be arising having ignored the adverted object and grasping something else. And they would be called 'having different objects' because, having arisen later, they would arise having grasped individual bases or other objects. But this is not possible, as it contradicts the commentaries. Therefore, in the normal course of events, this pre-arisen base-object condition cannot be obtained. However, at the moment near death, all consciousnesses—from adverting onwards—arise dependent on a single base. Thus, for those [consciousnesses] arising in relation to it, that same base is both their material support and their object. In this way, since there is neither a state of being without adverting nor a state of having different objects for them, this is their intention.

Tattha [M 0.0403] pana yadi āvajjanena āvajjitaṃ vatthuṃ agahetvā attano attano nissayavatthūni gaṇheyyuṃ. Nirāvajjanānināma javanāni bhaveyyunti idaṃ tāva na yujjati. Āvajjanena āvajji tappakārasseva gahaṇato. Yathā hi āvajjanaṃpi vatthuntveva āvajjati. Tathā javanānica vatthuntveva javanti. No aññathāti natthi javanānaṃ nirāvajjanatāti. Yathā ca nirāvajjanatā natthi, tathā bhinnārammaṇatāpi tesaṃ natthiyeva. Kasmā, vibhāgassa asambhavato. Nahi santatighanavasena ekībhūtamiva pubbāparaṃ pavatta mānesu bahūsu vatthusu ekamekaṃ vatthuṃ idamevāti visuṃ katvā āvajjanaṃvājavanānivā gahetuṃ sakkonti. Naca tathā asakkuṇeyyesu ṭhānesu ekantena dhammatovā kālatovā bhinnā rammaṇatānāma sakkā laddhunti iti bhinnārammaṇatāpi tesaṃ natthi yevāti. Ettāvatā imassa vatthārammaṇapurejātanissaya vidhānassa pakatikālepi labbhamānatā sādhitā hotīti.

Here, however, if, without grasping the object adverted to by adverting, they were to grasp their own respective base-objects, the impulsions would be without adverting—this, to begin with, is untenable. For it is by adverting that an object is adverted to, and what is grasped is of that very kind. Just as adverting adverts to an object as an object, so too do the impulsions impel towards the object as an object—not otherwise. Thus, there is no such thing as impulsions being without adverting. And just as there is no absence of adverting, so too there is no difference in their objects. Why? Because division is impossible. For in the continuous stream, which appears as if a single mass because of its dense succession, when many objects arise in sequence, it is not possible to distinctly grasp each single object as “this alone” either through adverting or impulsions. And in situations where this is not possible, a difference in objects, either by nature or by time, cannot be obtained. Thus, there is indeed no difference in objects for them. To this extent, the obtainability of this arrangement of pre-arisen base-object-dependence is established even in the normal course of events.

Apica, sabbaṃ paccuppannaṃ attano rūpakāyaṃ ārabbha rūpaṃ me aniccantivā etaṃ mamātivā samanupassantānaṃ ajjhattarūpesu idaṃ nāmarūpaṃ tassacittassa ārammaṇaṃ nahotīti navattabbaṃ. Ārammaṇa bhūtesu pana tesu kiñci ārammaṇamattaṃ kiñci ārammaṇapurejātaṃ kiñci vatthārammaṇapurejātaṃ hotīti sakkā vattunti. Kabaḷī kāro āhāroti kāmāvacarasattānaṃ paṭisandhito paṭṭhāya uppanno catusamuṭṭhānika rūpāhāroceva bahiddhāhāroca. Gabbhaseyyakānañhi yāva mātuyā āhārapharaṇaṃ nalabbhati, tāva kalalādikālesu tisamuṭṭhāniko ajjhattāhāroyeva upatthambhanakiccaṃ sādheti. Vuttañhetaṃ paṭṭhāne-paṭisandhikkhaṇe kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayoti, ojaṭṭhamakarūpasamuṭṭhāpanaṃ panassa bahiddhāhārupatthambhanaṃ laddhakāleyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yadievaṃ –

Moreover, for those who contemplate internal forms, taking as an object all present form in their own physical body and seeing 'my form is impermanent' or 'this is mine,' it should not be said that this name-and-form is not the object of their consciousness. But among those that are objects, some are merely object, some are pre-arisen object, and some are pre-arisen base-object—thus it can be said. 'Edible food' refers to both material nutriment arisen from four sources and external nutriment, which arise for beings in the sense-sphere, starting from rebirth-linking. For those in the womb, until nourishment from the mother is obtained, during the stages of the embryo and so on, only internal nutriment arising from threefold origination fulfills the supporting function. As it is said in the Paṭṭhāna: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, edible food is a condition for this body by way of the nutriment condition.' But it should be understood that the arising of material form with nutritive essence as the eighth factor and its support by external nutriment occur only when the external nutriment is obtained. If it is thus—

Yañcassa bhuñjati mātā, annaṃ pānañca bhojanaṃ. Tena so tattha yāpeti, mātukucchigato tiroti

Whatever food, drink, and edibles his mother consumes, by that he sustains himself there, hidden in his mother's womb.

Kasmā [M 0.0404] vuttanti. Pākaṭāhārena tassa yakkhassa bodhanatthanti. Imassakāyassāti gabbhaseyyakānaṃ tāva paṭisandhicittassa uppādakkhaṇe ekasamuṭṭhānikassa ṭhitibhaṅgakkhaṇesu dvisamuṭṭhāni kassa tatoparaṃ tisamuṭṭhānikassa ojāpharaṇakāle catusamuṭṭhānikassaca kāyassa. Itaresaṃpi yathāsambhavaṃ vattabbaṃ. Rūpaloke pana vināpi duvidhena ojāhārakiccena appanāpatta kammavisesena siddhassa suciraṃpi addhānaṃ pharituṃ samatthassa rūpa jīvitindriyassa tathārūpānañca bhavaṅgapariyāpannānaṃ arūpāhārānaṃ vasena anekakappānipi attabhāvassa pavatti veditabbā. Etenupāyena kammajakāyabahutaresu devesu petanirayesuca suciraṃpi kālaṃ bahiddhāhārena vinā attabhāvassa pavatti vattabbā. Tesu pana ajjhattāhāropi labbhatiyevāti kiñcāpi okkantikkhaṇe vipākakkhandhāpi vatthussa vippayuttapaccayā honti. Te pana cittacetasikādhammā sahajātarūpānanti ettha saṅgayhissantīti katvā okkantikkhaṇevatthuvipākānanti vuttaṃ.

Why is it said? For the purpose of informing that yakkha by means of manifest food. Regarding 'this body': for those in the womb, at the moment of the arising of the rebirth-linking consciousness, the body is of a single origination; at the moments of stability and dissolution, it is of two originations; thereafter, of three originations; and at the time of nutriment assimilation, of four originations. The same should be stated for others as is appropriate. In the realm of form, however, it should be understood that the continuation of existence for many eons occurs even without the twofold function of nutriment. This is by means of the material life faculty—which is accomplished through a special kind of kamma that has attained absorption and is capable of pervading for a very long time—and by means of such formless nutriments pertaining to the life-continuum. By this method, the continuation of existence for a very long time, even without external food, should be stated for the many devas whose bodies are kamma-born, and for those in the realms of ghosts and hells. Yet, internal nutriment is also obtainable for them. Although at the moment of conception the resultant aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of dissociation, since those mental and mental factors will be included here under co-arisen material form, it is therefore said: 'At the moment of conception, the physical base for the resultants...'

Sabbathāti sabbapakāraṃ sahajātantiādinā yojetabbaṃ. Pakāroca tividho hoti sahajātapaccayotiādivasena veditabbo. Rūpajīvitamiccayanti evaṃ porāṇehi vutto ayaṃ atthipaccayo avigatapaccayocāti yojetabbaṃ. Nanu kabaḷīkārāhāro rūpajīvitindriyañca sahajāte saṅgahetabbaṃ. Evañhi sati tividhova atthipaccayo siyāti.Na. Sahajananasaṅkhātassa sahuppādanalakkhaṇassa abhāvā. Sahuppādanalakkhaṇo hi sahajātapaccayo. Kabaḷīkārāhāroca ojaṭṭhamakarūpāni uppādentopi attano ṭhitikkhaṇeeva uppādeti, no uppādakkhaṇe. Yathāca mahābhūtā sahajātarūpāni upatthambhantā attanā saha uppādanapubbakāeva upatthambhanti, na tathā so āhāro. So pana vināva sahuppādanakiccena sahajātānipi asahajātānipi upatthambhatīti rūpajīvitaṃpi saha uppādanakiccena vināva saha jātarūpāni anupāleti. Iti ime dvepi dhammā sahajāta lakkhaṇābhāvāeva sahajātapaccaye asaṅgahitā. Idāni sabbepi [M 0.0405] catuvīsatipaccayā saṅgayhamānā cattāropaccayā hontīti dassetuṃ ārammaṇūpanissaya.La. Samodhānaṃ gacchantīti vuttaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ samodhānavidhi, catuvīsatiyā paccayesu adhipati paccayo tāva duvidho ārammaṇasahajātavasena. Tattha ārammaṇādhipati tīsu kammavajjesu samodhānaṃ gacchati. Ārammaṇa mattaṃpi hi kammena saha samodhānaṃ nagacchati. Kuto adhipati bhūtanti.

The term 'sabbathā' means 'in every way' and should be connected with 'co-arisen,' etc. The manner is threefold and should be understood as by way of the co-arisen condition, etc. Regarding 'rūpajīvitamiccayanti,' this is how the ancients explained it, and it should be connected thus: 'This is the presence condition and the non-disappearance condition.' Now, should not edible food and the life faculty of materiality be included among the co-arisen? If so, the presence condition would indeed be threefold. No. Because the characteristic of co-arising, which is called co-generation, is absent. The co-arisen condition has the characteristic of co-arising. Edible food, even while producing the material octad with nutritive essence, produces it only at the moment of its own stability, not at the moment of arising. And just as the great elements, while supporting co-arisen material phenomena, support them having co-arisen with them, food does not do so in the same way. It, however, without the function of co-arising, supports both co-arisen and non-co-arisen phenomena. Thus, the life faculty of materiality also sustains co-arisen material phenomena without the function of co-arising. Therefore, these two phenomena, due to the absence of the characteristic of co-arising, are not included in the co-arisen condition. Now, to show that all twenty-four conditions, when grouped, become four conditions—object, decisive support, etc.—it is said, 'they come to consolidation.' Herein, the method of consolidation is as follows: First, among the twenty-four conditions, the predominance condition is twofold: by way of object and by way of co-arising. Among these, the object predominance condition consolidates into three conditions, excluding the kamma condition. For a mere object does not consolidate with kamma. How then could it be a predominance?
