The ability to emerge more swiftly from the attained jhāna is called mastery in emerging (vuṭṭhānavasī). As for mastery in reviewing (paccavekkhaṇavasī), it is accomplished as soon as mastery in adverting (āvajjanavasī) is accomplished.

Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

But in the Vibhāvanī it is said:

Yattakaṃ kālaṃ icchati. Tattakaṃ cirataraṃ jhānaṃ thapetuṃ samatthatā adhiṭṭhānavasitānāmātipi vuttaṃ. Tathā paricchinna kālato anto avuṭṭhahitvā yathāparicchinnakālavaseneva vuṭṭhānasamatthatā vuṭṭhānavasitānāmāti. Taṃpi yujjatiyeva.

The ability to sustain the jhāna for as long as one wishes is also called mastery in resolution. Similarly, the ability to emerge according to the predetermined time, without emerging before that predetermined time, is called mastery in emerging. This too is fitting.

Pāḷiyañhi pathamajjhānaṃ yatthicchakaṃ yadicchakaṃ yāvaticchakaṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Adhiṭṭhānāya dandhāyitattaṃ natthītiādinā sīghataraṃvā hotu. [M 0.0425] Cirataraṃvā. Yattakaṃ kālaṃ jhānaṃ thapetuṃvā yattake kāle tato uṭṭhātuṃvā icchati. Tattakaṃ kālaṃ anūnaṃvā anadhikaṃvā katvā adhiṭṭhātuṃvā vuṭṭhātuṃvā samatthatāpi dassitāyeva hotīti. Evañcasati vuṭṭhānavasitāpi adhiṭṭhānavasitāya siddhāya siddhāevāti tāsaṃ dvinnaṃ visesakappanāpi nippayojanā hotīti daṭṭhabbā. Vasanaṃ vasī. Samatthatāti attho. Issara bhāvoti vuttaṃ hoti. Vasīeva vasitā. Yathā devoeva devatāti. Katvā padahatoti sambandho. Vitakkādikaṃ oḷārikaṅgaṃ pahānāyāti ettha pathamajjhānaṃ tāva vasībhūtaṃ katvā ṭhitassa vitakko oḷārikato upaṭṭhāti. Tadā ahovatame avitakkaṃ jhānaṃ assāti evamassa ajjhāsayo saṇṭhāti. Tadā avitakkaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjissāmīti puna tasmiṃ paṭibhāganimitte parikammaṃ karontassa sā bhāvanā vitakkavirāgabhāvanānāma hoti. Sāpi yāva vitakke nikanti na pariyādiyati, tāva parikammabhāvanānāma. Pariyādinnāya pana vitakkanikantiyā upacāra bhāvanānāma hoti. Esanayo sesajjhānupacāresupi. Evaṃ taṃtaṃjhānaṅgavirāgabhāvanābalena vitakkādikassa oḷārikassa tassa tassa jhānaṅgassa pajahanatthāya. Vicārādisukhumaṅguppattiyāti vicārādīnaṃ sukhumānaṃ catunnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ dvinnaṃ puna dvinnaṃvā jhānaṅgānaṃ tena tena vitakkādinā oḷārikena aṅgena vinā puna uppattiyā. Pāhatoti padahantassa. Padhānanāmakaṃ ātāpavīriyaṃ karontassāti attho. Dutīyajjhānādayoti dutīyajjhānādīni sesarūpāvacarajjhānāni. Yathārahanti idaṃ dvāvīsakammaṭṭhānesu dutīyajjhānādīnaṃ anurūpāni kasiṇaānāpāṇāni sandhāya vuttaṃ. Avasesesu pana aṭṭhārasakammaṭṭhānesu yasmā arūpajjhānāni nāma ārammaṇātikkamanavaseneva pavattanti. Tadatikkamanatthañca kasiṇugghāṭanaṃnāma hoti. Tasmā yesu tadugghāṭanaṃ sambhavati. Tāniyeva kasiṇāni dassetuṃ ākāsavajjitakasiṇesūti vuttaṃ. Ākāsakasiṇañhi ugghāṭīyamānaṃpi ākāsa meva hotīti natthi tattha tadatikkamanasambhavoti. Ugghāṭetvāti yathādiṭṭhe [M 0.0426] kasiṇanimitte kasiṇanimittasaññaṃ akatvā tattha ākāsaṃ anantaṃ ākāsaṃ anantanti ākāsasaññaṃ pavattentassa citte taṃkasiṇanimittaṃ antaradhāyati. Tappamāṇaṃ ākāsameva upaṭṭhāti. Evaṃ kasiṇasaññāvidhamanena ākāsasaññāpavattanenaca yaṃkiñci kasiṇaṃ ugghāṭetvā viyojetvāti attho. Laddhaṃ ākāsaṃ ārabbhāti pāṭṭhasesena sambandho. Esanayo pathamā ruppaviññāṇantiādīsupi. Anantavasenāti anantaṃ ākāsanti evaṃ pavattamanasikāravasena. Santametaṃ paṇītametanti parikammaṃ karontassāti ettha tathā sambhāvetvā parikammaṃ karontassapi ārammaṇassa samatikkantattā upari jhānaṃ hotiyevāti vuttaṃ catutthāruppamappetīti. Parikammaṃkatvāti so bhagavā itipi arahantiādinā samanussaraṇaparikammaṃ katvā. Tasminti tasmiṃ buddhaguṇādike ālambaṇe. Bhūmatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Nimitteti tassa ārammaṇassa ākārasaṅkhāte nimitte. Bhāvalakkhaṇe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Sādhukamuggahiteti ārammaṇassa vibhūtatara vasenavā cittassa tasmiṃ ninnapoṇapabbhāravasenavā suṭṭhu uggahite. Upacāroca sampajjati ariyasāvakānaṃ diṭṭhasaccānanti adhippāyo. Itaresaṃpi vā maraṇasaññāvavatthānesūti. Etthaca nīvaraṇavikkhambhanena jhānaṅgapātubhāvenacaupacārasampadā veditabbā. Evaṃ cattālīsakammaṭṭhānesuyathārahaṃsamathajjhānānaṃ pavattiṃ dassetvāidānitesusamathajjhānesukasiṇajjhānānaṃ nisandabhūtaṃabhiññā pavattiṃ dassetuṃ abhiññāvasenapavattamānantiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yo katādhikāro hoti. Āsannabhave samathajjhānesu katābhiyogovā hoti, pūritabodhisambhāro mahāpurisa jātikovā. Tassa aṭṭhavidhesu navavidhesuvā samathajjhānesusijjha mānesu abhiññāpi sijjhatiyeva. Rūpajjhānamattesupi sijjhantesu sijjhati yevātipi vadanti. Teneva hi aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ visuddhimaggeca āruppajjhānānaṃpaccayabhāvaṃanupagatassapiākāsakasiṇajjhānassa abhiññāpādakatāsambhavo vuttoti. Dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana nahi aṭṭhasu samāpattīsu cuddasahākārehi ciṇṇavasībhāvaṃ vinā upari [M 0.0427] abhiññādhigamo hotīti vuttaṃ. Taṃ pana thapetvā purisa visese avasesānaṃ bahūnaṃ ādikammikakulaputtānaṃ sādhāraṇavasena vuttanti yuttaṃ. Teneva hi visuddhimagge imehi pana cuddasahi ākārehi cittaṃ aparidametvā pubbe abhāvitabhāvano ādikammiko yogāvacaro iddhivikubbanaṃ sampādessatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti vuttaṃ. Tasmā tādisānaṃ aṭṭhasu samāpattīsu ciṇṇavasībhāvānaṃ abhiññākamme ādikammikakulaputtānaṃ kasiṇā nulomato kasiṇapaṭilomatotiādinā nayena vuttehi cuddasahi ākārehi attano rūpapañcamajjhānacittaṃ paridametvā tikkhaṃ sūraṃ abhinīhārakkhamaṃ katvā idāni iddhivikubbanaṃ karissā mīti ārabhantānaṃ abhiññāvasena pavattamānaṃ pana rūpāvacarapañca majjhānaṃ rūpādīsu chasu ālambaṇesu yathārahaṃ appetīti yojanā veditabbā. Abhiññāpādakapañcamajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvāti abhiññāya pādakatthāya yaṃabhiññājātikaṃ rūpāvacarapañcamajjhānaṃ sabbapathamaṃ samāpajjiyati. Tato bhavaṅgapavattivasena vuṭṭhahitvā. Adhiṭṭhātabbanti adhiṭṭheyyaṃ. Savatthukaṃ satarūpasahassarūpādikaṃ nimmitarūpaṃ. Taṃ adhiṭṭheyyaṃ ādi yassa avatthukassa āvibhāvatirobhāvādikassa kammassāti adhiṭṭheyyādikaṃ. Āvajjitvā parikammaṃkarontassāti ettha iddhividhe tāva yaṃyaṃsatādikaṃ nimmitarūpaṃvā āvibhāvādikaṃ nimmitakammaṃvā nipphādetuṃ icchati. Taṃ taṃ avajjitvā sallakkhetvā sataṃ homi sahassaṃ homītivā sataṃ hotu sahassaṃ hotūtivā idañcidañca hotu evañcevañca hotūtivā parikammaṃ karontassa. Dibbasotādīsu pana yaṃ yaṃ ārammaṇaṃ sotuṃvā passituṃvā jānituṃvā anussarituṃvā icchati. Taṃ taṃ sallakkhetvā asukassa asukānaṃvā saddaṃ suṇomītiādinā parikammaṃ karontassa. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana parikammaṃ katvā puna pādakajjhānasamāpajjanaṃ āgatameva. Yathāha abhiññāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya sace sataṃ icchati. Sataṃ homīti parikammaṃ katvā puna abhiññāpādakaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya adhiṭṭhāti. Adhiṭṭhānacittena saheva sataṃ hotīti. [M 0.0428] Tatthaca ādito pādakajjhānasamāpajjanaṃ parikamma cittassa samādānatthāya hoti. Pacchimaṃ pana abhiññāya anu balappadānatthāyāti. Tathā hi pādakajjhānabalena suṭṭhu samāhitaṃ parikammacittaṃnāma attano visaye abhiññācittagatikaṃ hoti. Pubbenivāsānussaraṇakāle teneva cittena tasmiṃ bhave atītaṃ dhammajātaṃ yāva paṭisandhiyā jānāti. Teneva hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ taṃsampayuttaṃ ñāṇaṃ parikammasamādhiñāṇanti vuttaṃ. Atītaṃsañāṇantipi vuccatīti. Sesābhiññāsupi tassa ñāṇassa visayaviseso yathārahaṃ vattabboti. Therena pana pacchimaṃ pādakajjhānasamāpajjanaṃnāma na sabbesaṃ hoti. Na hi abhiññāsu vasībhāvapattānaṃ puna pādakajjhānena kiccaṃ atthīti katvā taṃ idha nagahitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Rūpādīsuālambaṇesuyathārahamappetīti ettha iddhividhañāṇaṃ tāva tekālikabhūtesu chasu ārammaṇesu pavattati. Tañhi rūpādīsu chasu ārammaṇadhammesu yaṃ yaṃ nipphādeti. Taṃ taṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā pavattati. Pādakajjhānacittaṃ pana kāyagatikaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā dissamānenakāyena ākāsegamanakāle atītaṃ pādakajjhānacittaṃ ārabbha pavattati. Kāyaṃ cittagatikaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā adissamānena kāyena gamanakāle paccuppannaṃ rūpakāyaṃ ārabbha pavattati. Tathāpavattamānassa pana tassa ñāṇassa kiñcirūpaṃ ārammaṇa mattaṃ hoti. Kiñci ārammaṇapurejātaṃ. Kiñci vatthārammaṇa purejātaṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Anāgate idaṃnāma hotūti adhiṭṭhāna kāle anāgataṃ taṃtaṃrūpadhammaṃ ārabbha pavattatīti. Paccuppanno saddo dibbasotassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Atīte sattadivasāni anāgate sattadivasānīti etthantare kāle atītā nāgatapaccuppannabhūtaṃ parassacittaṃ cattārovā khandhā cetopariya ñāṇassa. Cittañhi jānanto taṃ sampayuttadhammaṃpi icchanto jānissatiyeva. Evañca katvā paṭṭhāne kusalā khandhā ceto pariyañāṇassa yathākammupagañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayoti ñāṇadvayaṃ ekato katvā vuttaṃ. Etthaca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ tāva paracittassa paccuppannālambaṇatānāma santativasenavā addhā vasenavā [M 0.0429] yojitā. Yadi hi khaṇikavasena yojeyya. Āvajjane paccuppannaṃ yaṃkiñci ekaṃ cittaṃ āvajjetvā niruddhe javanānipi tadeva āvajjanena saddhiṃ niruddhaṃ atītaṃ gaṇhantīti tāni kālato āvajjanena saha bhinnālambaṇāni nāma honti. Naca aniṭṭhe maggaphalavīthito aññasmiṃ ṭhāne kālamattenāpi tesaṃ tena saha bhinnālambaṇatā aṭṭhakathācariyehi anu matāti. Tasmā īdisesu ṭhānesu paccuppannaṃnāma santativasena addhāvasenaca gahetuṃ yuttanti. Mūlaṭīkāyaṃ pana khaṇikapaccuppanna vaseneva yojitaṃ. Nahi abhidhamme atītārammaṇattikaṃ santati addhānavaseneva vuttanti sakkā vattuṃ. Itarathā paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo āsevanapaccayena paccayoti vattabbo siyā. Na tu vutto. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo āsevanapaccayena paccayoticceva pana vutto, tasmā āvajjanādīni sabbāni cittāni paccekaṃ attanā khaṇavasena sahuppannāni parassa cittānigaṇhantīti yuttaṃ, naca tāni dhammato bhinnā lambaṇānināma honti. Gahaṇā kārassa abhinnattā. Āvajjanaṃpi hi cittanteva āvajjati. Javanānica cittaṃ cittanteva javanti. Tānica sabbāni cittānieva hontīti. Atītānantara cutito pana paṭṭhāya atītā khandhā khandhupani bandhā nāma gottakasiṇa nimittādikā paññattiyo nibbānañca pubbenivāsañāṇassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Paccuppannaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ dibbacakkhussāti evaṃ rūpādīsu chasu ālambaṇesu yathāraha mappetīti. Idāni abhiññāvasena pavakkhassa tassa pañcamajjhānassa kiccabhedena pabhedaṃ dassetuṃ iddhividhantiādigātha māha. Tattha yaṃ yaṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Yathā yathāca adhiṭṭhāti. Tassa tassa tathā tathāvā ijjhana saṅkhāto vidho koṭṭhāso pakārovā etassāti iddhividhaṃ. Taṃ pana tividhaṃ adhiṭṭhā niddhi vikubbaniddhi manomayiddhi vasena. Tattha attano pakativaṇṇaṃ avijahitvā tasseva sata sahassādi bahubhāva karaṇa vasenavā ākāsagamanādivasena vā bahiddhā nānāvaṇṇa pāṭihāriya [M 0.0430] dassana vasenavā pavattitā iddhi adhiṭṭhāniddhināma. Pakativaṇṇaṃ pana vijahitvā attānameva kumāravaṇṇanāgavaṇṇādikaṃ katvā dassanavasena pavattitā iddhi vikubbaniddhināma. Attano sarīrabbhantare aññaṃ sabbaso attanā sadisaṃ sarīraṃ nimminitvā nīharitvā dassanavasena pavattitā iddhi manomayiddhināma. Dive bhavaṃ dibbaṃ. Devaloke jātanti attho. Dibbañca taṃ sotañcāti dibbasotaṃ. Devānaṃ uḷārakammanibbattā dūrepi paṭicchannepi ārammaṇasampaṭicchanasamatthaṃ pasādasotaṃ. Dibbasotasadisattā pana idaṃ abhiññāñāṇaṃpi dibbasotanti vuccati. Kasiṇajjhāna saṅkhātenavā dibbavihārena paṭiladdhattā sayañca tasmiṃ dibbavihāre pariyāpannattā dibbañca taṃ sotañcāti dibbasotaṃ. Parassa cittaṃ vijānanti etenāti paracittavijānanaṃ. Tadeva cetopariyāyanti paricchijja jānanti etenāti katvā cetopariyañāṇantipi vuccati. Pubbe nivāso vuccati atītabhavesu attano chasu dvāresu āpātaṃ āgatā suṭṭhu viditā dhammā. Pubbe atītajātīsu gocara nivāsavasena nivasiṃsu attano chadvārikāni cittāni etthāti katvā. Sabbaññubuddhānaṃ pana paresaṃ chadvāragahitāpi dhammā pubbe nivāso hotiyeva, pubbe nivāsassa anussaraṇaṃ pubbenivāsānussati. Idha pana taṃ sampayuttañāṇaṃ adhippetaṃ. Pubbe vuttanayena dibbañca taṃ cakkhucāti dibbacakkhu. Taṃ sadisattā idaṃ abhiññāñāṇaṃpi dibbacakkhūti vuccati. Dibbavihāra vasena paṭiladdhattā sayañca dibbavihārasannissitattā dibbañca taṃ cakkhucāti dibbacakkhu. Yathākammupagañāṇaṃ anāgataṃsañāṇanti imāni dve ñāṇāni imasseva paribhaṇḍañāṇānināma. Nahi tesaṃ paṭilābhatthāya visuṃ cittaparidamanaparikammaṃnāma atthi. Dibbacakkhuñāṇe paṭiladdhe tesaṃpi paṭiladdhattāti. Tattha dibbacakkhunā nirayesu dukkhaṃ devesuvā sukhaṃ anubhavante satte disvā tesaṃ atītaṃ kammaṃ jānissāmīti parikammaṃ karontassa taṃ kammārammaṇaṃ yathākammupagañāṇaṃ pavattati. Tato cavitvā kattha bhavissantīti tesaṃ anāgate pavattiṃ passissāmīti parikammaṃ [M 0.0431] karontassa tesaṃ anāgatakhandhārammaṇaṃ anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ pavattati. Pubbe nivāsānussati ñāṇaṃ viyaca sabbaṃpi anāgatadhammajātaṃ etassa ārammaṇaṃ hotiyeva. Etañhi attano visaye sabbaññutañāṇagatikanti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ.

Indeed, in the Pali, one determines the first jhana as one wishes, for as long as one wishes. By means of the understanding that there is no slowness in determination, it can be made faster or slower. Whether one wishes to maintain the jhana for a certain time or to rise from it after a certain time, the ability to determine or rise, making it neither less nor more than that time, is indeed demonstrated. And thus, when this is so, since mastery in determination is accomplished, mastery in rising is also accomplished; therefore, it should be understood that even the conceptualization of a distinction between these two is useless. Mastery (vasanaṃ) is the master (vasī). This is the meaning of capability. It is said to be the state of lordship. Mastery (vasī) itself is mastery (vasitā), just as a god (devo) is divinity (devatā). The connection is 'having done, one strives'. Here, for the abandoning of the coarse factor of initial application (vitakka) and so forth: when one has first mastered and established the first jhana, initial application appears as coarse. At that time, his inclination is established thus: 'Oh, may there be a jhana without initial application for me!' Then, for one doing the preliminary work on that counterpart sign with the intention 'I will attain the jhana without initial application,' that development is called the development of dispassion toward initial application. As long as delight in initial application is not exhausted, that is called preparatory development. But when delight in initial application is exhausted, it is called access development. This method applies to the access of the remaining jhanas as well. Thus, by the power of the development of dispassion towards each respective jhana factor, for the sake of abandoning the coarse factor of initial application and so forth, which is that particular jhana factor. The arising of subtle factors like sustained application (vicāra) and so forth means the re-arising of the four, three, or two subtle jhana factors without that coarse factor of initial application and so forth. 'Striven' (padahato) means for one who strives, that is, for one making effort and energy called exertion (padhāna). 'The second jhana and so forth' refers to the second jhana and so forth, which are the remaining form-sphere jhanas. 'As appropriate' (yathārahaṃ) is said here with reference to the kasinas and mindfulness of breathing that are suitable for the second jhana and so forth among the twenty-two meditation subjects. But for the remaining eighteen meditation subjects, since the formless jhanas indeed occur only by way of transcending the object, and for that transcendence, there is what is called the removal of the kasina. Therefore, to show only those kasinas where such removal is possible, it is said 'in the kasinas excluding space'. For the space kasina, even when being removed, it is just space; thus, there is no possibility of transcending it there. 'Having removed' means that in the mind of one who, not making the perception of a kasina sign in the kasina sign as seen, develops the perception of space thus: 'Space is infinite, space is infinite,' that kasina sign disappears, and only space of that measure appears. Thus, by the destruction of kasina perception and the development of space perception, the meaning is 'having removed and separated any kasina'. 'Having obtained space as the object' is connected with the remaining part of the text. This method applies also to 'the first formless consciousness' and so forth. 'By way of infinity' (anantavasena) means by way of mental attention occurring thus: 'Space is infinite'. Here, for one doing the preliminary work, contemplating 'This is peaceful, this is sublime': even for one who, having thus conceived, does the preliminary work, since the object is transcended, the higher jhana certainly arises, as it is said, 'he applies his mind to the fourth formless attainment'. 'Having prepared' means that one, having done the preliminary work of recollection by 'He is indeed an Arahant' and so forth. 'In that' (tasmiṃ) refers to that object, the qualities of the Buddha and so forth. And this locative word is in the sense of 'basis'. 'In the sign' (nimitte) refers to the sign, which is the aspect of that object. And this locative word is in the sense of 'characteristic of being'. 'Well grasped' (sādhukaṃ uggahite) means that the object is well grasped either by way of its being very clear, or by way of the mind being inclined, tending, and leaning towards it. And access is achieved: this is the intention for noble disciples who have seen the truth, or for others, in the determination of death perception. And here, the accomplishment of access should be understood by the suppression of hindrances and the manifestation of jhana factors. Having thus shown the occurrence of serenity jhanas in the forty meditation subjects as appropriate, now, to show the occurrence of direct knowledge, which is the result of these serenity jhanas, especially the kasina jhanas, it is said 'occurring by way of direct knowledge' and so forth. Here, one who has made a foundation, or who in a near existence has applied himself to serenity jhanas, or who is of the nature of a great being who has fulfilled the requisites for enlightenment—for such a one, when the eightfold or ninefold serenity jhanas are being accomplished, direct knowledge is also accomplished indeed. Some also say that it is accomplished even when only the form jhanas are being accomplished. Thus, in the Atthasalini and the Visuddhimagga, it is said that even the space kasina jhana, even though it has not attained the state of being a condition for the formless jhanas, can be a basis for direct knowledge. However, in the Digha Nikaya commentary, it is said that without having practiced mastery in the eight attainments in fourteen ways, the attainment of higher direct knowledge does not occur. But it is appropriate to say that this is stated in a general way for the many remaining beginner clansmen, excluding special individuals. Thus, in the Visuddhimagga, it is said: 'It is not possible for a beginner meditator, who has not previously developed development and has not disciplined his mind in these fourteen ways, to accomplish miraculous transformations.' Therefore, for such beginner clansmen who have practiced mastery in the eight attainments for the work of direct knowledge, having disciplined their own fifth form-sphere jhana consciousness by the fourteen ways stated by the method of kasina in forward order, kasina in reverse order, and so forth, and having made it sharp, brave, and capable of resolve, for those who are now undertaking, thinking 'I will perform miraculous transformations,' it should be understood that the fifth form-sphere jhana, occurring by way of direct knowledge, is applied towards the six objects—form and so forth—as appropriate. 'Having emerged from the fifth jhana that is the basis for direct knowledge' means that the fifth form-sphere jhana, which is of the nature of direct knowledge, is attained first of all for the purpose of being a basis for direct knowledge. Then, having emerged by way of the occurrence of the life-continuum. 'To be determined' (adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ) is that which is to be determined (adhiṭṭheyyaṃ), namely, a created form with a basis, such as a hundred forms, a thousand forms, and so forth. That which is to be determined is the beginning of the action without a basis, such as appearing and disappearing, and so forth; this is 'that which is to be determined and so forth'. 'Having adverted and prepared' (āvajjitvā parikammaṃ karontassa): here, in the case of psychic powers, first of all, whatever created form, such as a hundred, or created action, such as appearing, one wishes to produce, one adverts to that, reflects on it, and does the preliminary work, thinking: 'May I be a hundred, may I be a thousand,' or 'May it be a hundred, may it be a thousand,' or 'May this and that be thus and thus'. But in the case of the divine ear and so forth, whatever object one wishes to hear, or to see, or to know, or to recollect, one reflects on that and does the preliminary work by thinking: 'I will hear the sound of so-and-so' or 'of so-and-sos' and so forth. However, in the commentary, the attainment of the basic jhana again after doing the preliminary work has indeed come. As it is said: 'Having attained the basic jhana for direct knowledge and emerged, if one wishes for a hundred, one does the preliminary work by thinking 'May I be a hundred,' then again attains the basic jhana for direct knowledge and emerges, and then determines. With the determining consciousness itself, it becomes a hundred'. And there, the initial attainment of the basic jhana is for the sake of taking up the preparatory consciousness. But the latter is for the sake of giving further strength to the direct knowledge. For indeed, the preparatory consciousness, well concentrated by the power of the basic jhana, becomes of the nature of direct knowledge consciousness in its own sphere. At the time of recollecting past lives, with that very consciousness, one knows the phenomena that occurred in that existence, up to the rebirth-linking. Thus, in the commentary, the knowledge associated with that is called preparatory concentration knowledge. It is also called 'knowledge of the past' (atītaṃsañāṇa). For the remaining direct knowledges as well, the specific scope of that knowledge should be stated as appropriate. However, according to the Elder, the latter attainment of the basic jhana does not apply to all. For those who have attained mastery in the direct knowledges, there is no need for the basic jhana again; therefore, it should be understood that it is not included here. Here, in 'applies towards the six objects—form and so forth—as appropriate,' the knowledge of psychic powers operates on the six objects that exist in the three times. For it produces whatever among the six objective phenomena—form and so forth—and operates making that its object. But the basic jhana consciousness, having determined the body as its mode of operation, operates taking the past basic jhana consciousness as its object when moving through the sky with a visible body. Having determined the body as mind-mode, it operates taking the present material body as its object when moving with an invisible body. But for such knowledge operating thus, some form is merely an object, some is an object arisen previously, and some is a basis-object arisen previously, it should be understood. At the time of determination, thinking 'May this be so in the future,' it operates taking that particular future form-phenomenon as its object. The present sound is the object of the divine ear. In the intermediate time of seven days past and seven days future, the past, future, and present mind of another, or the four aggregates, are the object of the knowledge of penetration of minds. For one knowing the mind, wishing to know its associated phenomena as well, one will know them indeed. And having done thus, in the Patthana, it is said, combining the two knowledges, that the wholesome aggregates are conditions for the knowledge of penetration of minds and the knowledge of destiny by way of object condition. And here, in the commentary, the state of having a present object for another's mind is explained either by way of continuity or by way of duration. For if one were to explain it by way of moment: having adverted to any one present consciousness in adverting, the impulsions, when it has ceased, would take that same past consciousness which has ceased together with the adverting; thus, they would indeed have different objects in time from the adverting. And their having a different object from that, even by mere time, is not accepted by the commentary teachers in any place other than the undesirable path-and-fruit process. Therefore, in such cases, it is appropriate to take what is called 'present' by way of continuity and by way of duration. However, in the Mulatika, it is explained only by way of momentary present. For it is not possible to say that in the Abhidhamma, the triplet of past object is stated only by way of continuity and duration. Otherwise, it would have to be said that the present phenomenon is a condition for the present phenomenon by proximity condition or by repetition condition. But it is not stated thus. But it is indeed stated that the past phenomenon is a condition for the present phenomenon by proximity condition or by repetition condition. Therefore, it is appropriate that all adverting and so forth consciousnesses take others' consciousnesses individually, arising together by way of moment, and they are not called 'having different objects in essence', because the mode of apprehension is not different. For adverting indeed adverts to the mind itself. And the impulsions impel the mind itself. And all these are indeed consciousnesses. But from the immediately past death-consciousness onwards, the past aggregates, what are called 'connections of aggregates,' concepts like family, kasina signs, and so forth, and Nibbana are objects for the knowledge of past lives. The present form-object is for the divine eye: thus, it applies towards the six objects—form and so forth—as appropriate. Now, to show the division by way of difference in function of that fifth jhana which will be spoken of as occurring by way of direct knowledge, he states the verse beginning 'psychic powers' and so forth. Here, whatever one determines, and however one determines, the division, part, or kind of this, which is called the success of that in that way, is psychic power (iddhividha). But this is threefold: by way of determination power (adhiṭṭhāniddhi), transformation power (vikubbaniddhi), and mind-made power (manomayiddhi). Here, the psychic power that occurs by not abandoning one's own natural appearance, but by way of making that very body into a multitude of hundreds, thousands, and so forth, or by way of going through the sky and so forth, or by way of displaying various colored marvels externally, is called determination power (adhiṭṭhāniddhi). But the psychic power that occurs by having abandoned one's natural appearance and by way of displaying oneself having made oneself into the appearance of a youth, a naga, and so forth, is called transformation power (vikubbaniddhi). The psychic power that occurs by way of creating another body entirely similar to oneself inside one's own body and drawing it forth and displaying it, is called mind-made power (manomayiddhi). 'Divine' (dibbaṃ) means that which exists in the divine realm. This is the meaning of 'born in the divine world'. 'And that is divine and that is ear' (dibbañca taṃ sotañca) is the divine ear (dibbasota). The sensitive ear produced by the superior kamma of devas, capable of receiving objects even far away or hidden. But because of its resemblance to the divine ear, this direct knowledge is also called 'divine ear'. Or, because it is attained through the divine abiding, which is called kasina jhana, and because it is itself included in that divine abiding, it is called the divine ear. 'They know another's mind with this' (parassa cittaṃ vijānanti etena) is the knowledge of knowing another's mind (paracittavijānanaṃ). That same knowledge is also called 'knowledge of penetration of minds' (cetopariyañāṇa) because 'they know by delimiting with this' (paricchijja jānanti etena). 'Past abode' (pubbe nivāso) is said to be the phenomena that have come into view and are well known at one's own six doors in past existences. It is so called because one's own six-door consciousnesses dwelt therein by way of sphere and dwelling in past existences. But for the Omniscient Buddhas, even others’ phenomena grasped at the six doors are indeed past abodes. The recollection of past abode is past-abode recollection (pubbenivāsānussati). But here, the knowledge associated with that is intended. By the method stated previously, 'And that is divine and that is eye' (dibbañca taṃ cakkhu) is the divine eye (dibbacakkhu). Because it resembles it, this direct knowledge is also called 'divine eye'. Because it is attained by way of divine abiding, and because it is itself dependent on divine abiding, it is called the divine eye. Knowledge of destiny (yathākammupagañāṇa) and knowledge of the future (anāgataṃsañāṇa): these two knowledges are indeed called the accessory knowledges of this divine eye. For there is no separate preliminary work of mind-disciplining for their attainment. When the divine eye knowledge is attained, they are also attained. Here, for one who, having seen beings experiencing suffering in hells or happiness in divine worlds with the divine eye, does the preliminary work, thinking 'I will know their past kamma,' the knowledge of destiny, having that kamma as object, occurs. Then, for one doing the preliminary work, thinking 'Having passed away from there, where will they be? I will see their future course,' the knowledge of the future, having their future aggregates as object, occurs. And like the knowledge of past-abode recollection, all future phenomena are indeed its object. For it is said in the commentary that in its own sphere, it is of the nature of omniscient knowledge.

Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

However, it is to be elucidated.

Anāgate sattadivasato paṭṭhāya cittacetasikadhammā dutīyadivasato paṭṭhāya yaṃkiñci ārammaṇaṃ etassa visayoti adhippetaṃ. Tampi yuttaṃviya dissati.

It is intended that mind and mental factors, from seven days onward in the future, have as their domain any object starting from the second day. That also appears to be appropriate.

Nahi bhavantarepi anāvatadhamme jānituṃ samatthaṃ etaṃ imasmiṃ bhave anāgatadhamme najānātīti sakkā bhavituṃ. Yathā cetaṃ, tathā pubbenivāsañāṇaṃpi imasmiṃ bhave parasantānagate atītadhammeti. Pāḷiyaṃ pana aṭṭhakathāsuca bhavantaragatadhammehi eva ñāṇadvayaṃ yojitaṃ. Taṃ pana asādhāraṇakālavasena ānubhāvavisesapākaṭatthaṃ yojitanti yuttaṃ siyāti. Gocarabhedoti dasakasiṇādīsu gocaresu samathajjhānānaṃ pavattibhedo.

For it is impossible that this knowledge, being capable of knowing phenomena not yet arisen in another existence, should not know future phenomena in this existence. Just as this is so, so too the knowledge of past lives concerns past phenomena in another's continuum within this existence. However, in the Pāli texts and commentaries, these two knowledges are associated only with phenomena occurring in another existence. Yet, it would be appropriate that this is explained as being for the purpose of making manifest a special power by way of an uncommon time. Difference in scope refers to the difference in the functioning of the serenity absorptions in their respective domains, such as the ten kasiṇas.

Samathakammaṭṭhānanayo.

The method of the tranquility meditation subject.

171. Sabbalokiyamahājanehi yathādiṭṭhaṃ puggalasattaitthi purisādikaṃ nicca dhuva sukha atta nimittañca atikkamitvā visesena passanti etāyāti vipassanā. Kiriyā kammaṃ. Bhāvanāpayogo. Vipassanāya kammaṃ vipassanākammaṃ. Vipassanā eva vā kammanti vipassanā kammaṃ. Vipassanākammassa ṭhānaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ bhumīti vipassanākammaṭṭhānaṃ. Khandhādidhammajātaṃ. Vipassanā kammameva vā uttaruttarassa bhāvanā visesassa ānisaṃsavisesassavā ṭhānaṃ āsannakāraṇanti vipassanākammaṭṭhānaṃ. Tasmiṃ vipassanākammaṭṭhāne sattavidhena visuddhi saṅgaho tīṇi lakkhaṇānītiādinā sambandho. Niccasīlameva sayañca dussilyamalato visuddhattā kāyaṃ vācañca tato visodhanato visuddhīti sīlavisuddhi. Subhāvita cittasantānameva sayañca [M 0.0432] nīvaraṇamalato visuddhattā taṃsamaṅgipuggalañca tato visodhanato visuddhīti cittavisuddhi. Cittasīsena cettha samādhi adhippeto. Dhammavavatthānañāṇasaṅkhātā diṭṭhieva taṃ samaṅgipuggalaṃ sakkāyadiṭṭhimalato visodhanato visuddhīti diṭṭhivisuddhi. Soḷasavidhaṃ aṭṭhavidhaṃ kaṅkhaṃ vitaranti atikkamanti etāyāti kaṅkhāvitaraṇā. Paccayapariggahañāṇaṃ. Sā eva taṃsamaṅgipuggalaṃ ahetu diṭṭhi visamahetudiṭṭhīhi saddhiṃ yathāvuttāhi duvidhāhi kaṅkhāhi visodhanato visuddhīti kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi. Maggoca amaggoca maggāmaggā. Tattha ñāṇadassanavisuddhādhigamanassa upāyabhūto manasikāravidhivā ariyamaggovā maggonāma. Tassa anupāyabhūto manasikārovā adhimānavatthūnivā amaggonāma. Maggassa maggato amaggassaca amaggato jānanaṃ dassanañca maggāmaggañāṇadassanaṃ. Tameva taṃsamaṅgīpuggalaṃ amagge maggasaññāya visodhanato visuddhīti maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi nāma. Upari visesaṃ paṭipajjanti etāyāti paṭipadā. Vipassanāparaṃparasaṅkhāto pubbabhāgamaggo. Paṭipadābhūtaṃ ñāṇadassananti paṭipadāñāṇadassanaṃ. Tameva niccasaññādito visuddhattā visuddhīti paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhināma, ariyamaggañāṇasaṅkhāta ñāṇadassanameva sammohamalato visuddhattā visuddhīti ñāṇadassanavisuddhināma. Etthaca sutamayādivasena siddhaṃ anumāna ñāṇaṃpi ñāṇamevāti taṃ paṭikkhipitvā atthapaccakkhañāṇameva gahetuṃ sabbattha dassanagahaṇaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ. Lakkhīyanti sallakkhīyanti ime aniccāevāti ekantena vinicchīyanti dhammā etenāti lakkhaṇaṃ aniccatā eva lakkhaṇanti aniccalakkhaṇaṃ. Pubbapade bhāvapaccayalopo. Aññohi anicco, aññā aniccatāti. Tattha yathāgamanakriyāyogena puriso gatoti vuccati. Na pana gamana kriyā puriso. Naca puriso gamanakriyā. Aññā hi kriyā, añño puriso. Tathā aniccatāyogena sabbo saṅkhatadhammo aniccoti vuccati. Na pana aniccatā so dhammo, naca so dhammo aniccatā. Aññā hi aniccatā, añño so dhammoti. Katamā pana sā aniccatāti. Vipariṇāmā kāro. Jīraṇākāro [M 0.0433] bhijjanākāroti vuttaṃ hoti. Taṃ pana ākāraṃ disvā tadākāravante dhamme ñāṇaṃ pavattati ayaṃ dhammo aniccoti. Tasmā sā aniccatāyeva idha lakkhaṇantipi vuccatīti. Esanayo sesesupi dvīsu. Tattha pana abhiṇhasaṃpaṭipīḷanākāro dukkhatānāma. Avasavattanākāro anattatānāmāti. Yathāvuttāya pana aniccatāya saha aniccassa dhammassa aniccena vā dhammena saha aniccatāya anuanupassanā aniccānupassanā. Esa nayo sesāsupi dvīsu. Yāva sarīre dhammānaṃ tividhalakkhaṇayuttatā attano ñāṇena paññāyati. Tāva tesu tividhalakkhaṇavibhāvanavasena punappunaṃ masanaṃ āmasanaṃ sammasanaṃ. Sammasanākārena pavattaṃ ñāṇaṃ sammasanañāṇaṃ. Udayo vuccati taṃtaṃ khaṇānurūpaṃ taṃtaṃ paccayānurūpañca navanavānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātu bhāvo ceva uparupari vaḍḍhanañca. Vayo vuccati yattha yattha laddhapaccayā navanavā dhammā pātubhavanti ceva vaḍḍhantica. Tattha tattha aladdhapaccayānaṃ purāṇadhammānaṃ antaradhānaṃ. Samūha santativasena pana udayapakkhassavā vayapakkhassavā samanupassanañāṇaṃ udayabbayañāṇaṃ. Tesu pana dvīsu pakkhesu udayakoṭṭhāsonāma uparupari pākaṭo hutvā āgacchati. Vayakoṭṭhāso pana apākaṭo. So eva ca aniccatāya paramā koṭīti tasseva suṭṭhutaraṃ samanupassanañāṇaṃ bhaṅgañāṇaṃ. Bhaṅge diṭṭhe evaṃ bhijjanasabhāvānaṃ dhammānaṃ anekasahassasoka dukkhavatthubhāvena tathā tathā bhāyitabbapakārasamanupassanañāṇaṃ bhayañāṇaṃ nāma. Loke pana kiñci bhayavatthuṃ passantāpi āsanne aññasmiṃ paṭisaraṇe sati na bhāyanti. Asati eva bhāyanti. Evaṃ bhāyitabbānaṃ tesaṃ sabbaso aññapaṭisaraṇābhāvadassanaṃ ādīnavañāṇaṃ nāma. Kutoci paṭisaraṇābhāvena tehi ukkaṇṭhatākāra sahitaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ nibbidāñāṇaṃnāma. Nibbindīyamānehi tehi attānaṃ vimuccituṃ ajjhāsayasahitaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ muccitukamyatāñāṇaṃ nāma. Suṭṭhu muccituṃ icchantassa sīghaṃ muccanatthaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ cattālīsāya ākārehi anekādīnavarāsi bhāva [M 0.0434] paṭisaṅkhānavasena suṭṭhuvipphārataraṃ pavattamānaṃ vipassanā ñāṇaṃ paṭisaṅkhāñāṇaṃ nāma. Tesaṃ pana anekādīnavarāsibhāve suṭṭhu diṭṭhe saṅkhāresu nikantiyā pariyādinnāya idāni muccanupāyo laddhoti adhimattabyāpāraṃ akatvā samena vāyāmena saṅkhāre pariggaṇhantassa saṅkhārapariggahe majjhattākārasahitaṃ saṅkhāresuvā bhayañca nandiñca pahāya udāsinabhāvasahitaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃnāma. Upari maggappavattiṃ vahituṃ samatthabhāvena magguppattiyā anulomehi thāmabalehi sampannaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ anulomañāṇaṃ nāma. Heṭṭhimānaṃvā ñāṇānaṃtaṃ anulomaṃ hoti lakkhaṇattayassa suṭṭhutaraṃ vibhāvanato. Uparimaggassavā anulomaṃ hoti tassa parikammabhāvato, padaṭṭhānattācātipi anulomañāṇaṃ nāmāti. Atta jīvasuññatādassana balena khandhesu kilesabandhanato vimuccamāno maggo suññatāvimokkho nāma. Saṅkhārānaṃ yāni nimittāni kilesānaṃ avassayo hoti. Tāni vidhamitvā sabbaso dhammānaṃ anātha bhāva dassana balena vimuccamāno maggo animittovimokkho nāma. Saṅkhāresu sabbaso assāsābhāva dassanabalena vimuccamāno maggo appaṇihitovimokkhonāma. Suññatānupassanāti anattānupassanā. Sā hi dhammānaṃ samūhaghana santatighana kiccaghana ārammaṇaghanesu taṃtaṃghana vinibbhujjana vasena pavattattā attā iti gahetabbassa kassaci sārassa abhāvānupassanato suññatānupassanāti vuccati. Animittā nupassanāti aniccānupassanā. Sāpi hi santati vicchedana vasena pavattattā ahanti gahitassa nimittassa vidhamanato animittānupassanāti vuccati. Apaṇihitānupassanāti dukkhā nupassanā. Sāpi hi mahāādīnavarāsi bhāva vibhāvanavasena pavattattā idaṃ mama etaṃ mamāti gahetabbassa kassaci paṇihita guṇassa abhāvānupassanato appaṇihitānupassanāti vuccatīti. Pātimokkhasaṃvarasīlanti vinayapaññattisīlaṃ. Tañhi sabbalo kiyasīlānaṃ jeṭṭhakattā patica hoti. Catubhūmakakusalānaṃ ādipabhavabhūtattā [M 0.0435] mukhañca. Iti patimukhaṭṭhena pātimokkhanti vuccati. Tamevaca dussilyamaggassa saṃvaraṇato pidahanato saṃvaroti vuccatīti. Yesaṃ dhammānaṃ uppattiyā cakkhādīni indriyāni viphanditāni honti. Lolāni honti. Tadanubandhāca akusaladhammā uppajjanti. Tesaṃ uppatti maggassa saṃvaraṇavasena pavattamānā sati indriya saṃvaronāma. So eva sīlanti indriyasaṃvarasīlaṃ. Ājīvanti jīvitaṃ kappenti etenāti ājīvo. Paccayapariyesanavāyāmo. Soyeva buddhapaṭikuṭṭhehi pupphadānādīhi micchāpayogehi tividhakuhanavatthuhica parisuddhattā ājīvapārisuddhināma. Sā eva sīlanti samāso. Tathārūpena parisuddhena bhikkhācārādinā payogena paṭiladdhānaṃ paccayānaṃ paṭiggahaṇa paribhuñjanakālesu sammohassa gedhassa madassa pamādassaca pahānatthaṃ taṃtaṃpayojanamariyādaṃvā paṭikūlalakkhaṇaṃvā dhātumattalakkhaṇaṃvā pariggahaṇa paccavekkhanavasena pavattaṃ paccayasevane paṭisaṅkhāñāṇaṃ paccaya sannissitasīlaṃnāma. Parisujjhatīti parisuddhi. Parisuddhieva pārisuddhi. Sā eva sīlanti samāso. Cattāri pārisuddhisīlānīti catupāri suddhisīlaṃ. Cittavisuddhīti ettha cittasaddena samādhi niddiṭṭhoti vuttaṃ duvidhopisamādhi cittavisuddhināmāti. Lakkhaṇarasapaccupaṭṭhānapadaṭṭhāna vasenāti ettha dhammānaṃ paccattasabhāvo lakkhaṇaṃnāma. Aggissa uṇhattaṃ viya. Tena sabhāvena sādhetabbaṃ kiccaṃvā sādhanapaccayā paṭiladdhaguṇasaṅkhātā sampattivā rasonāma. Aggissa parivācana jotanāni viya. Sā eva sampattivā kāriyasaṅkhātaṃ phalaṃvā paccupaṭṭhānaṃnāma. Aggissa dhūmo viya. Attano uppattiyā asādhāraṇapaccayasaṅkhātaṃ āsannakāraṇaṃ padaṭṭhānaṃnāma. Tesaṃ vasena nāmassaca rūpassaca pariggaho ñāṇena paricchinditvā gahaṇaṃ nāmarūpavavatthānaṃ diṭṭhivisuddhināma. Etthaca pariggaho duvidho saṅkhepa pariggaho vitthārapariggahoti. Tattha ajjhattadhamme dvidhā katvā idaṃ nāmameva, na rūpaṃ. Idaṃ rūpameva, na nāmaṃ. Aññaṃ nāmaṃ aññaṃ rūpaṃ. Tadubhayatoca añño attāvā jīvovā sattovā puggalovā manussovā devovā brahmāvā natthīti evaṃ paccakkhato sudiṭṭhaṃ katvā [M 0.0436] pariggaṇhanaṃ saṅkhepapariggahonāma. Ñāṇuttarikohi puggalo ettakamattenapi sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ vikkhambhetuṃ sakkoti saddhiṃ saññā cittavipallāsehīti. Tayo hi vipallāsā. Yathāha-anattani attāti saññāvipallāso cittavipallāso diṭṭhivipallāsoti. Tattha satthusāsanadhamme suṭṭhu patiṭṭhitena saddhāmattenapi diṭṭhi vipallāso vikkhambhito hoti. Itare pana nāmarūpapariggahe kateyeva vikkhambhitā honti. Yāvaca ete dve avikkhambhitā honti. Tāva nāmarūpapariggahoca aparisuddhoyeva hoti. Taṃmūlikāca kilesadhammā avikkhambhitā eva hontīti apica. Catunnaṃ āhārānaṃ vasena catudhā, pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ vasena pañcadhā, channaṃ dhātūnaṃ vasena chadhātiādinā nayena nāmarūpaṃ pariggahe tabbameva. Tattha cha dhātuyonāma pathavidhātu āpodhātu tejodhātu vāyodhātu ākāsadhātu viññāṇadhātuyo. Pakkusāti kulaputto hi imā cha dhātuyo pariggaṇhitvā anāgāmiphalaṃ patvā capitvā suddhāvāsesu nibbattoti. Yattake vā pana dhamme pariggaṇhanto attā meti pavattamāne saññācittadiṭṭhi vipallāse vikkhambhetuṃ sakkoti. Tattakāpi pariggahetabbā yevāti. Imasmiṃ pana saṅgahapakaraṇe yo yo cittacetasika vibhāgo rūpavibhāgoca heṭṭhā vutto. Tassa sabbassa vasena nāmarūpassa pariggaṇhanaṃ vitthārapariggahonāma. Ayaṃpana ādikammikānaṃ avisayo. Paṭividdhacatusaccānaṃ pana ābhidhammikattherānaṃ eva visayoti veditabbo. Nāmarūpaṃ pariggaṇhantassa pana nāmarūpa mattato uddhaṃ aññassa kassaci abhāvadassanatoca sarīrabbhantare jīvasaññito attā atthi. So karoti, so paṭisaṃvedeti, saṃsarati, sandhāvatīti evaṃ pavattā diṭṭhi pahīyati. Suddhe nāme evavārūpe evavā puggalasattakriyasaññitānaṃ īhābyāpārānaṃ sabbaso abhāvadassanato tadubhayasaṃyogeeva tesaṃ labbhamānatā dassanatoca tadubhayaṃvā ekamekaṃvā uddissa attāti pavattā diṭṭhi pahīyati. Attā jīvo satto puggalo manusso devo brahmāti evamādīsu vohāresuca vohāra matte [M 0.0437] aṭṭhatvā attānāma ekantato atthi jīvonāma ekantato atthītiādinā tadatthābhinivesavasena atidhāvanañca pahīyatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tadatthābhinivesotica attānāma atthi jīvonāma atthītiādinā daḷhataraṃ abhiniveso. Atidhāvananti nāmarūpaṃ attātiādinā gahaṇaṃ. Paccayapariggahoti etthapi duvidho paccayapariggaho saṅkhepato vitthārato cāti. Tattha vatthārammaṇavasena nāmassa cittotukāhāravasena rūpassa avijjātaṇhupādānakammavasena tadubhayassaca paccayaṃ pariggaṇhanto saṅkhepato pariggaṇhātināma. Heṭṭhā paccayasaṅgahe vibhattehi paṭiccasamuppādanaya paṭṭhānanayehi pariggaṇhanto vitthārato pariggaṇhātināma. Etthapi paṭṭhānanayena pariggaho ādikammikānaṃ avisayoeva. Paccayaṃ pariggaṇhantassapana yathāvavatthitassa sabbassa nāmarūpassa sabbaso paccayāyattavuttikatādassanato ahetukadiṭṭhi pahīyati. Attano anurūpapaccayasāmaggiyā vinā aññathā pavattiyā adassanato issaranimmāna kālanimmānādikā visamahetudiṭṭhica pahīyati. Hetusambhārapaccayehi kammappavattiyā vipākappavattiyāca aññassa kammakārakassavā vipāka vedakassavā kattuno abhāvadassanato kāraka vedaka diṭṭhi pahīyati. Anamataggeca saṃsāre tīsu addhāsu hetuphala paraṃparāvasena kevalassa nāmarūpamattasseva pavattidassanato ahosiṃ nukho ahamatītamaddhānanti evamādikāya puggalasatta visayāya soḷasavidhāya kaṅkhāyaca atikkamo hoti. Sabhāvadhammapavattiyāca suṭṭhu diṭṭhāya desanādhammassa sudhammatā dassanato buddhasubuddhatañca disvā satthari kaṅkhati dhamme kaṅkhatītiādinayapavattā aṭṭhavidhāpi kaṅkhā pahīyatīti. Lokuttaradhammānaṃ saṅkhatānaṃpi sataṃ asammasanupagattā tebhūmakasaṅkhāresūti vuttaṃ. Anusayasamūhanatthañca sammasananti katvā yattha kāmarāgādayo anusayā anusenti. Teyeva dhammā sammasanārahā hontīti vuttaṃ tebhūmakasaṅkhāresūti. Imassa ca padassa lakkhaṇattayaṃ sammasantassāti iminā sambandho. Atītādibhedabhinnesūti atītānāgatapaccuppannajjhattabahiddhādīhi [M 0.0438] ekādasahi bhedehi bhinnesu. Khandhādinayaṃārabbhāti paṭisambhidāmagge vibhattaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ dvārachakkaṃ ārammaṇachakkaṃ viññāṇachakkaṃ phassachakkaṃ vedanāchakkaṃ saññāchakkanti evamādikaṃ sammasanabhūmivibhāganayaṃ ārabbha anugantvā taṃnayānusārenāti attho. Tattha pana tevīsatiyā dhammakoṭṭhāsesu yassa yo koṭṭhāso pākaṭo hoti. Tena taṃ gahetvā sammasanaṃ ārabhitabbaṃ. Sakkontena pana sabbampi gahetvā ārabhitabbameva. Kalāpavasenasaṃkhipitvāti khandhapañcakena ye rūpaṃ tāva atītānāgatapaccuppannādibhedabhinnaṃpi samānaṃ sabbaṃ ekarūpapiṇḍabhāvena saṃkhipitvā esa nayo vedanā dīsupīti. Tatrāyaṃ nayo. Yaṃkiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃvā bahiddhāvā oḷāritaṃvā sukhumaṃvā hīnaṃvā paṇītaṃvā yaṃ dūre santikevā. Sabbaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhena dukkhaṃ bhayaṭṭhena anattā asārakaṭṭhena. Yākāci vedanā.La. Yākāci saññā.La. Yekeci saṅkhārā.La. Yaṃkiñci viññāṇaṃ.La. Sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhena. Dukkhaṃ bhayaṭṭhena anattā asārakaṭṭhenāti. Etthaca sabbaṃ rūpaṃ.La. Sabbaṃ viññāṇanti gahaṇameva kalāpavasena saṅkhipananti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Aniccaṃkhayaṭṭhenāti ettha rūpaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhena. Vedanā aniccā. Saññā aniccā. Saṅkhārā aniccā. Viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhenātiādinā nayena sammasitabbadhammapariggahena saheva sammasanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Itarathā sammasanaṃ na ruhati. Tadatthassa pana pākaṭattā idha aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhenātiādinā sammasanapadameva therena gahitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tattha rūpaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhenāti taṃtaṃrūpaṃ ñāṇena daḷhaṃ gahetvā ayaṃ pathavidhātu aniccā khayaṭṭhena. Ayaṃ āpodhātu aniccā khayaṭṭhenātiādinā sammasanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Tattha imasmiṃ kāye sabbaṃ thaddhakriyāmattaṃ pathavīnāma. Sāca kriyā sītuṇhaparivattiyāvā parivattati. Nānāhāraparivattiyā vā nānācittaparivattiyāvā nāniriyāpathaparivattiyāvā nānā kāyikakriyā parivattiyāvā parivattati. Nānāsantati saṅkanti hotīti attho. Tattha navanavāsu kriyāsantatīsu pātubhontīsu [M 0.0439] pubbapubbakriyāsantatiyo nassanti. Yasmāca santati nāma dhammato visuṃ natthi, tasmā navanavasantatīnaṃ pātubhāvonāma navanavakriyānaṃ uppattieva. Pubbapubbasantatīnaṃ nassanaṃnāma pubbapubba kriyānaṃ bhijjanamevāti. Evaṃ attano kāye nānāthaddhakriyānaṃ parivattiṃ passanto pathavidhātuyā khayavayaṃ passati. Tañca passanto taṃsahajātānaṃ rūpānaṃ khayavayaṃ passatiyeva. Āpo nāma ābandhanakriyāmattaṃ. Tejonāma sītakriyāmattaṃ uṇha kriyāmattañca. Vāyonāma vitthambhanakriyāmattaṃ. Imāca kriyā khaṇe khaṇe parivattantiyeva. Imāsañca, visuṃ visuṃ santatiparivattiṃ passanto āpādīnaṃ taṃsahajātarūpānañca khayavayaṃ passati. Santatiparivattiṃ pana bahiddhā cakkhunā disvā jānāti, sarīrabbhantare pana kāyasaṃphassena jānāti. Santatisarīrabhūtānaṃ pana dhātūnaṃ khayavayaṃ ñāṇenaeva passati. Tasmā attano sarīrabbhantare taṃtaṃsantati parivattiṃ ñatvāvā tathā tathā kappetvā vā rūpadhātūnaṃ aniccattaṃ ñāṇena sudiṭṭhaṃ katvā punappunaṃ sammasitabbaṃ. Sesakhandhesupi taṃtaṃsantatinānāttaṃ ñatvā vedanādīnaṃ khayavayaṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ katvā sammasanaṃ kātabbanti. Bhayaṭṭhenāti bhāyitabbaṭṭhena. Yañhi aniccaṃ hoti. Khaṇamattepi vipariṇāmadhammaṃ. Taṃ ekantena bhāyitabbameva. Kasmā, tañhi yo abhāyitvā vissāsaṃ karoti. Etaṃ meti attano aṅgaṃ katvā pariharati. Taṃ apariyantehi anekasahassehi abhisaṅkharaṇadukkhehivā vipariṇāmadukkhehivā abhiṇhaṃ pīḷeti. Bādhati. Iti nānādukkhadhammehi abhiṇhaṃ sampaṭipīḷanasabhāvattā ekantena bhāyitabbaṭṭhena dukkhaṃnāmāti. Attapaṭipakkhattā anattā. Yo hi ito uddhaṃ mayhaṃ abbhantarimataronāma natthīti evaṃ paramajjhattabhāvena pariggahito hoti. So attāti vuccati. Katamo pana tathāpariggahi tabboti. Yo attano vase sabbaso vattati. Yathā vuttehi abhisaṅkharaṇakiccehi vinā kevalaṃ attano chandenavā vasenavā ajjhāsayenavā āṇāvidhānenavā niccaṃ avirajjhamāno pavattati. So tathā pariggahetabboti. Tathārūpo eva hi dhammo [M 0.0440] niccaṃ sukhakāmānaṃ dukkhapaṭikūlānaṃ sattānaṃ attakiccaṃ karoti nāmāti. Yo pana niccaṃ sukhakāmānaṃ tesaṃ yathāpavattaṃ sukhaṃ viddhaṃseti vikireti. Dukkhapaṭikūlānaṃ tesaṃ abhisaṅkharaṇādi mūlakaṃ nānādukkhaṃ janeti vaḍḍheti. So attapaṭipakkhoeva hoti. Idañca rūpaṃ edisameva hoti. Iti attakiccassa akaraṇato attapaṭipakkhakiccassa karaṇatoca rūpaṃ anattānāmāti. Kasmā panetaṃ attano vase navattati attakiccaṃ na karoti attapaṭipakkhakiccaṃ karotīti āha asārakaṭṭhenāti. Tattha sāronāma paccayasāmaggiyā vinā kevalaṃ ajjhāsayamattena uppajjituṃvā uppajjitvāca paccayupatthambhena vinā yadicchakaṃ patiṭṭhātuṃ vā samatthabhāvasaṅkhāto thāmabalaviseso vuccati. Rūpaṃ pana sayaṃpi evarūpo sāronāma na hoti. Naca evarūpena sārena yuttanti. Nahi tassa paccayasāmaggiyā vinā uppajjituṃvā uppajjitvāpi paccayupatthambhena vinā khaṇamattaṃpi patiṭṭhātuṃvā thāmovā balaṃvā atthi. Yañca attano thāmena balena vinā kevalaṃ paccayasāmaggi baleneva uppajjati. Paccayupatthambheneva patiṭṭhāti. Taṃ aneka sahassāni paccayābhisaṅkharaṇadukkhāni janetvā ekantena niccaṃ attapaṭipakkhakiccaṃ karoti, pīḷeti, bādhatiyevāti. Esanayo vedanā aniccā khayaṭṭhenātiādīsu. Iti lakkhaṇattayaṃ samma santassāti sambandho. Addhānavasenāti ekekabhavaparicchinnassa pavattakālassa vasena. Nahi bhavantare uppannaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ aññaṃ bhavantaraṃ gacchati. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhaveeva asesaṃ nirujjhatīti. Apica, ekasmiṃ bhavepi tiṇṇaṃ vayānaṃ mandādīnaṃ dasannaṃ dasakānaṃ saṃvaccharautu māsa pakkhatithi ahoratti yāma pahārādīnañca vasena addhānabhedo yojetabbo. Santativasenāti sabhāgekasantānavasena pavattamānāya rūpasantatiyāvā arūpa santatiyāvā vasena. Khaṇavasenāti rūpārūpadhammānaṃ āyu parimāṇasaṅkhātassa khaṇassa vasena. Etthaca khaṇavasena sammasanaṃnāma sabbaññubuddhānaṃ eva visayo siyā, na sāvakānaṃ. Nahi te evaṃ parittake khaṇe uppādaṃvā nirodhaṃvā sampāpuṇituṃ sakkontīti. [M 0.0441] Tasmā addhāsantativasena sammasanameva idhā dhippetanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Lakkhaṇattayaṃsammasantassāti tesu tebhūmaka saṅkhāresu dhammesu tilakkhaṇāni āropetvā te dhamme punappunaṃ āmasantassa parimajjantassa. Tesaṃ dhammānaṃ anicca jātikataṃvā dukkhajātikataṃvā anattajātikataṃvā ñāṇe suṭṭhu pākaṭaṃ karontassāti attho. Visesato pana imasmiṃ ñāṇe aniccalakkhaṇadassanameva padhānaṃ. Tasmiṃ diṭṭheyeva itarāni kamena diṭṭhāni honti. Adiṭṭheca adiṭṭhānīti. Tasmā ādito aniccalakkhaṇasseva suṭṭhu pākaṭabhāvo adhippetoti. Tesvevāti tebhūmakasaṅkhāresu eva. Paccayavasenāti rūpakkhandhe tāva avijjātaṇhupādānakammāhārasaṅkhātānaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena. Vedanāsaññāsaṅkhāresu pana āhāraṭṭhāne phasso vattabbo. Viññāṇeca nāmarūpaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ nayo. Atītānantarabhave avijjātaṇhupādāna kammesu appahīnavasena samuditesu imasmiṃ bhave paṭisandhito paṭṭhāya rūpasantatiyo vedanāsaññāsaṅkhāra viññāṇasantatiyoca samudenti. Yāva maraṇakālā khaṇe khaṇe nānākalāpavasena udenti pasavanti. Tesu pana tasmiṃ bhave eva pahīnavasena niruddhesu tā rūpārūpasantatiyo nirujjhanti. Bhavantare puna anuppādasaṅkhātaṃ nirodhaṃ pāpuṇanti. Ettha pana yathā udake sati macchānāma honti, asati na honti. Evaṃ kammajesu nāmarūpesu sati itarāni nāmarūpāni honti. Asati na hontīti itarāni sabbāni kammajesu saṅgahetvā kammavasena udayabbayavidhānaṃ gahitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ avijjātaṇhupādānakammapaccayānaṃ vasena pañcakkhandhassa udayabbayapavatti hotīti. Kammavasena pana imasmiṃ bhave samudentānipi paṭisandhito paṭṭhāya khaṇe khaṇe kabaḷīkārāhārūpatthambhanaṃ laddhā eva yathā pavattarūpasantatiyo anubandha mānā navanavā rūpasantatiyo samudenti. Aladdhā pana nirujjhanti. Taṃ santatiyaṃ puna anuppādasaṅkhātaṃ ekabhavanirodhaṃ pāpuṇanti, yathā pavattasantatiyo vā chijjanti bhijjanti antaradhāyantīti.

171. Having surpassed the signs of permanence, stability, pleasure, and self in individuals, beings, females, males, and so forth, as they are perceived by the great multitude of worldly beings, one sees with special insight by means of this; thus it is called vipassanā. Action is kamma. Application is development. The action of insight is insight-action. Or insight itself is the action, thus insight-action. The place, basis, or ground of insight-action is called the ground of insight-action. This refers to the class of phenomena beginning with the aggregates. Or insight-action itself is the proximate cause for the successive distinction of development or for the special benefit; thus it is the ground of insight-action. In this ground of insight-action, the seven purifications are included, and the connection is made with the three characteristics, and so forth. Purity of virtue (sīlavisuddhi) is simply constant virtue itself, being purified from the stain of misconduct, and thereby purifying body and speech from it. Purity of mind (cittavisuddhi) is the well-developed continuity of mind itself, being purified from the stain of hindrances, and thereby purifying the individual endowed with it from them. Here, concentration (samādhi) is intended by the term 'mind'. Purity of view (diṭṭhivisuddhi) is view itself, which is called the knowledge discerning phenomena, purifying the individual endowed with it from the stain of identity-view. They overcome, they transcend the sixteenfold or eightfold doubt by this; thus it is called the overcoming of doubt (kaṅkhāvitaraṇā). It is the knowledge of discerning conditions. That very knowledge, by purifying the individual endowed with it from rootless views and distorted-cause views, along with the two kinds of doubt as stated, is purity by overcoming doubt (kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi). The path and the non-path are the path and non-path. Here, the method of attention that is a means for attaining the purity of knowledge and vision, or the Noble Path, is called the path. The method of attention that is not a means for it, or the objects of conceit, are called the non-path. Knowing and seeing the path as the path and the non-path as the non-path is the knowledge and vision of path and non-path. That very knowledge, by purifying the individual endowed with it from the perception of the non-path as the path, is called the purity of knowledge and vision of path and non-path. They proceed to higher distinctions by this; thus it is the path (paṭipadā). The preliminary path, which is called the succession of insight. The knowledge and vision that constitutes the path is path-knowledge and vision (paṭipadāñāṇadassana). That very knowledge, being purified from the perception of permanence, etc., is called purity of path-knowledge and vision (paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi). And the knowledge and vision called Noble Path-knowledge itself, being purified from the stain of delusion, is called purity of knowledge and vision (ñāṇadassanavisuddhi). And here, it should be understood that although inferential knowledge, established through learning, etc., is also knowledge, rejecting that, the term 'vision' (dassana) is used everywhere to mean grasping only direct experiential knowledge of the reality. Phenomena are discerned, thoroughly discerned, and definitively determined as 'these are impermanent' by this; thus it is the characteristic. Impermanence itself is the characteristic; thus it is the characteristic of impermanence (aniccalakkhaṇa). In the preceding word, the suffix denoting state is elided. For impermanent is one thing, impermanence another. Here, just as a person is said to have gone by means of the action of going, but the action of going is not the person, nor is the person the action of going; for the action is one thing, the person another. Similarly, all conditioned phenomena are called impermanent by means of impermanence, but impermanence is not that phenomenon, nor is that phenomenon impermanence; for impermanence is one thing, that phenomenon another. What, then, is that impermanence? It is the mode of alteration. It is said to be the mode of decay, the mode of disintegration. But seeing that mode, knowledge proceeds regarding phenomena possessing that mode: 'This phenomenon is impermanent.' Therefore, that impermanence itself is also called the characteristic here. This method applies to the remaining two as well. Here, the mode of constant oppression is called suffering. The mode of uncontrollability is called non-self. But the repeated contemplation of the impermanent phenomenon along with the aforementioned impermanence, or of impermanence along with the impermanent phenomenon, is the contemplation of impermanence (aniccānupassanā). The same method applies to the other two. As long as the phenomena in the body are discerned by one's own knowledge as possessing the three characteristics, so long is the repeated touching, re-touching, and thorough touching of them by way of distinguishing the three characteristics. The knowledge that proceeds by way of thorough touching is thorough-touching knowledge (sammasanañāṇa). Arising (udaya) is said to be the appearance of new phenomena in accordance with their respective moments and conditions, and their continuous growth. Passing away (vaya) is said to be the disappearance of old phenomena where new phenomena appear and grow, having obtained their conditions, and where conditions are not obtained. But the knowledge that contemplates the arising aspect or the passing away aspect in terms of a group or a continuity is the knowledge of arising and passing away (udayabbayañāṇa). Among these two aspects, the arising portion becomes increasingly evident, while the passing away portion remains obscure. And that (passing away) is the ultimate limit of impermanence; thus, the knowledge that contemplates it more clearly is the knowledge of dissolution (bhaṅgañāṇa). When dissolution is seen, the knowledge that contemplates phenomena, which are of such a disintegrating nature, in various ways as objects of thousands of sorrows and sufferings, and as fearful, is called the knowledge of fear (bhayañāṇa). But in the world, even seeing something fearful, people do not fear if there is another refuge nearby. They fear only if there is none. Thus, seeing the complete absence of any other refuge for those fearful things is called the knowledge of drawbacks (ādīnavañāṇa). Due to the absence of refuge from anything, the insight knowledge accompanied by the mode of weariness with them is called the knowledge of disenchantment (nibbidāñāṇa). The insight knowledge accompanied by the intention to free oneself from those things with which one is disenchanted is called the knowledge of desire for deliverance (muccitukamyatāñāṇa). For one who desires to be well liberated, for the sake of swift liberation, the insight knowledge that proceeds very extensively by way of reflecting on the state of those phenomena as a heap of manifold drawbacks in forty ways, is called the knowledge of reflection (paṭisaṅkhāñāṇa). But when the state of those phenomena as a heap of manifold drawbacks is well seen, and delight in formations is exhausted, and the means for liberation is now obtained, the insight knowledge that, without excessive effort, with balanced exertion, grasps formations, accompanied by a mode of neutrality in the grasping of formations, or accompanied by an indifferent state, having abandoned fear and delight in formations, is called the knowledge of equanimity toward formations (saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇa). The insight knowledge endowed with strength and power that is in conformity with the arising of the path, by virtue of its ability to lead to the higher path, is called knowledge of conformity (anulomañāṇa). Or it is in conformity with the lower knowledges because of its clearer discernment of the three characteristics. Or it is in conformity with the higher path because it is its preliminary work, and because it is its proximate cause; thus it is called knowledge of conformity. The path that is liberated from the bonds of defilements in the aggregates by the power of seeing the emptiness of self or life is called emptiness liberation (suññatāvimokkho). The path that is liberated by demolishing the signs of formations, which are the support for defilements, and by the power of seeing the complete helplessness of phenomena, is called signless liberation (animittovimokkho). The path that is liberated by the power of seeing the complete absence of comfort in formations is called desireless liberation (appaṇihitovimokkho). Contemplation of emptiness (suññatānupassanā) is contemplation of non-self (anattānupassanā). For it proceeds by way of dissecting the compactness of phenomena—such as mass-compactness, continuity-compactness, function-compactness, and object-compactness—and by contemplating the absence of any essence to be grasped as 'self'; thus it is called contemplation of emptiness. Contemplation of the signless (animittānupassanā) is contemplation of impermanence (aniccānupassanā). For it proceeds by way of cutting off continuity, and by demolishing the sign grasped as 'I'; thus it is called contemplation of the signless. Contemplation of the desireless (appaṇihitānupassanā) is contemplation of suffering (dukkhānupassanā). For it proceeds by way of distinguishing the state of being a great heap of drawbacks, and by contemplating the absence of any desirable quality to be grasped as 'this is mine'; thus it is called contemplation of the desireless. The virtue of restraint by the Pātimokkha is the virtue prescribed by the Vinaya. For it is the chief of all worldly virtues, and it is the face, being the original source of wholesome states in the four realms. Thus, it is called Pātimokkha in the sense of being 'towards the chief' or 'the face'. And that very virtue, by restraining and covering the path of misconduct, is called restraint. When the faculties, such as the eye, are agitated and restless due to the arising of certain phenomena, and unwholesome states arise following them, the mindfulness that proceeds by way of restraining the path of their arising is called sense-restraint. That itself is virtue; thus it is the virtue of sense-restraint (indriyasaṃvarasīla). They live, they sustain life by this; thus it is livelihood (ājīvo). It is the exertion in seeking requisites. That itself, being purified from wrong practices condemned by the Buddha, such as giving flowers, etc., and from the three kinds of deceitful actions, is called purity of livelihood (ājīvapārisuddhi). That itself is virtue; thus it is a summary. The virtue connected with the use of requisites (paccayasannissitasīla) is the knowledge of reflection that proceeds by way of grasping and reviewing the purpose, the characteristic of repulsiveness, or the characteristic of mere elements, in the use of requisites obtained by such a purified practice as alms-round, for the purpose of abandoning delusion, greed, intoxication, and negligence at the time of receiving and consuming them. It is purified; thus it is purity. Purity itself is purity. That itself is virtue; thus it is a summary. Thus, the four purities of virtue are the fourfold purity of virtue (catupārisuddhisīla). It is said that here, by the word 'mind' in 'purity of mind' (cittavisuddhi), concentration (samādhi) is indicated; thus, both kinds of concentration are called purity of mind. Here, by 'characteristic, function, manifestation, and proximate cause,' the intrinsic nature of phenomena is called the characteristic, like the heat of fire. The function (rasa) is the task to be accomplished by that nature, or the attainment called the quality obtained by the accomplishing condition, like the cooking and illuminating of fire. That very attainment, or the result called the effect, is called the manifestation (paccupaṭṭhāna), like the smoke of fire. The proximate cause (padaṭṭhāna) is the proximate cause, which is called the uncommon condition for its own arising. By means of these, the grasping of name and form, by defining them with knowledge, is the discernment of name and form (nāmarūpavavatthāna), which is purity of view (diṭṭhivisuddhi). And here, grasping is twofold: brief grasping and detailed grasping. Here, having divided internal phenomena into two, 'this is only name, not form; this is only form, not name; name is one thing, form another,' and having clearly seen directly that there is no other self, life, being, person, human, god, or Brahma apart from these two, such grasping is called brief grasping. For a person of superior knowledge can suppress identity-view even with this much, along with the distortions of perception and thought. For there are three distortions. As it is said: 'The distortion of perception, the distortion of thought, the distortion of view, regarding non-self as self'. Here, by one well-established in the Teacher's dispensation, the distortion of view is suppressed even by faith alone. But the others are suppressed only when the grasping of name and form has been done. And as long as these two are not suppressed, so long is the grasping of name and form impure, and the defilements rooted in it remain unsuppressed. Name and form should be grasped by way of the four nutriments in four ways, by way of the five aggregates in five ways, by way of the six elements in six ways, and so forth. Here, the six elements are the earth element, water element, fire element, air element, space element, and consciousness element. For the clansman Pakkusāti, having grasped these six elements, attained the fruit of non-returning, and having passed away, was reborn in the Pure Abodes. Or, one should grasp as many phenomena as one is able to suppress the distortions of perception, thought, and view that arise as 'self' and 'mine'. But in this compendium, the grasping of name and form by way of all the divisions of consciousness and mental factors, and the division of form, as stated below, is called detailed grasping. But this is not the domain of beginners. It should be understood that it is the domain only of Abhidhamma elders who have penetrated the Four Noble Truths. But for one who grasps name and form, by seeing the absence of anything else beyond mere name and form, the view that 'there is a self called a living being inside the body; it acts, it experiences, it wanders on, it transmigrates' is abandoned. And by seeing the complete absence of efforts and activities called 'person' or 'being' in pure name or pure form, and by seeing that they are obtained only in the combination of both, or by seeing that they are obtained by referring to either one, the view that 'this is self' is abandoned. And in such conventional terms as 'self,' 'life,' 'being,' 'person,' 'human,' 'god,' 'Brahma,' by not dwelling on mere convention, and by seeing the over-attachment by way of the strong adherence to the meaning that 'self definitely exists,' 'life definitely exists,' etc., that (over-attachment) is abandoned. And 'strong adherence to that meaning' means a stronger adherence by thinking 'self definitely exists,' 'life definitely exists,' etc. 'Over-attachment' means grasping name and form as 'self,' etc. Grasping of conditions (paccayapariggaha) is also twofold here: brief and detailed. Here, one who grasps the conditions for name by way of base and object, for form by way of mind, temperature, and nutriment, and for both by way of ignorance, craving, clinging, and kamma, grasps briefly. One who grasps by the methods of dependent origination and the Paṭṭhāna, as divided in the compendium of conditions below, grasps in detail. Here too, grasping by the Paṭṭhāna method is not the domain of beginners. But for one who grasps conditions, by seeing that all name and form, as they are established, are entirely dependent on conditions, the rootless view is abandoned. And by seeing that there is no other arising without its own appropriate combination of conditions, the distorted-cause view, such as divine creation, time creation, etc., is abandoned. And by seeing the absence of any other doer of kamma or experiencer of results, apart from the arising of kamma and the arising of results by way of causal conditions, the view of a doer and experiencer is abandoned. And by seeing the arising of mere name and form as a succession of cause and effect in the three periods of time in beginningless saṃsāra, the sixteenfold doubt concerning individuals and beings, such as 'Did I exist in the past?', is transcended. And by seeing the well-seen arising of phenomena according to their own nature, and by seeing the well-taught nature of the Dhamma, and by seeing the Buddha's perfect enlightenment, the eightfold doubt that arises in ways such as 'Does he doubt the Teacher? Does he doubt the Dhamma?' is abandoned. It is said 'in the three-worldly formations' because even supramundane phenomena, though conditioned, are not subject to thorough contemplation. And it is said 'in the three-worldly formations' because thorough contemplation is for the uprooting of latent tendencies, and those phenomena where latent tendencies such as sensual lust reside are the only ones worthy of thorough contemplation. And the connection of this word is with 'for one who contemplates the three characteristics'. 'Divided into past, etc.' means divided into eleven kinds: past, future, present, internal, external, and so forth. By 'referring to the method of aggregates, etc.' is meant, having taken up and followed the method of dividing the grounds of contemplation, such as the five aggregates, the six doors, the six objects, the six consciousnesses, the six contacts, the six feelings, and the six perceptions, as divided in the Paṭisambhidāmagga, that is, according to that method. Here, among the twenty-three categories of phenomena, whichever category is evident, one should take that and begin contemplation. But one who is able should indeed take all and begin. By 'summarizing by way of a group' means, by means of the five aggregates, having summarized all form, even if differentiated by past, future, present, etc., into a single mass of form; and the same method applies to feelings, and so forth. Here is the method: 'Whatever form there is, past, future, present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all form is impermanent in the sense of destruction, suffering in the sense of fear, and non-self in the sense of being without essence. Whatever feeling there is... whatever perception there is... whatever formations there are... whatever consciousness there is... all consciousness is impermanent in the sense of destruction, suffering in the sense of fear, and non-self in the sense of being without essence.' And here, it should be understood that the grasping of 'all form... all consciousness' is indeed summarizing by way of a group. Here, by 'impermanent in the sense of destruction,' contemplation should be done simultaneously with the grasping of phenomena to be contemplated, by saying 'Form is impermanent in the sense of destruction, feeling is impermanent, perception is impermanent, formations are impermanent, consciousness is impermanent in the sense of destruction,' and so forth. Otherwise, the contemplation does not succeed. But because its meaning is evident, it should be understood that here the Elder has taken only the term for contemplation, 'impermanent in the sense of destruction,' and so forth. Here, by 'form is impermanent in the sense of destruction,' having firmly grasped each respective form with knowledge, contemplation should be done by saying 'This earth element is impermanent in the sense of destruction, this water element is impermanent in the sense of destruction,' and so forth. Here, in this body, all that is merely the activity of hardness is called earth. And that activity changes by way of changes in cold and heat, or by way of changes in various foods, or by way of changes in various thoughts, or by way of changes in various postures, or by way of changes in various bodily activities. The meaning is that there is a transition of various continuities. Here, when new continuities of activity appear, the previous continuities of activity perish. And since continuity is not separate from phenomena, the appearance of new continuities is simply the arising of new activities. The perishing of previous continuities is simply the disintegration of previous activities. Thus, seeing the change of various hard activities in one's own body, one sees the decay and dissolution of the earth element. And seeing that, one also sees the decay and dissolution of the forms born together with it. Water is merely the activity of cohesion. Fire is merely the activity of cold and the activity of heat. Air is merely the activity of supporting. And these activities change moment by moment. And seeing the distinct changes of continuity of these, one sees the decay and dissolution of water, etc., and the forms born together with them. But one knows the change of continuity externally by seeing with the eye, and internally by bodily contact. But one sees the decay and dissolution of the elements that are the nature of continuity only with knowledge. Therefore, having known the change of each continuity within one's own body, or having conceived it in various ways, one should make the impermanence of the form elements well seen by knowledge and contemplate it again and again. In the remaining aggregates too, having known the distinctness of each continuity, one should make the decay and dissolution of feelings, etc., well seen and contemplate. By 'in the sense of fear' means in the sense of being fearful. For whatever is impermanent, having the nature of change even for a moment, that should certainly be feared. Why? For whoever, not fearing it, trusts in it, cherishes it by making it his own limb, that (phenomenon) constantly oppresses and afflicts him with endless thousands of sufferings from conditioning or sufferings from change. Thus, because of its nature of being constantly oppressed by various suffering phenomena, it is certainly suffering in the sense of being fearful. It is non-self because it is the opposite of self. For that which is grasped as supremely internal, thinking 'there is nothing more internal to me than this,' that is called self. What, then, should be grasped in that way? That which always proceeds entirely according to its own will, without the aforementioned activities of conditioning, merely by its own desire, or will, or intention, or command, constantly without failing. That should be grasped in that way. For such a phenomenon indeed performs the function of self for beings who constantly desire happiness and are averse to suffering. But that which destroys and scatters the happiness of those who constantly desire happiness, as it arises, and generates and increases various sufferings rooted in conditioning, etc., for those who are averse to suffering—that is indeed the opposite of self. And this form is just like that. Thus, because of not performing the function of self and performing the function of the opposite of self, form is called non-self. Why, then, does it not proceed according to its own will, not perform the function of self, and perform the function of the opposite of self? He says: 'in the sense of being without essence'. Here, 'essence' is called a special strength and power, which is the ability to arise merely by one's own intention without a combination of conditions, or having arisen, to persist as one wishes without the support of conditions. But form itself does not have such an essence. And it is not endowed with such an essence. For it has no strength or power to arise without a combination of conditions, or having arisen, to persist even for a moment without the support of conditions. And that which arises only by the power of the combination of conditions, without its own strength or power, and persists only by the support of conditions—that, having generated thousands of sufferings from conditioning, certainly always performs the function of the opposite of self, oppresses, and afflicts. This method applies to 'feeling is impermanent in the sense of destruction,' and so forth. Thus, the connection is with 'for one who thoroughly contemplates the three characteristics'. By 'in terms of the course of time' means in terms of the duration of existence, which is delimited by each single existence. For the five aggregates that arise in one existence do not go to another existence. They cease completely in that very existence. Moreover, even within a single existence, the division of time should be applied by way of the three kinds of decay (slow, etc.), the ten decades, the year, season, month, fortnight, lunar day, day and night, watch, and hour. By 'in terms of continuity' means by way of the continuity of form or the continuity of non-form that proceeds as a homogeneous continuity. By 'in terms of moment' means by way of the moment, which is called the lifespan of form and non-form phenomena. And here, contemplation in terms of moment would be the domain only of the All-knowing Buddhas, not of the disciples. For they are not able to attain arising or cessation in such a short moment. Therefore, it should be understood that here, contemplation in terms of time and continuity is what is intended. By 'for one who thoroughly contemplates the three characteristics' means for one who, having applied the three characteristics to those phenomena, the three-worldly formations, repeatedly touches and polishes those phenomena. The meaning is for one who makes the impermanent nature, or the suffering nature, or the non-self nature of those phenomena very evident in knowledge. But especially in this knowledge, the seeing of the characteristic of impermanence is primary. When that is seen, the others are seen in sequence. And when that is not seen, the others are not seen. Therefore, it is intended that the clear manifestation of the characteristic of impermanence is primary from the beginning. 'In those' means in the three-worldly formations themselves. By 'in terms of conditions' means, in the aggregate of form, by way of the conditions called ignorance, craving, clinging, kamma, and nutriment. But in feelings, perceptions, and formations, contact should be stated in place of nutriment. And for consciousness, name and form. Here is the method: When ignorance, craving, clinging, and kamma are accumulated in the immediately preceding past existence without being abandoned, the continuities of form, and the continuities of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness arise in this existence, starting from conception. They arise and produce moment by moment in various groups until the time of death. But when those (ignorance, etc.) have ceased in that very existence by way of being abandoned, those continuities of form and non-form cease. They attain cessation, which is called non-arising in another existence. Here, just as when there is water, there are fish, and when there is no water, there are no fish, so when there are kamma-produced name and form, there are the other name and form, and when there are not, there are not; thus, it should be understood that all the others are included in kamma-produced (name and form), and the process of arising and ceasing is taken by way of kamma. Thus, the process of arising and ceasing of the five aggregates occurs by way of the conditions of ignorance, craving, clinging, and kamma. But even those that arise in this existence by way of kamma, having obtained the support of physical nutriment moment by moment from conception onwards, and following along with the continuities of form that are proceeding as they are, new continuities of form arise. But when support has not been obtained, they cease. Again, in that continuity, they attain the cessation of that single existence, which is called non-arising, or the continuities that are proceeding as they are are cut off, broken, and disappear.

Vedanāsaññāsaṅkhārā [M 0.0442] pana bahiddhā ārammaṇesu āpātāgatesu ārammaṇasamphassaṃ laddhāeva chadvārikā kusalākusalavipāka kriyabhūtā samudenti. Navanavā santatiyo pātubhavanti. Aladdhā pana nirujjhanti. Santatiṃ na ghaṭenti. Viññāṇaṃca sahajāta nāmeca vatthurūpeca pavattamāneeva pavattati. Nivattamāne nivattatīti. Khaṇavasenāti vuttappakāre paccaye anapekkhitvā kevalaṃ nāmarūpānaṃ pavattikkhaṇavasena. Khaṇasaddena cettha sammasanañāṇe vuttarūpasantati nāmasantatiyopi gahetabbā. Nahi sāvakānaṃ ñāṇaṃ khaṇavasena nāmarūpānaṃ udayaṃvā vayaṃ vā sampāpuṇituṃ sakkotīti. Yathā pana rattandhakāre anto leṇe mahanto tamokhandho jāyati. Dīpaṃ jālentassa pana dīpobhāso ekakkhaṇe eva sakalaṃ antoleṇaṃ pharamāno udeti. Tamokhandho veti. Ālokassa udayo hoti. Tamokhandhassa vayo. Puna dīpe nibbāpīyamāne tamokhandhassa udayo hoti. Ālokassa vayo. Eva mevaṃ sarīre nānāutuvasenavā nānāhāravasenavā nānācitta vasenavā nāniriyāpathavasenavā nānāpayogavasenavā udayapakkhānaṃ vayapakkhānañca nānāsantatīnaṃ udayañca udayato vayañca vayato sudiṭṭhaṃ katvā samanupassantassāti attho. Evaṃ samanupassantassa pana āraddhavipassakabhāvaṃ pattassa udayabbaya ñāṇe tikkhe sūre vahante dasavidhā vipassanupakkilesasaṅkhātā pāripanthakadhammā uppajjanti. Te dassetuṃ obhāsotiādigātha māha. Tattha obhāsoti vipassanā cittasamuṭṭhito sarīrobhāso. Pītīti vipassanācittasampayuttā pañcavidhā pīti. Passaddhīti duvidhāpassaddhi. Adhimokkhoti saddhādhimokkho. Paggahoti vīriyaṃ.
