Sukhanti somanassaṃ. Ñāṇanti vipassanā ñāṇaṃ. Upaṭṭhānanti sati. Upekkhāti tatramajjhattupekkhā ceva āvajjanupekkhā ca. Nikantīti obhāsādīhi saha vipassanāya ālayaṃ kurumānā sukhumā taṇhā. Ayameva pana ekantato vipassanupakkileso hoti. Obhāsādayo pana tassā vatthubhūtattā [M 0.0443] upakkilesāti vuttā. Tesu hi uppajjamānesu na vata me ito pubbe evarūpo obhāso uppannapubbo. Evarūpā pīti.La. Upekkhā uppannapubbā addhā maggaṃ pattosmi. Phalaṃ pattosmīti evaṃ assādasahitā amagge maggasaññā aphale phalasaññā uppajjati. Tadā koci abyatto yogāvacaro kammaṭṭhānaṃ vissajjetvā adhimānavasena vikkhipanto vicaratīti. Byatto pana tāvadeva sabhiṃ paṭilabhitvā idāni mama etesu obhāsādīsu etaṃ mama eso ha masmi eso me attāti cittassa nikāmanākāro paññāyati. Naca lokuttaradhammonāma īdisassa nikāmanassa vatthu. Addhā mama saṃkilesadhammo uppanno. So vaḍḍhamāno maṃ niyyānamukhato pātetvā vaṭṭamukhe yojessati. Handa tesveva lakkhaṇattayaṃ āropetvā nikantiṃ sodhetvā yathāpavattaṃ vipassanāvīthiṃ paṭipādessāmīti te obhāsādayo eva tāva pariggaṇhāti. Ayaṃ me obhāso anicco khayaṭṭhena dukkho bhayaṭṭhena anattā asārakaṭṭhenātiādinā sammasatīti attho. Evaṃ te obhāsādike vipassanāya upakkilesabhūte paripantha dhamme pariggaṇhitvā tappariggahavasena tesu nikantiṃ pariyādi yitvā ṭhitassa uppannaṃ maggāmaggalakkhaṇavavatthānañāṇaṃ maggāmaggañāṇa dassanavisuddhināma. Amaggesu obhāsādīsu maggasaññāmalato yathā vuttanikantimalatoca visuddhattā. Tañhi ñāṇaṃ tesu nikantiyāpi vikkhambhitāya eva obhāsādipaṭibandhato suṭṭhu parisuddhaṃnāma hotīti.

But feelings, perceptions, and formations, when external objects come into range and contact with them is gained through the six doors, arise as wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, or functional states. New continuities appear. But if contact is not gained, they cease and do not form a continuity. And consciousness, together with its co-arisen mental factors and its physical basis, continues to occur as long as it is occurring, and ceases when it ceases. 'By way of the moment' means solely by the moment of the occurrence of name-and-form, without relying on conditions in the manner previously described. Here, by the term 'moment,' the continuities of form and name, as described in the knowledge of comprehension, should also be understood. For the knowledge of disciples is not capable of comprehending the arising or passing away of name-and-form by way of the moment. Just as in the darkness of night, a great mass of darkness arises inside a cave. But when a lamp is lit, the light of the lamp instantly arises, spreading throughout the entire cave. The mass of darkness vanishes. The arising of light occurs; the passing away of the mass of darkness. Then, when the lamp is extinguished, the arising of the mass of darkness occurs; the passing away of the light. In the same way, for one who contemplates, having clearly seen the arising from its arising and the passing away from its passing away of the various continuities of the side of arising and the side of cessation in the body, due to various seasons, various foods, various states of mind, various postures, and various applications—this is the meaning. For one who contemplates thus, having attained the state of an ardent meditator, when the knowledge of arising and passing away becomes sharp, strong, and proceeds well, ten kinds of obstructive states, known as the defilements of insight, arise. To show these, he stated the verse beginning 'illumination.' Therein, 'illumination' is the bodily radiance produced by insight consciousness. 'Rapture' is the five kinds of rapture associated with insight consciousness. 'Tranquility' is the two kinds of tranquility. 'Resolution' is faith-resolution. 'Exertion' is energy. 'Happiness' is mental pleasure. 'Knowledge' is insight knowledge. 'Establishment' is mindfulness. 'Equanimity' is both equanimity of neutrality towards things and equanimity of adverting. 'Delight' is the subtle craving that, along with illumination and the rest, makes a home in insight. This alone is exclusively a defilement of insight. But illumination and the rest are called defilements because they are its basis. For when these arise, with a taste for them, the perception of the path in what is not the path and the perception of the fruit in what is not the fruit arises, thinking, 'Never before has such illumination arisen in me, such rapture... such equanimity arisen before. Surely I have attained the path! I have attained the fruit!' Then, some unskilled meditator, abandoning the meditation subject, wanders about distracted due to conceit. But a skilled one, having immediately gained discernment, understands: 'Now, in regard to these states of illumination and the rest, the mind's inclination to crave, thinking "This is mine, this I am, this is my self," becomes apparent. And a supramundane state is not an object for such craving. Surely a defiling state has arisen in me. If it grows, it will make me fall from the entrance to liberation and yoke me to the entrance of the round of rebirths. Come now, having applied the three characteristics to these very states, having purified the delight, I will re-establish the course of insight as it was proceeding.' Thus, he first comprehends those states of illumination and the rest. The meaning is that he comprehends them thus: 'This illumination of mine is impermanent in the sense of passing away, suffering in the sense of being fearsome, not-self in the sense of being without substance,' and so on. Thus, for one who stands firm, having comprehended those obstructive states of illumination and the rest which have become defilements of insight, and by means of that comprehension having completely overcome the delight in them, the knowledge that arises which defines the characteristics of path and not-path is called the purification by knowledge and vision of what is path and what is not-path. This is because it is purified from the stain of perceiving the path in what is not the path—illumination and the rest—and from the stain of delight as described. For that knowledge, with delight suppressed, is indeed called thoroughly purified from the impediment of illumination and the rest.

[245] Vibhāvaniyaṃ pana

However, the Vibhāvaniya states:

Aniccādivasena obhāsādi paṭibandhapariggahaṃ visuṃ avatvā maggāmaggajānanamatteneva maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhināma vuttā. Sā aṭṭhakathāya na sameti.

That, without separately stating the comprehension of the impediments of illumination and the rest by way of impermanence and so forth, it is called the purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not, merely by the knowledge of what is the path and what is not. This does not agree with the commentary.

Tathā paripanthavimuttassāti tathā pariggahetvā tato vipassanupakkilesaparipanthato vimuttassa yāvānulomāti yāvaanulomañāṇā. [M 0.0444] Tilakkhaṇaṃ āropetvāti sambandho. Vipassanāparipākaṃāgammāti saṅkhārupekkhābhāvaṃ patvā tividha vimokkhamukhabhāvappattiyāceva sattaariyapuggalavibhāgassa paccaya bhāvappattiyāca vipassanāñāṇassa paripākaṃ āgamma paṭicca. Idāni appanā uppajjissatīti vattabbakkhaṇeti sambandho. Appanā tica sotāpattimaggaappanā. Dvetīṇivipassanācittānīti tikkhapaññassa dve vipassanācittāni. Mandapaññassa tīṇi vipassanācittāni. Yaṃkiñcīti tīsu lakkhaṇesu aññataraṃ yaṃkiñci. Yāsikhāpattāsānulomāsaṅkhārupekkhāti matthakapattā anulomañāṇasahitā yā saṅkhārupekkhā atthi. Sā vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanātica vuccatīti yojanā. Saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃ anulomañāṇanti imāni dve ñāṇāni vuṭṭhānagāmini vipassanānāmāti vuccantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Idaṃ pana paripākagatavipassanā dassanavacanaṃ. Etthaca vuṭṭhānanti maggo vuccati. So hi vipassanāñāṇassa ārammaṇabhūta saṅkhāranimittatovā sayaṃ saṃyojanavatthubhāvatovā vuṭṭhāti. Taṃ samaṅgipuggalaṃvā puthujjanabhāvato samudayapahānavasena vaṭṭa pavattatoca vuṭṭhāpeti. Tasmā vuṭṭhānanti vuccati. Avassaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ gacchanti etāyāti vuṭṭhānagāminīti evaṃ dvinnaṃ ñāṇānaṃ vuṭṭhāna gāminibhāvo veditabbo. Tatoparanti dvinnaṃvā tiṇṇaṃvā vipassanā cittānaṃ pavattiyā paraṃ nibbānaṃ ālambitvāti maggassa āvajjanaṭṭhāniyaṃ hutvā tassa purecarabhāvena nibbānameva ārammaṇaṃ katvā. Tato yevaca taṃ vipassanānāmaṃ nalabhatīti. Puthujjana gottamabhibhavantanti etena gottaṃ bhavati abhibhavatīti gotrabhu. Gottanti cettha paripuṇṇakilesa samāyogena anariyabhāvasaṅkhātā puthujjanajāti vuccatīti imamatthaṃ dasseti. Ariyagottamabhisambhontañcāti etena gottaṃ bhavati pāpuṇātīti gotrabhu. Gottantica taṃtaṃ kilesa visuddhabhāva saṅkhātā ariyajāti vuccatīti imamatthaṃ dasseti. Maggo appanā vīthiṃ otaratīti sambandho. Dukkhasaccaṃparijānantoti tebhūmaka dhammānaṃ ekantadukkhabhāvaṃ paricchijja jānanto. Parijānanañcettha tesaṃ dukkhabhāva [M 0.0445] paṭicchādakassa sammohassa pahānameva daṭṭhabbaṃ. Samudaya saccaṃpajahantoti attano cittasantāne anusayabhāvena pavattamānaṃ taṇhāsaṅkhātaṃ samudayasaccaṃ ekadesenavā anavasesenavā apacchāvattikaṃ katvā pajahanto. Nirodhasaccaṃsacchikarontoti cakkhumā viya nabhamajjhe virocamānaṃ candamaṇḍalaṃ attano santāne ekadesassavā sakalassavā kilesa vaṭṭassavā āyatiṃ bhāvino vipākavaṭṭassaṃvā attano santāne puna anuppādadhammabhāpattivasena nirodhasaṅkhātaṃ nibbānaṃ paccakkhaṃ karonto. Maggasaccaṃbhāvanāvasenāti ito pubbe anamatagge saṃsāre anuppannapubbassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggasaccassa uppādanasaṅkhātāya bhāvanāya vasena. Maggacetanāya pana ānantarikaphalattā taṅkhaṇe apanītaggike padese puna udakaṃ āsiñcitvā nibbāpento viya maggānukūlapavattivasena dukkhaparijānanādīni cattāri kiccāni anukubbantāni tatoparaṃ dvevā tīṇivā phalacittāni pavattanti. Tatoparaṃ bhavaṅgapāto hotīti dassetuṃ tatoparantiādimāha. Yathā pana pasādacakkhunāvā dibbacakkhunāvā kiñcirūpaṃ passantassa tāni cakkhūni taṃ rūpaṃ paccakkhaṃ katvā pacchā tassa puggalassapi paccakkhato pātubhūtaṃ katvā nirujjhanti. Na tāva tesaṃ uppattikkhaṇe taṃ rūpaṃ tassa ahaṃ idaṃnāma passāmīti pākaṭaṃ hoti. Pacchā pana paccavekkhana vāresu pavattamānesueva taṃrūpaṃ tadanubandhāca nānākārā tassa pātubhūtā honti. Evamevaṃ idhapi paccavekkhanavāresu pavattamānesueva nibbānañca tadanubandhāni maggaphalādīnica pātubhavantīti vuttaṃ punabhavaṅgaṃ.La. Pavattantīti. Idāni paccavekkhanañāṇassa bhūmiṃ dassetuṃ maggaṃphalañcanibbānantiādigātha māha. Tattha paṇḍitoti ariyāya paññāya samannāgato phalaṭṭho. Hīneti pahīne. Seseti apahīne uparimaggavajjhe. Imāni pana dve pahīnāvasiṭṭhakilesapaccavekkhanāni kesañci jīvitasamasīsipuggalānaṃ kilesa vibhāgesu akovidānañca nalabbhantīti vuttaṃ paccavekkhativānavāti. Etthaca visuddhimagge tāva sabbapathamaṃ maggapaccavekkhanaṃ vuttaṃ. Tato phalapaccavekkhanaṃ. [M 0.0446] Tato pahīnakilesapaccavekkhanaṃ. Tato avasiṭṭhakilesapaccavekkhanaṃ. Avasāne nibbānapaccavekkhanaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṭisambhidāmaggaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana sabbapathamaṃ kilesapaccavekkhanaṃ adhippetaṃ. Vuttañhi tattha paccavekkhanesu pathamaṃ kilesapaccavekkhanaṃ hoti. Tato maggaphalanibbānapaccavekkhanānīti. Taṃ pana pāḷiyaṃ paccavekkhana ñāṇassa niddesato pubbe pathamaṃ chinnamanupassane paññāvimutti ñāṇanti evaṃ visuṃ vimuttiñāṇassa āgatattā vuttaṃ. Tattha chinnanti tena tena maggena samucchinnaṃ kilesajātanti attho. Pāḷi anu sārena vuccamāne pana pathamaṃ pahīnaṃ kilesānaṃ paccavekkhanaṃ. Tato paccekaṃ maggaṅgabojjhaṅgādīnaṃ paccavekkhanaṃ. Tato tesaṃ ārammaṇabhūtassa nibbānassa paccavekkhanaṃ. Tato phaladhammānaṃ paccavekkhanaṃ. Tato tesaṃ ārammaṇabhūtassa nibbānassa paccavekkhananti vattabbaṃ hoti. Pāḷiyañhi paccavekkhanañāṇaniddese nibbānaṃ maggavārepi phalavārepi dvikkhattuṃ āgatanti. Iti nibbānapaccavekkhanaṃ nāma itaresaṃ paccavekkhanānaṃ ādimhivā majjhe antarantarāvā avasānevā yatthakatthaci pavattatīti siddhaṃ hoti. Tathā kilesapaccavekkhanaṃpi maggaphalapaccavekkhanānaṃ ādimhivā pacchāvāti. Evañhi sati maggaṃ phalañca nibbānanti ayaṃ gāthāpi aviruddhā hotīti. Evañca katvā adhimānaniddesaṭṭhakathāsu so hi maggaphalanibbāna pahīna kilesā vasiṭṭhakilesa paccavekkhanena sañjātasomanasso ariyaguṇapaṭivedhe nikkaṅkhoti vuttaṃ. Etthaca sotāpannassa pañca paccavekkhanāni honti. Tathā sakadāgāmissa pañca. Anāgāmissa pañca. Arahato pana avasiṭṭhakilesonāma natthīti cattārīti ekūnavīsati paccavekkhanāni hontīti. Idañca paripuṇṇa vasena labbhamānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Aparipuṇṇaṃpi pana hotiyeva. Tathā hi cūḷadukkhakkhandhasuttaaṭṭhakathāyaṃ sā pana na sabbesaṃ paripuṇṇā hoti. Eko hi pahīnakilesameva paccavekkhati. Eko avasiṭṭhakilesameva. Eko maggameva. Eko phalameva. Ekonibbānameva. Imāsu pana pañcasupaccavekkhanāsu ekaṃvādvevā no laddhuṃ navaṭṭatīti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ chabbisuddhikamena bhāvetabbo catubbidho maggo [M 0.0447] ñāṇadassanavisuddhināma vuccatīti sambandho. Maggasaddena cettha catubbidhaṃ maggañāṇaṃ tadanukūlapavattivasena phalañāṇañca gahitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etthāti vipassanākammaṭṭhāne. Tatthāti tesu anupassanā maggaphalesu. Abhinivisanaṃ abhiniveso. Heṭṭhā silāpathaviyaṃ nikhātasinerupādassa viya ajjhattakhandhesu daḷhaṃ gahetvā pavattīti attho. Attā iti abhiniveso attābhiniveso. Taṃ attābhinivesaṃ. Muñcantīti ajjhattadhammānaṃ kevalaṃ paccayāyatta vuttitāya khaṇabhaṅgassaca adiṭṭhattā so abhiniveso pavattati. Tasmā taṃ dvayaṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ katvā rūpaṃ anattā vedanā anattātiādinā punappunaṃ samanupassanāvasena taṃ abhinivesaṃ vimocayamānāti attho. Vimokkhamukhaṃ hoti, suññatavimokkha saṅkhātassa maggassa phalassaca pavesanadvārabhūtattā, vipallāsa nimittanti viparītavasena āsanaṃ upagamanaṃ pavattanaṃvā vipallāso. Anicce niccanti upagamanaṃ pavattanaṃvāti attho. So eva kile suppattiyā āsannakāraṇattā nimittanti vipallāsanimittaṃ. Muñcantīti ajjhattadhammānaṃ khaṇabhaṅgassa adiṭṭhattā taṃnimittaṃ hotīti tesaṃ khaṇabhaṅgaṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ katvā rūpaṃ aniccaṃ vedanā aniccātiādinā punappunaṃ samanupassanāvasena taṃnimittaṃ vimocayamānāti attho. Taṇhāpaṇidhinti taṇhāeva abhisaṅgavasena ārammaṇe cittassa paṇidahanato daḷhaṃ thapanato paṇidhīti taṇhāpaṇidhi. Taṃtaṇhā paṇidhiṃ. Muñcantīti ajjhattadhammānaṃ mahāādīnavarāsibhāvassa adiṭṭhattā sopaṇidhi hotīti tesaṃ mahāādīnavarāsibhāvaṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ katvā rūpaṃdukkhaṃ vedanādukkhātiādinā punappunaṃ samanupassanāvasena taṃpaṇidhiṃ vimocayamānāti attho. Tasmāti yasmā etā vimokkhamukhabhūtā tisso anupassanā evaṃ visesa nāmikā honti. Tasmā. Yasmā saṅkhāresu suññatadassanavasena atthasiddhināma kevalaṃ attākinivesabhūtassa diṭṭhigāhassa paṭipakkhabhūtassa ñāṇasseva ānubhāvo hoti, tasmā tathā samanupassitvā vimuñcantassa vipassanāpi maggopi sahajātañāṇa kiccena nāmaṃ labhatīti vuttaṃ yadivuṭṭhāna.La. Suññatovimokkho nāmahotimaggoti. [M 0.0448] Aniccadassanavasena atthasiddhināma nimittāti nivesabhūtassa mānagāhassa paṭipakkhabhūtāya saddhāyapi ānubhāvo. Tasmā tathā samanupassitvā vimuccantassa vipassanāpi maggopi sahajātasaddhā kiccena nāmaṃ labhatīti vuttaṃ yadianiccato.La. Animitto vimokkhonāmāti. Dukkhadassanavasena atthasiddhināma paṇidhisaṅkhāta taṇhāgāhapaṭipakkhabhūtassa samādhissapi ānubhāvo. Tasmā tathā samanupassitvā vimuccantassa vipassanāpi maggopi sahajātasamādhikiccena nāmaṃ labhatīti vuttaṃ. Yadi dukkhato. La. Appaṇihito vimokkhonāmāti. Vuttañhetaṃ paṭisambhidāmagge aniccato manasikaroto saddhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti. Dukkhato manasikaroto samādhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti. Anattato manasikaroto paññindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hotīti. Magge pana tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ kiccavisesonāma vipassanāgamanavaseneva siddhoti vuttaṃ maggo. La. Nāmāni labhatīti. Tattha suññatavimokkhena vimutto ariyasāvako sotāpattimaggakkhaṇe dhammānusārīnāma hoti. Majjhe chasu maggaphalakkhaṇesu diṭṭhippatto nāma. Arahattaphalakkhaṇe paññāvimuttonāma. Animittavimokkhena vimutto sotāpattimaggakkhaṇe saddhānusārīnāma. Upari sattasu ṭhānesu saddhāvimuttonāma. Apaṇihitavimokkhena vimutto pana aṭṭhasupi ṭhānesu kāyasakkhināma. Soyeva arūpajjhānaṃ pādakaṃ katvā vimutto arahattaphale ṭhito ubhatobhāgavimutto nāmāti ettāvatā yaṃ heṭṭhā vuttaṃ vipassanāparipākamāgammāti saṅkhārupekkhābhāvaṃ patvā tividhavimokkhamukhabhāvappattiyāceva sattaariyapuggalavibhāgassa paccayabhāvappattiyāca vipassanāñāṇassa paripākaṃ āgamma paṭiccāti. Taṃ sarūpato niddiṭṭhaṃ hotīti. Maggavīthiyaṃ phalañca maggāgamana vasena tathā tīṇi nāmāni labhatīti yojanā. Yathāvuttanayena vipassantānanti yadi anattato vipassatītiādinā vuttappakāranayena vipassantānaṃ catunnaṃ phalaṭṭhānaṃ puggalānaṃ. Yathāsakaṃphalanti sotāpannassa sotāpattiphalaṃ. Sakadāgāmissa sakadāgāmiphalantiādinā nayena [M 0.0449] attano attano santakabhūtaṃ yaṃ yaṃ phalaṃ vipassanāgamana vaseneva suññatādivimokkhotica vuccati. Namaggāgamanavasenāti adhippāyo. Etthaca vipassanāgamana vasena maggassa animitta nāmalābhonāma suttantikapariyāyena vutto. Abhidhamme pana animitto nāmamaggo naāgato. Nahi so nippariyāyato animittonāma hoti. Hīnapaṇītādivasena vibhāgārahassa saṅkhāranimittassa sabbhāvato. Teneva hissa dukkhapaṭipadā dandhā bhiññādivasenavā pāramidhammānaṃ parittamahantādivasenavā hīna paṇīta paṇītatara paṇītatama vibhāgo sandissatīti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana aniccānupassanā saṅkhāresu niccanimittaṃ vidhamanavasena pavattattā animittānupassanānāma samānāpi sayaṃ saṅkhāranimitte pariyāpannattā ekantena attanonāmaṃ maggassa dātuṃ nasakkoti. Tasmā maggo abhidhamma pariyāyena animittanāmaṃ nalabhatīti vuttaṃ. Suttantikapariyāyena pana yathā pathavikasiṇārammaṇaṃ jhānaṃ pathavikasiṇanti vuccati. Evaṃ suññatādināmaṃ nibbānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā pavattāni maggaphalānipi ārammaṇavasenapi suññatādināmaṃ labhanti. Ārammaṇakaraṇavasena pana sampayogavasenavā palibodhakarāca nimittakarāca paṇidhikarāca rāgādayo kilesadhammā tesu natthi. Tasmā tāni aññaṃ āgamanaṃvā ārammaṇaṃvā anapekkhitvā attano sabhāvenapi suññatādināmaṃ labhantīti dassetuṃ ārammaṇavasenātiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sarasavasenāti attano sabhāvena. Nāmattayanti suññatādi nāmattikaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbāsu maggavīthi phalasamāpattivīthīsu. Sabbesaṃpīti sabbesaṃpi maggaphalānaṃ. Samamevāti samānameva. Sadisameva. Etthapanāti etesu pana yathāvuttesu maggaphalesu. Yasmā sabbādiṭṭhiyoca soḷasavidhā vicikicchāca attadiṭṭhimūlikā eva honti. Attadiṭṭhiyā niruddhāya nirujjhanti sabbānica apāyagāmi kammānināma attadiṭṭhiyā satiyāeva vipaccanti. Asatiyā na vipaccanti. Diṭṭhasaccānañca sā diṭṭhi sabbaso pahīnā hoti. Tasmā sotāpattimaggaṃ.La. Pahīnāpāya gamanoti vuttaṃ. Apāyaṃ gacchanti [M 0.0450] etehīti apāyagamanāni. Diṭṭhivicikicchāvippayuttā akusaladhammāceva pubbekataduccaritakammānica. Pahīnāni apāyagamanāni etassāti pahīnāpāyagamano. Paṭividdhacatusaccānaṃ pahīnaattadiṭṭhīnaṃ bodhipakkhiyadhammā ekantena uparūpari vaḍḍhanapakkhe ṭhitā honti. Kilesadhammā pana hāyanapakkhe. Tasmā te anukkamena parihāyitvā gacchantā uparima koṭiyā sattahi bhavehi sabbaso parikkhayaṃ gacchantīti vuttaṃ sattakkhattuparamosotāpannonāma hotīti, tattha sattakkhattusaddena sattapaṭisandhigahaṇavārā vuccanti. Paramoti ukkaṃsaparicchedo. Iti sattakkhattuṃ paramo etassāti. Sattakkhattuparamo. So pana devesu sattakkhattu paramo, manussesu sattakkhattu paramo, ubhayattha sattakkhattu paramoti tividho hoti. Yathāha –

“Thus liberated from obstacles” means having grasped it thus, one is liberated from the obstacle of the corruptions of insight. “Up to conformity” means up to conformity knowledge. “Having imposed the three characteristics” is the connection. “Due to the ripening of insight” means having reached the state of equanimity towards formations, and due to attaining the state of the three gateways to liberation and the state of being a condition for the classification of the seven noble individuals, the knowledge of insight ripens accordingly. “Now absorption will arise” is the moment to be spoken of—this is the connection. And absorption here is the absorption of the path of stream-entry. “Two or three insight consciousnesses” means two insight consciousnesses for one with sharp wisdom, and three insight consciousnesses for one with dull wisdom. “Whatever” refers to any one of the three characteristics. “That equanimity towards formations which has reached the peak and is accompanied by conformity” means that equanimity towards formations which has reached the summit, accompanied by conformity knowledge, is also called “insight leading to emergence.” The knowledge of equanimity towards formations and conformity knowledge—these two knowledges are called “insight leading to emergence.” This is what is meant. This statement indicates insight that has reached maturity. And here, “emergence” refers to the path. For it emerges from the sign of formations, which is the object of insight knowledge, or from its own state as a basis for the fetters. It also causes the person endowed with it to emerge from the state of a worldling and from the continuation of the round of rebirth by means of abandoning the origin. Therefore, it is called “emergence.” By this, one inevitably goes to emergence; thus, it is “leading to emergence.” In this way, the fact that the two knowledges lead to emergence should be understood. “After that” means after the occurrence of two or three insight consciousnesses, having taken Nibbāna as its object, having become the adverting for the path, and by its nature as a precursor, having made Nibbāna itself its object. And from that point on, it does not receive the name “insight.” “Overcoming the lineage of the worldling” means by this, one overcomes the lineage, thus one is a “change-of-lineage” being. And here, “lineage” refers to the state of a worldling, described as the condition of being conjoined with the full range of defilements; this is the meaning it shows. “And attaining the noble lineage” means by this, one attains the lineage, thus one is a “change-of-lineage” being. And here, “lineage” refers to the noble state, described as the condition of being purified from the various defilements; this is the meaning it shows. “The path enters the absorption process” is the connection. “Fully understanding the truth of suffering” means knowing through penetration the exclusively sorrowful nature of the phenomena of the three planes. And “full understanding” here should be seen as simply the abandoning of the delusion that conceals their nature as suffering. “Abandoning the truth of origin” means abandoning, either partially or completely and irreversibly, the truth of origin, known as craving, which proceeds as a latent tendency in one's own mental continuum. “Realizing the truth of cessation” means directly experiencing Nibbāna, known as cessation, like a person with sight seeing the disk of the moon shining in the middle of the sky, by bringing about the state of non-re-arising in one's own continuum for the round of defilements, either in part or in whole, or for the future round of results. “By means of developing the truth of the path” means by means of the development consisting of producing the eightfold path, which had never before arisen in beginningless saṃsāra. Since path-volition has an immediate result, at that moment, two or three fruition-consciousnesses arise immediately after, which, by proceeding in conformity with the path, accomplish the four functions of fully understanding suffering and so on, just like extinguishing a fire by pouring water again on a place where the fire has been removed. To show that after that there is a lapse into the life-continuum, he said, “After that,” and so on. Just as when a person sees some form with the sensitive eye or the divine eye, those eyes, having made that form directly present, and then having made it manifest as directly present to that person, cease. But at the moment of their arising, that form is not yet clear to him as “I see this thing.” Later, however, only when the reviewing processes are occurring, do that form and its various associated aspects become manifest to him. In the same way here, only when the reviewing processes are occurring, do Nibbāna and its associated things, such as the path and fruition, become manifest. It is said that the life-continuum then... proceeds. Now, to show the basis of the knowledge of reviewing, he spoke the verse beginning, “The path, fruition, and Nibbāna.” Therein, “the wise one” is a fruition-attainer endowed with noble wisdom. “In the inferior” means the abandoned defilements. “In the remaining” means the unabandoned defilements to be cut off by a higher path. But these two reviews—of abandoned and remaining defilements—are not obtained by certain individuals who are on the verge of death or who are not skilled in the classification of defilements; thus it is said, “he reviews or not.” And here, in the Visuddhimagga, first the reviewing of the path is stated, then the reviewing of fruition, then the reviewing of abandoned defilements, then the reviewing of remaining defilements. At the end, the reviewing of Nibbāna is stated. In the commentary to the Paṭisambhidāmagga, however, the reviewing of defilements is intended to be first. For it is said there: “Among the reviews, the first is the reviewing of defilements, then the reviews of the path, fruition, and Nibbāna.” But that is said because in the Pāli, before the exposition of the knowledge of reviewing, the knowledge of liberation came separately, as “wisdom in contemplating what is cut off, the knowledge of liberation.” Here, “what is cut off” means the host of defilements eradicated by the respective paths. But when speaking in accordance with the Pāli, it should be said that first is the reviewing of the abandoned defilements, then the reviewing of the path factors, enlightenment factors, etc., individually, then the reviewing of Nibbāna which is their object, then the reviewing of the states of fruition, then the reviewing of Nibbāna which is their object. For in the Pāli exposition of the knowledge of reviewing, Nibbāna is mentioned twice, in the section on the path and in the section on fruition. Thus, it is established that the reviewing of Nibbāna occurs somewhere—at the beginning, in the middle, in between, or at the end—of the other reviews. Likewise, the reviewing of defilements occurs either at the beginning of or after the reviewing of the path and fruition. When this is so, the verse “The path, fruition, and Nibbāna” is also not contradicted. And having done so, it is said in the commentaries on the Adhimānaniddesa: “For he, with gladdened mind born of reviewing the path, fruition, Nibbāna, abandoned defilements, and remaining defilements, is without doubt in the realization of the noble qualities.” And here, for a stream-enterer there are five reviews. Likewise, for a once-returner, five. For a non-returner, five. But since an Arahant has no remaining defilements, there are four. Thus, there are nineteen reviews. And this is said with reference to what is obtained in its complete form. But it also occurs in an incomplete form. Thus, in the commentary to the Cūḷadukkhakkhandha Sutta it is said: “But it is not complete for everyone. For one person reviews only the abandoned defilements. One, only the remaining defilements. One, only the path. One, only the fruition. One, only Nibbāna. But among these five reviews, it is said that it is not proper not to obtain one or two.” Thus, the fourfold path to be developed by the method of the six purifications is called the purification by knowledge and vision; this is the connection. And it should be seen that by the word “path” here, the fourfold path knowledge is taken, and by way of proceeding in conformity with it, the fruition knowledge is also taken. “Here” means in the insight meditation subject. “Therein” means in those contemplations, path, and fruition. Adherence is `abhinivesa`. The meaning is the proceeding by grasping firmly onto the internal aggregates, like the foot of Mount Sineru planted in the rock of the earth below. The adherence “self” is self-adherence. Relinquishing that self-adherence. “Relinquishing” means: because the fact that internal phenomena are merely dependent on conditions and their momentary dissolution is not seen, that adherence persists. Therefore, having seen that pair clearly, by means of repeated contemplation such as “form is not-self, feeling is not-self,” they release that adherence. This is the meaning. It becomes a gateway to liberation, because it is the entrance door for the path and fruition designated as the emptiness liberation. “The sign of perversion” means perversion is the approaching, undertaking, or proceeding in a contrary way. The meaning is the undertaking or proceeding as “permanent in the impermanent.” That itself, being the proximate cause for the arising of defilements, is the sign; thus, “the sign of perversion.” “Relinquishing” means: because the momentary dissolution of internal phenomena is not seen, that sign occurs. Therefore, having seen their momentary dissolution clearly, by means of repeated contemplation such as “form is impermanent, feeling is impermanent,” they release that sign. This is the meaning. “Craving-aspiration” means craving itself, due to attachment, is the placing or firm establishment of the mind on an object; thus, it is aspiration. This is craving-aspiration. Relinquishing that craving-aspiration. “Relinquishing” means: because the nature of internal phenomena as a great mass of dangers is not seen, that aspiration occurs. Therefore, having seen their nature as a great mass of dangers clearly, by means of repeated contemplation such as “form is suffering, feeling is suffering,” they release that aspiration. This is the meaning. “Therefore” means because these three contemplations, which are gateways to liberation, are thus specially named. Therefore. Because the accomplishment of the goal by means of seeing formations as empty is simply the power of knowledge, which is the opponent of the grasping of views that is the adherence to self, therefore, for one who thus contemplates and is liberated, both insight and the path acquire the name by the function of concomitant knowledge. As it is said: “If the emergence is from emptiness... the path is called the emptiness liberation.” The accomplishment of the goal by means of seeing impermanence is also the power of faith, which is the opponent of the grasping of conceit that is the adherence to a sign. Therefore, for one who thus contemplates and is liberated, both insight and the path acquire the name by the function of concomitant faith. As it is said: “If from impermanence... it is called the signless liberation.” The accomplishment of the goal by means of seeing suffering is also the power of concentration, which is the opponent of the grasping of craving, known as aspiration. Therefore, for one who thus contemplates and is liberated, both insight and the path acquire the name by the function of concomitant concentration. As it is said: “If from suffering... it is called the desireless liberation.” And this is said in the Paṭisambhidāmagga: “For one who attends to impermanence, the faculty of faith is predominant. For one who attends to suffering, the faculty of concentration is predominant. For one who attends to not-self, the faculty of wisdom is predominant.” But on the path, the special function of the three states is established solely by means of the approach of insight; thus it is said: “the path... acquires the names.” Therein, a noble disciple liberated by the emptiness liberation is called a “Dhamma-follower” at the moment of the stream-entry path; in the six intermediate path and fruition moments, he is called “one attained to view”; at the moment of Arahantship fruition, he is called “one liberated by wisdom.” One liberated by the signless liberation is called a “faith-follower” at the moment of the stream-entry path; in the seven higher stages, he is called “one liberated by faith.” But one liberated by the desireless liberation is called a “body-witness” in all eight stages. That very one, liberated after making the formless jhāna his basis, standing in the fruition of Arahantship, is called “one liberated in both ways.” Thus far, what was stated earlier—

Katamoca puggalo sattakkhattuparamo idhekacco puggalo tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti, avinipātadhammo niyato, sambodhiparāyano, so sattakkhattuṃ deveca manusseca sandhāvitvā saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo sattakkhattu paramoti.

And what sort of person is a seven-times-at-most? Here, a certain person, with the utter destruction of the three fetters, is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, assured, and bound for enlightenment. Having transmigrated and wandered among devas and humans for seven times, he makes an end of suffering. This person is called a seven-times-at-most.

Ettha hi ca saddo aniyamattho. Etena yoca deveeva sattakkhattuṃ saṃsarati. Yoca manusseeva sattakkhattuṃ saṃsarati. Yoca deveca manusseca missakabhava vasena sattakkhattuṃ saṃsarati. Tividho peso sattakkhattu paramonāmāti dasseti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana missakabhava vasenassa attho vutto. Etthaca yasmā mahaggatajjhānassaca uparimagga vipassanā yaca ānubhāvaṃ anapekkhitvā kevalaṃ imassa maggassa ānubhāvagatiyā eva sattakkhattuparamonāma vutto. Soca pāḷiyaṃ katamesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā. Sattakkhattuparamassa kolaṃ kolassa ekabījissa sakadāgāmissa yoca diṭṭhevadhamme arahāti vuttattā kāmabhaveeva jhānarahito sukkhavipassakovā [M 0.0451] parihīnajjhānovā daṭṭhabbo. Tenevaca paṭisambhidāmaggaṭṭha kathāyaṃ tayopi ime sotāpannā kāmabhavavasena vuttā. Rūpārūpabhave pana bahukāpi paṭisandhiyo gaṇhantīti vuttaṃ. Aṅguttaraṭṭhakathāyañca aṭṭhamaṃ bhavanti kāmabhave aṭṭhamaṃ paṭisandhinti vuttaṃ. Tasmā ye kāmabhaveyeva sattavārato oraṃvā diṭṭhadhamme yevavā uparimaggaṃ gaṇhanti. Tesaṃ tathārūpo pavattiviseso upari maggavipassanābalena siddhoti veditabbo. Tathā hi aṭṭhakathāsu upari tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ vipassanā niyāmetīti vuttaṃ. Ye pana diṭṭhadhammevā sakkaanāthapiṇḍikavisākhādayo viya sattasu bhavesu yatthakatthaci bhavevā jhānaṃ uppādetvā brahmalokaṃ gacchanti. Yeca brahmalokeyeva sotāpattimaggaṃ labhitvā tattheva parinibbāyanti. Tesaṃ tathārūpo pavatti viseso mahaggatajjhānabalena siddhoti. Yasmāca pāḷiyaṃ sattakkhattuṃ devecāti etena kāmabhave satta opapātika paṭisandhiyo dasseti. Sattakkhattuṃ manussecāti etena satta gabbhaseyyakapaṭisandhiyo dassetīti ubhayena cuddasa paṭisandhiyo dassitā honti. Tasmā tena pariyāyena labbhamāne cuddasabhave sandhāya sakkapañhasutte –

Here, the word 'ca' has an indefinite meaning. By this it is shown that this seven-times-at-most person is of three kinds: one who wanders for seven times only among devas, one who wanders for seven times only among humans, and one who wanders for seven times among both devas and humans by way of a mixed existence. In the commentary, however, its meaning is stated in terms of a mixed existence. And here, since the designation 'seven-times-at-most' is given without regard to the power of the exalted jhānas and of insight into the higher paths, but solely by the progression of the power of this path itself, and since in the Pāli it is stated, 'Of which five is there a conclusion here? The seven-times-at-most, the family-to-family, the single-seed, the once-returner, and the one who is an Arahant in this very life,' he should be understood as one who is only in the sense-sphere existence, devoid of jhāna, a dry-insight practitioner, or one who has fallen away from jhāna. For this very reason, in the commentary to the Paṭisambhidāmagga, it is said that these three stream-enterers are spoken of in terms of the sense-sphere existence. However, it is said that they take many rebirths in the form and formless existences. And in the commentary to the Aṅguttara Nikāya it is said that the eighth existence, the eighth rebirth, is in the sense-sphere. Therefore, for those who, in the sense-sphere existence, attain a higher path in less than seven times or in this very life, it should be understood that their particular course of existence is accomplished by the power of insight for a higher path. Indeed, in the commentaries it is said, 'Insight determines the three higher paths.' But as for those who, like Sakka, Anāthapiṇḍika, Visākhā, and others, in this very life or in any existence whatsoever among the seven, having generated jhāna, go to the Brahma-world; and those who, having attained the path of stream-entry in the Brahma-world itself, attain final Nibbāna right there—their particular course of existence is accomplished by the power of the exalted jhānas. And since in the Pāli, by 'seven times among devas' it indicates seven spontaneously arisen rebirths in the sense-sphere, and by 'seven times among humans' it indicates seven womb-born rebirths, thus by both, fourteen rebirths are shown. Therefore, with reference to the fourteen existences obtainable by that method, in the Sakkapañha Sutta—

Ito satta tato satta, saṃsarāni catuddasāti vuttaṃ. Tathā aṅguttareca tikanipāte sace udāyi ānando avitarāgo kālaṃ kareyya, tena cittapasādena sattakkhattuṃ devesu devarajjaṃ kareyya. Sattakkhattuṃ imasmiṃyeva jambudīpe mahārajjaṃ kareyya. Apica udāyi ānando diṭṭhevadhamme parinibbā yissatīti vuttaṃ. Keci pana imehi suttapadehi sattakkhattu paramassa sotāpannassa kāmabhave cuddasa paṭisandhiyo icchanti. Mahāvaggasaṃyuttaṭīkāyañca keci pana kāmabhave sattakkhattuṃeva uppajjati, na tato uddhanti vadanti. Taṃ vīmaṃsitabbanti vuttaṃ. Vibhaṅge pana tattha tattha aṭṭhānasuttesuca aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo aṭṭhamaṃ bhavaṃ nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatītica, aṅguttare chakkanipāte abhabbo diṭṭhasampanno puggalo aṭṭhamaṃ bhavaṃ nibbattetunti [M 0.0452] ca, mahāniddese ajitapañhe sohāpattimaggañāṇena abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇassa, nirodhena sattabhave thapetvā anama taggesaṃsāre ye uppajjeyyuṃ nāmañca rūpañca, etthete nirujjhanti. Vūpasamanti. Atthaṃ gacchanti. Paṭipassambhantītica, evaṃ daḷhaṃ katvā vuttattā yathāvuttanayeneva tesaṃ suttapadānaṃ attho veditabboti. Rāgadosamohānanti kāmarāgassa dosassa tadekaṭṭhamohassaca. Tanukarattāti yathā sotāpannasantāne uppajjantā dhammikesu kāmavatthūsu balavantā hutvā uppajjanti. Yato tesaṃ methunavatthusamāyogopi pavattati, tathā uppajjituṃ asamatthe katvā saṃlikhanavasena tanukaraṇato. Adhiccuppattivasenaca pariyuṭṭhānamandatāvasenaca tanukabhāvaṃ sādhanatoti attho. Tattha adhiccuppattivasenāti kadāci cirena uppattivasena. Pariyuṭṭhānamandatāyāti cirena uppajjantānaṃpi mandataraṃ pariyuṭṭhānavasena. Mahāsivattherena pana tesaṃpi methunavatthu samāyogo icchito. So mahāṭṭhakathāyaṃ paṭikkhitto. Yañca chakkanipāte migāsālavatthumhi abrahmacārinopi isidattassa brāhmaṇassa sakadāgāmittaṃ bhagavatā byākataṃ, taṃpi tassa āsannamaraṇakāle adhigamavasena byākatanti veditabbaṃ. Sakiṃdeva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā āgamanato sakadāgāmīnāma hotīti yojanā. Yamettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā pathamaparicchede vuttameva. Arahattaṃbhāvetvāti arahattamaggaṃ bhāvetvākhīṇā cattāro āsavā yassāti khīṇāsavo. Dakkhiṇā vuccati kammañca kammaphalañca saddahitvā āyatiṃ phalapaṭilābhatthāya dinnadānaṃ. Dakkhanti vaḍḍhanti sattā etāyāti katvā. Tāya pana dakkhiṇāya vipattikarānaṃ kilesānaṃ sabbaso abhāvato sampattikarānañca sīlakkhandhādiguṇānaṃ sabbaso paripuṇṇattā dakkhiṇeyyesu aggo jeṭṭhako hutvā taṃdakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggahituṃ arahatīti aggadakkhiṇeyyo. Puggalabhedoti catunnaṃ phalaṭṭhapuggalānaṃ saṅkhepabhedo. Vitthārabhedo pana evaṃ veditabbo, aṭṭhakathāsu tāva catuvīsati sotāpannā, dvādasa sakadāgāmino, aṭṭhacattālīsa anāgāmino, dvādasa [M 0.0453] arahantoti phalaṭṭhānaṃ channavutibhedo vutto. Tattha saddhādhimutto paññādhimuttoti dve sotāpannā honti. Te ekabījī kolaṃkolo sattakkhattuparamocāti tīhi guṇitā cha. Puna catūhi paṭipadāhi guṇitā catuvīsati honti. Tividha vimokkhacatupaṭipadānaṃ pana bhedena dvādasa sakadāgāmino dvādasa arahantoca honti. Anāgāmino pana avihesu tāva tayo antarāparinibbāyino, eko upahacca parinibbāyī, eko uddhaṃ soto akaniṭṭhagāmīti pañca. Teyeva sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī asaṅkhāraparinibbāyīcāti dvīhi guṇitā dasa. Tathā atappasu dassasudassīsu ticattālīsa honti. Akaniṭṭhe pana uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmīnāma natthīti cattāro sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyino cattāro asaṅkhāraparinibbāyinoti aṭṭhāti. Sabbe aṭṭhacattālīsa hontīti. Suttanipātaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana dvādasa sotāpannā, dvādasa sakadāgāmino, catuvīsati anāgāmino, dve arahanto, cattāro maggaṭṭhāti catupaññāsa honti. Teyeva saddhādhura paññādhura vasena dvīhi guṇitā aṭṭhasataṃ puggalā hontīti āgato. Etthāti etasmiṃ puggalabhede. Sabbesaṃpīti catunnaṃ phalaṭṭhānaṃpi sādhāraṇāva. Na nirodhasamāpatti viya ekaccānaṃeva sādhāraṇāti adhippāyo. Ativiya mamāyitassa abhinindi tassa ajjhositassa attano cittasantānassa apavattikaraṇaṃ nāma bahalarāgavimuttānaṃeva sijjhatīti vuttaṃ, anāgāmīnañceva arahantānañcalabbhatīti. Tesaṃpi aṭṭhasamāpattilābhīnaṃ kāmarūpabhavagatānaññeva idha gahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kasmā, ādito paṭṭhāya anupubbanirodhabaleneva gantabbattā. Tenāha tatthātiādi. Tatrāyaṃ vidhi, pathamajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya tattha gate saṅkhāre aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati. Tato dutīyajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya tatthagate saṅkhāre tatheva vipassati. Tato tatīyaṃ jhānaṃ. Tato catutthaṃ jhānaṃ. Tato pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ. Tato ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ. Tato viññāṇañcā yatanaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya tatthagate saṅkhāre tatheva vipassati. [M 0.0454] Tato ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya nānābaddhaavikopanaṃ saṅghapatimānanaṃ satthupakkosanaṃ addhāna paricchedoti imaṃ catubbidhaṃ pubbakiccaṃ karoti. Tato nevasaññā nāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjati. Ekaṃvā dvevā cittavāre atikkamitvā acittako hoti nirodhaṃ phusatīti. Tatthatatthevāti tato tato jhānato tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vuṭṭhitakāleeva. Vipassantoti nirodhassa samatha vipassanā yuganandhabaleneva pattabbattā vipassanābalenapi cittasantānassa saṇhasukhumabhāvā pādanatthaṃ idaṃ pathamajjhānaṃ aniccantiādinā nayena vipassanto. Yāvaākiñcaññāyatanaṃgantvāti yāva ākiñcaññāyatanajjhānaṃ, tāva samāpajjanavuṭṭhānavipassanāvasena gantvā. Āvajjanādhiṭṭhāna paccavekkhanānipettha icchitabbāniyeva. Teneva hi paṭisambhidāmagge pañcavidhā vasiyo nirodhaparikammesu vuttāti. Tatoparanti ākiñcaññāyatanajjhānagate saṅkhārevipassanānantaraṃ, adhiṭṭhātabbanti adhiṭṭheyyaṃ. Attano sarīrābandhe parikkhāre thapetvā nānābandhāni civarādīni parikkhārāni aggiādinā parissayena māvinassantūtivā, ekasīmāyaṃ saṅghakamme karīyamāne saṅgho maṃ pabhimānessati, tadā vuṭṭhahāmītivā, satthā maṃ kenacikāraṇena pakkosā pessati, tadā vuṭṭhahāmītivā adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ. Ādisaddena nirodhabbhantareeva maraṇaṃ nukho me bhavissatīti evaṃ pavatto addhāna paricchedo gahito. Dvinnaṃ.La. Vocchijjaticittasantati tadatthāya ādito paṭṭhāya tathārūpassa payogavisesassa suṭṭhu katattā. Tatoti tasmiṃ kāle. Anāgāmino anāgāmi phalacittaṃ nirāvajjanaṃpi nipparikammaṃpīti adhippāyo. Tathāhi ādito paṭṭhāya punappunaṃ pavattitaṃ vipassanāparikammameva tassa parikammaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati. Na visuṃ āsannaparikammaṃ nāma atthīti. Paccavekkhananti phalapaccavekkhanaṃ. Evaṃ duvidhaṃ kammaṭṭhānanayaṃ niddisitvā idāni yadatthaṃ so niddisīyati, tadatthe sotujane niyojento bhāve tabbanti gāthamāha. Tattha paṭipajjitabbāti paṭipatti. Paṭipajjantivā etāya uparupari visesanti paṭipatti. Sīlādidhammo. Rasīyati [M 0.0455] nirāmisasukhānubhavanavasena anubhavīyatīti raso. Jhānamagga phalabhūto adhigamadhammo. Arahatta phalamevavā. Tadubhayaṃ paṭicca uppannapītisomanassamevavā. Paṭipattiyā raso paṭipatti raso. Soeva assāditabbaṭṭhena assādo cāti paṭipatti rasassādo. Sāsane paṭipattirasassādaṃ patthayantena bhikkhunā iccevaṃ mayā niddiṭṭhaṃ uttamaṃ bhāvanādvayaṃ bhāvetabbanti sambandho.

It is said: 'Seven existences from this world, seven from that world, making fourteen rounds of transmigration.' Similarly, in the Aṅguttara Nikāya, in the Book of the Threes, it is said: 'If, Udāyī, Ānanda, still not free from passion, were to pass away, by the clarity of his mind, he would exercise sovereignty among the gods seven times. Seven times he would exercise great sovereignty in this very Jambudīpa. Moreover, Udāyī, Ānanda will attain final Nibbāna in this very life.' Some, however, interpret these sutta passages to mean that a stream-enterer who is a 'seven-times-at-most' may take fourteen rebirths in the realm of sensual desire. And in the sub-commentary to the Mahāvagga Saṃyutta, it is said that some say one is reborn only seven times in the realm of sensual desire, and not beyond that, and that this should be investigated. However, in the Vibhaṅga and in the Aṭṭhāna Suttas here and there, it is said: 'It is impossible, there is no occasion, for a person accomplished in view to generate an eighth existence; such a possibility does not exist.' And in the Aṅguttara Nikāya, in the Book of the Sixes, it is stated: 'A person accomplished in view is incapable of generating an eighth existence.' And in the Mahāniddesa, in the Ajita's Questions, it is said: 'Through the knowledge of the stream-entry path, with the cessation of volitional consciousness, setting aside seven existences, whatever name-and-form might arise in beginningless saṃsāra, here they cease, are pacified, come to an end, and are tranquillized.' Since it has been stated so firmly, the meaning of those sutta passages should be understood in the manner stated. By 'lust, hatred, and delusion' (rāgadosamohānaṃ) is meant sensual lust, hatred, and the delusion associated with them. By 'attenuated' (tanukarattāti) is meant that whereas in the continuum of a stream-enterer, defilements arise strongly regarding lawful sensual objects—since for them even the occasion of sexual intercourse occurs—for the once-returner they are made incapable of arising in that way, by way of attrition, thus achieving attenuation. The meaning is that attenuation is achieved by way of infrequent arising and by way of weak obsession. Here, 'by way of infrequent arising' means by way of arising only occasionally and after a long time. And 'by way of weak obsession' means by way of a weaker obsession even for those that arise after a long time. However, the Elder Mahāsīva held that even for them, the occasion of sexual intercourse is possible. This is refuted in the Great Commentary. And what was declared by the Blessed One in the Book of the Sixes, in the story of Migasālā, that even Isidatta the brahmin, though not celibate, was a once-returner, this too should be understood as declared by way of his attainment at the time of his approaching death. The explanation is that one is called a 'once-returner' (sakadāgāmī) because of coming to this world just once more. What is to be said here has already been stated below in the first chapter. By 'having developed arahantship' (arahattaṃ bhāvetvā) is meant having cultivated the path to arahantship. One whose four taints are destroyed is called 'one with destroyed taints' (khīṇāsavo). Dakkhiṇā is said to be a gift given with faith in kamma and its results, for the sake of obtaining future fruit. It is so called because beings 'prosper' (dakkhanti) and 'grow' (vaḍḍhanti) by it. Because of the complete absence of defilements that cause failure and the complete perfection of qualities that lead to success, such as the aggregate of virtue, the Arahant, being foremost and chief among those worthy of offerings, is worthy to receive that offering, hence 'foremost worthy of offerings' (aggadakkhiṇeyyo). By 'classification of persons' (puggalabhedo) is meant a brief classification of the four kinds of persons established in fruition. However, the detailed classification should be understood thus: In the commentaries, a ninety-sixfold classification of persons established in fruition is stated: twenty-four stream-enterers, twelve once-returners, forty-eight non-returners, and twelve arahants. Among them, there are two kinds of stream-enterers: the faith-devoted and the wisdom-devoted. These, multiplied by the three types—the one-seeder, the family-to-family, and the seven-times-at-most—become six. Again, multiplied by the four paths of practice, they become twenty-four. By the distinction of the three liberations and the four paths of practice, there are twelve once-returners and twelve arahants. The non-returners are as follows: In the Aviha realm, there are three who attain parinibbāna in the interval, one who attains parinibbāna upon landing, and one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, making five. These same five, multiplied by two—the one who attains parinibbāna with prompting (sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī) and the one who attains parinibbāna without prompting (asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī)—become ten. Similarly, in the Atappa, Sudassa, and Sudassī realms, there are forty-three. However, in the Akaniṭṭha realm, since there is no 'one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm,' there are four who attain parinibbāna with prompting and four who attain parinibbāna without prompting, making eight. All together, they are forty-eight. However, in the Suttanipāta Commentary, it is stated that there are twelve stream-enterers, twelve once-returners, twenty-four non-returners, two arahants, and four persons on the path, making fifty-four. These same fifty-four, multiplied by two according to the vehicle of faith and the vehicle of wisdom, become one hundred and eight persons. By 'here' (ettha) is meant in this classification of persons. By 'all' (sabbesaṃpi) is meant that it is common to all four kinds of persons established in fruition. The meaning is that it is not common to only some, like the attainment of cessation. It is said that the non-occurrence of one's own mental continuum, which is excessively cherished, delighted in, and clung to, is accomplished only by those liberated from strong lust, and is obtained only by non-returners and arahants. Even among them, it should be understood that only those who have obtained the eight attainments and exist in the sensual or form existences are meant here. Why? Because from the beginning, one must proceed by the power of successive cessation. Therefore, it is said: 'There, etc.' This is the method there: After attaining the first jhāna and emerging, one contemplates the formations therein as impermanent, unsatisfactory, and non-self. Then one attains the second jhāna, emerges, and similarly contemplates the formations therein. Then the third jhāna. Then the fourth jhāna. Then the fifth jhāna. Then the base of the infinity of space. Then, after attaining the base of the infinity of consciousness and emerging, one contemplates the formations therein in the same way. Then, after attaining the base of nothingness and emerging, one performs these four kinds of preliminary tasks: ensuring the safety of one's various belongings, being responsive to the Sangha, heeding the Teacher's call, and determining the duration. Then one attains the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. After one or two thought-processes have passed, one becomes without mind and touches cessation. By 'there and there' (tatthatattheva) is meant from each jhāna, at the very time of emerging from that jhāna. By 'contemplating' (vipassanto) is meant that because cessation is to be attained only by the power of serenity and insight yoked together, and for the purpose of producing the subtle and refined nature of the mental continuum by the power of insight, one contemplates in the manner beginning with 'this first jhāna is impermanent,' etc. By 'having gone up to the base of nothingness' (yāva ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ gantvā) is meant having gone up to the jhāna of the base of nothingness by way of entering, emerging, and contemplating. Adverting, resolving, and reviewing are indeed desired here. For this very reason, in the Paṭisambhidāmagga, five kinds of mastery are stated regarding the preliminaries to cessation. By 'beyond that' (tatoparaṃ) is meant after contemplating the formations in the jhāna of the base of nothingness. What is to be resolved (adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ) is the resolve (adhiṭṭheyyaṃ). Having secured one's own bodily requisites, [one resolves]: 'May my various belongings, such as robes and other requisites, not be destroyed by dangers like fire'; or, 'If the Sangha is performing a formal act within a single boundary and requires my presence, then I will arise'; or, 'If the Teacher sends for me for some reason, then I will arise'—this is the act of resolving. By the word 'etc.' (ādi) is included the determination of duration that occurs thus: 'Lest death should occur for me within the attainment of cessation.' The mental continuum is cut off for that purpose, because such a special exertion has been thoroughly made from the beginning. By 'at that time' (tato) is meant at that time. The meaning is that for the non-returner, the non-returner fruition consciousness is without adverting and without preliminary work. For thus, the insight preliminary work, repeatedly practiced from the beginning, itself stands in the place of its preliminary work. There is no separate proximate preliminary work. By 'reviewing' (paccavekkhaṇaṃ) is meant reviewing the fruition. Having thus explained the twofold method of meditation, now, enjoining the listeners to that purpose for which it is explained, he speaks the verse: 'One should cultivate it' (bhāvetabbaṃ). Here, 'to be practiced' (paṭipajjitabbaṃ) is practice (paṭipatti). Or, that by which one progresses higher and higher is practice. This refers to the Dhamma beginning with virtue. That which is tasted, that which is experienced by way of experiencing spiritual happiness, is 'flavor' (raso). This refers to the Dhamma of attainment, which is the jhāna, path, and fruition; or, just the fruition of arahantship; or, the joy and gladness arisen dependent on both. The flavor of practice is the practice-flavor. And that same practice-flavor, by reason of being something to be savored, is 'savor,' hence 'the savor of the practice-flavor' (paṭipatti rasassādo). The connection is that a monk desiring the savor of the practice-flavor in the Dispensation should cultivate this supreme twofold development, thus explained by me.

Iti paramatthadīpaniyānāma abhidhammatthasaṅgahassa

Thus, the commentary on the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha named 'The Exposition of the Ultimate Meaning'.

Catutthavaṇṇanāya kammaṭṭhānasaṅgahassa

The fourth exposition on the summary of meditation subjects.

Paramatthadipanā niṭṭhitā.

The Paramatthadīpanī is completed.

Nigama paramatthadīpanī

Conclusion to The Exposition of the Ultimate Meaning.

172. Cārittena kulācārena sobhite ñāti mitta dhana bhogasampattiyā visāle kule udayo vaḍḍhi yassa soti cārittasobhitavisālakulodayo. Tena. Saddhāya abhivuḍḍhānaṃ parisuddhānañca attano sīlasutacāgādiguṇānaṃ udayo vaḍḍhi etasminti saddhātivuḍḍhaparisuddhaguṇodayo. Tena. Nampavhayenāti nampanāmakena upāsakena. Paṇidhāyāti bhusaṃ nidhāya hadaye thapetvā upādāya paṭicca. Parānukampanti paresaṃ attano mandabuddhīnaṃ pacchimajanānaṃ anukampaṃ anudayaṃ kāruññaṃ paṇidhāyāti sambandho. Patthitanti abhiyācitaṃ. Puññena tena vipulenāti tena vipulena abhidhammattha saṅgahapakaraṇassa karaṇapuññena. Tumūlasomanti evaṃ nāmakaṃ vihāraṃ. Vuttañhi khuddasikkhāṭīkāyaṃsīhaḷadīpe tumūlasomavihāre saṅghassa pākavattaṃpi tāla paṇṇaṃ vikkiṇitvā karīyati. Na hi tattha paṇṇena attho atthi. Sabbepi iṭṭhakacchannā pāsādādayoti. Eso kira vihāro ādito abhayagirirañño aggamahesibhūtāya somadeviyā kārāpitattā yāvajjatanāpi somavihārotveva paññāyittha. Tumūlasaddo pana vipulasaddapariyāyo.

172. One whose rise in a vast family is adorned by good conduct and family traditions, whose relatives, friends, wealth, and prosperity flourish—such a one is called 'adorned with good conduct and flourishing in a vast family.' By this. For those who grow in faith and whose virtues—such as morality, learning, generosity, and so on—are purified, their arising and increase are called 'the arising of virtues purified by faith.' By this. 'By name Nampa'—by the lay follower named Nampa. 'Having resolved'—firmly placing it in the heart, taking it up, relying on it. 'Compassion for others'—having compassion, kindness, and sympathy for other beings, for later generations with weak understanding, resolving thus—this is the connection. 'Requested'—earnestly sought. 'By that abundant merit'—by that abundant merit of composing this Abhidhamma compendium. 'Tumūlasoma'—a monastery of such a name. For it is stated in the Khuddasikkhāṭīkā: 'In Sri Lanka, at the Tumūlasoma Monastery, even the provision for the Saṅgha's food is made by selling palm leaves. Indeed, there is no need for leaves there, for all the buildings, including the mansions, are roofed with bricks.' This monastery, it is said, was originally built by Queen Somadevī, the chief queen of King Abhayagiri, and even to this day, it is known as the Soma Monastery. The term 'Tumūla,' however, is a synonym for 'vipula' (vast).

Athettha [M 0.0456] vattati saddo, tumūlo bheravo mahā;

Hatthināge padinnamhi, sivīnaṃ raṭṭhavaḍḍhaneti.

And here a sound arises, tumultuous, dreadful, great; when given to the noble elephant, for the prosperity of the Sivi kingdom.

Ādīsu

And so forth.

Viya. Soca vihāro saṭṭhimattehi mahāpariveṇehi saṇṭhito hotīti ativiya vipulo mahanto vitthiṇṇo hoti. Tasmā so vipulattā mahantattā vitthiṇṇattā tumūla somoti vuccati. Taṃ tumūlasomaṃ. Atthato mahāsoma vihāranti vuttaṃ hoti. Etena thero attano ācariyavaṃsassa vasana vihāraṃ kitteti. Attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pana nāmarūpaparicchede kittitaṃ. Dhaññādhivāsanti tasmiṃ vihāre ādikammikabhūta mahindattherādīnaṃ puññavantattherānaṃ ajjhāvuṭṭhabhūtaṃ. Dīpapasādaka mahāmahindattherassa hi vaṃse jātattā tasmiṃ vihāre ādikammikabhūto mahātheropi mahindattheronāmāti dhātuvaṃse vutto. Uditoditanti ativiya uditaṃ. Nabhamajjhe puṇṇacandamaṇḍalaṃ viya sakalasīhaḷadīpe ativiya uggatanti attho. Ariyamaggapaññāvasena pariyattivesārajjādi paññāvasenavā avadātehi pariyodātehi guṇehi sotitāti paññāvadātaguṇasotitā. Te eva lajjīpāpagarahino. Maññantūti anussarantu. Puññavibhāvodaya maṅgalāyāti vipulānaṃ puññānaṃ vaḍḍhisaṅkhāta maṅgalatthāya. Tatrāyaṃ yojanā, puññena tena vipulena dhaññādhivāsaṃ uditoditaṃ tumūlasoma vihārañca tattha nipāsino mahindattherādike paññāvadāta guṇasobhite lajjibhūte bhikkhūca puññavibhavodayamaṅgalāya āyukantaṃ maññantu pacchimā janāti. Athavā, taṃvihāraṃ aññe paññāvadāta guṇasobhita lajjī bhikkhū maññantūti yojanā. Etena thero pacchimajanānaṃ chasu anuttariyadhammesu anussatānuttariyasaṅkhātaṃ puññavisesañca mayaṃpi tādisaguṇabhāgino bhavissāmāti ussāhanupāyañca paṭipādesīti.

Similarly, that monastery, established with around sixty great monastic residences, was exceedingly vast, large, and extensive. Therefore, because of its vastness, largeness, and extensiveness, it is called Tumūlasoma. That Tumūlasoma, in meaning, is called the Great Soma Monastery. By this, the Elder praises the dwelling-place of his own teacher's lineage. Moreover, his own dwelling place is praised in the Nāmarūpapariccheda. Dhaññādhivāsa—in that monastery, which was the initial abode of great elders like Mahinda Thera and other virtuous elders, it was thoroughly inhabited. Because he was born in the lineage of the great Mahinda Thera, the illuminator of the Island (of Sri Lanka), even the great Elder Mahinda Thera himself is mentioned in the Dhatuvaṃsa (Chronicle of Relics) as the initial resident of that monastery. Uditodita—exceedingly renowned. Like the full moon in the middle of the sky, he was exceedingly prominent throughout the entire island of Sri Lanka—this is the meaning. Endowed with the wisdom of the noble path, or by means of the wisdom of proficiency in the scriptures, etc., purified by pure and thoroughly pure qualities, thus, he is called 'purified by wisdom and clear virtues.' They are indeed modest and disdainful of evil. Maññantu—may they remember. Puññavibhāvodaya maṅgalāya—for the sake of the auspicious increase of abundant merit. Here, the connection is: 'For the sake of the auspicious increase of abundant merit, may future generations remember that illustrious Dhaññādhivāsa, the Tumūlasoma monastery, and the wise, virtuous, modest monks like Mahinda Thera who resided there, throughout their life.' Alternatively, the connection is: 'May other wise, virtuous, and modest monks remember that monastery.' By this, the Elder instructs future generations in the six unsurpassed qualities of the Dhamma, that is, unsurpassed recollection, and the special merit, thinking, 'May we too become partakers of such virtues,' thus showing the way to strive and practice.

Paramatthadīpanī nigamakathā

The Exposition of the Ultimate Meaning: Concluding Remarks.

Ettāvatāca –

And thus far –

Nagare dīparaṅgamhi, gāme ti nāmake;

Aṭṭhasuññadvayekamhi, sāke jātena yā mayā.

In the city of Dīparaṅga, in the village named Nāma; in the Saka year one thousand two hundred and eight, by me who was born.

Muṃrvāgāme araññamhi, laṅghatīti vissutālaye;

Vasatā mahato bhikkhu, gaṇassa hitakārinā.

in the forest near the village of Muṃrvā, at the abode renowned as 'Laṅghati'; dwelling there, a benefactor of the great community of monks.

Paramatthadīpanīnāma, saṅkhatā sāradassinā;

Sāresīnaṃ hitatthāya, sārāsāravivekinaṃ.

The commentary named 'The Exposition of the Ultimate Meaning', composed by the discerning one; for the benefit of those who seek the essence, discriminating between essence and non-essence.

Suniṭṭhitā ayaṃ ṭīkā, nibbhayā nirupaddavā;

Navapañcadvayekamhi, sāke komudasārade.

This commentary is well-completed, fearless, and without obstacles; in the Saka year one thousand two hundred and fifty-nine, in the Komuda autumn.

Tathā kalyāṇasaṅkappā, sādhūnaṃ amatapphalā;

Niṭṭhaṃ gacchantu sabbepi, nibbhayā nirupaddavā.

Likewise, may all wholesome intentions of the good, bearing the fruit of the deathless, reach completion, fearless and without obstacles.

Yathā lokamhi jotanti, ubho candimasūriyā;

Tatheva paramatthesu, ayaṃ paramatthadīpanī.

As in the world both the moon and the sun shine, so too in the ultimate truths does this Paramatthadīpanī shine.

Pāḷiyattesu sā subhā, saddaniruttidīpanī;

Ubho lokamhi jotantu, saddhammo yāva tiṭṭhatīti.

Beautiful in the Pali texts, she illuminates grammar and etymology; may both shine in the world, as long as the True Dhamma lasts.

Tattha nagare dīparaṅgamhīti dīpavāsimahājanaṃ rañjetīti dīparaṅganti laddhanāme nagare. Gāme nāmaketi rohitamigānaṃ nivāsabhūmitale patiṭṭhitattā evaṃnāmake mahāgāme. Sāketi kaliyuge. Yā mayāti paramatthadīpanīnāma yāṭīkā mayā saṅkhatāti sambandho. Laṅghatīti vissutālayeti evaṃvissute araññavihāre. Sāresīnanti sāragavesīnaṃ. Sārāsāravivekinanti ayaṃ sāro ayaṃ asāroti evaṃ sārañca asārañcavive cetvā jānituṃ samatthānaṃ. Sāketi kaliyuge. Komudasāra deti kumudapupphayutte saradautu pariyāpannepacchi makattikamāse. Amatapphalāti nibbānapayojanā. Subhāti atthabyañjanasampattiyā sobhaṇā. Saddhammoti tividhaṃ satthusāsanaṃ vuccatīti.

There, 'in the city of Dīparaṅga' means in the city that has obtained the name Dīparaṅga because it delights the great populace dwelling on the island. And 'in the village named Nāmaka' means in the great village thus named because it is established on the ground, the dwelling place of rohita deer. And 'Sāka' means in the Kali Yuga. And 'yā mayā' (that by me) refers to the connection that the commentary named Paramatthadīpanī was composed by me. And 'Laṅghati' means in the forest monastery thus renowned as 'Laṅghati'. And 'Sāresīnaṃ' means of those seeking the essence. And 'Sārāsāravivekinan' means of those capable of knowing by distinguishing thus: 'This is essence, this is non-essence,' thus distinguishing essence and non-essence. And 'Sāka' means in the Kali Yuga. And 'Komudasārade' means in the last month of Kattika, which falls within the autumn season, abounding with water lilies. And 'Amatapphalā' means having Nibbāna as its purpose. And 'Subhā' means beautiful by virtue of the excellence of meaning and expression. And 'Saddhamma' is said to be the threefold teaching of the Teacher.

Iti abhidhammatthasaṅgahapakaraṇassa catutthasaṃvaṇṇanā

Thus concludes the fourth exposition of the treatise Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha.

Bhūtā paramatthadīpanīnāmā yaṃṭīkā

This commentary named 'The Exposition of the Ultimate Meaning' has come into being,

Sabbākārena niṭṭhitā.

completed in every respect.
